Trend Spotting & Execution: Stay on top of audio trends, meme formats, and social media viral moments, quickly pitching and executing relevant ideas tailored to our audience.

• 
Copywriting: Craft fun, engaging captions, on-screen text, and hooks that resonate with our community of mamas and moms-to-be.

• 
Event & Project Support: Assist on-site with photoshoots, store events, and other exciting marketing campaigns.

• 
Performance Curiosity: Collaborate with the team to analyze content performance, testing what works best and continually refining our content strategy based on data.

Who You Are

We are looking for someone who loves social media (especially TikTok), video editing, and isn't afraid to step in front of or behind the camera to produce quick, on-trend content.

• 
Education: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Marketing, Digital Media, Communication, Visual Design, or a related field.

• 
Creative & Bold: You have a strong visual eye, passion for branding, and aren't afraid to try new creative concepts or experiment with funny/trending video ideas on the fly.

• 
SoMe Native: You naturally stay up to date on TikTok and Instagram trends, algorithm shifts, and emerging digital content styles.

• 
Data-Curious: You don't just love creating content—you are genuinely curious about reach, engagement, and understanding why certain videos go viral or drive conversions.

• 
Work Experience: Prior experience in content creation, video editing (CapCut, Premiere, InShot, Canva, etc.), or managing brand social channels is preferred (portfolio or work samples are a huge plus!).

• 
Language: Fluent in English. If you can speak Dutch, Swedish, or German, it is a plus.

What We Offer

• 
Paid Position: Fair compensation.

• 
Real Impact & Creative Freedom: Your ideas won't just sit in a pitch document—you'll see them come to life across channels with thousands of active followers.

• 
Flexibility: Work 8–10 hours a week (2 days in the office) with schedule flexibility designed to fit around your university classes and exams.

• 
Growth & Mentorship: Gain hands-on experience in a fast-paced DTC e-commerce environment, learning directly from experienced e-commerce and brand marketers.

• 
Warm Team Culture: Join an open, supportive, and passionate team located in Copenhagen.

• 
Perks: Free lunch, office located in the city center, and a great discount on momkind products!

How to Apply

Ready to bring your creative energy to momkind?

Please send your CV, a short cover letter, and a link to your portfolio, TikTok/Instagram profile, or video work samples if available.

• Contact Person: Lauren Blair Klarskov

We review applications on a rolling basis, so don't hesitate to reach out! We can't wait to meet you.

For more information or questions please contact us at lauren@momkind.dk

Working at

momkind

Momkind is a Ecommerce business founded in 2019 offering products for pregnancy, postpartum, nursing and beyond. Through co-creation with the momkind community we test and develop products for all stages of motherhood. Working at momkind is fun, engaging and interesting. We work collaboratively, and we dare to take risks and to learn from our mistakes. We're on a growth journey and becoming part of the company in this stage means loads of responsibility and an exciting opportunity to develop and learn.

jobs.occupation: Business Consultant, Regulatory Banking Services, Netcompany Banking Services
jobs.description:
Job Description

Would you like to work with financial regulation and compliance while contributing to the development of a growing regulatory services business at Netcompany Banking Services?

As a Business Consultant, you will work with compliance and risk management while supporting legal and governance matters for financial institutions. You will combine your regulatory expertise with an analytical and structured approach to help our customers navigate complex regulatory requirements and strengthen their compliance and risk frameworks.

We are currently expanding our regulatory services offering, where you will play an important role in delivering and further developing our services to financial institutions. Our services within the compliance and risk areas cover the regulatory process from monitoring legislation and assessing compliance risks to annual planning, data-supported compliance reviews and regulatory reporting.

We focus on the use of automation and new technologies to develop efficient and scalable regulatory services. Working closely with colleagues across data and technology, you will contribute to high-quality customer deliveries and the continued development of regulatory Services.

Netcompany Banking Services

We deliver various IT solutions and services to banks and savings institutions across Denmark and other Nordic countries. We provide a modern, cloud-based core banking platform serving more than 50 Nordic banks with over 2 million end customers. Our solutions encompass daily banking operations, mobile and internet banking, payments, investment management, risk management, compliance, and open banking.

Responsibilities

As a Business Consultant, you will support the Head of Regulatory Banking Services in delivering high-quality regulatory services to financial institutions. You will contribute to daily customer deliveries while helping to develop and standardise processes, control frameworks and reporting models.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• 
Prepare and maintain compliance risk assessments and annual compliance plans for financial clients.

• 
Develop control frameworks, control questions and supporting documentation, including reviewing and quality-assuring data and control results.

• 
Prepare compliance review reports, quarterly and annual reports, and follow up on identified risks, observations and recommendations.

• 
Monitor and assess relevant financial regulation and contribute to translating regulatory requirements into control activities, policies, procedures and governance documentation.

• 
Contribute to the development of regulatory services, including supporting risk management activities and collaborating with data and technology specialists to improve and automate processes.

About you

We imagine that you have:

• 
A relevant academic degree, such as law, business law or a related field, combined with around 2–5 years of experience in compliance, financial regulation or similar areas.

• 
Solid knowledge of financial regulation and preferably experience from a compliance function within a financial institution, ideally in the second line of defence.

• 
Practical experience with regulatory risk assessments, control frameworks, documentation and compliance reporting. Experience with risk management is an advantage.

• 
Strong analytical and communication skills, a structured approach to your work and an interest in data, technology and the digitalisation of regulatory processes.

• 
Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must. Your day-to-day working environment will, however, primarily be Danish-speaking.

Join an inclusive community

We highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand your network.

Send us an application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

jobs.occupation: Team Manager, Guest & Host Care (maternity cover)
jobs.description:
Landfolk is growing, and we want to make our support across booking channels even better. We’re looking for a Team Manager as a maternity cover for our international Guest & Host Care team, with a particular focus on the external booking channels we work with, including Airbnb, Booking.com, Holidu, HomeToGo and Vrbo.

What excites us about this role

Great support starts with a team that has the confidence, guidance and tools to help. Your day-to-day work will bring together people and operations. You’ll create the conditions for your team to succeed, help your colleagues grow and ensure guests and hosts receive knowledgeable, personal support, with quality at every step.

You’ll work closely with the other Team Managers to set clear priorities, maintain high service standards and build a supportive, motivated team. You’ll also help shape the workflows that make our collaboration with external booking channels work in practice.

You’ll lead by example in support and turn everyday experience, feedback and data into improvements to our processes, tools and collaboration. You’ll have real influence on how we work, in a tech-driven organisation that actively uses data, automation, agents and AI.

What you’ll actually do

You’ll balance daily support, people management and improvements to how the team works.

Your key responsibilities:

• 
Lead and develop your team members through ongoing guidance, monthly one-to-ones and specific, constructive feedback

• 
Ensure helpful, timely support by email, chat and phone, with clear standards for quality and follow-up

• 
Develop support workflows for external booking channels, so the team can confidently navigate both Landfolk’s processes and those of each platform

• 
Help resolve complex guest and host cases, disputes and compensation requests within agreed guidelines

• 
Plan shifts for our student employees and ensure coverage during holidays, sickness and peak season

• 
Take part in recruitment and creating thoughtful onboarding programmes together with your manager and relevant colleagues

• 
Use data and support insights to improve service quality, response times and workflows

• 
Build a supportive, inclusive team culture with room for learning, ownership and honest feedback

The role calls for flexibility and availability to meet the needs of the team and the business, particularly during peak season(s).

About you

You’re motivated by helping both people and operations succeed. You bring structure to a busy day, set clear priorities and stay calm when a situation needs extra care.

You might be a great fit if you:

• 
Have experience in customer service, support, hospitality or a marketplace business, ideally with previous team leadership or people management responsibilities.

• 
Enjoy helping others develop through practical conversations, coaching and feedback.

• 
Can balance high service standards, efficient operations and your team’s well-being.

• 
Take a structured approach to staffing, follow-up and process improvements.

• 
Are comfortable picking up the phone yourself and handling difficult conversations with guests and hosts.

• 
Are curious about our tech-driven organisation and how data, automation and AI can support great service.

• 
Are fluent in written and spoken English. Additional language skills are a plus, but not a requirement.

Experience with external booking platforms is an advantage. What matters most is your ability to learn new systems and turn complex workflows into a straightforward day-to-day experience for the team.

Curious about Landfolk?

At Landfolk, we believe the most memorable holidays happen in homes that are loved and lived in. We’re united by curiosity and driven by a shared purpose of helping people reconnect with nature, culture and the people they love.

Here’s a chance to make your mark on a fast-growing and purpose-driven scaleup with more than 9,000 handpicked holiday homes in Norway, Sweden, Germany, Italy, France, Spain and Denmark.

With us, you’ll:

• 
Learn and grow with more than 100 talented colleagues across tech, commercial, customer care, and creative teams

• 
Be trusted, take ownership and let curiosity guide your work and development

• 
Work in a welcoming, open-minded atmosphere where teamwork and laughs come naturally

• 
Explore how AI can support your work, experiment with your team, and share what you learn

• 
Enjoy flexible working hours, a beautiful office in Aarhus and plenty of moments to come together

• 
Join trips to beautiful holiday homes

Together we’ve already accomplished pretty impressive results, and we’re nowhere near done. Read more about Landfolk

Ready to join us?

Your CV doesn’t have to tick every box. We’re interested in how you think, the questions you ask, and the ideas you’re excited to explore.

Send us your CV and a few words about why you’d like to join the team. Include your answers in a short cover letter and send it along with your CV.

We review applications and interview candidates on a rolling basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as you’re ready, and no later than 30 November 2026.

A few tips before you apply

We look forward to hearing from you.

Bring your service mindset. Enjoy regular daytime hours.

Do you love making people feel welcome, noticing the little details and making a busy day run smoothly? Perhaps you work in a restaurant, hotel, cabin crew or another service role, and you’re ready for working hours that leave more room for life outside work.

At Adversus, we’re looking for an Office Manager to make our office in the heart of Aarhus a welcoming, enjoyable and well-organised place for more than 70 colleagues.

This is a part-time position of approximately 25–30 hours per week, Monday to Friday, with working hours scheduled between 8:30 am and 3:00 pm.

Your role

You’ll take ownership of the practical details that make everyday office life work. From having fresh coffee ready to creating a welcoming space for colleagues and guests, your work will make a difference people notice and appreciate.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Keeping fridges, coffee, snacks and drinks stocked.

• Receiving, unpacking and distributing deliveries.

• Setting out our individually portioned lunches and tidying up afterwards.

• Keeping coffee machines clean and ready for the next cup.

• Keeping shared spaces, meeting rooms and storage areas tidy and organised.

• Handling cardboard, recycling and returnable bottles and cans.

• Monitoring supplies and helping place orders.

• Taking care of practical tasks as they come up.

There’s room for your ideas, too. Whether it’s baking a cake, making the terrace inviting for summer or decorating for Christmas, you’ll have the freedom to add thoughtful touches that make the office feel special.

This is a hands-on role. You should be comfortable with an active working day, including occasional heavy lifting when receiving deliveries or restocking drinks.

What you bring

You know that great service often means noticing what’s needed before anyone asks.

You might have experience as a waiter, flight attendant, receptionist, barista or in another hospitality or service role. That experience would be a great foundation, but there’s no specific education or office background required.

We’re looking for someone who:

• Enjoys helping people and making them feel welcome.

• Takes initiative and follows things through.

• Notice the details while keeping track of everyday priorities.

• Likes keeping things organised and running smoothly.

• Is happy to roll up their sleeves and handle practical tasks.

• Works independently and takes pride in doing a job well.

• Brings warmth, humour and a friendly attitude to the workplace.

Meet Adversus

Adversus is a Danish SaaS company based in central Aarhus. More than 70 colleagues work across teams including Development, Sales and Customer Success.

Our culture is informal and social, with room for different personalities, a good laugh and people who care about each other. In this role, you’ll get to know colleagues across the entire company and become a familiar part of everyone’s working day.

What we offer

• Regular weekday hours and afternoons free.

• A varied role with responsibility and freedom to organise your day.

• An office in the heart of Aarhus.

• A lunch scheme.

• Health and dental insurance.

• Social events and a friendly Friday atmosphere.

• Colleagues who value what you do.

Interested?

Send us your application and tell us a little about yourself, your service experience and why you’d enjoy taking care of everyday life at Adversus.

We’d love to hear from you.

For more information or questions please contact us at jtr@adversus.io or phone number 60141577

**Would you like to use your PCB design skills to create advanced hearing devices that help people with hearing loss connect more easily with the world around them?

**As a PCB Designer at GN Hearing, you will follow your designs from early ideas and prototypes through to finished products ready for production.

Whether you bring established PCB design experience or are ready to build further on a solid foundation, you will have knowledgeable colleagues around you and opportunities to contribute your perspective.

**Welcome to GN Hearing

**You will join Electronic Integration, part of Product Development in R&D at our headquarters in Ballerup. We are responsible for making the electronic components in our hearing aids as compact as possible while maintaining reliable performance and signal integrity.

We work closely with colleagues in mechanical design, electroacoustics, software, radio systems and production. Our team values practical problem-solving and knowledge-sharing, with room for questions and learning from different levels of experience.

**Your contribution is appreciated, and you will:

**

• Design schematics and PCB layouts in Cadence Allegro and OrCAD Capture

• Contribute to PCB solutions from concept development and prototyping through to production release

• Review solutions and design test verification together with PCB design colleagues to resolve issues early

• Work with cross-functional project teams to inform design decisions and develop new solutions

• Collaborate with our production unit in Præstø to make sure that designs are manufacturable

• Create clear and accurate PCB documentation

• Participate in sourcing and qualifying PCB suppliers

**To perform well in the role, we imagine that you:

**

• Bring a relevant degree, e.g. a bachelor’s in electronic engineering

• Have experience with PCB design, and would like to continue developing your skills in a product development environment

• May have experience with PCB manufacturing, assembly processes and IPC standards

• Are familiar with PCB design tools such as Cadence Allegro, OrCAD Capture or Capture CIS Database, or are willing to learn relevant tools

• Enjoy working closely with others to create quality outcomes

• Can communicate proficiently in English

We pride ourselves on encouraging flexible work whenever possible. We trust our people to fulfill their responsibilities, to know when in-person collaboration is better than hybrid, and to be present when it is needed most.

**We are focused on an inclusive recruitment process

**All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. As such, we encourage you to submit your CV without a photo to ensure an equal and fair application process.

Should you have any special requirements for the interview, please let the Hiring Manager know upon accepting the invitation to the interview.

**How to apply?

**Use the ‘APPLY’ link no later than November 27, 2026. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and we may close the position before the application deadline if we find the right candidate. We therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Feel free to only submit your up-to-date CV, including a few sentences outlining your motivation for applying.

**Join us in bringing people closer

**GN brings people closer through our advanced intelligent hearing, audio, video, and gaming solutions. Inspired by people and motivated by innovation, we deliver technology that enhances the senses of hearing and sight. We enable people with hearing loss to overcome real-life problems, improve communication and collaboration for businesses, and provide great experiences for audio and gaming users.

GN Store Nord A/S has entered into a definitive agreement for the sale of GN’s Hearing business to Amplifon S.p.A. to create a global leader in audiology. For GN Group, this creates an opportunity to expand our position in the large audio and video peripherals markets. Read more about the announcement **here.

****We hope you will join us on this journey and look forward to receiving your application.

**

**WHY SPEKTR

**At spektr, we are on a mission to automate the world’s most complex compliance workflows through AI. Founded by the team behind HelloFlow (acquired by Trulioo), spektr is building the infrastructure and AI agents to run compliance at scale.

_Compliance, built like product.

_Financial services has changed enormously. Much of the technology behind compliance hasn’t. Teams still spend hours on manual checks, disconnected systems slow down launches, and entering a new market can mean rebuilding the same processes all over again.

We’re changing that. spektr gives regulated businesses one platform for onboarding, monitoring and investigations, with configurable workflows and AI agents that do the legwork. Product, Operations and Compliance can move together, with the control they need to grow.

It’s a huge opportunity in an industry that has moved slowly for too long. We’ve built a product we’re proud to put in front of the most demanding customers. Now we’re looking for people who want to help get it into their hands.

• $26M raised, including a $20M Series A led by NEA, with backing from Northzone, Seedcamp and PreSeed Ventures.

• Customers worth getting excited about. We work with businesses including Pleo, Trustly, Nexi and Santander. These are large accounts with complex problems, ambitious teams and plenty of room for us to make a difference.

• Three offices: Copenhagen, London and Iași, with customers across more than 15 countries.

**THE OPPORTUNITY

**We are looking for an AI Engineer who is, first and foremost, a product builder. In this role, you won't just be running experiments in a notebook; you will own the end-to-end AI strategy and its direct impact on our customers.

In this role, you will own everything related to AI, LLMs, and intelligent automation.

This is a high-impact role in a fast-growing company. We are looking for someone who thrives in a dynamic environment, loves solving complex compliance puzzles, and is eager to shape the next generation of compliance technology.

**What You Will Be Doing

**

• AI Strategy & Ownership: Own the end-to-end AI roadmap—from selecting the right models (SOTA commercial vs. fine-tuned open source) to deciding how they are integrated into the product core.

• Agentic Feature Design: Design and deploy LLM-powered features including autonomous agents, advanced RAG pipelines, and intelligent document understanding.

• Product-Led AI: Collaborate directly with founders to translate complex compliance "puzzles" into scalable AI solutions. You own the "Why" behind every model choice.

• Continuous Innovation: Stay at the bleeding edge of AI/ML research, proactively identifying new papers or releases that can give spektr a competitive advantage.

• Engineering for Reliability: Turn non-deterministic AI outputs into deterministic product value. You ensure our agents are accurate, explainable, and hallucination-free.

**What We Are Looking For

**

• The Product Mindset: You are a product person at heart. You care about whether the AI actually solves the user's problem, not just if the loss curve is going down.

• High-Agency Builder: You prefer building systems over following manuals. You identify bottlenecks in our AI workflows and fix them before they become tickets.

• AI/ML Expertise: 2+ years of experience in ML, AI, or Data/Backend roles with a deep understanding of modern LLM stacks.

• Technical Mastery: Strong skills in TypeScript (our core) and/or Python, with hands-on experience in frameworks like LangChain or equivalent orchestration layers.

• RAG & Vector Mastery: You’ve built production-grade RAG pipelines and understand the nuances of embedding, retrieval strategy, and re-ranking.

• Evaluation Obsession: You understand that "it works on my machine" doesn't apply to LLMs. You have experience setting up evaluation frameworks to measure and improve model performance.

• Cloud & Scale: Experience deploying AI services in AWS or containerized environments, ensuring they are scalable and cost-effective.

• Communication: You can explain the trade-offs of a specific model architecture to a founder and a technical bottleneck to a peer with equal clarity.

**OUR TECH INTERESTS

**

• Models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, and Open Source (LLaMA, Mistral).

• Stack: TypeScript, Python, LangChain, etc

• Infra: AWS, Kubernetes, CI/CD for LLMs.

**OUR PROCESS

**

• Intro call with our Talent team (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (30 minutes)

• Technical Interview (60 minutes)

**How To Apply

**We hire the smartest, kindest, and most unrelenting people and let them do their best work. You’ll be joining a team with a proven track record and the "Product-Market Fit" to change an entire industry.

spektr is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, disability, sexual orientation or any other characteristic, and we assess every candidate against the same role requirements.

In this Head of Employee Experience role, you'll be…

• 
Setting the vision and one roadmap for our Employee Experience across the employee journey, so colleagues experience one Formalize in every office and every new country.

• 
Building a scalable, intuitive model where people, systems, processes, IT and offices simply work, so day-to-day operations run smoothly on their own, freeing up your team to give personal, high-touch support when it matters most

• 
Setting up one front door for every question on people, workplace and IT, with one ticketing system and a shared knowledge base, solving most questions through self-serve and the rest first time.

• 
Leading a team of around ten across People Operations, Workplace and Internal IT with clear ownership, and making your team's time here a real springboard for their HR careers.

• 
Owning workplace standards, vendors and budgets, and opening new offices on time and on budget from one playbook.

• 
Working with our People Business Partners and Talent Acquisition on journeys that cross teams, such as onboarding and country launches.

Who is the Employee Experience team?

Employee Experience is the team that treats our colleagues like our best customers. We bring People Operations, Workplace, and Internal IT together under one roof because a great workday relies on all three: a contract and conversations that make sense, an office where we celebrate wins together, and a laptop that works from hour one.

Within People Operations, a back office sets standards, systems and automation, while People Operations Partners in the front office are the daily face for colleagues. Our People Business Partners, focused on managers and leaders, work closely with us.

Our principle is high touch where it matters, effortless everywhere else, with one front door for every question and the ambition that colleagues hardly need us.

What you bring

• 
Proven leadership experience across the broader employee experience spectrum, combining People Operations with workplace and internal IT, ideally in a scaling international tech company.

• 
A builder's instinct. Your energy comes from systems, standards and support models that work every day. Events and celebrations matter but aren't the core, so if confetti is what drives you, this probably isn't your role.

• 
You think in models, linking the structural basis to the human interaction it enables, and you know where high personal-touch adds value and where good design does the job better.

• 
Strong on digital: people systems, automation and AI are how the team scales, and you're comfortable owning tooling decisions and the budget behind them.

• 
A strong sense of fairness and consistency, with standards explicit enough to guide people rather than slow them down.

• 
A hands-on leader who builds teams across disciplines and grows people into bigger roles.

• 
Clear communication in English, the credibility to partner effectively with our leadership team, and the ability to work from our Copenhagen office (or Aarhus).

What do we offer you?

• 
A monthly salary ranging from 65,000 to 70,000 DKK.

• 
Continuous development through a clear and transparent career framework, so you always know what the next step looks like, with biannual growth talks and regular check-ins.

• 
Thorough pre- and onboarding to set you up for success.

• 
A culture of ownership, trust and independence, with the support you need.

• 
An office-first culture in a central location in Copenhagen or Aarhus, with benefits including pension, lunch, health insurance and social events.

• 
A strong team spirit where we celebrate wins and enjoy time together across offices.

• 
Our annual Global Summit, where the whole company meets and connects.

Our recruitment process

• 
Send your application and upload relevant information

• 
15–30-minute online interview with our Talent Acquisition team

• 
30-minute interview with our Hiring Manager

• 
30-minute interview with our interim Head of Talent Acquisition

• 
Completion of Personality Assessment

• 
In-person team workshop in Aarhus with representatives of People Operations, Workplace and Internal IT, where you work on a real case such as our future onboarding

About Formalize

Formalize is a tech company founded in 2021 with offices in Aarhus, Copenhagen, Milan, Munich and Madrid. Currently, we are a team of +200 people from +30 nationalities operating in multiple European markets and are one of the fastest growing SaaS scale-ups. We thrive on ambition, deliver impact through pragmatism, and embrace passion and honesty. We are celebrating our wins, learning from our mistakes, and growing together as a team.

Our journey began within the whistleblowing compliance sector, highlighted by the award-winning Whistleblower Software by Formalize, laying the foundation of our success story. Now, we have extended our expertise to a larger compliance universe, including data compliance, risk, and privacy. Our Formalize product helps companies to effortlessly navigate and stay ahead in the ever-changing landscape of compliance. Our platform adapts to regulatory changes, continuously adapting to meet and foresee the evolving needs of our users, ensuring businesses remain compliant and confident in their operations.

Still curious? Read more about us here: About Formalize.

Ready to apply?

We will hold interviews and hire on an ongoing basis. For more information or questions, please contact the responsible recruiter in the Talent Acquisition team. Apply now with your resume and other relevant information through our Career Page. We look forward to seeing your application!

Digital Marketing & E-commerce Specialist – Help Us Scale LeanSails Across Europe

Would you like to help grow a digital business and bring a traditional industry into the future?

At LeanSails, we're on a mission to make buying new sails easier, more transparent, and more affordable for sailors. We've developed a digital sales platform where boat owners can configure their own sails, explore different options, and get instant pricing online.

Having established our business in Denmark, we're now taking the next exciting step: expanding into Sweden, Finland, and eventually the rest of Europe.

We're looking for a Digital Marketing & E-commerce Specialist who is excited about taking ownership of our digital marketing activities and helping us grow our business.

Your Role

You'll become a key part of a small company with big ambitions. You'll have the opportunity to work across the entire digital customer journey – from the first ad impression to the moment a customer orders their new sails.

Your role will combine hands-on digital marketing with contributing to our growth strategy as we enter new markets.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Digital Advertising: Planning, setting up, managing, and optimizing campaigns on Google Ads, Facebook, and Instagram.

• 
SEO & Organic Traffic: Improving our search engine visibility and developing relevant content to attract potential customers.

• 
E-commerce Optimization: Improving our webshop, customer journey, and conversion rates.

• 
Data & Analytics: Using Google Analytics and other tools to understand customer behavior and improve marketing performance.

• 
International Expansion: Planning and executing marketing activities as we launch in new European markets.

• 
Business Development: Contributing ideas and initiatives to improve our digital business model and drive growth.

You'll have plenty of opportunities to shape your own responsibilities, bring new ideas to the table, and influence how we achieve our goals.

Who Are You?

We imagine you have a relevant educational background in digital marketing, e-commerce, communication, or a related field.

You might be a recent graduate or have a few years of professional experience. What matters most to us is your motivation, curiosity, willingness to take responsibility, and ability to turn ideas into action.

Ideally, you:

• 
Have an interest in, and preferably some hands-on experience with, Google Ads, Meta Ads, and digital marketing.

• 
Understand e-commerce and how to attract visitors and convert them into customers.

• 
Have an analytical mindset and enjoy using data to make decisions.

• 
Are proactive, independent, and comfortable experimenting with new ideas.

• 
Enjoy working in a small company where ideas can quickly turn into action.

• 
Communicate confidently in both Danish and English.

You don't need to know anything about sailing! We'll teach you what you need to know about the industry. Your interest in digital business, marketing, and growth is far more important.

What We Offer

At LeanSails, you won't be managing just one small part of a large marketing department.

You'll join a small, entrepreneurial team where you can work across different areas of digital marketing and see the direct impact of your efforts on the company's development.

We offer:

• 
An exciting position with real responsibility and the opportunity to make a difference.

• 
Hands-on experience with international e-commerce and digital business growth.

• 
An informal working environment with short decision-making processes.

• 
Close collaboration with experienced professionals from the sailmaking industry and business development.

• 
Great opportunities to develop your skills as the company grows.

• 
A workplace in Helsingør, Denmark, with flexibility in your daily work.

Employment Type

We are looking for a permanent employee to join the LeanSails team. This position is therefore not open to freelancers, independent consultants, or marketing agencies.

We welcome applications from both recent graduates and experienced candidates. Our priority is finding the right person who wants to become part of our company and contribute to its long-term development.

About LeanSails

LeanSails is a Danish e-commerce company selling custom-made sails directly to boat owners through an innovative digital platform.

We combine years of experience in the sailmaking industry with a modern digital business model that makes buying new sails simpler, more transparent, and more accessible.

Our ambition is to establish LeanSails as a strong European brand in online sail sales.

_Do you enjoy turning data into insights and forecasts that help a global business make better decisions? Are you motivated by working across markets and functions, balancing availability, inventory and commercial priorities?

_We are looking for a Specialist, POSM Demand Planning to join our Global Merchandising & Supply Chain organisation in Copenhagen. In this role, you will support our global demand planning for Point of Sale Materials (POSM), covering areas such as packaging, accessories, displays, sellable items and services.

**Your role

**As our Demand Planning Specialist, you will help develop accurate, reliable and insight-driven item-level forecasts aligned with our commercial, marketing and inventory objectives.

You will work closely with clusters and global teams, with particular focus on new launches and item transitions. Through strong analysis and collaboration, you will help us improve availability while managing inventory and reducing the risk of obsolescence.

**Your Key Responsibilities

****In this role, you will:

**

• Support and execute the global POSM demand planning process, ensuring forecasts are delivered according to agreed timelines and standards.

• Consolidate and validate forecasts across clusters, ensuring strong data quality and timely cross-functional input.

• Develop item-level forecasts across packaging, accessories, displays and sellable POSM.

• Maintain statistical baseline forecasts using demand history, market intelligence, marketing plans, sell-in signals and lifecycle changes.

• Monitor forecast accuracy and bias, identify key demand drivers and conduct root-cause analyses to recommend corrective actions.

• Translate planning and performance data into clear, actionable insights and recommendations.

• Partner with Marketing, Clusters, Supply Planning and Procurement to build reliable forecasts for new launches and SKU transitions.

• Support phase-in and phase-out planning and proactively identify potential excess inventory, shortages and obsolescence risks.

• Work closely with clusters and global functions to align demand plans with commercial calendars, marketing campaigns, inventory targets and supply constraints.

• Contribute to improvements in planning processes, data and systems, helping strengthen planning quality, efficiency and inventory outcomes.

**What We’re Looking For

**You are analytical and comfortable working with data, but equally confident turning numbers into a clear story for stakeholders. You enjoy collaborating across functions and markets, challenging assumptions constructively and taking ownership when something needs to move forward.

**We Imagine That You Bring

**

• 1–3 years of relevant experience within Demand Planning, Supply Planning and/or Merchandise Planning.

• A relevant educational background in areas such as Supply Chain, Logistics, Engineering, Finance & Economics or International Business, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail.

• Practical experience with forecasting, statistical modelling and root-cause analysis.

• An understanding of end-to-end supply chain and inventory trade-offs.

• Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills.

• The ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively across functions.

• A curious, proactive and solution-oriented mindset.

• Strong skills in Excel and PowerPoint.

• Experience with Logility or a similar demand planning system, and/or Aptos or another allocation system.

• Knowledge of Power BI, Power Query or QlikView is considered an advantage.

• Fluency in English.

Experience from retail, fashion or FMCG, as well as working in a global organisation across multiple markets or clusters, would be an advantage

**Additional Information

**

• Global Career Band 5B

**Did we get your attention?

**If you see yourself in the position and would like to become part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you!

We process applications on a continuous basis, which is why we encourage you to send your application as soon as possible.

You can also read more about Pandora on our corporate site.

**About Pandora

**Pandora is the world's largest jewellery brand, specialising in the design, crafting and marketing of accessible luxury jewellery made from high-quality materials. Each piece is created to inspire self-expression, allowing people to share their stories and passions through meaningful jewellery. Pandora jewellery is sold in more than 100 countries through 7,000 points of sale, including more than 2,800 concept stores.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, Pandora employs around 39,000 people worldwide and crafts its jewellery with 100% recycled silver and gold. Pandora is committed to leadership in sustainability and has set out to halve greenhouse gas emissions across its value chain by 2030. Pandora is listed on the Nasdaq Copenhagen stock exchange and generated revenue of DKK 32.5 billion (EUR 4.4 billion) in 2025.

With an IoT platform connecting more millions of devices, and growing - Trackunit is building the connectivity layer underneath the construction industry. Every one of those units carries a cellular radio, and every one of those radios sits inside a web of standards, type approvals, and patent licences that decides whether we can ship and where we can ship.

You will join our IoT Division, Device Reliability Engineering (DRE) team as an expert on IoT certifications, standards, and licensing including Standard Essential Patents (SEP). This position shapes both our exposure and our coverage arguments, and it means this role works in every direction at once, with suppliers, regulatory approvals, legal advisors, product and engineering, and with customers.

This is a role for someone who can hold a genuinely complex domain in their head and then explain it in three sentences to a customer who has never heard the phrase “patent exhaustion.”

Experience level: a deep specialist role. We expect solid, hands-on experience with cellular device approvals and licensing — likely 10+ years across regulatory, certification, or IP/licensing work in mobile, IoT, or telecom hardware. This is a senior individual contributor position with no direct reports, high autonomy, and direct executive visibility.

With locations in the heart of Copenhagen, Kolding, Aarhus, and Aalborg, we offer a flexible setup with the possibility to work from one of our locations — or remotely from anywhere in Denmark.

****What's in it for you?

• A domain you will own, not administer. IoT Cellular License, SEP and certification strategy is an executive-level topic at Trackunit right now, with real financial exposure attached. You will not be filing paperwork in a corner, you will be shaping the position the company takes.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and we support them through training, coaching, and mindfulness as well as with an open feedback culture to enable you to identify your strengths and opportunities.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us or something we state in a job posting. We offer a flexible setup because we believe you know best how to structure your work. Once you have chosen how you work best, let us know what you need: we got you covered with the IT equipment you need for your work.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. And this priority starts with our hiring — we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We only assess candidates on their qualifications and merit. Learn more about TIDE and other DE&I initiatives here.

****What you'll do

****Your work splits roughly into four parts: licensing, approvals, guidance, and governance.

• Own our SEP position. Understand where our cellular SEP exposure actually sits across our device portfolio, track the relevant patent pools and licensing programmes, and maintain a clear, evidence-based view of what is covered through our supply chain and what is not.

• Run supplier licensing due diligence. Establish and maintain a consistent set of asks across module suppliers — coverage confirmation, standards and generations covered, and honest disclosure of known gaps — so responses can be compared side by side and fed into supplier qualification.

• Support licensing negotiations and claims. Work alongside our General Counsel, external patent counsel, and economic advisors on royalty basis questions, valuation and apportionment arguments, and claims that reach us through our OEM customers. You bring the technical and supply chain substance; they bring the legal strategy.

• Own global type approvals and certification. Plan and steer RED/CE, FCC, ISED, UKCA, and the wider set of regional approvals, plus GCF/PTCRB and carrier certification, across a multi-region device portfolio. Keep certification on the critical path of new product programmes rather than at the end of them.

• Stay ahead of regulatory change. Cyber Resilience Act, RED delegated acts, radio spectrum and network sunsets, environmental and product compliance requirements — know what is coming, when it bites, and what it means for our roadmap.

• Make the complex simple, and guide without over-promising. Write and maintain the internal playbooks, customer-facing explainers, and OEM guidance that turn this domain into something a commercial colleague or a customer can act on. Be the person Sales, Legal, and customers come to when a licensing notification lands, explaining the landscape accurately, saying clearly where the limits of our position are, and pointing customers to independent specialist advice where that is the right answer.

• Build the governance. Response protocols, decision records, escalation paths, and embedding licensing and compliance requirements into how we qualify suppliers and run the product development lifecycle.

****Who you are

****We think you'll need

• Strong working knowledge of cellular connectivity (e.g. LTE-M, NB-IoT, LTE Cat-1/1bis, 5G) and the direction of travel, plus a real understanding of the module and chipset landscape.

• Solid, practical experience with licensing and Standard Essential Patents in mobile or IoT devices: FRAND principles, patent pools, patent exhaustion and the limits of sublicensing, and how royalties are actually structured and argued.

• Hands-on experience with global type approvals and regulatory certification for radio products — RED/CE, FCC, and the regional approvals that come with selling hardware worldwide.

• Experience working across a hardware supply chain with module suppliers, test houses, notified bodies, and certification partners.

• Communication as a core skill, not a bonus. You can take a genuinely complicated subject and land it in plain language, in writing, with an audience that has no background in it.

• The judgement to know what we can and cannot say to a customer, and the discipline to hold that line even when it would be easier not to.

**What Matters More Than The Checklist

**

• You are honest about uncertainty. In this domain, no one can offer a blanket guarantee, and the people who claim otherwise create problems later. We would rather be accurate than reassuring.

• You are curious and self-driven, this is a field that changes constantly, and nobody is going to hand you a reading list.

• You finish things. A clear one-page answer delivered this week beats a perfect analysis that arrives after the decision was made.

• You are comfortable being the only person in the room who knows a subject, and you use that position to make others smarter rather than to make yourself indispensable.

On AI: experience with AI tooling is not a requirement, but a strong motivation and interest in working with it is. We already use AI in our daily engineering work, including MCP servers and agents against our own platform, and we see clear potential in applying it to research, documentation, and compliance workflows. We don't expect you to have experience with this but we do expect curiosity and a willingness to learn.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this role and your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification, we still encourage you to apply.

****How you'll grow here

****This is a specialist role with an unusually wide view of the business, and we've set it up that way on purpose.

• Executive proximity. You will work closely with the SVP of IoT Division, while reporting into a central function for IoT, as the Device Reliability Engineering. You will help in presenting to executive leadership on exposure, risk, and recommendations. Your analysis will inform on a product technical matter (Not Legal) but with real financial and commercial decisions.

• Cross-functional reach. Legal, Finance, Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Sales all depend on this domain. Few roles at Trackunit touch as many parts of the company.

• External network. You will work with external patent counsel, economic consultants, module suppliers, certification bodies, and industry forums — building a network that extends well beyond Trackunit.

• Room to define the function. This discipline is being built out now. What it becomes — and whether it grows into a team — is substantially yours to shape.

**Coming Together To Connect Construction

**We're committed to construction one of the largest industries in the world. Over the past two decades, Trackunit has been pioneering technological progress within construction. Today, we are not only a leading IoT provider but a thought leader, supporting and shaping the agenda for an entire industry on a global scale.

We believe in taking a people approach in everything we do. Being human-centric is not restricted to our products — it's a way of life at Trackunit. We're proud to be a truly global team. Our colleagues get together in hubs spread across the globe, but we embrace the idea of working remotely and in environments that inspire you. Everything we do, we do it to eliminate downtime and build the most useful industry for the world.

 Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen

Are you driven by challenging the status quo? Then you might be our new postdoc! The position is to be filled by 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The primary tasks are to validate biomarkers for the intake of commonly consumed foods and to utilize them in estimating dietary intake in nutrition studies. For this, the postdoc will work with LC-MS metabolomics profiles of human samples and will develop data-driven frameworks for the implementation of biomarkers of food intake as dietary assessment tools. The position is affiliated with the Foodprints project funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation.

  Responsibilities and qualifications

  We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher interested in elucidating how an objective dietary assessment contributes to a better understanding of diet-cardiometabolic risk interactions by performing metabolomics analyses and integrating omics with self-reported dietary data from human studies. Additionally, the candidate will be involved in the supervision of the group’s Ph.D., Master and Bachelor students. The work will involve:

   	
• LC-MS data extraction and preprocessing 	
• Integration of diet and metabolomics data through uni- and multivariate statistical analyses

jobs.description:
Are you an experienced software engineer looking for something different? Imagine developing software in the morning, testing it on real hardware in the afternoon, and eventually watching it take flight.

At Acodyne, you will work alongside engineers developing next-generation unmanned aircraft, applying your software engineering experience to challenges that extend far beyond the screen.

You will have the opportunity to work across the software stack, from embedded systems and flight control integration to simulation, telemetry, and ground-based applications. You'll join a small, ambitious team where your contributions will have a direct impact on the aircraft we build.

Your Role

As part of our growing engineering team, you will develop and integrate software for our high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAVs and their supporting systems.

You will work closely with electronics, mechanical, and aerospace engineers to turn ideas into working solutions, taking software from development through simulation, hardware integration, and real-world flight testing.

We believe that reliable software starts with good engineering practices. Code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are important parts of how we want to develop our systems.

You will:

• 
Develop and maintain software for our aircraft and supporting systems.

• 
Work with embedded Linux platforms, flight computers, sensors, actuators, and communication systems.

• 
Integrate and extend existing flight control technologies such as ArduPilot or PX4.

• 
Develop tools for telemetry collection, monitoring, data analysis, and ground control.

• 
Build and maintain simulation environments and automated tests to validate software before flight.

• 
Contribute to reliable development workflows, continuous integration, testing, and release processes.

• 
Collaborate across engineering disciplines to integrate and troubleshoot software and hardware.

• 
Participate in prototype development, system integration, and flight test activities.

• 
Document software designs, interfaces, and test results to support future certification and compliance.

About You

We're looking for an experienced software engineer who enjoys solving challenging technical problems and takes pride in building reliable, maintainable software.

You've worked in a professional software development environment and understand the value of good engineering practices. Version control, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and reproducible builds are a natural part of how you work.

You're comfortable taking ownership, making pragmatic engineering decisions, and collaborating with people from different technical backgrounds. You enjoy learning new technologies and aren't afraid to venture beyond your existing expertise.

You don't need to be an aerospace expert. We value strong software engineering fundamentals, technical curiosity, and the ability to master new domains.

You likely have:

• 
Several years of professional software development experience.

• 
Strong programming skills in C/C++ and experience developing software for Linux.

• 
Experience working with modern development workflows, including Git, code reviews, automated testing, and CI/CD.

• 
An understanding of software architecture, debugging, and maintaining complex software systems.

• 
Some experience with embedded systems, hardware interfaces, or resource-constrained environments.

• 
A pragmatic, hands-on approach to engineering and an interest in working with physical systems.

• 
The ability to work independently while contributing constructively to a multidisciplinary team.

It would be a plus if you have:

• 
Experience with robotics, UAVs, autonomous systems, or flight control software.

• 
Familiarity with ArduPilot, PX4, MAVLink, or similar technologies.

• 
Experience with simulation, hardware-in-the-loop testing, or real-time systems.

• 
Knowledge of networking, telemetry, data acquisition, or distributed systems.

• 
Experience using AI-assisted development tools or working with machine learning technologies.

We don't expect you to tick every box. We're more interested in your engineering mindset, technical curiosity, and ability to learn.

As an early-stage startup pushing the boundaries of innovation, we offer a salary typical for our phase of growth.

About Acodyne

Acodyne is on a mission to develop the world's fastest unmanned eVTOL aircraft for heavy payloads, initially to serve off-shore, remote areas and general logistics.

Beyond developing the aircraft, we're exploring how intelligent software, automation, and data-driven systems can shape the future of unmanned cargo operations.

We are a small, ambitious engineering team with plans to grow significantly. We're based at Avedøre Airfield, where your daily work will primarily take place.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and interviews will be conducted continuously.

Please note that we are currently unable to provide visa sponsorship or relocation assistance.

Perks and benefits

This job comes with several perks and benefits

Working at

Acodyne

Acodyne is building the world’s fastest unmanned eVTOL cargo aircraft for heavy payloads. Designed for missions where time, access, and risk define the outcome, whether it’s offshore logistics or frontline resupply. With a proprietary ducted-fan system and fixed-wing efficiency, the E200 model carries 200 kg at 450 km/h, delivering critical supplies up to 10× faster than land and at a fraction of helicopter cost. We are currently 20 people, based at our workshop at Avedøre Airfield, and plan to double our team in the next year.

Veo is an AI-powered sports camera and analysis ecosystem built for one job: turning what happens on a pitch into proof. Capture, viewing, data and analytics, sharing- all in one system, all pointed at the same thing.

That's bigger than football. Every player, on every pitch, gets access to the kind of proof only the top academies used to keep for themselves. It's the future we're building.

Every youth match still has a moment nobody saw. A run that won the game, underneath everyone's radar. A kid written off before anyone actually checked. We exist to close that gap, one match at a time.

One camera on any pitch feeds an AI that tracks every player and the ball for the whole game, turning what happened into evidence instead of somebody's opinion.

That's the actual job here. Not shipping features. Building the system that gives proof to someone who used to rely on a hunch.

If you've ever watched a match and wondered who else saw what you saw, you already know why this matters.

We're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

We are looking for a Product Compliance Manager to join Veo's newly established Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) team.

As Veo continues to grow, we navigate a broad range of regulatory requirements across our products and business, from certifications, product safety, and environmental regulation to market access and broader compliance obligations.

In this role, you will focus on product-related regulatory compliance and certifications, while also working across Veo's broader compliance agenda. You will work closely with colleagues across Hardware, Product Development, Production, Procurement and other parts of the business to understand applicable requirements and help translate them into practical processes and solutions.

You will join a small GRC team with a broad mandate and significant exposure across Veo. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys understanding regulation, technology, and business.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Coordinate Veo's product certification and market-access activities across relevant markets, working closely with Hardware, Production and other internal stakeholders.

• Monitor and assess new and changing regulatory requirements relevant to Veo and help determine their practical implications for our products and business.

• Develop and maintain a structured overview of regulatory and certification requirements applicable to Veo's products throughout their lifecycle.

• Drive and coordinate implementation of regulatory and compliance requirements across relevant business functions, ensuring clear ownership, appropriate documentation and timely follow-up.

• Work with regulatory frameworks relevant to Veo's products, including areas such as product safety, batteries, electrical and electronic equipment, environmental requirements, waste and recycling obligations and related product compliance requirements.

• Coordinate with external certification bodies, laboratories, consultants and other specialists where required.

• Maintain and develop compliance documentation, certification records, technical files, declarations and other evidence required to demonstrate compliance.

• Support the assessment of regulatory and compliance implications when Veo enters new markets, introduces new products or makes material changes to existing products.

• Support Veo's broader compliance activities, including policies, procedures, monitoring, due diligence, risk assessments and training.

• Support customer, auditor and other stakeholder requests relating to compliance and certifications.

• Contribute to the continued development of Veo's broader GRC framework and take part in cross-functional compliance projects as required.

**Your qualifications:

**

• Relevant higher education in engineering, technology, law, business, quality/compliance, or another relevant discipline.

• Relevant professional experience within product compliance, regulatory compliance, certification, quality/regulatory affairs or a similar area, preferably from an international company.

• Experience working with regulatory requirements affecting hardware or electronic products is an advantage.

• Experience with one or more areas such as product safety, product certifications, battery regulation, electrical/electronic equipment regulation, environmental product requirements, waste/recycling regulation or similar regulatory regimes.

• Experience coordinating certification processes, testing, technical documentation, declarations or interactions with certification bodies and laboratories is highly relevant.

• Broader compliance experience, for example within sanctions and export controls, third-party due diligence, anti-bribery and corruption or other corporate compliance areas, is an advantage.

• An ability to understand complex regulatory requirements and translate them into practical requirements for technical, operational and commercial teams.

• Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating initiatives across different functions and areas of expertise.

• A structured approach to documentation, monitoring and follow-up, combined with the ability to identify and prioritize material compliance risks.

• Strong business understanding and a pragmatic approach to compliance. You should be comfortable finding solutions that meet regulatory requirements while enabling the business to operate effectively.

• Comfortable working independently and taking ownership in an environment where processes and frameworks are still being developed.

• Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

At Veo, the Governance, Risk & Compliance team provides oversight, coordination and assurance across the company. We work closely with teams throughout Veo to ensure that regulatory requirements and risks are identified, appropriately owned and effectively managed.

You will report to the Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance and will have considerable opportunity to shape how Veo approaches compliance as the company continues to grow.

Contact Martin Eger Larsen one mel@veo.co if you have any questions

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

outcomes.

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

We value diversity and inclusion and welcome applicants from all backgrounds, even if your experience doesn’t completely match every qualification listed. What matters most is your creativity, potential, and ability to make meaningful contributions.
