**Your impact begins here

**As Senior Clinical Genetics Data Scientist, you will turn human genetic evidence into clear recommendations that guide clinical development decisions. You will lead defined projects that combine trial and population genetic data with clinical outcomes and molecular measurements. Your work will help explain disease biology, understand why people respond differently to treatment and identify where patient stratification, or asset differentiation could matter. It helps teams decide with confidence, for people living with serious chronic diseases.

**What You’ll Bring

**You are an independent, systematic scientist with sound judgement, who communicates uncertainty openly, acts on feedback and sees work through to its outcome.

• A PhD in statistical genetics, genetic epidemiology, bioinformatics or a related quantitative discipline; or a relevant master’s degree with equivalent demonstrated research and applied experience.

• Demonstrated independent ownership of complex human genetics projects, from study design and data preparation to robust interpretation and communication of results.

• Strong, hands-on experience in GWAS design, execution and interpretation, including linkage disequilibrium, population structure, relatedness, multiple testing, power and validation.

• Proficiency in R and/or Python, Linux and genetics tools such as PLINK, BCFtools, GATK, REGENIE, SAIGE or equivalent, with reproducible programming, version control, documentation and quality review.

• Practical experience processing SNP array and WGS data, including quality control, genotype harmonisation, phasing and imputation, variant calling, filtering and functional annotation.

• Hands-on experience conducting and interpreting pQTL analyses, including cis and trans mapping, multiple-testing control and integration with GWAS or colocalisation evidence.

• The ability to coordinate stakeholders, manage project risks and dependencies, and present complex findings clearly in English to audiences with different technical backgrounds.

**Desirable, But Not Essential

**Experience in clinical trial genetics, pharmacogenetics or clinical development, particularly in cardiometabolic, obesity or renal disease; rare-variant and gene-based tests, genetic risk prediction or advanced causal inference; or work with secure cloud computing, biobank-scale resources and regulated analytical environments.

**What You’ll Do

**You will own project outcomes from the scientific question to validated results and practical recommendations.

• Plan and run GWAS, pQTL and related analyses of disease phenotypes, clinical endpoints, biomarkers and treatment response, using trial and external cohort data.

• Prepare SNP array and whole-genome sequencing data into analysis-ready datasets, and use fine-mapping, colocalisation and causal inference to prioritise plausible variants, genes, pathways and biomarkers.

• Investigate pharmacogenetic associations and genetically informed subgroups, separating prognostic signals from evidence of differential treatment benefit.

• Turn findings into decision-focused reports and presentations, with clear uncertainty and limitations, and contribute genetics content to publications and regulatory documents.

• Build documented, version-controlled workflows, mentor colleagues through code review and feedback, and use genetic and clinical data within approved consent, governance and quality requirements.

**Who You’ll Work With

**You will join Clinical Omics Sciences, part of Translational & Clinical Omics in Research & Development. Here, colleagues explore scientific ideas and advance them towards clinical testing, bringing together curiosity, data, technology and collaboration.

Your closest partners will be Clinical Development Teams, translational scientists, human genetics researchers, biostatisticians, data managers and data engineers. You will also coordinate agreed work with external collaborators and suppliers. You will explain your technical choices in accessible language, build alignment on the question, deliverables and decision, and speak up early when something stalls.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will be trusted to determine and execute the analytical approach for your projects, within agreed objectives and quality requirements. You will be supported to perform at your best, make your voice heard and grow through practical project experience, scientific feedback and relevant learning offerings. You will also help raise the standard for the whole team by shaping shared workflows, templates and methods.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 651,000 to

956,900 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate's skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here

We seek an experienced, highly motivated, and independent laboratory technician to support the Novo Nordisk Foundation Center for Protein Design (CPD) at the University of Copenhagen (UCPH). This is a full-time position, starting as soon as possible, and employment through 31 July 2032.

  Our research:

  The CPD is a multidisciplinary centre that works across the university—notably with the Departments of Biology, Drug Design and Pharmacology, Chemistry, and Computer Science—and with national and international academic and industrial partners. CPD is funded by an initial grant of 700M DKK for seven years from the Novo Nordisk Foundation. At capacity, the CPD is expected to have ≈8 research groups, ≈80 researchers, and support staff. Research will encompass the growing protein design landscape with computational, experimental, applied and hybrid projects.

  The CPD's vision and mission are to accelerate protein design by deepening understanding of sequence-to-structure/function relationships in proteins, and to train the next generation of protein scientists to apply protein-design approaches and methods to a diverse array of fundamental and real-world challenges.  

  CPD research is broadly organised into three themes: Programmable De Novo Protein Design, aimed at improving methods for protein design by combining rational, physics-based and AI-based approaches; Contextualised Protein Design, which is about designing proteins that are fit for purpose, such as working directly and optimally in cells, chemical reactors, etc.; and Biodesign for Sustainability and Healthcare, for instance working with biotech and industry to deliver synthetic proteins to address grand challenges in these areas.

  Further information on the CPD see: cpd.ku.dk.

  Your job:

  Specifically, we seek a talented laboratory technician and team player to help set up, equip and support research in newly refurbished labs. You will join the CPD Operations and Management Team, work closely with another laboratory technician and the CPD Experimental Officer, and fulfil a key role supporting CPD researchers.

  Tasks of the Laboratory Technician will include:

   	
• Assist in setting up, establishing, and organising newly refurbished CPD laboratories together with a laboratory technician and the CPD Experimental Officer. 	
• Order, track, and manage laboratory supplies, consumables, and chemical inventory, including invoice processing. 	
• Solicit and evaluate quotes from multiple vendors for large equipment purchases in accordance with university and public procurement guidelines. 	
• Process purchase orders, verify deliveries, monitor invoices, and register new equipment. 	
• Serve as a key contributor to safety compliance, chemical registration, and risk assessment coordination. 	
• Drive and maintain environmental sustainability initiatives in KU, targeting LEAF (Laboratory Efficiency Assessment Framework) 	
• Establish and maintain rigorous safety routines, waste management and documentation. 	
• Contribute to onboarding new researchers, visiting scientists, and students, including safety introductions, lab space allocation, and workflow introductions. 	
• Contribute to the offboarding processes by ensuring proper handover of samples and data and chemical/waste disposal. 	
• Prepare shared stock solutions and reagents 	
• Contribute to practical laboratory classes and guide new researchers on standard operating procedures.   Profile:

  To succeed in this role, we anticipate that you have a lab technician (laborant) degree or similar. We also expect you to be a service-minded team player who likes managing the day-to-day operation of a laboratory, including carrying out administrative tasks like obtaining quotations and handling purchasing and procurement activities.

  Preferably, you have experience with hands-on expertise in solid-phase peptide synthesis and peptide purification, solid knowledge of biochemistry laboratory safety regulations, and a keen interest in collaborating with researchers from different backgrounds. You should bring a strong motivation for optimising lab organisation and safety, alongside a genuine interest in teaching students and guiding new researchers within a dynamic, international academic environment.

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• Highly structured, detail-oriented, and able to prioritise and execute tasks independently 	
• Knowledge of biochemical and/or chemical research and teaching laboratories 	
• Understanding of Good Laboratory Practice, chemical and biological safety regulations, standard documentation practices, and inventory management 	
• Strong and proven organisational, communication, and networking skills 	
• Good written and spoken Danish and English language skills   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Experience with solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) and peptide purification 	
• Experience with Kemibrug, SDI and RejsUd 	
• Experience with the LEAF or similar green laboratory sustainability programmes 	
• Perform routine recombinant protein expression and purification to generate shared stocks 	
• Experience with mammalian cell lines and preparing bacterial competent cells   Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the NNF Center for Protein Design, located at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative, stimulating working conditions in a dynamic, international research environment.

  Terms of salary and employment
 The employment as a laboratory technician (TAP) is a full-time (37 hours/week) position with employment through 31 July 2032. The starting date is as soon as possible, and, ideally, the successful candidate will be in place by March 2027 to coincide with the preparations for opening newly refurbished labs.

  Employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and HK Stat, Organisationsaftalen for kontorfunktionærer, laboranter og it-medarbejdere. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector on this page Lønoverblik

  The monthly salary will be based on of work experience, with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experience and qualifications.

  Questions
 For further information regarding the position, please contact CPD Experimental Officer, Ana Almeida, ana.almeida@sund.ku.dk.

  Learn more about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, https://drug.ku.dk/, and Center for Protein Design https://cpd.ku.dk/

  Application
 Your application should be in English and include:

   	
• A cover letter outlining your fit to the role and motivation for applying (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum Vitae (incl. the names of two references (max. two pages)  	
• A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education   Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply Now” below. Only online applications will be accepted.

  Application deadline: 4 January 2027, 23:59 [CET]

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not meet the above requirements.

  Interviews are expected to be held in January 2027.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and welcomes applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion, or sexual orientation. Appointment will be based on merit alone.

  As part of the International Alliance of Research Universities (IARU) and among Europe’s top-ranking universities, the University of Copenhagen promotes research and teaching to the highest international standard. Rich in tradition and modern in outlook, the University gives students and staff the opportunity to cultivate their talent in an ambitious and informal environment. An effective organisation – with good working conditions and a collaborative work culture – creates the ideal framework for a successful academic career.

 ⑴ Social Media Management and Digital Communications

Develop and implement social media content plans in accordance with the Center's events and communication objectives.

Coordinate photography, video recording, editing and the archiving of promotional materials for the Center's activities.

Oversee the daily operations of the Center's library, including book classification, cataloguing, registration, lending, returns and collection management.

Establish and maintain library management procedures and reader services, including opening arrangements, reservations and visitor reception.

Actively promote the opening of the library to the general public and expand its readership among local residents and communities.

Plan and organise reading promotion activities, book-sharing sessions, cultural talks and other public cultural activities.

Promote the library's resources and services to increase its visibility and accessibility within the local community.

⑶ Cultural Communications and General Support

Support the promotion and publicity of the Center's cultural events, exhibitions, performances, lectures and cultural exchange activities.

Photograph cultural events and create visual content for the Center's promotional and communication purposes.

Assist in establishing and maintaining relationships with local communities, schools, cultural institutions and other relevant organisations to expand partnerships and promote public cultural services.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Mechatronic Design for Remotely Operated Vehicles
jobs.description:
Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM), part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites application for an 18-month postdoc position within Mechatronic Design for Remotely Operated Vehicles (ROVs). The position is available from March 2027, and the specific start date will be agreed upon with the successful candidates.

 

What we offer 

Successful candidates will join an interdisciplinary engineering research environment at SDU Sønderborg and contribute to the development of ROVs and associated subsea mechatronics. The work combines engineering design, numerical modelling, prototyping, fabrication, integration, and experimental validation in laboratory and marine environments.

The positions offer opportunities to:

• 
Develop and evaluate mechatronic components, subsystems, and integrated ROV platforms.

• 
Design underwater actuation mechanisms, transmissions, structural components, and pressure-resistant enclosures, including sealing and mechanical interfaces.

• 
Integrate underwater sensors, actuators, embedded electronics, and control hardware.

• 
Perform CAD modelling, engineering analysis, simulations, design optimisation, and prototype fabrication.

• 
Conduct laboratory and field testing to improve the performance, reliability, and robustness of subsea mechatronic technologies.

• 
Publish research in international scientific journals and conferences, collaborate with research partners, and contribute to student supervision where relevant.

 

What we expect 

Applicants must hold a PhD degree in mechatronics, mechanical engineering, robotics, marine engineering, or a closely related discipline at the time of employment. We seek motivated researchers with strong mechatronic design skills and hands-on experience in developing, integrating, and testing electromechanical systems.

Applicants should have demonstrated expertise in mechatronic design and practical experience in several of the following areas:

• 
Mechanical and mechatronic design, including actuation, transmissions, structural design, and electromechanical integration.

• 
CAD and engineering modelling or analysis, such as finite element analysis, multibody dynamics, or related methods.

• 
Integration of sensors, actuators, embedded electronics, and control hardware.

• 
Rapid prototyping, additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and experimental development.

• 
Experimental testing, instrumentation, data acquisition, system characterisation, and troubleshooting.

• 
Basic programming and control using tools such as Python, C/C++, MATLAB/Simulink, or ROS/ROS 2.

Experience in subsea engineering, ROV development, underwater actuation, pressure-resistant enclosures, waterproofing, sealing, or marine instrumentation is an advantage but not a requirement. Applicants should have a publication record appropriate to their career stage, sound scientific judgement, good written and spoken English, and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

 

Workplace description 

The positions will be based at the Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM), Department of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, University of Southern Denmark, in Sønderborg. The research environment brings together expertise in mechanical engineering, mechatronics, modelling, control, and experimental engineering.

Get a glimpse of (work)life through the eyes of some of our many excellent researchers at SDU in Sønderborg. 

 

Further information 

For further information about the position, please contact:

• 
Lars Duggen, Head of Unit, SDU Mechatronics (CIM), at duggen@sdu.dk

• 
Mrudul Chellapurath, Assistant Professor, at mrch@sdu.dk

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications highlighting the publications most relevant to the position.

• 
A research statement.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
Documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is December 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

jobs.occupation: PhD position in biogas production from hydrothermal liquefaction process water
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 1 April 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
PhD position in biogas production from hydrothermal liquefaction process water

Research area and project description:
Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) converts wet biogenic residues such as manure, biogas digestate and organic household waste into a renewable biocrude that can be upgraded to marine and aviation fuels. Alongside the biocrude, HTL produces large volumes of process water rich in dissolved organics and nitrogen. Treating this water efficiently while recovering its energy and nutrients is essential for the sustainability and economics of future full-scale HTL plants.

The PhD position is part of the Horizon Europe Innovation Action CARAVEL (2027-2030), coordinated by Aarhus University with 16 partners from 8 countries. CARAVEL will demonstrate the first integrated HTL value chain at TRL8, including circular management of process water and hydrochar. It is a collaborative project, so frequent exchange with the international partners from academia and industry is essential.

The PhD project will investigate anaerobic digestion (AD) as a route to convert HTL process water into biogas while managing nitrogen. HTL process water contains compounds such as phenols and N-heterocycles that can inhibit methanogenesis, and inhibition thresholds depend on feedstock and process conditions. The PhD student will determine biomethane potential and inhibitory effects of process waters from different feedstocks in batch co-digestion tests with manure, demonstrate co-digestion in a full-scale experimental thermophilic biogas reactor, and optimise mono-digestion in a pilot-scale anaerobic fixed-bed biofilter, including micro-aeration to enhance the degradation of inhibitory compounds. A central aim is to link process water composition to methane yield, process stability and nitrogen conversion.

The work combines laboratory experiments with pilot- and full-scale operation at AU Foulum, which hosts both HTL and biogas research facilities. Techniques include biomethane potential testing, reactor operation, gas analysis, VFA, COD and nitrogen analysis, and GC-MS characterisation of process water.

Qualifications and specific competences:
Applicants must have a relevant Master's degree, e.g. in environmental, chemical or biological engineering, biotechnology, microbiology or a similar field.

Experience with anaerobic digestion, biogas processes or wastewater treatment is expected. Practical experience with laboratory or pilot-scale bioreactor operation and relevant analytical techniques (e.g. gas chromatography, VFA, COD and nitrogen analysis) is desired. Knowledge of hydrothermal liquefaction or other thermochemical conversion technologies is an advantage but not a requirement.

The successful candidate has demonstrated excellent academic results, has good collaboration and communication skills in English and is also able to work independently.

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Burrehøjvej 43, 8830 Tjele, Denmark.

Contacts:

• Professor Henrik Bjarne Møller, e-mail: henrikb.moller@bce.au.dk (main supervisor)

We’re looking for an experienced Financial Controller to take full ownership of our numbers as we scale. You’ll run a tight month-end close, get our SaaS revenue accounting airtight, and build the finance processes that let us grow fast without drowning in manual work. If you like turning messy into robust, read on.

About Pandektes

Legal research hasn’t changed much in decades. Lawyers still spend countless hours navigating fragmented sources, outdated systems, and complex databases just to find the information they need.

At Pandektes, we’re changing that.

Our ambition is to build the leading global platform for legal research and the largest AI-powered legal database. By combining artificial intelligence, intelligent search, and continuously updated legal sources, we’re redefining how legal knowledge is accessed, understood, analyzed, and applied.

Pandektes has raised more than _€_17.5 million and most recently closed a _€_13.5 million Series A round (October 2026) led by Alstin Capital, PROfounders and Scale Capital. Pandektes already serves more than 450 customers across Denmark, Germany and Switzerland.

We’re still early in the journey, and joining our team now means you’ll have big impact on shaping how we scale.

About the role

This is a hands-on role responsible for ensuring the accuracy and integrity of financial information, overseeing the month-end close, management accounts, financial reporting and statutory compliance, while continuously improving financial processes, systems and internal controls and working closely with Senior Management, external service providers and the wider business teams. The role will combine strong technical accounting expertise with a proactive, solutions-focused approach and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

What you’ll do

• 
Own the monthly and annual close – reviewing journals, accruals, prepayments, provisions and balance sheet reconciliations, and delivering accurate trial balances and financial statements on time

• 
Make sure our SaaS revenue (subscription, usage-based and implementation) is recognised correctly, and reconcile revenue schedules to billing, contracts and the general ledger

• 
Produce reliable monthly P&L, balance sheet and cash flow reporting

• 
Take over revenue billing from the sales team and run it within finance

• 
Manage our outsourced service providers and review the reconciliations they prepare – bank, intercompany, payroll, fixed assets and other control accounts

• 
Design and maintain financial policies, controls and approval limits across payments, expenses, procurement and system access

• 
Oversee AP, AR and cashbook accounting, manage payments through Corepay, and keep an eye on working capital

• 
Lead statutory accounts and external audits, and oversee VAT, corporate tax and compliance with our tax advisers

• 
Coordinate intercompany accounting and reporting across our entities in Denmark, Germany, Switzerland and the UK

• 
Improve finance processes, systems and automation – and over time, build and develop a small accounting team

What you’ll bring

• 
7+ years in commercially focused accounting roles, ideally with previous experience as a Financial Controller

• 
A recognised Danish accounting qualification (or equivalent, e.g. ACA, ACCA or CIMA)

• 
Hands-on experience with subscription and deferred revenue, including month-end revenue reconciliations

• 
A track record of independently running the month-end close and producing accurate management accounts

• 
Experience with intercompany balances, foreign currencies and reporting across international subsidiaries

• 
Exposure to international tax, VAT and transfer pricing, and experience running a local audit process

• 
A strong grasp of internal controls, segregation of duties and fraud risk

• 
Experience improving finance operations in a growing, scaling business – and a love for systems and automation

• 
A sharp eye for detail and the analytical instinct to tell a real business issue from an accounting error

How we work

We place great value on a vibrant, inspiring, and challenging company culture. This is achieved through a talented and passionate team that believes in achieving great things together.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We believe that ownership is what brings us the best teams – you can expect a lot of freedom and responsibility. The key is open communication, trust, and a shared passion to transform the legal world.

We are a growing team based in Copenhagen, Hamburg, London and Zurich. This role will be based in our Copenhagen HQ.

What we offer

• 
Competitive compensation + an attractive warrant program

• 
A collaborative work environment where your input is not only valued but often implemented within hours

• 
A central office in Copenhagen, where you can work closely with an ambitious and growing team

• 
International team events – last time we went to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you join us next time

25 vacation days per year + public holidays

Your own Pleo card for necessary work expenses

Paid parental leave

Why join the Queue

You’ll be part of a global team with colleagues from 40+ nationalities, where diverse perspectives, open dialogue, and cross-cultural collaboration are part of everyday work.

We’re also a global team of 40+ nationalities working across Denmark, the U.S., South Korea, Australia, and Japan. We believe in trust - in the digital experiences we protect and in the culture we build together.

The role

The Senior Product Manager will own the company's internal scientific software, so every team works from the same clean, consistent data with tools that fit together.

The company creates, moves and decides on large volumes of chemistry and biology data. Today each team builds its own solutions. The company is moving to a new data platform built for its molecules and will build custom internal products on top of it.

The Product Manager is the person who sees that three teams are building three versions of the same thing and turns them into one that works for everyone. Success is measured in time saved for the scientists: the software should save more than it costs.

Responsibilities

Product ownership

• Owns the roadmap for the internal scientific software, starting with the three products above.

• Gathers and challenges requirements from computational design, chemistry and biology, and turns parallel requests into shared solutions.

• Prioritises with the leadership team: what gets built, in what order, and why.

• Makes sure the products connect to each other and to the data platform.

• Runs user testing and adoption with the scientists, and tracks the time saved.

Delivery and leadership

• Works agile, and knows where agility stops. Ships working products within months without painting the platform into a corner.

• Leads and coordinates 3–6 developers, a mix of contractors and hires. A front-end engineer may report directly.

• Helps shape the software team as it grows.

Hands-on, at the start

• Contributes to the build until the development team is in place. The stack is Python on the back end, React/Redux on the front end, and AWS serverless services.

• Judges which components fit together and which will break, including AI-assisted code.

The profile

The ideal candidate has experience from an environment where software is built and shipped, and a scientific background. Beyond that, in order of importance:

• People leadership. Has led developers or cross-functional teams, internal or contracted, and aligned stakeholders who don't report to them.

• Product management track record. Has owned a software product or platform from idea to adoption.

• Drug discovery experience. Has worked close to design, synthesis, screening or compound selection. Broader R&D software is also relevant.

• Scientific background. A chemistry or biology degree (either is fine). Knows what they don't know, and asks.

• Hands-on coding. Can build in Python and React. Judgement matters more than depth.

Mindset: curious enough to ask "what's a canonical SMILES?", pragmatic about agile, and happy to start hands-on and grow into leading a team.

Nice to have: AWS serverless, lab automation or screening data, ELN/LIMS or compound registration, startup or scale-up experience. The working language is English.

Set-up, package and process

• Reporting. To the VP of AI & Computational Drug Design, with a weekly 1:1 and short daily stand-ups.

• Location. On site in Copenhagen, enough to work alongside the chemists and biologists in the lab. There is no fixed number of days.

• Career path. Starts senior and hands-on, and grows into leading a dedicated software team.

• Package. A competitive salary, pension, a performance bonus, and participation in the company's warrant programme.

• Process. A short screening call, then an online session where the candidate presents software they have built, then on-site interviews. The target start is early 2027.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellowship Position in Causal inference at the Section of Biostatistics and The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed
jobs.employer_name: KU - SUND - Institut For Folkesundhed - Kbh K
jobs.description:
The Department of Public Health at University of Copenhagen, Denmark, together with the The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomeds offers a Postdoctoral Fellowship position in causal inference with special focus on continuous-time causal inference, identification, and instrumental variables methods. 

  The anticipated hiring date is March 1, 2027, or as soon as possible hereafter.

  About the Centre

  The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and Computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTBiomed) will support a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed will leverage large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods including machine learning to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease.

  About the Section of Biostatistics
 The Section of Biostatistics carries out independent research in biostatistical applications and methods; it undertakes teaching of students at various educations, undergraduate as well as postgraduate, and it offers biostatistical advice to staff and students in all disciplines of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences. The section is internationally renowned for a high research level, especially within time-to-event analysis, while other competence areas include e.g. causal inference, latent variable modelling and prediction models. The section aims to maintain a strong position in these areas but also wants to expand into new areas of biostatistical research. The underlying idea is to produce high-level methodological research that is relevant in practical applications.

  More information on the Section of Biostatistics can be found at: https://biostat.ku.dk/. 
  

  Job Description
 We invite highly qualified, thorough, and motivated applicants to apply for a postdoctoral position in causal inference and statistical methodology. The successful candidate will conduct methodological research at the intersection of causal inference, event-history analysis, statistical machine learning, and semiparametric theory. Research will focus on the development of statistical methods for longitudinal and time-to-event data, with particular emphasis on continuously monitored data, dynamic treatment strategies, identification, and instrumental variable methods. Potential research directions include:  

   	
• causal inference for survival and competing risks outcomes 	
• continuous-time longitudinal causal models 	
• semiparametric and machine-learning-based estimation methods 	
• identification and estimation under instrumental variable assumptions 	
• methods for treatment switching, treatment discontinuation, and dynamic treatment interventions 	
• development of efficient and robust estimators for causal effects under complex longitudinal data structures   Example projects include the development of methods for causal inference with continuously observed treatment processes, incorporation of instrumental variables into survival analysis, and machine-learning-based estimation procedures for time-varying treatment effects. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute both theoretically and computationally, including development of new methodology, investigation of statistical properties, implementation of software, simulation studies, and applications to biomedical research questions. The candidate must participate in the interdisciplinary and dynamic research environment within the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed. The successful applicant is also encouraged to develop independent research directions aligned with the overall goals of the centre.

  The specific tasks of the position will include:

   	
• Manage own academic research and administrative activities. 	
• Conduct research in line with the goals of SMARTBiomed. 	
• Lead write-up of research papers pertaining to their own work and collaborate in the preparation of research publications. Ensure, where appropriate, that software research outputs are provided to ensure maximum utility. 	
• Present papers at conferences or public meetings. 	
• Contribute to the administrative activities of SMARTBiomed and the research group of appointment.   The postdoctoral fellow will also be encouraged and mentored to develop new proposals and research initiatives to support additional research. Over the course of the position, opportunities to teach at either the graduate or undergraduate level exist.

   

  Profile

  We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:
 Essential experience and skills:

   	
• A Ph.D. in Statistics/Biostatistics, or similar disciplines.  	
• Strong skills in theoretical methods development.  	
• Experience and interest in data analysis and programming (e.g., in R) is further highly desirable.  	
• Strong English, scientific writing, and oral communications skills 	
• The ability to work independently, effectively, and collaboratively.    

  Terms of employment 
 The position is fixed term, limited to a period of 3 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 36,877.42 DKK/approx. 4,933.00 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2020.

  Questions
 More information about the positions is available by contacting Associate Professor Helene Rytgaard, Section of Biostatistics, hely@sund.ku.dk, Professor Erin Gabriel, Section of Biostatistics, erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk, or Professor Torben Martinussen, Section of Biostatistics, tma@sund.ku.dk.   

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Letter indicating your motivation for application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do. 	
• List of publications and archived works in progress.    

  Deadline for applications: December 1st, 2026.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in Biophysics of Lipid Nanoparticles for Nucleic Acid Delivery at the Department of Pharmacy
jobs.description:
We are offering a PhD fellowship in Biophysics of Lipid Nanoparticles for Nucleic Acid Delivery commencing 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

  Our group and research

  Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have revolutionized the field of nucleic acid therapeutics and are now central to the development of mRNA-based medicines. Understanding the connection between nanoparticle composition, structure, and biological performance is essential for further advances in the field. The Vaccine Design and Delivery group investigates these relationships through a combination of biophysical, structural, and analytical approaches. The group also focuses on in vitro testing, in vivo imaging of biodistribution, and in vivo immunogenicity and protection studies in animal models. The overarching goal is to enable the rational design of more effective delivery systems. The PhD candidate will join a new research program led by Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani, an expert in advanced physicochemical methods to study lipid self-assembly. 

  Project description

  The overall aim of the PhD project is to advance the understanding of lipid nanoparticle (LNP) systems for nucleic acid delivery through the integration of formulation design, structural characterization, and interaction studies. The candidate will employ state-of-the-art biophysical and structural techniques to investigate the nanoscale structure of LNPs and their behavior in biologically relevant environments. By combining advanced nanoparticle formulation with cutting-edge characterization methods, including scattering techniques and electron microscopy, the project seeks to establish quantitative relationships between LNP composition, structure, and biological interactions. These approaches will be used to investigate how LNP properties govern interactions with biological media and membranes, generating fundamental insights that will guide the rational design of more effective delivery systems. The PhD candidate will work under the supervision of Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani within the Vaccine Design and Delivery group. The PhD fellowship is part of a larger research project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark through a Sapere Aude: DFF-Research Leader grant.

  Principal supervisor is Professor Camilla Foged, Department of Pharmacy, camilla.foged@sund.ku.dk, Direct Phone: +45 35 33 64 02.

  Co-Supervisor is Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani, federica.sebastiani@sund.ku.dk

  Start:            1 March 2027 (or after agreement)

  Duration:     3 years as a PhD student

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
• Carrying through an independent research project under supervision.    	
• Completing PhD courses or other equivalent education corresponding to approximately 30 ECTS points. 	
• Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team. 	
• Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project 	
• Teaching and disseminating your knowledge. 	
• Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project   PhD Programme Description:

  The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., Physical chemistry, Biophysics, Nanotechnology or related fields).

  The successful candidate will specifically work on 1) formulation of mRNA-LNPs; 2) investigating the structure and morphology of LNPs in the absence and presence of biomimetic fluid; 3) understanding the mechanism of interaction of LNPs with model membranes.

  The project combines a range of experimental biophysical methods, including lab-based techniques and experiments at large-scale neutron and X-ray scattering facilities in Europe.

  Qualifications:
 If you have completed your academic education in Denmark, the admission to the PhD programme requires a relevant Master’s degree (equivalent to 180 ECTS BSc + 120 ECTS MSc).

  If you have an academic education from abroad, you must have either a degree equivalent to a Danish master's degree (180 ETCS + 120 ECTS MSc), or at a minimum, a bachelor’s degree equivalent to a Danish bachelor's degree (180 ECTS) and be academically qualified at master's level.

  As part of the assessment of whether you meet the educational requirements, you must also achieve a positive academic evaluation and be assessed as the best qualified for the position.

  Required Qualifications 

  In connection with the appointment special importance will be attached to the applicant having the professional and personal qualifications stated below:

   

   	
• Obtained a Master´s degree in Physical chemistry, Biophysics, Nanotechnology, or related areas 	
• Excellent English speaking, reading and writing skills 	
• Creativity and ability to be both team-oriented and independent 	
• Capability of working at the interface between different disciplines 	
• Ability to thrive in an international research environment   Other important criteria are:

   	
• The grade point average achieved 	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Previous publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other professional activities 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in physical and colloidal chemistry for nanomedicine applications 	
• Language skills 	
• Interest in travelling to large-scale synchrotron and neutron facilities to perform experiments   Preferred Qualifications 

  We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with an open-minded attitude towards quantitative analysis of the experimental data. The ideal candidate should also have a strong background and/or hands-on research experience within one or several of the fields mentioned below:

   	
• Lipid self-assembly and their biophysical characterization 	
• Small angle X-ray and neutron scattering (experiments and advanced data analysis) 	
• Surface-sensitive techniques (QCM-D, ATR-FTIR, NR, SPR) 	
• Coding (e.g. Python)   Highly motivated and ambitious candidates are encouraged to apply. Solid experience and an excellent track record gained in the field of lipid self-assembly and scattering will be considered a distinct advantage. We encourage all the qualified individuals - regardless of their personal background and status - to apply.

  Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Department of Pharmacy, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment.

  The Dept. of Pharmacy offers a wide range of instrumentation (e.g., microfluidic mixing, cell labs). Core facilities at UCPH allow to access state-of-the-art equipment via a fee-for-service scheme (e.g., SAXS, cryoTEM). A substantial part of the work will rely on access to large scale facilities for neutron and x-rays scattering (national and international).

  Terms of employment 

  The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is 1 March 2027 (or after agreement).

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31.800 DKK/Roughly 4.200 EUR (August 2026 level) plus pension.

 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Assistant Professor Federica Sebastiani.

  General information about PhD studies at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences is available at the Graduate School’s website: https://healthsciences.ku.dk/phd/guidelines/

  Application procedure

jobs.description:
We are offering a PhD fellowship commencing in February 2027.

  Job Description
 The Perrier Lab at the Department of Neuroscience, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen, is seeking a motivated and talented PhD fellow to study the impact of gain-of-function (GOF) mutations in GABAA  receptors implicated in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs).

  DEEs are severe early-onset conditions characterized by intractable epilepsy, intellectual disability, developmental delay or regression, movement disorders, and autism spectrum disorders. Although missense variants in GABAA receptor subunits are often assumed to cause loss of receptor function (LOF), recent work by our collaborators at the University of Sydney (Australia) and Filadelfia Hospital (Denmark) shows that GOF variants are just as prevalent, and their functional outcomes closely correlate with patient phenotypes.

  Project Overview
 The main goal of this project is to understand how mutations that increase inhibitory signaling in the brain can nevertheless lead to DEE. To address this, you will investigate animal models carrying GOF GABAA receptor mutations found in patients, examining their effects at multiple levels:

   	
• In Vivo  	 		
• Monitor animal behavior and record electrocorticographic (ECoG) activity to detect abnormalities linked to patient symptoms. 	 	 	
• In Vitro 	 		
• Use brain slice preparations to measure neuronal activity at the microcircuit level, comparing GOF mutants to wild-type littermates. This approach will clarify if microcircuits from the thalamocortical loop are impaired in GOF DEE models and if impairments are responsible for the epileptic phenotype. 	 	   Based on these findings, you will contribute to the design and testing of targeted treatments aimed at correcting the underlying defects, first in vitro and subsequently in vivo. This project will be conducted in close collaboration with Filadelfia Hospital, which maintains a cohort of patients affected by these rare and severe conditions.

   

  Principal supervisor: Professor, Jean-François Perrier, Department of Neuroscience, E-mail: perrier@sund.ku.dk. Direct Phone: +45-23812746.
 Start:     February 2027
 Duration:     3 years as a PhD student

  Qualification Requirements

   	
• A master’s degree (or equivalent) in neuroscience, pharmacology, physiology, or a related field. 	
• Experience with in vitro electrophysiology (patch clamp recordings of neurons in slices) is an absolute requirement. 	
• Experience with animal behavior studies is also required. 	
• Skills in optogenetics and experience with the thalamo-cortical system would be an advantage. 	
• Strong motivation, excellent communication skills in English (both oral and written), and the ability to work independently and as part of a team. 	
• Willingness to engage in teamwork   The preferred applicant should have an excellent academic track record, solid research experience and be highly motivated to deploy diverse strategies to extract novel findings of importance to pathophysiology. Previous research experience in an ambitious research environment is required.

  Duties

  The PhD fellow will investigate how the mutation affects the electrical properties of thalamo-cortical microcircuits. To do this, he-she will prepare brain slices from mice and use the patch-clamp technique to record single-neuron activity. The project will also incorporate calcium imaging, optogenetics and pharmacological approaches. The fellow will be responsible for designing, conducting, and analyzing these experiments, with ongoing support from the principal investigator and other group members.

  Our group and environment

  The candidate will join the Perrier Lab and be part of the “From disease-causing variants to targeted therapy in GABA-A receptor related epilepsies” consortium—a collaboration between the University of Copenhagen, Filadelfia Hospital (Denmark), and the University of Sydney (Australia), funded by the Lundbeck Foundation. Our facilities include state-of-the-art laboratories, cutting-edge core facilities, and modern office spaces.

  This position provides a unique opportunity to develop expertise in the mechanisms underlying developmental and epileptic encephalopathies. We strive for academic excellence, collegial respect, and responsible freedom, offering a creative, welcoming, and stimulating environment within a strong scientific community.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Fellow in Economic Analysis of Nature Restoration Measures Across Different Farming Systems
jobs.description:
Postdoctoral Fellow in Economic Analysis of Nature Restoration Measures Across Different Farming Systems

Are you interested in Economics of nature restoration in agriculture and can you contribute to the development of the Horizon Europe research project BALANCE? Then the Department of Environmental Science invites you to apply for a two-year Postdoc position. 

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two –year position from 1 May 2027 or as soon possible. 

Job description
• This section may include topics such as: 
• You will be contributing to/establishing/developing ... 
• You will be working primarily with ... 
• The position will focus on aspects of/elements of ... 
• You will be involved in ... 
• These activities will be in close collaboration with ...
The postdoctoral researcher will contribute to an interdisciplinary, EU-wide project investigating how nature restoration and nature-positive farming systems can contribute to biodiversity and farming. You will be working primarily with assessment of the short-, medium- and long-term costs and benefits of different nature restoration measures across different farming systems, with a focus on farm income, farm productivity and farm production. You will also develop methods for upscaling the findings on costs and benefits to the EU level. You will be involved in collaborations with researchers in agricultural and environmental economics as well as researchers in other disciplines and stakeholders collaborating in the same project.

Your profile
Applicants should hold a PhD in Environmental or Agricultural Economics or similar. Candidates should demonstrate strong skills in quantitative economics methods. Documented experience with farm economics and biodiversity is desirable.

We are looking for a candidate with:
• Strong analytical skills
• Experience in quantitative economic assessment related to agri-environmental challenges
• Experience in data collection from scientific articles and public and advisory reports 
• Demonstrated ability to publish scientific work in peer-reviewed journals
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English
• Ability to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary research environment
The following qualifications will be considered an advantage:
• Experience in assessing environmental or agronomic topics across different spatial and time scales 
• Familiarity with policy-related research
• Experience in collaboration across disciplinary boundaries, particularly between natural and social sciences
We value motivated candidates with strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, who can engage constructively with researchers and stakeholders from different disciplinary and professional backgrounds. 

Who we are
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department under the Faculty of Technology at Aarhus University. The expertise ranges from economics, policy analysis, social science, and geography to physics, chemistry, microbiology and mathematical modelling. Both basic and applied research is conducted related to some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution, pollution control, land management, climate change, and energy systems, relevant to the quality of soil, water, air, biodiversity, and other ecosystem services. Advisory services within these areas are offered to ministries and other stakeholders. Currently, about 170 staff and PhD-students are working at the department. Further information may be found at http://www.envs.au.dk/en/. The department is located at Risø Campus in Roskilde, 35 kilometers west of Copenhagen.

The selected candidate will be affiliated with the Environmental Social Science and Geography research unit. The unit employs approximately 25 staff, focusing on interdisciplinary analysis of the interlinkages between the environment and society from political science, economics and sociology perspectives. The strategic focus of the unit includes environmental policy development, regulation and instruments, understanding of actions and actors in policy formulation and implementation, spatially integrated modelling as well as policies and economics of ecosystem services and nature-based solutions. Research findings are used for dissemination to the research community, in advisory services to decision makers as well as for teaching.

Our ambition is to have an inclusive and open working environment. 

What we offer 
The department offers:

• an exciting interdisciplinary and international environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

jobs.description:
Section of Epidemiology - Perinatal, Obstetric & Pediatric Epidemiology (POPE) group
Department of Public Health
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
University of Copenhagen

Do you have a strong methodological foundation and an interest in designing, analysing and interpreting epidemiological observational studies? Do you enjoy working with large-scale datasets from national registries and cohort studies to address important public health questions? And would you like to contribute to research with high societal relevance, focusing on health and development from early childhood to adulthood?

If so, we invite you to apply for a full-time position (37 hours/week) as Staff Scientist in the Perinatal, Obstetric & Paediatric Epidemiology (POPE) Group at the Section of Epidemiology, University of Copenhagen, starting 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. In this role, you will execute analytical tasks within epidemiological research projects using national registry and cohort data, while developing and maintaining research data resources.

About Section of Epidemiology and the POPE group 

The Section of Epidemiology conducts research on determinants of health and disease across the life-course, with the aim of improving public health and advancing epidemiological theory.

You will join the POPE group, whose research focuses on maternal, child, and adolescent health from a life-course perspective. Our work examines how perinatal and early childhood exposures influence health outcomes throughout childhood and into young adulthood. Research topics include preterm birth, infections and vaccinations during pregnancy, mental health, and psychiatric treatment. The POPE group extensively uses Danish registry data and the Danish National Birth Cohort (DNBC), which provides rich self-reported and biological data. DNBC is a nationwide birth cohort including more than 96,000 individuals born in 1996-2003 whose mothers enrolled during pregnancy – more details here. The group is deeply involved in ongoing and future DNBC data collections, long-term follow-up, and international cohort collaborations. For more details read here: POPE

About the Department
The Department of Public Health provides the scientific foundation for researchers and educators who aim to improve public health, both nationally and globally, and to create greater insight into the links between health, the individual, and society as well as the ethical, equity, and political implications. This is achieved through research, education, and engagement with stakeholders and the general public along with a broad multidisciplinary research agenda that addresses most aspects of public health at a high international level. More information about the Department of Public Health is available here.

About the Position
The Staff Scientist will play a central role in advancing and executing epidemiological research within the POPE group. Working collaboratively with researchers, external collaborators, and colleagues across the Department of Public Health, with opportunities of conducting independent research, while the primary responsibility is to contribute and execute projects led by others based on large-scale Danish registry and cohort data. Responsibilities will include developing and maintaining research data resources, ensuring rigorous data quality, performing advanced analytical and statistical workflows, and contributing to the establishment/maintenance of data infrastructures that enable high-quality epidemiological research and peer-reviewed publications. The tasks include:

• 
Developing, maintaining, and quality assuring large-scale epidemiological data resources based on Danish national registries and cohort data including the DNBC.

• 
Contributing to the design, implementation, and conduct of epidemiological research projects by preparing analytical datasets, performing descriptive and statistical analyses, and supporting the interpretation and dissemination of findings.

• 
Coordinating key research activities related to the DNBC, including the ongoing 25-year follow-up and international federated analyses across cohorts.

• 
Establishing data set-ups where cohort data are embedded within register-based populations for resources beyond DNBC

• 
Providing methodological and analytical support to a broad range of epidemiological research projects within the group, contributing expertise in study implementation, data handling, troubleshooting and project development as needed.

• 
Taking responsibility for data security, exportation of analysis results, data governance and GDPR compliance within the POPE group

Profile and Qualifications

• 
Preferably a PhD in epidemiology and/or, public health or related fields.

• 
Advanced methodological and analytical skills, including demonstrated experience with data management, study design, statistical modelling, and interpretation of observational epidemiological data.

• 
A proven ability to envision, plan, and execute epidemiological research projects independently, while delivering work to agreed deadlines.

• 
Proven experience working with large and complex datasets from Danish national registries, large cohorts, or other longitudinal data sources using R, STATA and/or SAS.

• 
Strong scientific writing skills, with a track record of preparing and publishing peer-reviewed publications and project documentation.

• 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to provide expert methodological guidance and explain complex findings to researchers from diverse backgrounds in a collaborative fashion.

• 
Fluency in Danish (both written and spoken) is required, as the role involves working extensively with Danish national registry data and documentation.

• 
Experience in, or a strong interest in perinatal and life-course epidemiology, including research on child development, adolescent health, and/or mental health.

Place of employment
The place of employment is Section of Epidemiology, Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen located near the city lakes in Central Copenhagen.

Terms of employment
The position is a full-time position (37 working hours weekly).
The starting date is 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Employment will be in accordance with the provisions of the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations). The monthly salary will be based on seniority with the possibility to negotiate a salary supplement based on prior experiences and qualifications.

Questions
For further information regarding the position, please contact Professor and Research group leader Katrine Strandberg-Larsen, email: ksla@sund.ku.dk. For questions regarding the recruitment procedure, please contact HR at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences: HR-IFSV@adm.ku.dk

Application
Your application must include the following:

• 
Cover letter, including motivations for applying for this position (max. 1 page).

• 
Curriculum Vitae, including education, work/research experience, language skills, and any other skills relevant to the position.

• 
A certified/signed copy of certificate(s) of education.

 Please submit your application by clicking on “Apply for position” below. Only online applications will be accepted.

Application deadline: 30 November 2026

We reserve the right to reject material received after the deadline, and to reject applications that do not meet the abovementioned requirements.

The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the diversity of society and encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their personal background.

jobs.description:
Do you want to shape the production IT behind some of Europe’s largest dairies, and are you motivated by taking the AVEVA platform to the next level across more than 50 sites?

“To support our growth, we are looking for you to join Arla as an Aveva MES engineer to deliver great results within our MES environment. Together, we support Europe’s largest dairies, a wide range of products and the farmers who own Arla Foods through great IT solutions. By contributing to these solutions, you will make a real difference for the entire organization, and your colleagues near and far. Join us to help us create a dairy of the future,” says Arne Bo Jensen, Senior Manage, Head of IT Product.

The Arla AVEVA System Platform is installed in various versions on more than 50 dairy sites across Europe, where operational teams use it as their primary industrial software platform to monitor and optimise plant performance and execute global production targets. We are now upgrading the platform on all sites as an important step in Arla’s digitalisation strategy. You will join the AVEVA team within Digital Manufacturing in IT Solutions, working in a hybrid delivery model that combines Agile and traditional project methodologies. Working closely with your team, key business stakeholders and external consultants, you will be part of the ongoing development and rollout of the platform and help standardise solutions across all our dairies.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Developing and implementing new system functionality on AVEVA System Platform and InTouch.

The ideal candidate brings:

• A background in production environments or projects.

What do we offer?

This position is based in Aarhus, Denmark or Gdańsk, Poland, and you should expect approximately 20 travel days per year, primarily to our sites across Europe. You will help support Europe’s largest dairies, a wide range of products and the farmers who own Arla through great IT solutions, making a real difference for the entire organization and your colleagues near and far.

Would you like to join us?

For more information, please contact Arne Bo Jensen, Senior Manager - Head of IT Product on aboj@arlafoods.com.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Geotechnical Stability of Coastal Dikes - DTU Sustain
jobs.description:
Are you interested in starting your research career by contributing to the reduction of flooding risks associated with coastal dike instabilities?

Join DTU Sustain as a PhD candidate and perform pioneering research in slope stability, uncertainty characterisation and risk predictions.

As a PhD student, you will investigate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment of dikes, accounting for uncertainties in soil characterisation through modelling. The project offers a unique opportunity to work with slope stability analysis, statistical methods, physical modelling and risk assessment while addressing one of the pressing challenges of climate change in the built environment. 

You will become part of an ambitious and highly interdisciplinary research environment at DTU Sustain, collaborating closely with the Center for Coasts and Climate Adaptation, The Danish Environmental Protection Agency (formerly Danish Coastal Directorate) and Ghent University, while benefiting from access to state-of-the-art facilities in soil mechanics, geotechnical engineering and physical modelling. The position also includes international research stays with our collaborators, providing opportunities to develop a broad scientific network and gain hands-on experience with complementary expertise and facilities.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate you will be responsible for developing, validating and implementing computational tools for the stability assessment in collaboration with team members, supervisors and international collaborators.

In detail your responsibilities will include:

• Implement and benchmark simplified limit equilibrium methods against advanced computational modelling for dike instabilities
• Assess the reliability of simplified and advanced slope stability methods
• Characterise and map the uncertainty of the soil conditions in coastal dikes
• Evaluate the impact of climate change on the stability assessment
• Publish high-quality research in leading international journals and present findings at international conferences.
• Contribute to courses and assist in co-supervision of MSc and BSc students
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the candidates will be based on the material they submit and one or two stages of interview, online and/or in person. 

The assessment of applications will be ongoing and will start before the application deadline.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms 
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. The desired start date is 1 April 2027 depending on academic approval.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Varvara Zania, vaza@dtu.dk

You can read more about the Department of Environmental and Resource Engineering at www.sustain.dtu.dk/en/

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 14 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree, but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

jobs.occupation: Semiconductor process specialists - thin film deposition, plasma etching and characterisation - DTU Nanolab
jobs.description:
DTU Nanolab is looking for experienced engineers and physicists within thin film deposition, thin film plasma etching and thin film characterization in its ISO 4 & 5 cleanroom for micro- and nanofabrication.

We are seeking process specialists for the process specialist team. The team is responsible for thin-film deposition equipment (PVD, CVD, thermal processing), plasma etching systems, and a large suite of characterization tools (AFM, SEM, XRD, XPS, EDX, optical and stylus profilers, ellipsometers, reflectometers, PL mappers, and more). Responsibilities span the full equipment lifecycle, from procurement and implementation to documentation, maintenance, troubleshooting and the development of in-depth tool and process expertise needed to support users throughout a system's lifetime. 

The job
We are seeking people with experience and interest in plasma etching (ICP, IBE), plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD), AFM, sputter deposition, RTP annealing, PE-ALD, XRD and photo spectrometry. The job includes

• Process development of new processes and maintenance of current processes
• Documentation, including user manuals and process documentation
• In charge of QC and calibration procedures 
• Helping, training and education of users
• Assisting in fault finding in cooperation with technicians
• Assisting in procurement of new equipment: Specifications, demo runs and run-in
• Networking with other cleanroom labs in Europe
You will work closely with other process specialists and technicians in the Process Group, as well as with other DTU Nanolab groups, researchers, students and engineers from DTU and commercial companies. A large part of your working day will be spent in ISO 4 and 5 cleanrooms, where you will wear a full cleanroom suit.

Our expectations of you
You must have a M.Sc. or Ph.D. degree within either engineering or physics within a relevant field (micro/nanofabrication, experimental physics or similar) and have knowledge and experimental skills within the area of either plasma etching or thin film deposition and within different relevant characterization tools. 

Furthermore, we expect you to possess skills and qualifications in one or more of these areas:

• Plasma enhanced deposition (PECVD) and other CVD techniques (ALD and LPCVD)
• Plasma etching (ICP etching)
• PVD techniques (sputter deposition, e-beam evaporation and thermal evaporation)
• Thermal processing (oxidation, annealing and rapid thermal annealing)
• Thin film characterization techniques (AFM, XRD, photo spectrometry and other relevant)
• Hands-on experience working in a cleanroom environment
• Have a broad understanding of micro and nano processing
• Have an eye for detail and work meticulously
• Work well in teams with people from different backgrounds
• Service-minded
• Self-driven and able to plan your own working day
• Communicate well in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Danish is an advantage.
At DTU Nanolab, safety is a top priority, and we are looking for candidates who can thrive in a highly safety-conscious environment and meet the following physical and mental requirements: Is able to work in an environment where it can be necessary to wear specialized safety and protective equipment. Is able to respond quickly and effectively in emergency situations, including evacuation in case of alarms. Is able to perform tasks that require work while standing up and mobility for longer periods.

What we offer in return
We offer an interesting and challenging job in an international work environment. The work is highly hands-on and with a large degree of variation. We place emphasis on a high level of professionalism among our staff, so skills development is an integral part of our organization. We offer a great flexibility in the position. Please note that this is not a research position, but a technical position, with a main focus to facilitate academic and industrial users within the field of thin film processing and characterization.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Academic Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

Application and contact
Please submit your online application no later than 30 November 2026. Open the “Apply now” link, fill out the form and attach your motivated application, CV and exam certificates. 

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Head of Operations, Leif Steen Johansen on +45 25 34 89 92 or lesjo@dtu.dk.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Nanolab is the National Center for Nanofabrication and Characterization in Denmark and an open-access research infrastructure at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU). As one of Europe’s largest fair-access micro- and nanofabrication centers, it offers a large cleanroom and advanced electron microscopy facilities. DTU Nanolab supports cutting-edge research and small-scale production within MEMS/NEMS, photonics, and quantum technologies, covering nano- and microfabrication as well as advanced analysis of hard and soft matter.
