Would you like to help Whiteaway Group’s engineers spend less time working around tools and infrastructure, and more time building software?

We’re modernizing the platform behind software development at Whiteaway Group. We’re moving away from legacy systems, expanding our cloud platform and automating more of the work that slows teams down. We’re looking for a Platform Engineer to join our Platform Squad in Aarhus and help make it easier for our engineers to build, deploy and run software.

We treat our platform as a product, and our engineers are the people who use it every day. You’ll work directly with development teams to understand where they lose time, decide what to improve and see whether the changes make their work easier.

What you’ll help us achieve

Make it easier for teams to deploy and run their software. You’ll improve CI/CD pipelines and build self-service tools so teams can handle more routine tasks themselves. You’ll work with developers to find the steps that cause delays or require manual work, then help simplify or automate them.

Help us move away from legacy infrastructure while keeping the platform reliable. You’ll build and operate infrastructure on AWS and Kubernetes, using Terraform to make changes repeatable. You’ll also improve monitoring and observability so teams can spot and diagnose problems, and help make secure access easier to manage.

Shape how we improve the developer experience. You’ll help the squad decide which platform improvements will make the biggest difference to development teams. We’re also exploring where AI could help the platform squad and the teams we support, and you’ll have room to test ideas where they solve a real problem.

What you’ll bring

You might be a Platform Engineer, DevOps Engineer, Cloud Engineer or Site Reliability Engineer. You might also be a software engineer who has spent a significant part of your time building or operating cloud infrastructure.

We’re interested in what you’ve improved and how you went about it. Perhaps you’ve automated a deployment that used to require several manual steps, made a production issue easier to diagnose, or built a tool that helped other engineers work more independently.

We’re looking for hands-on experience in several areas of our stack: AWS, Kubernetes and Docker, Terraform, Linux and networking, and Git, GitHub and CI/CD. Experience with Node.js or Go is also relevant. If you’ve worked with GitOps, Argo CD, Datadog, Spacelift, Cloudflare or cloud security, that’s a plus.

Your team and how we work

You’ll join four Platform Engineers in a Tech organisation of around 45 people. Whiteaway Group is one of Scandinavia’s largest e-commerce companies for home appliances, with more than 300 employees. As we continue investing in the platform, you’ll have a say in what the squad builds and how we support development teams across the business.

We make time for learning and sharing knowledge through pair programming, hackathons and Improvement Mondays. You’ll also have access to learning resources and personal development opportunities.

We work primarily from our Aarhus office and offer one fixed day per week to work from home. We also offer a pension scheme, a lunch scheme, an on-site gym and free parking.

Interested?

Send us your application and CV via our careers site. We’d love to hear about a platform, tool or workflow you’ve improved: what problem you tackled, what you changed and what difference it made.

We review applications and hold interviews on a rolling basis, and we’ll hire as soon as we find the right person.

Whiteaway Group is an ambitious, successful and fast-growing e-commerce and retail company. We sell white goods and premium home products to customers throughout the Nordics via several online shops and the Skousen franchise.

The idea for Whiteaway Group arose in the backroom of a Danish kitchen store. The foundation was innovation, business acumen and excellent customer experience. And it still is. Many years later we are the leading supplier in Scandinavia in our field and we are almost 300 dedicated employees working from offices in Sweden, Denmark, and Norway.

We are looking for a Financial Controller to lead the operational and analytical work behind our monthly close, group consolidation, project controlling and control environment of a fast-growing energy trading and technology group – and to rebuild them AI-first, so our numbers are faster, more reliable and ready for scale.

Why this role matters

Hybrid Greentech is scaling fast as a VPP, BRP and electricity retailer across Denmark, and Northern Europe. Energy trading means large and volatile daily revenue, cost and cash transactions – so quality , accuracy and liquidity control are not back-office topics; they decide how fast we can grow. This role exists to give management, the board and investors numbers they can trust, on time, and to build controls and automation that scale with the business rather than with headcount. The same discipline is needed in our consultancy arm, where technical consultants deliver advisory and EPC management projects: clear project economics, timely invoicing and early warning when a project drifts.

The role

As Financial Controller, you report to our Finance Manager and work closely with the CFO and our accountant in a small, hands-on finance team. You lead the operational and analytical work within the financial steering, reporting and finance and business analytics; running the month-end close, the consolidation of our group entities in Denmark and abroad, balance sheet reconciliations, project controlling and the day-to-day operation of our internal controls. This is an individual contributor role with high ownership and direct visibility towards management.

You will work in close collaboration with our settlement team, project managers and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting, partner with our accountant on more complex accounting topics, and work across trading, portfolio management, commercial and engineering. We are a tech-first company with high AI adoption, and we expect you to work that way too: AI tools, scripting and automation are your default approach to removing manual work from close, reconciliation and reporting – combined with the judgement to know when a number needs a human review.

**What you will do

**

• Lead and execute the monthly close and group consolidation, including account mapping, intercompany eliminations, reconciliations and variance analysis, and prepare the monthly financial and business review for the CFO, management and the board.

• Set up and run project controlling – project budgets, hours and utilisation, work in progress, milestone and fixed-fee revenue recognition and timely invoicing – giving project managers and business owners clear steering on margin, estimate-to-complete and cash.

• Automate and rebuild our reporting flow – from ERP trial balances to consolidated P&L, balance sheet and cash flow – using AI tools, scripting and data pipelines, replacing manual spreadsheet steps with controlled, repeatable and documented processes.

• Operate and strengthen our internal controls within the framework set by the Finance Manager, including segregation of duties, payment and bank authorisations and documented business procedures, and drive follow-up on auditor recommendations.

• In close collaboration with Settlement, ensure trading-related balances – settlement, imbalance costs, customer prepayments and deposits, and collateral posted to TSOs, DSOs and exchanges – are correctly recognized, invoiced and reconciled

• Support cash and liquidity forecasting and management with the Finance Manager and CFO, including rolling cash forecasts, collateral and trading risk capital tracking, and early warning on cash exposure.

• Prepare and analyse the annual budget and monthly forecast updates for the Finance Manager and CFO, maintaining our driver-based budget model and following up on budget-versus-actual deviations with business owners.

• Handle key accounting areas such as revenue recognition and accruals, capitalisation of development projects, grant periodisation and month-end cost accruals, collaborating with our accountant on more complex accounting topics.

• Support in the year-end close and audit for all group entities, including annual reports, tax specifications and intercompany agreements, in close collaboration with Finance Manager and our external auditors.

• Work closely with our Settlement team and business owners to ensure adequate financial steering and reporting – turning data into insight on gross profit by revenue stream, cost of execution and unit economics, and building dashboards that let the business self-serve.

**

What you bring**

_Experience and skills (Required)

_

• 5+ years of experience as a controller, in audit or in a group finance role, ideally in a multi-entity set-up.

• A relevant degree in accounting, finance or economics (e.g. cand.merc., HD-R or cand.merc.aud.).

• Proven hands-on experience running month-end close, consolidation and year-end audit under the Danish Financial Statements Act (Årsregnskabsloven)

• Hands-on experience with ERP systems, preferably e-conomic

• Solid understanding of balance sheet accounting, revenue recognition, capitalised development costs, accruals and intercompany transactions.

• Experience with project controlling – budgets, work in progress, utilisation and project margin follow-up – ideally in a consultancy, engineering, Trading or EPC business.

• A genuine AI-first way of working: you use AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT or Copilot daily and can show concrete examples of finance processes you have automated (e.g. with Python, SQL, Power Query, APIs or low-code tools).

• Strong Excel and financial modelling skills combined with a structured, control-minded approach and high attention to detail.

• The ability to work independently in a fast-paced scale-up, prioritise under pressure and explain financial matters clearly to non-finance colleagues.

• Language: English (required); Danish

_Nice to have

_

• Experience from energy trading, utilities, commodities or financial services – e.g. settlement, collateral, imbalance or margin processes.

• Experience with e-conomic, time registration or PSA tools, ERP migration to a more scalable platform, and BI tools such as Power BI.

• Experience with public grant-funded projects, transfer pricing or building internal controls in a growth company.

• A background from a Big 4 or mid-tier audit firm.

**What we offer

**

• Real responsibility: the chance to improve how close, controls and reporting are run in a scaling energy trading group – not just maintain them.

• An AI-first workplace where you get the tools and the mandate to automate, experiment and rethink how finance is done, working closely with our CFO, trading and tech teams with exposure to board and investor reporting.

• Competitive compensation and performance-based incentives.

• A collaborative environment with short decision lines, high trust, and strong cross-functional execution.

• The opportunity to work with forward-looking customers and partners driving electrification and the green transition in Northern Europe.

Ready to apply?

Ready to build an AI-first finance function for a company where every megawatt-hour traded must be settled, reconciled and controlled? If you combine accounting rigour with a builder's mindset, we would love to hear from you.

Deadline

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis until 10 December. We reserve the right to close this vacancy earlier if a suitable candidate is identified and accepted.

Do you want to head up quality and food safety at Harboe’s production site in Skælskør? Do you possess a strong professional background within QA/QC, and are you motivated by driving a proactive quality culture in close collaboration with production? Then you might be the one we are looking for.

Harboes Bryggeri produces and sells beer, soft drinks, and malt- and fruit-based ingredients and beverages. Production takes place at our breweries in Skælskør and at the fully owned Darguner Brauerei in Germany. Both sites produce and package beverages in glass, cans, and PET, while Dargun also handles draught beer. Malt-based ingredients and concentrates are produced in Skælskør.

Quality and food safety are fundamental to everything we do. The Quality Department plays a key role in ensuring compliance, maintaining high standards, and safeguarding product quality from raw material to finished goods.

The position and Key responsibilities

As Quality Manager, you will have overall responsibility for leading Harboe’s Quality Department and ensuring the effective operation, maintenance, and continuous alignment of our quality management system.

You will become a part of the Group Quality Team and report directly to the Plant Director in Skælskør, with a dotted line reference to the Director, R&D, ESG and Quality.

Your primary focus will be to lead and develop our QA and QC teams while ensuring that our quality and food safety standards are consistently implemented and maintained across the organisation. Through visible leadership and close collaboration with production and other key stakeholders, you will ensure that quality remains an integral part of daily operations.

Building on our existing quality management system, you will drive systematic and continuous quality improvements. You will ensure compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements while ensuring that the quality function supports customer expectations and operational needs.

• Leading and developing the Quality Department, including QA and QC teams, ensuring clear priorities, strong collaboration, and a high level of engagement.

• Maintaining close cooperation with production, including handling of deviations, root cause analysis, and follow-up on corrective actions.

• Ensuring professional handling of customer complaints, including documentation, investigation, and timely follow-up.

• Ensuring compliance with food legislation, regulatory requirements, and quality standards, including communication and documentation.

• Supporting supplier quality requirements, including hygiene standards and HACCP-based controls through training and monitoring.

jobs.description:
Build software at scale. Influence how we build it. Help modernize a product area at the heart of construction projects.

Dalux is growing, and we are looking for an experienced software developer to join our Box Collab team.

You will build software in our File Management product (Box) that enables communication and collaboration across construction stakeholders—for example, file comments, sharing, versioning, and review. This domain is widely used and deeply integrated across the Dalux product suite, so reliability, performance, and strong technical design are essential. In Box Collab, we foster an engaging, enjoyable work environment where people take ownership and accountability for outcomes. You’ll join a young, skilled team with strong opportunities to influence both product evolution and architectural direction.

**Your role

**As an Experienced Software Developer, you will take ownership of complex product and technical problems from idea to production.

You will join a full-stack development team working closely with a Product Manager and Product Designer. We expect experienced developers to contribute beyond their individual tasks: helping make good technical decisions, improving the codebase and architecture, sharing knowledge, and raising the engineering standard around them.

Within Box Collab, there is a particular focus on strengthening and evolving the technical foundation of the product while continuing to deliver new functionality.

Your work can include:

• Owning complex features and technical problems end-to-end

• Designing and implementing scalable, maintainable solutions

• Contributing to architectural decisions and the technical direction of Box Collab.

• Improving the structure of an established codebase and reducing technical debt

• Helping evolve boundaries and modularity within the application

• Sparring with and mentoring other developers

• Working closely with Product Management and Design to understand problems and find the right solutions

• Bringing new ideas, technologies, and development practices into the team when they create real value

We expect experienced developers to have opinions, challenge existing solutions, and be comfortable having their own ideas challenged in return.

**AI-assisted software development

**We are significantly increasing our focus on AI-assisted development across Dalux.

We are actively exploring how AI can improve the software development lifecycle – from understanding requirements and exploring technical approaches to coding, testing, review, debugging, refactoring, and automation.

The Box Collab team is already experimenting with how these tools can improve its day-to-day development work.

As an experienced developer, we want you to take an active role in that development: experimenting with new workflows, critically evaluating their value, sharing what works, and helping establish good engineering practices around AI-assisted development.

Practical experience using AI as part of your development workflow is an advantage. More importantly, you should be curious about how these tools are changing software engineering and willing to continue evolving your own way of working.

**Technologies we work with

**Box Collab is a full-stack product area primarily built with:

• C# / .NET

• Angular / TypeScript

• MSSQL

• Elasticsearch

Our wider platform runs on a distributed cloud architecture using AWS.

Experience with our exact technology stack is useful, but strong software engineering fundamentals and the ability to understand and improve complex systems matter more.

**What would make you a particularly strong match?

**We are looking for an experienced software developer with strong technical fundamentals and the ability to influence the software around you.

For this particular team, we would especially value:

• Str ong professional experience with C# and .NET

• Strong DB management experience, including indexing strategies and query performance optimization.

• Experience improving or modernizing established software systems

• An understanding of Domain-Driven Design, modular architecture, or similar approaches to structuring complex applications

• Experience mentoring or providing technical sparring to other developers

• Practical experience with AI-assisted development tools and workflows

You do not need to match every point.

Technical judgment, curiosity, and the ability to make an established product better are more important than having worked with exactly the same technologies or architectural patterns before.

**Product development at Dalux

**Our product teams bring developers, Product Managers, and Product Designers together.

Developers are expected to understand the problem being solved and contribute to finding the solution – not simply implement specifications handed to them.

As an experienced developer, you will have an important voice in balancing user value, usability, technical feasibility, business viability, and long-term technical health.

Our products are relied upon by professionals worldwide, making performance, stability, maintainability, and quality important parts of everyday engineering.

**What You Can Expect From Dalux

**Dalux is a software company at heart.

As an experienced developer, you can expect:

• Significant ownership of the software you build

• Real influence on technical solutions and engineering practices

• Skilled colleagues who enjoy technical discussion and constructive challenge

• Close collaboration between Engineering, Product Management, and Design

• Short paths from technical ideas to decisions and implementation

• Opportunities to improve an established product and architecture

• A healthy work-life balance, with a strong focus on a sustainable work week and no overwork culture.

• Clear opportunities for professional and career growth.

• An environment actively investing in AI-assisted software development

• High levels of trust and freedom in how you solve problems

• A social workplace with monthly events and employee-driven clubs

All Dalux software development takes place in-house at our headquarters in Vibenshuset, Copenhagen. Working together in person is an important part of how we collaborate, share knowledge, and make decisions quickly.

**About Dalux

**Dalux is a Danish software company founded in 2005 by Bent Dalgaard and Torben Dalgaard.

We build digital tools that make the construction industry smarter and more efficient. Using our own 3D BIM technology, Dalux develops user-friendly software used in more than 140 countries worldwide.

Our core technology is developed entirely in-house, giving our developers the opportunity to influence both the products and the technology behind them.

**Interested?

**If you are looking for a role where you can remain hands-on while gaining greater technical influence and helping evolve an established product and architecture, we would like to hear from you.

We recruit continuously as Dalux grows.

**Application deadline:

**Ongoing

SENIOR BACKEND DEVELOPER

🚀 We're looking for an ambitious, self-driven Senior Backend Developer to join our engineering team. You'll work primarily with TypeScript and AWS serverless technologies, with occasional work in our React/Next.js frontend. A growing part of our platform is integrating with enterprise customers and external systems, so you'll design and own APIs and integrations that need to hold up under real-world use.

This is a high-impact role with end-to-end ownership, from requirements to a production-ready solution, and a chance to contribute meaningfully to the green transition.

🛠️ What You'll Be Doing

• Taking features from design through implementation and into production

• Building and operating event-driven, distributed systems — async processing, retries, failure handling, idempotency

• Designing APIs and integrations for enterprise and external systems — stable contracts, versioning, auth, error handling, backwards compatibility

• Working in and improving our existing codebase — refactoring, automated testing, managing technical debt

• Occasional frontend work in React/TypeScript

🧠 Your Experience

• 3 to 5+ years of professional software development, with substantial recent experience in TypeScript/Node.js and AWS serverless or event-driven architectures

• Strong hands-on experience with AWS services - Lambda, DynamoDB, queues, event buses, API services, infrastructure as code

• Experience with NoSQL data modelling and production data systems

• Good understanding of authentication, authorization and application security

• Experience operating production systems - debugging, monitoring, safely deploying changes

• Comfortable with Git-based workflows and CI/CD

• Some React/TypeScript experience, and willingness to make occasional frontend changes

✅ What We Expect at Senior Level

You can independently take a feature or technical problem from requirements to a production-ready solution. You're comfortable navigating unfamiliar code, understanding the blast radius of a change, and making pragmatic calls between delivery speed, reliability and maintainability.

You think carefully about system boundaries and integration contracts, understanding that APIs used by customers and external systems need to evolve safely and behave predictably when either side fails. You understand rollback, backwards compatibility, failure modes and safe deployment for systems handling production data.

You communicate trade-offs clearly and take responsibility for the quality of what you ship.

You're comfortable using AI-assisted development tools as part of your day-to-day work, and curious about how they can improve how software is designed, built, tested and maintained - not just for code generation, but for understanding unfamiliar code, planning changes, testing, reviewing, debugging and documentation. At the same time, you apply strong engineering judgement: you treat AI-generated output as a draft to review and validate, and you remain responsible for the correctness and security of what you ship.

🌟 Nice to Have

• Enterprise integrations - SSO/federated identity, webhooks, customer-facing APIs

• AWS CDK or similar IaC tooling

• DynamoDB single-table or composite-key modelling

• IoT, connected devices, telemetry or high-volume event processing

• Multi-tenant SaaS platforms

• Energy tech, EV charging, batteries, solar or energy management

• Data platforms, analytics or data lakes

• ISO 27001 or NIS2 experience

• Next.js

You don't need experience with every technology in our stack. We value strong fundamentals and the ability to learn unfamiliar domains fast.

🌆 What Is It Like to Work at FLEXECHARGE?

• Our office sits in Frederiksberg - bright, comfortable, and a genuinely nice place to spend your workday

• You're covered with pension contributions

• Lunch is on-site, delicious, and genuinely healthy and nutritious

• We like each other's company outside of work too, so think Friday bars, plus company team events and team buildings on a team level

• Opportunities for individual development

🤝 Our Interview Process

Here's roughly what happens once we've had a look at your application:

• A first conversation, about 30 minutes, you'll talk with our recruiter, get a feel for the role, ask whatever's on your mind, and we'll both get a sense of whether this is worth pursuing further

• Time with the team - a conversation with Artur, our Head of Engineering, and Robert, our CTO

• A technical stage - one or more interviews with the team, which may include a case exercise and follow-up discussions. These can take place remotely or at our office.

• A conversation with Max, our CEO, alongside someone else from the team

Hiring carefully matters to us - we want to get to know you properly, and we want you to get a real feel for us too. If there's anything we can do to make the process work better for you, tell us.

We'd love to hear from you. Find a link to apply here 👉 https://thehub.io/jobs/6ab5030dfd5518f38b6960b2?utm_source=client&utm_medium=dashboard&utm_campaign=startupshared

📍 Location & Practical Details

This is an on-site role based in Copenhagen.

Only candidates currently located in Copenhagen, or those who clearly state in their application that they plan to relocate, will be considered.

Please note:

• We do not offer visa sponsorship for this role

• We do not offer relocation services

🔐 Data Privacy (GDPR)

• Applications for this role are processed exclusively through The Hub (thehub.io), our recruitment platform, in accordance with their privacy policy and applicable GDPR requirements. As part of our interview process, conversations may be recorded and transcribed via Microsoft Teams, and AI tools may be used to summarize interview notes to support our hiring team's evaluation. Your data will be handled confidentially, retained only during the interview process, and used only for this recruitment process. jobs.occupation: Senior Project Engineers - Substations and Export Cables
jobs.description:
Business Area Wind is responsible for Vattenfall’s Onshore and Offshore Wind, as well as other non-hydro renewable initiatives like PV/Solar and batteries. We currently develop, construct and operate wind generation assets across Sweden, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands and the UK.

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets. You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

We are looking for several Senior Project Engineers to strengthen our offshore transmission engineering capabilities within Business Area Wind, Offshore, Engineering.

We are seeking engineers with experience in one or more of the following areas:

• Offshore substations

• Onshore substations

• Offshore export cables

• Onshore export cables

We welcome engineers from all relevant disciplines across these scopes, with particular interest in HV and LV systems for onshore and offshore substations, and civil engineering for onshore substations and onshore export cable routes. Your assigned scope will reflect your background and experience.

You will take ownership of assigned engineering work packages, from FEED and tendering through delivery and handover.

In these roles, you will apply your experience to shape and challenge supplier solutions from the owner’s perspective, coordinate technical expertise and resolve delivery issues.

Within the project, you will report to the respective Package Manager and work autonomously within your assigned scope, drawing on technical specialists and collaborating with Interface Managers, Procurement and other project functions.

Your responsibilities:

• 
Deliver assigned engineering work packages in accordance with contractual requirements and project and contract milestones. Plan and coordinate activities, and monitor and report on safety, quality, progress and cost within your scope.

• 
Apply a systems engineering mindset so decisions within your scope support the performance, integration, optimisation and delivery of the overall transmission system—not individual contracts in isolation.

• 
Keep the design basis, requirements, interface decisions and contractual scope aligned, coordinating the impact of changes on affected packages.

• 
Work with Interface Managers and project teams to define and resolve technical and contractual interfaces, including scope boundaries, engineering inputs and delivery dependencies.

• 
Assess supplier proposals and technical decisions with safety as the highest, non-negotiable priority. Consider functionality, availability, quality, constructability and maintainability alongside CAPEX, OPEX, schedule and delivery risk.

• 
Coordinate technical specialist input and challenge unnecessary complexity and over-specification in supplier solutions.

• 
Identify and manage scope-related risks and opportunities, maintain an up-to-date risk and opportunity register, and coordinate mitigation. Keep technical positions, assumptions, deviations and residual risks visible throughout the project lifecycle.

• 
Support supplier qualification and technical evaluation. Incorporate Employer’s Requirements and specialist input into tender documentation, making scope boundaries and interface requirements clear. Assess bids, deviations and assumptions to support negotiations and award.

• 
Follow supplier engineering while respecting supplier design responsibility. Coordinate technical reviews, verify supplier documentation against contractual requirements, and resolve technical queries, deviations and changes with relevant stakeholders. Align technical decisions with the respective Technical Authority.

• 
Coordinate manufacturing or construction quality surveillance, inspections and acceptance testing, including FAT where applicable. Verify supplier documentation and technical completion, and support construction and commissioning teams in resolving technical issues and ensuring interface readiness. Verify as-built documentation and support taking-over, handover and close-out for safe, reliable and efficient operation and maintenance.

• 
Share lessons learned and contribute to improving requirements, engineering practices and project delivery.

We welcome applications from candidates at either Intermediate or Senior level. For Intermediate-level candidates, we are particularly interested in individuals who demonstrate strong technical capabilities, a high level of motivation, and a willingness to learn and develop further

Location: The role will be based in one of Vattenfall’s office locations in Kolding (Denmark), Amsterdam (Netherlands) or Hamburg (Germany). Some travel to other Vattenfall offices, project locations, supplier facilities and construction sites should be expected.

Qualifications

Your profile:

• B.Sc. or M.Sc. in electrical engineering, power engineering, structural engineering, civil engineering, mechanical engineering or another relevant engineering discipline.

• At least five years of relevant engineering experience, including responsibility for electrical, structural, civil or mechanical engineering work packages in the development or delivery of one or more of the following: onshore or offshore HV substations, subsea export cable systems or onshore HV cable systems. Owner-side experience is preferred.

• Experience in major project development or delivery, including technical oversight, interface coordination or acceptance of supplier work. Experience in multi-contract delivery, where the owner retains responsibility for integration across suppliers and packages, is preferred.

• Experience reviewing and challenging supplier and contractor engineering, including interfaces with other disciplines, fabrication, construction and installation.

• A systems engineering mindset, demonstrated by resolving interfaces between disciplines, suppliers and packages in the interests of the overall transmission system.

• Strong safety and engineering judgement, including the ability to distinguish essential requirements from unnecessary complexity.

• Commercial awareness of how technical choices affect CAPEX, OPEX, schedule, contractual risk and project delivery.

• Self-motivated and able to work autonomously, with good communication and influencing skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across disciplines and packages.

• Professional working proficiency in English.

• Willingness to travel to project, supplier and construction locations as required.

Additional Information

Our offer

We offer an international and collaborative working environment, attractive employment conditions and opportunities for personal and professional development. You will work with experienced colleagues across disciplines and be encouraged to ask questions, share knowledge and contribute to continuous improvement.

More Information

Incoming applications are reviewed and evaluated on an ongoing basis. Therefore, this vacancy may be filled before the application deadline. The application deadline is November 29, 2026.

We welcome your application in English and kindly request that you do not send applications by any means other than via our website as we cannot guarantee that we will be able to process applications that are not made via our website.

For more information about the recruitment process you are welcome to contact our recruiter Sandra Domschke (sandra1.domschke@vattenfall.de) or Adam Hammond (adam.hammond@vattenfall.com).

At Vattenfall we are convinced that diversity contributes to building a more profitable and attractive company and we strive to be a good role model regarding diversity. Vattenfall works actively for all employees to have the same opportunities and rights regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, transgender identity or expression, religion or other belief, disability or sexual orientation. Click here for further information.

The security of Vattenfall and its employees is essential. A pre-employment screening will therefore form part of the recruitment process and will reflect the requirements of the role. The screening will be conducted by a third party, DISA Global Solutions AB.

Vattenfall is a European energy company with approximately 20 000 employees. For more than 100 years we have electrified industries, supplied energy to people’s homes and modernized our way of living through innovation and cooperation. jobs.occupation: Join us as a Student Data Engineer in Fund Accounting Products
jobs.description:
Would you like to put your studies into practice in an AI-first engineering environment and work with data engineering and AI-assisted development that creates real business value? Would you like to build your technical skills while contributing to solutions used across Nykredit? Then you might be our new Student Data Engineer in Fund Accounting Products.

As a Student Data Engineer in Fund Accounting Products, you will play an important role in our team, helping us build reports, automate processes and develop the data flows and platforms that support fund valuation, alternatives and fund accounting.

Nykredit is investing heavily in AI, and our team takes an AI-first approach. We actively consider how AI can help us code, test and solve problems more efficiently, while taking responsibility for the quality of the results.

You will also become part of the Nykredit Group, where we offer opportunities and development for those who are curious and eager to learn. Through our student network, Nykredit Youth, you will be invited to professional events and networking opportunities with other students and young colleagues across the Group.

Are you motivated by data engineering and new technologies?

Then you have come to the right place. Your focus will be on reports, data processing, event-driven streaming pipelines and the platforms supporting our business domains.

You will work with technologies such as Python, SQL, Microsoft Fabric, Apache Spark, Azure and Kafka, alongside colleagues using GitHub, Terraform and Grafana for development, deployment and monitoring. These are technologies you will have the opportunity to work with and learn about, not a checklist of things you need to know before applying.

Your tasks will include:

• Developing and improving reports used by the business.

• Preparing, transforming and validating financial data.

• Automating manual tasks using Python and SQL.

• Helping build and test event-driven streaming pipelines and integrations using Kafka.Working with SimCorp Dimension and bringing its data into our Wealth Data Hub.

• Improving monitoring and automation of data flows and operational tasks.

• Exploring how AI can help us modernise legacy code, automate operations and improve data quality.

• Investigating data quality issues and improving existing solutions.

You will start with well-defined tasks and gradually take on more responsibility as you learn, working alongside experienced engineers on real deliveries.

The position is 10–15 hours per week at our headquarters, Nykredit Huset, Sundkrogsgade 25 in Nordhavn, where most of the team is based.

**AI as part of your everyday work

**We work with an AI-first approach: when tackling a task, we actively consider how AI can help us solve it better and more efficiently, while taking responsibility for the quality of the result.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Large-Signal Modelling and Transient Stability Analysis of Wind Turbine Generators under Grid Fault Conditions
jobs.description:
The WindConnect (wind farm control and integration in sector-coupled power systems https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101227683) consortium unites leading experts from academia and industry across Europe, leveraging expertise in wind energy, power systems, power electronics, control engineering, artificial intelligence, and energy economics. This multidisciplinary collaboration addresses the pressing challenges of integrating wind energy into sector-coupled power systems including green hydrogen production, while ensuring grid stability, flexibility, and sustainability.

At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, AAU Energy, a position as PhD stipend is available within the general study program. The PhD stipend is open for appointments from 1st March 2027 or soon after. The position is for 3 years, and it is funded by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Networks programme under the WindConnect project.

• On the date of recruitment (expected to be 1 March 2027), applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding the recruitment date. Applicants must not hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.
• The project offers you competitive salaries (plus allowances) and funding for technical and personal skills training and participation in international research events.
• You will participate in international secondments to other organisations in the network.
AAU Energy is a dynamic engineering research department in continuous growth and inspiring surroundings. AAU Energy has a very international environment and covers all areas of clean and sustainable energy systems of the future within electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technology. AAU Energy has campuses in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, this position is located in Aalborg.

The mission is to be world leading in both research and research-based education of the energy engineers of the future. AAU Energy has approx. 300 employees of many nationalities, of which 25 are administrative staff. In addition, AAU Energy constantly has approx. 50-70 guest researchers from around the world.

Research and teaching are in the absolute world elite in the field of energy, and we have extensive and leading workshop and laboratory facilities, where research and innovation are carried out in direct collaboration with industry to a great extent.

The position is offered in relation to the research program "Power Electronic Control Reliability and System Optimization" and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Applied Power Electronic Systems”.

The increasing integration of wind turbine generators significantly alters power system dynamics, particularly under grid fault conditions. While grid-forming (GFM) wind turbine generators contribute to voltage and frequency regulation, they may exhibit significant nonlinear large-signal behaviour during disturbances, including current limiting, control mode switching, and loss of synchronism. In multi-converter systems, these transient dynamics are further shaped by interactions among multiple GFM units and the surrounding grid strength. Conventional small-signal models are therefore inadequate, motivating large-signal modelling and transient stability analysis frameworks for GFM wind turbine generators under grid faults.

This poses the following key research questions:

• How can large-signal models of GFM wind turbine generators be developed to accurately capture nonlinear dynamics, particularly current limiting and control mode transitions during grid faults?
• How do multiple wind turbine generators interact during grid faults, and how do grid strength and system configurations influence their transient stability?
• What are the dominant dynamic mechanisms governing transient stability, and how can reduced-order models be developed while preserving the essential nonlinear dynamics and stability characteristics?
This project will be in close collaboration with Ørsted. The PhD student is expected to work closely with colleagues from Ørsted and visit their facilities. The aim of this PhD project is to develop large-signal modelling and transient stability analysis methods for wind turbine generators under grid fault conditions, with particular emphasis on multi-inverter systems. The project seeks to identify key mechanisms affecting transient stability and to provide modelling and analysis tools that support robust control and protection design for future wind-dominated power systems.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
• Curriculum Vitae (CV)
• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Project description (3-5 pages), which describes the applicant’s initial thoughts and ideas related to the specific project applied for. Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

Our IoT team builds the devices and edge software that connect our customers' production lines to the Factbird platform, from sensors on the line to industrial edge computers running computer vision right next to the machines. We're a small team with broad ownership, and we're hiring an Embedded Platform Engineer to help build and run the platform our edge products stand on.

**This role is onsite in Copenhagen, Denmark. We welcome applications from candidates based in Spain who are open to relocating to Copenhagen.

**

About the Role

As Embedded Platform Engineer, you'll work hands-on across Factbird EDGE, our industrial edge platform, together with the rest of the IoT team: the operating system, the device software, and the vision models that run on it. You'll take ownership of the infrastructure around the devices: provisioning and recovery, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability, the systems that keep our unattended devices reliable, secure, and safely updatable in factories you may never visit.

You'll work in Rust on embedded Linux, with Yocto, AWS IoT Greengrass, GStreamer and ONNX Runtime at the core, alongside our Cloud and DevOps engineers and the people building our AI capabilities. Part of the job is shaping the role with the team as our edge products grow.

You'll thrive here if you like working across a system end to end, from the bootloader to the cloud connection, and if you'd rather fix the root cause in the build than patch around it on the device.

What you'll do

Embedded Linux & the EDGE platform

• Develop our Yocto-based Linux distribution: layers, BSPs, kernel configuration, and reproducible builds

• Build and maintain the Rust components that run on our edge devices

• Bring up new hardware platforms, debug on target, and keep the platform secure and maintainable over a long device lifetime

• Keep our CI and on-hardware testing healthy, so changes reach devices with confidence

Edge inference & vision

• Work with our ML and vision engineers on the device side of our computer vision capabilities: camera pipelines, video streaming, and model inference that runs efficiently on industrial hardware

• Share ownership with our ML engineers of how trained models move from our model pipeline onto devices and how they perform there: packaging, rollout, rollback, and drift monitoring

• Help bring new edge runtimes for vision workloads from development into production

Fleet infrastructure & ownership

• Own device provisioning, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability

• Make deployments to devices in the field safe and boring: staged rollouts, health checks, and recovery paths

• Help diagnose issues on devices at customer sites, working with Support, Product, and Cloud to turn them into lasting fixes

• Share knowledge in both directions: learn the parts of the platform others built, and make sure what you build doesn't live only in your head

**What we're looking for

**

We're looking for an engineer who has shipped embedded Linux into production and lived with it afterwards: someone who has debugged a device they couldn't touch, and who wants real responsibility rather than a ticket queue.

You work independently, but you don't work alone. You can take a loosely defined problem and move it forward without daily direction, and you pull others in early, because on a small team the best fix is one more than one person understands. You're disciplined where it matters, in releases and rollouts, and curious where it pays off, in vision and new hardware.

You don't need everything below. Yocto is the core. Rust matters, but strong C/C++ engineers who have started with Rust are welcome too. The rest you can grow into with us.

**

The ideal background**

• Hands-on experience shipping embedded Linux to production, including Yocto: layers, BSPs and images you've built and maintained yourself, not just consumed

• Strong systems programming in Rust, or deep C/C++ experience on embedded Linux and real exposure to Rust that you want to build on

• An advantage if you have worked with AWS IoT Core or Greengrass, video pipelines or ML inference on edge hardware, or in industrial settings where devices run unattended for years

• A solid grasp of embedded security and update mechanisms: signed images, A/B or similar update schemes, and secure device provisioning

• You can explain a technical trade-off clearly, whether you're talking to another engineer, Support or a customer, and you do it in fluent English

• We welcome applications from people eager to move to Denmark, as long as you already have the legal right to live and work here.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

Here's what you can look forward to:

• Flexible working hours: We trust you to manage your time. Life isn't one-size-fits-all, and neither is work.

• Competitive salary: We offer compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact.

• Internet reimbursement: Stay connected and productive, wherever you choose to work from.

• Thoughtful, human onboarding: We'll support you step by step, giving you the context, tools, and guidance you need to feel confident from day one.

• A career path that grows with you: Through bi-yearly Individual Development Plan conversations, we'll work together to shape a career journey that fits your ambitions.

• Company-wide gatherings & team days: We regularly come together across teams and regions to connect, celebrate, and align on what's next.

• A global, inclusive culture: We're proud of our diverse backgrounds and perspectives — and we actively celebrate them in how we work and collaborate.

**We'd love to hear from you

**

If this role feels like a match, we'd be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit — feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Have questions? You can always reach out to Cristina Vartej at **crva@factbird.com

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Causal inference jointly at the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and the Pioneer Center for AI
jobs.description:
A three-year position as Assistant Professor in causal inference jointly within The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and The Pioneer Center for AI to be employed at the Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen. The position is available from 1 March 2027, with the exact start date to be agreed with the successful candidate.

About the Pioneer Centre for SMARTbiomed: The Pioneer Centre for Statistical and computational Methods for Advanced Research to Transform Biomedicine (SMARTBiomed) will support a critical mass of researchers who focus on method and software development for analysis and inference from massive human data, advancing applications in medicine. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed will leverage large-scale, multimodal biomedical data combined with focused innovation in statistical and computational methods including machine learning to advance our understanding, treatment, and prevention of human disease. More information can be found here: https://smartbiomed.dk/

About the Pioneer Center for AI: The Pioneer Centre for Artificial Intelligence focuses on fundamental research, and within an interdisciplinary framework, develops platforms, methods, and practices addressing society’s greatest challenges. Hosted by the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Computer Science, cooperating institutions, Denmark’s Technical University, IT University of Copenhagen, Aalborg University, and Aarhus University co-lead the efforts along with Director, Professor Serge Belongie. More information on the center can be found here: https://www.aicentre.dk/ 

Information about the Department of Public Health can be found at: https://publichealth.ku.dk/

Job description
A successful candidate will conduct causal methods research at an international level. In the position, the candidate will work with both Erin Gabriel, (Causality theme lead and Co-director of SMARTbiomed and Professor at the Department of Public Health) and Sebastian Weichwald (Causality co-lead at the Pioneer Center AI and Associate professor at the Department of Mathematics) and aid in the supervision of a joint PhD student. The position is meant to be a bridge between the two centers, in causality, a theme both centers share. Specifically

The responsibilities will primarily consist of:

• 
Manage their own academic research and administrative activities

• 
Conduct research in line with the overlapping goals of the two pioneer centers in causal inference

• 
Contribute to evolving the research priorities of the two pioneer centers

• 
Support the collaborative infrastructure of the two pioneer centers

• 
Lead research papers pertaining to their own work and collaborate in the preparation of research publications. Ensure that software research outputs are provided to ensure maximum utility.

• 
Be a part of the supervision of the associated joint PhD student

• 
Develop ideas for new research projects

• 
Present papers at conferences and public meetings

• 
Take part in research-based teaching

• 
Supervise students, research assistants and postdocs outside of the joint student associated with the position

• 
Applying for funding for the next stage of their career

• 
Contribute to the administrative activities of both centers as needed

• 
Participation in formal pedagogical training programme for assistant professors

Profile
The successful applicant should have a PhD in Applied math, Statistics, Biostatistics, Computer science or a closely related area (e.g., pure mathematics with work in computational biology). The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

Assessment of applicants 
General criteria apply to the appointment of professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation and societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

Find information about each criterion here: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/criteria-for-recognising-merit.

Place of employment
The Department of Public Health, University of Copenhagen.

Terms of employment
The employment as Assistant Professor is a full-time and fixed-term position for 3 years. Starting date is 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation. Currently, the monthly salary starts at 39,993 DKK/approx. 5,349 EUR (August 2026 level). Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.

Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

Questions
For further information please contact Erin Gabriel by email: erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk and Sebastian Weichwald email: sweichwald@math.ku.dk (using the subject prefix “[P41]”).

Foreign applicants may find this link useful: ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

Application procedure
Your application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format. Additional documents will not be considered as part of the evaluation.

• 
Cover letter (Max 1 page): Stating at which level you are applying, substantiate your qualification for the position and your motivations.

• 
Curriculum vitae (Max 3 pages): including education, research experience, other relevant skills

• 
Complete list of publications and preprints.
Highlight up to two publications that are particularly representative of your research. For each, provide no more than two sentences explaining its significance to you and the field, and your specific contribution. The selected publications need not be your most highly cited.

• 
Research plan (Max 3 pages): Description of current and future research plans

• 
Teaching portfolio (max 3 pages): outlining teaching experience and teaching plans

• 
Diplomas: Master and PhD degree or equivalent. If you do not yet have a PhD diploma, please just upload a PDF stating your (expected) PhD date.

Application deadline: 10 December 2026, 23.59pm CET 

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above mentioned requirements.

The further process
After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities. 

The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

Moment Professionals is recruiting on behalf of FPRT a Strategic Projects & Business Operations Manager based in Vojens, Denmark. We are looking for a project manager with a consultant's or project developer's mindset, who takes ownership of cross-functional business projects, takes the first step in understanding and structuring an issue and brings the CEO clear recommendations. The role suits you if you want to build structure in a company that is being built right now, with pragmatic, lightweight project management appropriate for a greenfield environment.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the CEO and take over the project management of FPRT's business and corporate projects, which the CHRO carries today alongside HR. The role has no direct reports to begin with, and you work across most of the company, with the Chief Production Officer, the process engineers, production, data, finance, HR and supply chain, as well as external implementation partners and advisers. The CEO communicates briefly and precisely, often on chat, takes challenge well and builds the collaboration on trust. Your mandate grows as that trust grows.

In the first months the SAP implementation is the largest task. An external partner implements the system, and you are FPRT's internal business project lead for the implementation: you keep track of progress and next steps, translate operational needs into clear requirements together with the functional owners and drive the solution into daily use across production planning, stock management, logistics and the integration of the systems FPRT selects in this period. Next come warehouse and logistics, selected governance and cross-functional operating processes, and business cases, for example for a new factory. Along the way you coordinate grant applications, public funding submissions and bank and investor material with internal owners and external partners.

You take the first step in understanding and structuring an issue, identify what information and expertise are needed, and then involve the right people. When a financing partner sends a long list of questions with a 48-hour deadline, you draft the answers from the documents that exist, mark how certain each answer is and bring them to the CEO and the right colleagues for a short validation. You prepare decisions as options, risks, advantages and price on one page with a clear recommendation, and you escalate delays and unresolved risks with a recommendation of your own.

The role is based in Vojens. You have the flexibility to work from home when a task needs focus, and in intense project periods you are on site every day, sometimes for a month or more. English is used a lot in daily work, and Danish is preferred, since FPRT is building a company in Denmark. If your Danish is not fluent yet, the right competencies count most.

And then there are the benefits:

A central role close to the CEO with direct influence on how a new company is built, ownership of business systems, processes, funding and business cases from day one, a mandate that grows with the trust you build, a culture where challenge with facts is welcome, and flexibility to work from home when focus requires it.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried the title project manager or to come from defence. What matters is that you take ownership of cross-functional business projects, structure an issue before you involve the right people, and give a firm recommendation with the reasoning behind it. You also take pride in:

• 
challenging the CEO and colleagues with arguments and keeping the dialogue constructive.

• 
finding the information yourself and knowing when to escalate.

• 
keeping project management agile, with the minimum structure that makes it work.

• 
working with a risk until it is reduced, once you have identified it.

• 
involving busy colleagues firmly and kindly, so they like working with you.

What you need to bring:

• 
Either a relevant degree in business administration, finance, economics, engineering management or a related field, or equivalent experience, and at least five years of relevant experience or a strong track record of cross-functional business projects.

• 
Basic project management skills, including stakeholder management and risk assessment, gained through education or practice.

•

About the role

We are looking for a Senior Newbuilding Manager to take commercial ownership of complex newbuilding and vessel investment projects across their full lifecycle, from initial business case and market engagement through contracting, construction and delivery.

This is a senior commercial role requiring strong judgement, negotiation capability and the ability to navigate high-value, complex investment decisions in a global environment. You will work closely with Fleet Technology, Network Strategy, Chartering, Vessel Portfolio Management, Finance, Treasury, Legal and other key functions to ensure projects deliver the right balance of commercial value, contractual protection, technical requirements and long-term value.

Beyond individual newbuilding projects, you will provide senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage agenda, supporting transactions such as sale and purchase (SnP), purchase options, sale and leaseback arrangements, newbuild for time charter and contract amendments.

Key responsibilities

• Lead commercial yard due diligence and counterparty assessments, including financial strength, risk and compliance, together with Finance, Treasury and Compliance.

• Act as the commercial contract owner throughout the project lifecycle, managing contractual milestones, payments, guarantees, options, claims and amendments.

• Coordinate cross-functional project teams and ensure high-quality, timely governance submissions, decision papers and management reporting.

• Provide flexible senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage portfolio during peak periods, including SnP transactions, purchase options, sale and leaseback projects, newbuild for time charter and contractual amendments.

• Monitor shipyard capacity, pricing, market dynamics and competitor activity, translating market intelligence into actionable commercial analysis and recommendations.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with key shipyards, shipbrokers, OEMs, advisers and internal stakeholders.

• Contribute to consistent commercial processes, knowledge sharing and lessons learned across the Newbuilding team.

• Work closely with fellow Senior Newbuilding Managers, providing support and project coverage as portfolio priorities and workloads evolve.

• Identify and escalate material commercial exposures and decisions outside agreed mandate to the Head of Newbuilding, while maintaining ownership and momentum of agreed workstreams through completion.

Who we are looking for

You are a commercially strong shipping professional who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You are comfortable taking ownership of significant commercial commitments, challenging assumptions and navigating complex negotiations involving multiple internal and external stakeholders.

You bring:

• Significant commercial experience within shipping, vessel investment, newbuilding, sale and purchase, or a comparable capital-intensive industry.

• Proven experience leading complex commercial negotiations and managing high-value contractual commitments within defined mandates.

• Strong commercial judgement and the ability to balance price, vessel specification, delivery schedule, contractual risk and long-term value.

• Experience developing investment cases and translating complex commercial considerations into clear recommendations for senior management.

• A strong track record in tendering and contracting, combined with a solid understanding of key financial indicators including CAPEX, cash flows and total cost of ownership.

• The ability to manage several complex projects simultaneously and respond effectively to changing priorities and periods of high workload.

• Strong stakeholder management skills and experience working across multiple functions in a global, matrix organisation.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage confidently at senior levels.

• A good understanding of vessel specifications and maritime technology.

• Experience working with Asian shipyards is considered a strong advantage.

• A high degree of ownership, commercial integrity and attention to detail.

What success looks like

Success in this role will be measured through:

• Commercial value and contractual protection secured across assigned investments and projects.

• Quality and timeliness of investment recommendations, decision papers and governance submissions.

• Delivery within approved cost, schedule, mandate and contractual parameters.

• Effective management of commercial risks, options, milestones and contractual deadlines.

You will play an important role in ensuring that major vessel investments are commercially robust, well governed and positioned to create long-term value, while strengthening our ability to engage strategically with the global shipyard market.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in quantitative genetics and genomics with a focus on inbreeding depression and genetic diversity management
jobs.employer_name: Center for Kvantitativ Genetik og Genomforskning
jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for an exciting two-year postdoctoral position in the field of quantitative genetics and genomics applied to inbreeding management in livestock populations. The primary focus of this position is to investigate the genetic bases of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position starting on 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible. 

Job description
This is an opportunity to integrate a top research environment and contribute to advancing the state of the art in inbreeding management, while working within a collaborative project involving key industry partners.

The overarching objective of the project is to quantify the impact of inbreeding depression load on economically important traits in dairy cattle breeds and to investigate whether recessive variants contributing to inbreeding depression segregate in genomic regions experiencing rapid accumulation of inbreeding. Particular attention will be given to regions surrounding monogenetic traits (e.g. polled locus, milk caseins) which have been subjected to strong selection pressure in recent years.

You will apply state-of-the-art quantitative genetic and genomic modelling approaches to evaluate the effect of inbreeding depression on a broad range of production and functional traits recorded in dairy cattle populations. To support these analyses, you will have access to extensive databases containing phenotypic records routinely collected on farm, as well as large-scale pedigree and SNP genomic datasets currently used in genomic evaluations. High-density SNP genotyping and whole-genome sequence data will also be available to search for causal variants and more finely describe the genetic architecture of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle. Ultimately, the project aims to incorporate these findings into practical mating software readily available to dairy farmers. Therefore, these activities will be carried out in close collaboration with industry partners to ensure practical implementation in the field. 

Within this position, the successful candidate will also have the opportunity to contribute to other research projects related to genetic diversity management and quantitative trait modelling across other livestock species. 

Your profile
• A Ph.D. in Quantitative Genetics, Population Genetics or similar.
• Good programming skills (R, Python or Julia)
• Experience in the use of software to estimate variance components is a plus (e.g. DMU, BLUPF90 or similar) 
• A team player and a good communicator
• A good track record of publication in international peer-reviewed journals
• Fluent in English (written and spoken)
Who we are
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and genomics at Aarhus University (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). We conduct basic and applied research in animal, plant, and human genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. Research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development and application on practical problems across species, in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strives for an excellent working environment, in which we value self-leadership, open communication, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

What we offer
The successful candidate will be offered: 

• An interdisciplinary environment, in which the candidate will be able to exchange across disciplines and diverse applications (livestock, plants and biomedicine).
• An international research environment characterized by collaboration, professionalism, commitment to diversity and inclusion.
• Computational resources, including access to the GenomeDK high-performance computing cluster.
• A healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment 

The primary place of work is C. F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000, Aarhus C (Denmark).

Contact information
For further information, please contact Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Alban Bouquet, +45 2070 2677, alban.bouquet@qgg.au.dk
Associate Professor Zexi Cai, +45 8715 7928, zexi.cai@qgg.au.dk

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.
