jobs.description:
Job Title: Seasonal Roasted Almond Maker & Sales Assistant – Lyngby Station

Do you love the warm scent of freshly roasted almonds, cozy holiday vibes, and chatting with happy customers? Join our team at Lyngby Station for the Christmas season!

We are looking for 1–2 energetic, friendly, and reliable seasonal workers to run our roasted almond stall at Lyngby Station in Kongens Lyngby. The position starts immediately and runs all the way up to December 23, 2026.

Your Responsibilities

As our almond maker (mandelbrænder), you will be the face of the stall, spreading holiday cheer while serving delicious, warm treats to commuters, students, and local shoppers. Your daily tasks will include:

• 
Roasting and preparing candied almonds in our kettle (full training is provided).

• 
Greeting customers with a big smile, handing out samples, and handling payments.

• 
Keeping the stall and workspace clean, tidy, and hygienic throughout the day.

• 
Restocking almonds, sugar, cones, and packaging as needed.

What We Are Looking For

• 
Outgoing and service-minded: You enjoy talking to people and creating a welcoming atmosphere.

• 
Reliable and independent: You show up on time and can manage the stall smoothly on your own, even during busy rush hours.

• 
Comfortable working outdoors: Since this is an outdoor stall, it can get quite cold during the winter months, so you must be prepared to dress warmly (though the warm kettle helps!).

• 
Hygiene-conscious: You take pride in keeping a clean food-handling area.

• 
Age 18 or older: Required due to working with hot kettles and heating equipment.

• 
Previous experience in retail, customer service, or food stalls is a plus, but not required – a positive attitude and big smile are what matter most!

• 
English speakers are very welcome!

What We Offer

• 
Full hands-on training: We will teach you everything you need to know about roasting the perfect batch of almonds safely.

Cozy work environment: Work right in the heart of the Christmas spirit at a busy and lively station.

• 
Flexible scheduling: Both full-time and part-time shifts are available, making it ideal as a seasonal job alongside studies or other commitments.

Practical Details

• 
Location: Lyngby Station, 2800 Kongens Lyngby

• 
Period: Immediate start until December 23, 2026

• 
Opening & Working Hours:

• 
Monday – Friday: 10:30 – 18:30

• 
Saturday: 10:00 – 17:00

• 
Sunday: Optional / as agreed

• 
Please note: As this is an outdoor stall, opening hours and shifts are subject to weather conditions.

How to Apply

We conduct interviews on an ongoing basis and will hire as soon as we find the right candidate, so do not wait to reach out!

Send a brief application or a few lines about yourself to s@lles.dk or call/text Alexander at 60 14 50 50.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor at the Department of Public Health
jobs.description:
The Department of Public Health at the Faculty of Health, Aarhus University, invites applications for a full-time position as Associate Professor with a research and teaching profile in the area of complex interventions. The expected starting date is February 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is a three-year position that expires on January 31st, 2030.

About the Department
The Department of Public Health is a research-intensive environment dedicated to advancing scientific knowledge and developing applied solutions to major public health challenges. Our research spans theoretical, basic, and applied sciences, with the shared ambition of generating impactful knowledge and improving population health. Academic excellence is at the core of everything we do. We are committed to conducting rigorous and innovative research and delivering high-quality teaching. We teach across public health, sport science, health science, nursing science, related methodological disciplines, and the medical degree programme.

Rooted in our respective disciplines, we foster interdisciplinary collaboration to strengthen research, education and innovation. We are equally committed to cultivating a healthy and supportive workplace characterised by open dialogue, mutual respect and an informal atmosphere. We believe that academic excellence and personal well-being are mutually reinforcing and essential to long-term success.
You can read more about the department here and about the faculty here.

Your job responsibilities
As an Associate Professor of Public Health, you will contribute to the department’s research and teaching environment and to the faculty’s overall research strategy. You will contribute to the development of the department both individually and in collaboration with others via your research of high international quality. You ensure that your teaching maintains a high academic and didactic standard. You possess professional collaborative skills and a broad academic network which you are able to bring into play in your contribution to the academic development of Aarhus University and its profile both nationally and internationally. 

Your primary responsibilities will include:

• Conducting and publishing research of high international quality, including in leading journals and with leading publishers within your field.
• Developing your research profile and contributing to the department's objectives, including raising research external funding for your research projects.
• Teaching and supervising students at Bachelor's and Master's level and contributing to the continued development of innovative teaching activities.
• Participating in the supervision of PhD students and contributing to the faculty's PhD courses.
• Disseminating research findings to academic audiences, stakeholders, and the wider public.
You will report to the Head of Department Michael Baggesen Klitagaard.

Your competences 
You have established yourself as a recognised researcher within your field and can document research and teaching qualifications at a high international level. You have a well-developed international network, experience in attracting significant external research funding from national and international funding bodies, and clear potential and motivation to establish yourself as a research leader, to establish your own research group, and to consolidate an independent research agenda. In the assessment process, emphasis will be placed on experience gained through employment, visiting appointments, or extended research stays at recognised universities or research institutions outside the candidate's primary institution.

Your personal qualities include the ability to build trust-based relationships with colleagues, students, and external partners. As a teacher, you communicate current and relevant knowledge in a clear, engaging, and inspiring manner. As a supervisor, you are professional, inclusive, and supportive. You value collaboration and contribute positively to the collegial culture that characterises the Department of Public Health, the Faculty of Health Sciences, and Aarhus University more broadly. You are motivated to contribute to the department's continued development and to help maintain an inclusive, supportive, and high-performing work environment.

We expect you to be fluent in oral and written English. International applicants are expected to learn Danish, and Aarhus University arranges Danish teaching. 

In order to be assessed as qualified for an Associate Professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Shortlisting will be applied as part of the assessment process.

Questions about the position
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Head of Department Michael Baggesen Klitgaard tel.: (+45) 4022 7649. Your place of work will be the Department of Public Health, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. 

Terms of employment
• Appointment as an associate professor requires research and teaching qualifications at the level that can be achieved through the satisfactory completion of a period of appointment as an assistant professor, but may also be obtained in other ways.
• The applicant is required to have completed a university pedagogical programme or an equivalent programme.
• Further information on the appointment procedure can be found in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
• The appointment is in accordance with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (Akademikerne).
• Remuneration is in accordance with the above, and the Salary agreement catalogue for staff at Health.
• The yearly base salary for a fulltime associate professor is DKK 706.233,06 (including a position related supplement, a pre-agreed associate professor supplememt and pension (18.07%)). Additional supplement(s) can be negotiated dependent on experience, special qualifications and performance of special functions. Authorisation supplement(s) will be granted, if relevant for the position. Your local eligible trade union representative at Aarhus University negotiates your salary on your behalf.
• Researchers recruited from abroad are offered a special researcher tax scheme with a lower tax rate.
• Travel and moving expenses may be covered according to the employee in question and, to a limited extent, the accompanying family.
• Further information on qualification requirements and job description can be found in the Ministerial order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities.
Application
Your application must include the following:

• Motivated application
• Curriculum Vitae
• Diploma
• Template for applicant - associate professor
• A list of publications
• A teaching portfolio. We refer to Guideline on the use of teaching portfolios
• The five publications stated as the most important in the 'Template for applicant - associate professor' must be submitted
• Research plan, which is part of the 'Template to applicant - associate professor' can be uploaded separately (optional)
• Coauthor statement(s) can be uploaded (optional)
• References/recommendations can be uploaded separately in the e-recruitment system (optional)
We refer to the faculty’s Guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

International applicant?
Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including assistance with relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about the International Staff Office and the range of services here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.occupation: Laboratory Technician at NIVI Research Center
jobs.description:
The research group of Associate Professor Stephan Brouwer is looking for an engaged laboratory technician with experience in molecular biology, immunology, mammalian cell culture, and preferably with experience in BSL2/GMO-2 practices and research. The position is permanent and open for appointment from 1 March 2027.

  About us
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI), launched in December 2023, has a unique mission to harness airway immunity through innovative vaccine research and development to prevent airborne epidemics. NIVI has two parts:

  · NIVI Research Center (NIVI-R): A state-of-the-art research center anchored to the University of Copenhagen, Department of Immunology and Microbiology (www.isim.ku.dk).

  · NIVI Development (NIVI-D): A company that focuses on translational sciences and advancing vaccine development.

  NIVI-R conducts scientific research, while NIVI-D works to quickly turn that research into new vaccine candidates. NIVI-D accelerates clinical trials (phases 1 and 2) and ensures a smooth transition to partners for later stages of development.

  By connecting science, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory processes, and product development, NIVI aims to streamline the journey from research to real-world vaccines.

  Your tasks
 As part of a newly established research center, you will contribute to the setup and development of a completely new laboratory. This will include assisting with laboratory organization, implementation of workflows and procedures, inventory management systems, and establishing best practices for laboratory operations. You will work closely with the other laboratory technicians and scientific staff within NIVI-R to create a well-functioning research environment while helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the laboratory.

  As the laboratory technician, you will carry out several routine laboratory tasks; including maintenance of mammalian cell lines, molecular biology protocols (e.g., Protein purification, IVT-mRNA synthesis, DNA and RNA extraction/purification, Western-Blot/SDS-PAGE, PCR, qRT-PCR), Immunological assays (e.g. ELISA/Luminex, Neutralization assay, Flow cytometry), preparation of laboratory reagents, and other daily lab routines.

  You will also participate in various research projects that involve the development of vaccines and the characterization of vaccine responses, and close collaboration with the group’s scientists.

  The following will also be part of the role:

   	
• Documenting all laboratory work accurately using electronic lab notebooks. 	
• Monitoring laboratory stocks and ensuring timely replenishment. 	
• Organizing the laboratory and related space to be a clean, safe, and functional environment.   Profile
 Essential experience and skills:

  We are looking for someone with experience in molecular biology techniques (e.g., PCR, western blot, DNA/RNA work), mammalian cell culture (e.g., maintaining, freezing, and characterizing cell lines), and immunologic assays (ELISA, Flowcytometry).

   	
• A degree as a laboratory technician (Academy Profession degree or similar) is required. 	
• You must be good at working independently and organized, and be self-motivated 	
• Have good interpersonal and communication skills, both in Danish and English; spoken and written   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Experience with laboratory research in (BSL-2/GMO-2) labs. 	
• Experience with immunological assays: Proficiency in techniques such as ELISA/Luminex, Western Blotting, or Flow Cytometry (FACS) to support vaccine efficacy studies. 	
• Experience with cell culture, routine mycoplasma testing, and the validation of sterile reagents and media. 	
• Experience in animal research (active FELSA/ABD certification).   Terms of salary and employment
 Your employment will be at NIVI Research Center, Department of Immunology and Microbiology, University of Copenhagen. The position is full-time (37 hours per week), permanent, and is open for appointment from 1 March 2027.

  Employment as laboratory technician will be in accordance with the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and OAO/HK STAT. The position is placed in salary group 4.

  Depending on qualifications a supplement may be negotiated.

  Question
 For further information please contact Stephan Brouwer: stephan.brouwer@sund.ku.dk

  Application
 Please submit your application in English by clicking "Apply for position" below. 

  The application should consist of the following:

   	
• Letter of application/motivation (max 1 page) 	
• Your CV incl. education, a list of laboratory skills/techniques, previous employments, language skills and other relevant skills 	
• Copy of relevant certificate/diploma   Deadline for application is 9 December 2027, 23.59 CET.
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

   

  University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, nationality, race, religion or sexual orientation. Appointment will be based on merit alone

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology invites applications for a postdoctoral position in Cognitive Computational Neuroscience and Human Movement Perception by 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  The position is a fixed-term position for 30 months/2.5 years.
 
 Introduction
 The postdoc will be part of a project entitled "Mapping Experience of Action: Redefining Theories of Consciousness" funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. The project is headed by Professor Thor Grünbaum and Associate Professor in Cognitive Psychology Mark Schram Christensen Department of Psychology, University of Copenhagen.

  This interdisciplinary project develops a novel scientific approach to the study of consciousness by investigating conscious experiences of movement. Combining psychophysical experiments, computational modelling, and philosophical analysis, it examines how bodily and neural signals contribute to movement awareness. The project aims to advance our understanding of consciousness and critically evaluate leading neuroscientific theories of conscious experience.

  Applicants are asked to develop a short project description for the postdoc. It is critical that applicants are able to situate their project and research plan within the framework of the overall project. It is a requirement that applicants request from Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen (markc@psy.ku.dk) the original project proposal prior to submitting the application.

  Candidates with various background may be considered for the position. Examples of relevant backgrounds are PhDs in cognitive (neuro)science, computational neuroscience, cognitive modelling, biomedical engineering, sports science with a focus on behavioural neuroscience, or similar. The candidates are expected to have strong skills in cognitive modelling, experimental design, data handling and data analysis documented in relevant scientific publications.

  The postdoc will be working in close collaboration with the other project members which has academic backgrounds in cognitive neuroscience and philosophy, and student assistants with background in Cognitive Data Science.  The position will be placed in the Cognition, Intention and Action research group, part of the Section for Cognition and Brain Sciences, Department of Psychology.  It is expected that the successful candidate will be present, part of the team, and take part in the activities in the Lab on a daily basis.
 
 Duties and Responsibilities
 The primary focus of the postdoctoral position will be on research within the main project. However, a certain amount of teaching obligations may be required. Additional tasks beyond research and teaching may also be considered, but to a limited extent. The university will determine the final scope of the various responsibilities, and the emphasis may vary over time.
 
 Qualification Requirements 
 Appointment as a postdoctoral researcher requires research qualifications at a level at least equivalent to those obtained through the satisfactory completion of a PhD programme within the relevant field.

  Strong skills in data handling and analysis are crucial, and experience with cognitive/computational modelling within human behavioural science or neuroscience is key to the content of the project. 

  You can find further information about the qualification requirements for postdoctoral positions here: Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities (In Danish only).

  You can also find further information about the postdoctoral position on our English webpage on career paths for early‑career researchers at the University of Copenhagen: Career at The University of Copenhagen.
 
 Strategy of the Faculty of the Social Sciences
 The Department of Psychology is part of the Faculty of the Social Sciences. The faculty is a successful academic community that strives to put knowledge into action by:

  Engaging partners in the co-creation of knowledge, learning and social change.

  Empowering our students to become reflective and responsible citizens who have the vision, the knowledge and the competences to change society for the better.

  Energising global, European and Danish communities of knowledge by innovating research methodologies and by research findings with impact.

  For more on the faculty’s strategy, please see: Strategy for the Faculty of Social Science.
 
 Assessment Criteria
 Applicants will primarily be assessed in relation to their research qualifications, including their publications, ability to conduct independent research and participate in research collaborations, and their experience of research management. In addition, the applicant’s research plan and research potential will be assessed in relation to the overall project described above.

  Teaching qualifications are not a requirement.
 
 Application
 Please submit your application online. To apply, please click on the “Apply now” icon at the bottom of this page. The application must be written in English, and include the following attachments in PDF or Word format:

   	
• CV (max. 3 pages) 	
• Cover letter including the preferred starting date (max. 1 page) 	
• Documentation of qualifications (exam certificates and PhD diploma) 	
• Complete publication list (attached publications must be marked with an asterisk). The list must be structured systematically and divided into the following categories: 	 		
• Peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Monographs and anthologies 		
• Articles in journals 		
• Book chapters/anthology contributions, etc. 		
• Non-peer-reviewed publications: 		
• Publications disseminating research findings, etc.
 		  	 	 	
• You can attach a maximum of 3 publications. The publication dates must be clearly marked on the list. The selected publications must be uploaded as attachments and numbered 1-3.
 	  	
• A short project description (max. 2 pages). 	 		
• The description should outline your ideas for the postdoc project situated in the state-of-the-art research in the field of the project. It should include your proposals for specific types of experimental and modelling approaches that you envision to contribute with to the project. The description must not exceed 2 standard pages, corresponding to approx. 4,800 characters (including title, punctuation, figures, footnotes and references, but excluding bibliography). A substantial breach of this will result in the application being excluded from consideration.
 		  	 	 	
• Research plan (max. 2 pages) 	 		
• The plan should include a brief account of previous research, current research projects, and a forward-looking outline of planned research contribution over the coming years. This may include specific references to the project proposals funded by Independent Research Foundation Denmark, and how the candidate expect to contribute to the project at large. 	 	   
 Salary and Terms of Employment
 Terms of appointment and salary will be in accordance with an agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). The salary range for postdoctoral positions starts at DKK 39,000/approximately EUR 5,100 + an 18.07 % pension contribution. It is possible to negotiate salary supplements on an annual basis.
 
 Recruitment Process
 After the application deadline, the Head of Department will consider advice from the appointment committee and select applicants for assessment. All applicants will be notified whether they have been shortlisted. The Head of Department will set up an expert assessment committee to assess the shortlisted applications. The selected applicants will be informed who is serving on the committee. Each shortlisted applicant will be offered the opportunity to comment on the committee’s assessment before the appointment is announced.

  You can find further information on our recruitment process at: Recruitment process.
 
 International Applicant?
 The University of Copenhagen offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including support before and during your relocation and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information about our services at: For international researchers at the University of Copenhagen.
 
 An Equal Opportunity Workplace
 The University of Copenhagen is committed in its pursuit of academic excellence to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc. To learn more about our diverse workplace and our participation in the HRS4R HR Excellence in Research, please visit HR Excellence in Research.
 
 Contact Information
 For additional information about the position, please contact Associate Professor Mark Schram Christensen at email markc@psy.ku.dk or phone +45-3532 2448.

  For more Information about the recruitment process, please contact HR South at hr-soendre@adm.ku.dk. Please refer to ID number: 211-2675/26-2I

  Any applications or additional material submitted after the deadline will not be considered. However, changes may be made to the submitted application right up until the deadline.

jobs.occupation: Regional Director – Nordics & Baltics | Successful International Group
jobs.description:

Our client is a successful international distributor of specialty chemicals, with operations across a number of international markets and a presence in more than 20 countries.

The group holds a strong international position and is currently working to strengthen its presence and drive further growth in the Nordics and Baltics.

Your primary task will be to set the strategic direction and ensure the continuous development of the business. You will play a central role in translating the group's ambitions into concrete goals and results, as well as creating the organizational and commercial framework for future growth.

In close collaboration with the Sales Director, you will develop and implement the strategy for the region and ensure progress through clear leadership, prioritization, and strong cooperation with the rest of the organization.

The role requires the ability to deliver results through others while maintaining a strategic overview and an understanding of the business's commercial opportunities.

About You

You have leadership experience and a strong strategic understanding. You possess the ability to gain commitment, set direction, and develop an organization through clear leadership, involvement, and trust.

You do not necessarily need to have held a director-level position previously. The most important thing is that you have the ambition, the strategic overview, and the ability to take overall responsibility for a business unit's development and results.

We imagine that you:

• Have experience in commercial leadership and organizational development, including developing and implementing strategies and translating them into concrete goals and results.
• Are a clear leader who sets direction, builds engagement, and ensures progress.

You can be based anywhere in Denmark, as there are good opportunities for remote work. If you live outside daily commuting distance, you will be expected to work from the office approximately once a week.

Application

We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to upload your CV as soon as possible.

Please upload your CV and, optionally, a short cover letter using the Apply for the Position button.

The job advertisement will be removed once the position has been filled.

All inquiries and applications will, of course, be treated confidentially.

Want to Know More?

You are welcome to contact Carsten Lindberg Hartvigsen by phone at +45 41 81 34 00 if you have any questions regarding the position.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in computational multimodal data integration for crop stress regulatory networks
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applications for a postdoctoral position in computational biology, focused on the integration of multimodal single-cell, epigenomic and literature-derived data into gene regulatory networks. The position is financed by the Novo Nordisk Foundation through the Ascending Investigator grant “Accelerating crop resilience with AI-enabled gene function prediction and stress regulatory networks” (NNF26OC0113093).

  The position is for 3 years. Start date is 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project  Climate-driven heat and drought increasingly destabilise crop yields, yet the gene regulatory networks that govern stress responses in crops remain poorly resolved, because they have mostly been measured in whole organs. This programme will resolve them at the level of individual cell types and their cis-regulatory elements, in four major Nordic crops – rapeseed, potato, wheat and barley – under heat, drought and the two combined.

  The postdoc is the computational integrator of the grant: the person who turns the data the grant generates into regulatory networks. The single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data are generated by a PhD student and a technician on the group’s 10x Genomics platform; your job begins when the sequencing reads arrive. This is a purely computational position – no wet-lab work is involved. Concretely, you will:

   	
• Build the analysis backbone for the single-cell stress atlases: quality control, doublet and ambient-RNA handling, integration across four species, three stress conditions, three organs and three time points, and cell-type annotation using conserved markers – with pipelines the PhD students can run and extend. 	
• Integrate the modalities into gene regulatory networks. Infer transcription factor–target relationships by extending the group’s TEA-GCN method to single-cell data; identify cis-regulatory elements from accessible chromatin using known motifs, de novo motif discovery, convolutional neural networks and DNA language models; and link the two into TF–CRE–target triplets. Benchmark against SCENIC+, MAESTRO and related frameworks and adopt what works. 	
• Rank regulatory relationships by conservation across the four crops to obtain a high-confidence core, and develop the comparative methods this needs. 	
• Connect the networks to the rest of the grant’s work: to the group’s literature-derived knowledge graph and gene-function predictions, and to the open web platform through which the grant’s data, models and predictions are shared, so that regulators and targets can be prioritised for validation in rapeseed with traceable evidence. 	
• Co-supervise and train the PhD students and master’s students on the computational side, and help build the group’s single-cell and multi-omics analysis capacity.   Who are we looking for?  You hold a PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, genomics, plant molecular biology or a related field, and you have analysed single-cell or other high-dimensional omics data independently. We are looking for a computational scientist who can take raw multimodal data through to a defensible biological claim, and who is comfortable working alongside the experimentalists who generate the data.

  Essential:

   	
• A PhD (or a thesis submitted by the start date) in a relevant field 	
• Documented experience with the analysis of single-cell RNA-seq and/or single-cell ATAC-seq data, or with comparable multimodal genomic data 	
• Strong programming proficiency in Python or R, and experience building reproducible analysis workflows (e.g. Snakemake/Nextflow, version control, containers) 	
• A publication record demonstrating independent scientific contribution 	
• Excellent written and spoken English   Advantageous:

   	
• Experience with gene regulatory network inference, motif analysis or cis-regulatory element prediction 	
• Experience with deep-learning models of regulatory sequence (CNNs, DNA language models) or with graph-based methods 	
• Experience with comparative or cross-species analysis of transcriptomic data 	
• Experience with plant abiotic stress biology or with crop species 	
• Experience co-supervising students   Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  The postdoc will work closely with the two PhD students funded by the same grant (literature-derived knowledge graphs and gene-function prediction; single-cell stress experiments) and with collaborators Prof. Ryan Lister (University of Western Australia, multimodal single-cell genomics) and Prof. Zoran Nikoloski (University of Potsdam, regulatory network inference).

  The group is part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located on the Frederiksberg Campus in Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Computational resources include a 196-thread/1 TB RAM workstation and guaranteed GPU access through LUMI and uCloud.

  Inquiries about the position can be made to Associate Professor Marek Mutwil, mutwil@plen.ku.dk.

  Terms of employment  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  Application procedure  Your application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent). If the PhD is not yet awarded, documentation of the expected date of the defence 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reproductions of up to three particularly relevant papers 	
• Research statement (max. two pages) describing your previous work and how you would approach the multimodal integration and network-inference tasks described above 	
• Names and contact details of two or three references   The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Application deadline: The deadline for applications is 31 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorised recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. Afterwards an assessment committee will be appointed to evaluate the selected applications. The applicants will be notified of the composition of the committee and the final selection of a successful candidate will be made by the Head of Department, based on the recommendations of the assessment committee and the interview committee. The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in February 2027.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Single-Molecule and Single-Vesicle Imaging of Neurodegenerative Diseases
jobs.description:
Are you interested in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases using cutting-edge fluorescence microscopy and single-vesicle imaging? Do you want to contribute to uncovering how protein aggregation and membrane interactions drive the development of Parkinson's disease? Then the Department of Chemistry at Aarhus University invites you to apply for a postdoctoral position within the ERC Starting Grant-funded project SPARTA.

We are seeking a highly motivated and ambitious postdoctoral researcher to join our research group at the Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University. The successful candidate will develop and apply advanced single-molecule and single-vesicle imaging approaches to investigate the dynamic interactions between α-synuclein oligomers and biological membranes, aiming to uncover fundamental mechanisms of neurodegeneration and contribute to the development of novel strategies for early disease detection.

This is a fixed-term 2-year position starting on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The successful candidate will join the ERC Starting Grant-funded project SPARTA, aiming to uncover the molecular mechanisms of α-synuclein aggregation and membrane interactions in Parkinson’s disease.

The position will primarily involve:

• Investigating α-synuclein aggregation and interactions with lipid membranes.
• Developing and applying advanced single-molecule and single-vesicle fluorescence microscopy.
• Exploring how membrane composition and properties influence protein aggregation and membrane disruption.
• Performing quantitative image analysis and computational data analysis.
• Developing novel single-vesicle assays for studying neurodegenerative disease mechanisms.
The research will be conducted in an interdisciplinary environment at the Department of Chemistry, Aarhus University, in collaboration with researchers in biophysics, molecular biology, and neuroscience.

Your profile
We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a strong background in experimental biophysics and quantitative fluorescence microscopy.

The ideal candidate should have:

• A PhD in nanoscience, biophysics, biochemistry, or a related field.
• Experience with single-molecule or single-vesicle fluorescence microscopy, preferably TIRF microscopy.
• Experience with lipid membranes, liposomes, or protein–membrane interactions.
• Strong skills in quantitative image analysis and data processing, preferably using Python.
• Experience in scientific publishing and communicating research findings.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment.
• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
• Experience with α-synuclein, protein aggregation, or neurodegenerative diseases is an advantage but not a requirement.
We value scientific curiosity, creativity, independence, and a collaborative mindset.

Who we are
The Department of Chemistry at Aarhus University offers an international and interdisciplinary research environment with state-of-the-art facilities and strong collaborations.

The successful candidate will join the research group led by Assistant Professor Mette Galsgaard Malle, focusing on single-molecule and single-vesicle imaging to understand molecular interactions and disease mechanisms.

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is the Department of Chemistry, Gustav Wieds Vej 14, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Assistant Professor Mette Galsgaard Malle, malle@inano.au.dk.

Deadline 
All applications must be received no later than 2 December 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. jobs.occupation: Operational Project Coordinator for International Collaboration on Quantum Education
jobs.description:
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is expanding its

  talented and international team to add to its cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, we are running an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that drives research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to quantum algorithms and applications. The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

   

  Start date is 15/1 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

   

  The project: The NQCP Education and Workforce development (E&W) group is establishing an international collaboration on technology driven quantum education.  The collaboration will use the advances in quantum technology to train students through BSc and MSc studies. The mission is to establish a quantum technology ready workforce and ensure the long-term return on the large-scale investments in quantum technologies for the benefit of society.

   

  Responsibilities: The operational project coordinator will be an integral part of the international collaboration, facilitating the steering group, managing the operational workflow, and leading the logistical execution across partner hubs. In addition, the role includes coordinating mobility, the transfer of best practice and ensuring ongoing evaluation.

  We are looking for the following qualifications: NQCP E&W seeks an experienced coordinator. We imagine that you have a track-record of coordinating international consortia and have an innovative approach to international educational cooperation. You thrive in an ambitious and collaborative working environment and enjoy being a part of a large team with a common mission. You engage naturally with colleagues, students and visitors and have a deep desire to extend your passion for quantum science and technology to the coming generations of students. 

  Why Us?  

  Joining NQCP now, you will get involved in a well-established and ambitious programme, which offers excellent opportunities to build a career in advancing quantum computing. We want to make Denmark a world leader in quantum research, and we hope to attract people from all over the world.

  Life in Denmark is supported with strong social services (free universal healthcare, free/subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care institutions and excellent public schools). Our work culture is very egalitarian and prioritises work life balance. Dual career families are the norm, and workplaces offer flexibility to support everyone in having both an exciting career and good family time. Danish cities are known for having excellent infrastructure, for example through widespread bike path networks. We can also offer a thriving food-scene, excellent museums, and beautiful natural scenery.

  Terms of salary and employment

  The employment and salary are made in accordance with the Circular on the Collective Agreement concerning academics in the state sector concluded between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

   

  Employment will be as academic officer or special consultant. The salary is based on seniority. Negotiation for salary supplement is possible. The working hours are 18.5 hours per week on average and the working hours are flexible. The position is for 4 years.

   

  Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance.

   

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Curriculum vitae, including a short cover letter, with information about your education, experience and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Motivation letter (max. one page) 	
• Diplomas (Masters degree or equivalent)    

  Deadline for applications: 25 November 2026

  Further information 

  For further information please Kim Splittorff, split@nbi.ku.dk.

   

  The Faculty of Science at the University of Copenhagen – or SCIENCE – is Denmark's largest science research and education institution with 4,000 employees and 9,700 Bachelor and master students in 12 departments. The faculty has an annual budget of DKK 3 billion. 

  Learn more about The Faculty of Science at www.science.ku.dk 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/. 

   

  The University of Copenhagen wish to reflect the diversity of society and encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of personal background.

PhD Project in studying the molecular basis of flower color and patterns

  The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in AI-driven knowledge extraction for plant metabolism. The project is part of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars (Grant Agreement No. 101312557), funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. Stripes&Stars trains ten doctoral candidates across eight European countries in modern breeding of ornamental and fruit crops, using flower and fruit colour – anthocyanins and other flavonoids in petunia, calibrachoa, poinsettia and bilberry – as its scientific showcase. The network brings together seven beneficiaries (TU Wien, Klemm + Sohn, Università Campus Bio-Medico, Utrecht University, University of Copenhagen, Lantana Bio, UiT The Arctic University of Norway) and associated partners at Galab, the University of Helsinki, the University of Amsterdam and Chulalongkorn University.

  The project

  Anthocyanins represents one of the most widespread plant pigments giving rise to the diverse colors to fruits, vegetables and flowers. Flower pigmentation is a critical trait guiding the attraction of pollinators. Some flowers develop remarkable patterns through spatial  accumulation of anthcocyanins in distinct and repetitive patterns. Yet, we still don’t know the molecular mechanisms governing flower patterns

  You will:

  -Develop a protoplast pipeline for isolation of cells derived from distinct flower petal patterns

  -Map the proteomes of different cell types

  -Employ biotin-dependent proximity labeling to map the protein networks of the anthocyanin biosynthetic pathway.

  -Elucidate regulatory proteins facilitating anthocyanin pathway assembly and disassembly.

  Planned Secondments: Klemm (1 month) to sample plant material from the flower diversity panel. TU Wien (Prof. Heidi Halbwirth, 2 months) for protoplast optimization for cell type protomics profiling and expression of fusion constructs. Lantana Bio (3 months) to translate findings to optimize a bioproduction process of tailored anthocyanins in yeast. You will also take part in the network’s training programme of schools, workshops and transferable-skills courses.

  Who are we looking for

  We are looking for candidates within the fields of Biology, chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology or biotechnology, who wish to join a dynamic research group working on plant biochemistry and biosynthesis of specialized metabolites. Applicants can have a background in elucidation/characterization of metabolic pathways, plant molecular biology/biochemistry, metabolic engineering or plant transformation.

  Important scientific values

  We will specifically select candidates displaying an open mindset, ability to collaborate within research teams and contribute to a healthy work environment. The candidate is encouraged to communicate their research openly with a curiosity towards different viewpoints and disciplines.

  MSCA guidelines

  This position is subject to the eligibility rules of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks:

   	
• Mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. 	
• You must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment. 	
• You may be of any nationality.   Our group and research- and what do we offer

  The successful applicant will join Tomas Laursen and the Dynamic Metabolons Research Group, which specializes in the organization of biosynthetic pathways for production of bioactive compounds. We combine microscopy, metabolomics and proteomics with fundamental biochemistry to study biosynthesis of plant specialized metabolites from the single enzyme- to the whole plant level. 

  The Dynamic Metabolons research Group is a part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences, which hosts four Sections spanning from molecular biology to crop science and environmental chemistr. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern laboratories, plant growth facilities, and a metabolomics platform hosted within the Section. 

  The principal supervisor is Associate Professor Tomas Laursen, tola@plen.ku.dk. 

  The PhD programme 

  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the programme
 To be eligible for the PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. chemistry, biochemistry or molecular biology. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The terms of employment and salary are in accordance to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in PhD programme

   	
• Carry out an independent research project under supervision    	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in the research field 	
• Excellent English language skills   Application and Assessment Procedure

   Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application, including any preferences for working on biosynthesis or transport 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for BSc and MSc degrees and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If the latest degree has not been completed, please include a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records and a written statement from the institution or supervisor. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application deadline: 

  The deadline for applications is 31 January 2027, 23:59 GMT+1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified, whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. jobs.occupation: 2 PhD fellowships MSCA in AI-driven discovery of plant metabolic pathways
jobs.description:
The Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN) invites applicants for two PhD fellowships in AI-driven discovery of plant metabolic pathways – doctoral candidates DC7 and DC8 of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars. Both projects are part of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network Stripes&Stars (Grant Agreement No. 101312557), funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. Stripes&Stars trains ten doctoral candidates across eight European countries in modern breeding of ornamental and fruit crops, using flower and fruit colour – anthocyanins and other flavonoids in petunia, calibrachoa, poinsettia and bilberry – as its scientific showcase. The network brings together seven beneficiaries (TU Wien, Klemm + Sohn, Università Campus Bio-Medico, Utrecht University, University of Copenhagen, Lantana Bio, UiT The Arctic University of Norway) and associated partners at Galab, the University of Helsinki, the University of Amsterdam and Chulalongkorn University. The University of Copenhagen hosts the network’s two data-science doctoral candidates (DC7 and DC8), who together provide the computational backbone for predictive colour and specialised-metabolite engineering.

  Start dates: DC7 is expected to start 1 June 2027 (month 3 of the network) and DC8 1 January 2028 (month 10 of the network), or as soon as possible thereafter. Please state in your application which project you are applying for; you may apply for both.

  Project DC7: Knowledge graph construction for specialised metabolite pathways (Stripes&Stars WP4–5)  Flavonoids and anthocyanins colour petunia flowers and bilberry fruit, protect plants against UV light and stress, and attract pollinators – and roughly 20% of the carbon flux in plants passes through the flavonoid pathway. Yet knowledge of the enzymes, transporters and regulators that control which pigment accumulates where is scattered across tens of thousands of papers. This project will make that knowledge computable.  You will:

   	
• Use the PlantConnectome large-language-model pipeline to extract and interlink knowledge on enzymes, substrates, transporters, transcription factors, stresses and genetic modifications that regulate pigment and specialised-metabolite biosynthesis, from more than 70,000 publications, into the first comprehensive knowledge graph of plant specialised-metabolite pathways 	
• Extend the graph to environmental context – in particular how concurrent stresses (e.g. high light with heat or drought) reshape pigment and specialised-metabolite accumulation, and whether the regulators involved are shared across ornamental and fruit species 	
• Apply symbolic reasoning and link prediction (e.g. AnyBURL rule mining and graph neural networks) to infer missing pathway components and regulatory relationships, yielding testable hypotheses and engineering targets for the experimental partners 	
• Build an interactive, ChatGPT-like interface to the graph, so that consortium members and the wider community can retrieve complete, evidence-linked information on genes, enzymes, pathways and phenotypes 	
• Work closely with DC8 (network-based pathway prediction, also at UCPH) so that graph and expression evidence are integrated into one explainable framework   Secondments: TU Wien (Prof. Heidi Halbwirth, 3 months) to integrate graph predictions with enzyme characterisation and pigment pathway analysis, and Klemm + Sohn (Stuttgart, 2 months) to validate predicted targets in an applied breeding context. You will also take part in the network’s training programme of schools, workshops and transferable-skills courses.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of bioinformatics, computer science, data science or computational biology, or plant biochemistry with a strong computational interest. Experience with natural language processing, large language models, graph databases or knowledge-graph reasoning is an advantage. An interest in plant metabolism is essential; a formal background in it is not.

  Project DC8: Multi-omics co-expression networks for predicting novel metabolic pathways (Stripes&Stars WP4–5)  Which genes make a petunia petal purple, a poinsettia bract white, or a bilberry flesh blue? Many of the enzymes, transporters and regulators are still unknown, and the ones we know were found one at a time. This project will find them systematically from expression data.  You will:

   	
• Build advanced co-expression and regulatory networks from consortium and public RNA-seq data using the group’s TEA-GCN algorithm, which aggregates linear and non-linear correlations across conditions to yield condition-specific, explainable networks 	
• Integrate cell- and tissue-resolved expression, proteomic and epigenomic datasets to delineate the regulatory subnetworks that drive pigment and specialised-metabolite production 	
• Combine these networks with the DC7 knowledge graph and explore neurosymbolic reasoning – coupling learned graph representations (graph neural networks, knowledge-graph embeddings) with symbolic rules mined from the literature graph – to infer missing pathway members and regulators with explanations a biologist can check 	
• Predict and prioritise engineering targets (regulators, enzymes, environmental cues) for experimental validation by the network’s experimental partners, and follow how those predictions fare 	
• Consolidate network- and graph-based predictions into a shared resource for the consortium   Secondment: University of Amsterdam (Prof. Ronald Koes, 3 months) to integrate transcriptomic and epigenetic datasets from petunia. You will also take part in the network’s training programme of schools, workshops and transferable-skills courses.

  Who are we looking for?  We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science or data science, or plant biology with a strong quantitative interest. Experience with transcriptomics, network inference, graph machine learning or knowledge graphs is an advantage. An interest in plant metabolism is essential; a formal background in it is not.

  Eligibility and what we value  MSCA eligibility rules  This position is subject to the eligibility rules of the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks:

   	
• Mobility rule: you must not have resided or carried out your main activity (work, studies) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. 	
• You must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment. 	
• You may be of any nationality.   What we value  Coding experience is welcome but not required at entry – we teach it. What we cannot teach quickly, and therefore select for, is scientific judgment:

   	
• questioning data rather than accepting it – asking what was measured, how, and against which expectation 	
• noticing anomalies and treating them as information rather than noise 	
• organising several lines of investigation in parallel and knowing when to stop or redirect one 	
• connecting computational evidence to a concrete biological question 	
• changing your mind when the evidence changes   We are equally interested in candidates from biology who want to learn computation and candidates from computer science, physics or engineering who want to learn biology.

  Our group and research – and what do we offer?  The Mutwil group at PLEN works at the interface of comparative and evolutionary plant biology and AI-driven biological discovery. We build large cross-species gene expression atlases, comparative co-expression networks and knowledge graphs, and we use machine learning and large language models to turn the plant literature and omics archives into testable hypotheses. The group comprises several PhD students, postdocs and master’s students, and maintains a portfolio of widely used community resources under the .plant.tools domain, including PlantConnectome, CoNekt, diurnal.plant.tools and evorepro.plant.tools.

  The group is part of the Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. We are located on the Frederiksberg Campus in Copenhagen.

  We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment. Our research facilities include modern molecular biology laboratories, plant growth facilities and dedicated high-performance computing and GPU resources.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Marek Mutwil, Department of Plant and Environmental Sciences (PLEN), University of Copenhagen. E-mail: mutwil@plen.ku.dk.

  The PhD programme  A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Getting into a position on the PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the programme
 To be eligible for the PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. chemistry, biochemistry or molecular biology. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 
 Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The terms of employment and salary are in accordance to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programme   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project 	
• Complete the secondments and network-wide training activities of the Stripes&Stars Doctoral Network   We are looking for the following qualifications   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Programming experience (e.g. Python) is an advantage; strong analytical reasoning is essential 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience, e.g. with NLP, LLMs, knowledge graphs or graph machine learning 	
• Other relevant professional activities 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in making biological knowledge computable 	
• Good written and spoken English 	
• Fulfilment of the MSCA mobility and eligibility criteria stated above   Application and assessment procedure  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page), stating which project you are applying for (DC7, DC8, or both, in order of preference) and your motivation 	
• Written answers to the four questions below (max. 250 words each). You may use AI tools to help draft your answers; please say so if you do. The written answers are a starting point for the interview, where we will explore your reasoning in conversation. 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor and Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorised English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application questions

   	
• Research interest. Which biological question would you like to work on in this project, and what evidence would you need to answer it? 	
• Reading data. A gene has an expression value of 100 under control conditions, 200 under heat stress, 200 under drought, and 400 under heat and drought combined. What do you conclude, and what would you want to know before concluding it? 	
• Working in parallel. You have two weeks, a set of publicly available expression data, and a literature you do not yet know. How would you organise the two weeks, and what would you deliver at the end of each? 	
• Changing your mind. Describe a case where you believed something about a project or dataset and evidence made you revise it. What was the evidence?   Application deadline: The deadline for applications is 31 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process  After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment. The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held in February 2027.

  Questions  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the principal supervisor, Associate Professor Marek Mutwil (mutwil@plen.ku.dk).

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of Science is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Er du vores nye musikansvarlige i
Ungehuset Hampen?
Er du en dygtig musiker, der elsker at dele din passion med andre? Og har du lyst til
at gøre en forskel for unge gennem musikken?
Så er det måske dig, vi leder efter!
I Ungehuset Hampen søger vi en musikansvarlig, der har lyst til at skabe musikglæde,
udvikle unges musikalske evner og gøre vores musiklokale til et levende samlingspunkt for
unge mellem 13 og 18 år.
Vi søger en medarbejder til 5,75 timer om ugen fordelt på to vagter mandag-torsdag i
tidsrummet kl. 18.30-21.30.
Fællesskab, aktiviteter og udvikling
Ungehuset Hampen ligger centralt i Ølstykke i Egedal Kommune. Vi er et stort ungehus
med masser af liv, aktiviteter og muligheder for at udforske nye interesser og fællesskaber.
Hos os kan de unge blandt andet spille musik i vores øvelokale, danse i vores
dansestudie, dyrke sport, game, lave mad eller hænge ud med vennerne. Vi har også et
stort udeområde med blandt andet klatretårn og trampoliner.
Vi lægger stor vægt på de unges trivsel, udvikling og sociale fællesskaber. Vi ønsker at
skabe et sted, hvor alle føler sig velkomne, og hvor der er plads til at prøve sig frem,
udfolde sine interesser og opdage nye sider af sig selv.
Din rolle som musikansvarlig
Du bliver den, der hjælper de unge med at omsætte deres musikalske idéer til virkelighed.
Nogle kommer måske med erfaring og ambitioner, mens andre først lige er begyndt at
spille. Du skal kunne møde dem dér, hvor de er, og hjælpe dem med at udvikle sig – både
musikalsk og i samspillet med andre.
Dine opgaver bliver blandt andet at:
• Undervise og vejlede unge i rytmiske instrumenter som guitar, bas, trommer, sang og klaver.
• Skabe rammer for sammenspil, bands og andre musikalske fællesskaber.
• Arbejde struktureret med de unges musikalske udvikling og fastholde deres motivation.
• Gribe de unges idéer og hjælpe dem med at føre dem ud i livet.
• Bidrage til musikprojekter og indgå i det bredere musiknetværk i Ung Egedal.

Har du erfaring med musikproduktion, indspilning eller sangskrivning, er det et stort plus.
Vi forestiller os, at du…
• Spiller på mindst ét rytmisk instrument – og gerne flere.
• Har lyst til at lære fra dig og formidle din musikalske viden på en engagerende måde.
• Er imødekommende, nysgerrig og god til at skabe relationer til unge.
• Kan motivere unge med forskellige musikalske forudsætninger og ambitionsniveauer.
• Har lyst til at bidrage til livet i ungehuset og indimellem deltage i andre aktiviteter.
• Sætter pris på godt kollegaskab, samarbejde og et positivt arbejdsmiljø.
Det vigtigste er ikke, at du kan alt fra starten, men at du har en stærk musikalsk profil, lyst
til at dele din viden og mod på at skabe noget sammen med de unge.
Hvad kan vi tilbyde dig?
• En alsidig arbejdsplads med engagerede kolleger, der brænder for unge og deres
udvikling.
• Muligheden for at sætte dit eget præg på musikmiljøet i Hampen.
• Et stærkt kollegialt fællesskab og et godt arbejdsmiljø.
• En hverdag med plads til initiativ, kreativitet og nye idéer.
• Mulighed for at blive en del af større musikprojekter og samarbejder på tværs af Ung Egedal.

Ungehuset Hampen er en del af Ung Egedal, hvor vi samarbejder om at skabe
meningsfulde fritidstilbud og udviklingsmuligheder for unge i kommunen.

Arbejdstidspunkt: Kl. 18.30-21.30.
Arbejdssted: Ungehuset Hampen, Ølstykke, Egedal Kommune.
Ansøgningsfrist: Torsdag den 03. december 2026.
Samtaler: Torsdag d. 10. december 2026.
Opstart: Hurtigst muligt.
