jobs.occupation: Senior Store Operation & Retail Delivery Manager
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about driving operational excellence, improving business performance, and enabling retail teams to deliver outstanding results? Then we might have just the job for you at Specsavers.

Join Specsavers as our new Senior Store Operations & Retail Delivery Manager and play a key role in shaping operational performance, supporting retail transformation initiatives, and driving sustainable growth across Northern Europe.

Your role

As our Senior Store Operations & Retail Delivery Manager, you will be responsible for supporting the execution of strategic initiatives, operational plans, and performance improvement programmes across our Northern Europe retail business.

Working closely with the Director of Stores, Heads of Stores, Business Performance Managers, and Regional Relationship Managers, you will help create the conditions for stores to improve profitability, strengthen operational excellence, and deliver outstanding customer experiences.

You will act as a key link between regional field teams, support functions, and business leaders, ensuring that the right tools, frameworks, and initiatives are in place to support long-term business success. You are a strong collaborator who thrives in complex environments, enjoys working across functions, and is motivated by helping others achieve measurable business results.

Finally, you are ready an everyday where you combine working from home with being at the Northern European Support Office in Copenhagen along with frequent visits to the countries in the region.

Key responsibilities include:

• Driving business improvement and performance programmes across multiple markets.

• Identifying opportunities to improve profitability, efficiency, and operational performance.

• Supporting strategic planning and execution together with regional and country stakeholders.

• Ensuring retail tools, processes, and initiatives are effectively implemented and continuously improved.

• Building strong partnerships across functions to deliver sustainable business outcomes.

Your new team

You'll join the Northern Europe Store Operations function and work closely with senior retail leaders, business performance specialists, regional relationship managers, and a broad range of support functions.

The team plays an important role in supporting our store network, helping country teams deliver sustainable growth, operational excellence, and outstanding customer experiences.

As part of an international and highly collaborative environment, you'll contribute to projects and initiatives that directly influence business performance across multiple markets.

What are we looking for?

We are preferably looking for a candidate with the following competencies:

• Strong experience in retail operations, business performance, or operational excellence.

• Experience from a similar role or i.e. a Regional Relationship Manager role

• Commercial and financial acumen, including business planning and performance analysis.

• Experience leading cross-functional projects and driving measurable business improvements.

• Working with operating and supporting teams individually and remotely

• Excellent stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills.

• A data-driven and analytical approach to solving business challenges.

It would be an advantage if you have:

• Leadership experience working in franchise, partnership, or multi-site retail environments.

• Experience across multiple markets or countries.

• Knowledge of business transformation, change management, or performance improvement programmes.

• Experience using Power BI or similar reporting tools.

As a person, we believe that you are:

• Commercially minded and focused on creating results.

• A strong collaborator who builds trust and alignment across teams.

• Structured, proactive, and comfortable managing complexity.

• An engaging communicator who can influence stakeholders at all levels.

What awaits you upon joining Specsavers

At Specsavers, you'll get more than just a job. You will join us on a journey to make eye health and hearing services accessible to everyone.

We offer an exciting and challenging role in an organisation with strong ambitions, where you'll be part of a collaborative and supportive culture.

Joining us, you’ll get:

• Competitive compensation and benefits.

• Professional and personal development opportunities.

• A collaborative and inclusive culture.

• The opportunity to influence business performance across multiple countries.

• Exposure to senior stakeholders and strategic initiatives within an international organisation.

Is this your next step? Then apply today

To apply, please send us your CV using the button below. We want to respect your time, so including an application letter is optional. Feel free to apply as soon as possible. Please avoid including any photos or references to your age in your CV. It contributes to a fairer and more unbiased assessment.

We review CVs and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis. Our recruitment process typically consists of an initial screening, two rounds of interviews, and a personality assessment feedback session.

If you have any questions regarding the role, please contact the hiring manager Jacob Vejen by e-mail: jacob.vejen@specsavers.com.

Diversity & Inclusion at Specsavers

Specsavers will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other legally protected factor.

In line with our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion, we integrate these principles into all aspects of our work, from product development to team building.

jobs.occupation: Legal Counsel - Employment Law Leaning (Mat Cover)
jobs.description:
About Pleo

Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.

The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.

Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

About the role

We're looking for an interim In-house Legal Counsel to join our Legal team at Pleo in Copenhagen, Denmark. In this role, you'll serve as a trusted legal advisor across the business, protecting our interests and enabling growth as we scale our fintech platform. If you're excited about working at the intersection of legal strategy and operational excellence, and are passionate about building a compliant, well-governed fintech company, then this is the opportunity for you!

Please note that the role is a parental leave cover and therefore fixed-term until 30 September 2027.

Who you’ll be working with and reporting to

You'll report to one of our Associate Director, Legal and work closely with teams in People, Fraud, Finance, Product, Compliance and Operations. Our legal team is highly collaborative and dedicated to managing legal risk while enabling business velocity.

What you’ll be doing

As an In-house Legal Counsel, you will:

• 
Serve as the primary point of contact for business queries across all departments, providing timely, practical legal guidance on day-to-day operational matters.

• 
Support our People team on employment law, workplace policies, and labor compliance, including contract reviews, policy drafting, and regulatory adherence across multiple jurisdictions.

• 
Corporate administration by drafting, reviewing, and amending internal policies, procedures, and standardised legal templates that the business can use efficiently.

• 
Assist managing fraud and compliance escalations by conducting liability assessments, performing compliance checks, and providing risk mitigation advice to protect the business.

• 
Assist with customer disputes and regulatory engagement with the UK Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS), supporting escalations, preparing responses, and helping to ensure we meet all regulatory deadlines and requirements.

What you bring

You'll thrive in this role if you have:

• 
A Cand.Jur or equivalent legal qualification recognised in Denmark.

• 
2-5 years of legal experience – ideally in fintech, financial services, or a fast-growing scale-up environment where you've handled a broad range of matters.

• 
Knowledge about employment law and HR compliance – you understand the nuances of employment contracts, workplace policies, and labor law across multiple jurisdictions.

• 
Strong vendor and contract management skills – you can review, negotiate, and draft commercial agreements efficiently.

• 
Excellent communication skills – you can translate complex legal concepts into practical business advice for non-legal stakeholders.

• 
A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset – you see problems as opportunities and can manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

• 
Experience with compliance and risk management in a regulated industry is a plus as well as managing regulatory escalations and disputes, particularly with financial regulators or ombudsman services.

Why is this role a good fit for you

This role is a good fit for you if:

• 
You want a real look at how the law works in practice, where you implement it and explain it rather than argue it in theory

• 
You want genuine input into decisions, balancing the technically correct answer against what actually works commercially

• 
You like building things that outlast you: templates, policies and process that the business will use long after your contract ends

This role is not a good fit for you if:

• 
You want a clean roadmap. The team is under-resourced and the workload is heavy, so expect more firefighting than planned work

• 
You're looking for a permanent role. This is a 12-month fixed-term contract covering parental leave

• 
You want to specialise deeply or lead. This is a broad, hands-on individual contributor role where you'll be supported, not managing

How you’ll develop in this role

In your first three months at Pleo, you'll:

• 
Take over the routine employment workload so it runs independently of your manager

• 
Get to know the business well enough that your advice fits how Pleo actually operates, not just what the regulation says

• 
Start shaping the policies and templates the move from startup to corporate needs

Across the 12 months you'll build in-house practice and a working knowledge of fintech regulation that's hard to get anywhere else, with direct support from an experienced lead. Plenty of people use a contract like this as the step that takes them from theory into commercial legal work for good.

The location

This role will is a hybrid role with an expectation of spending on average 3 days a week in our Copenhagen office.

Show me the benefits!

💳 Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!)

🍜 Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office

🏥 Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis

🌴 We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays

🏠 For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options

🏖️ Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice

❤️🩹 We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far

👶 Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work

The interview process

We want to ensure you're set up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:

• 
Intro call (30 minutes) – A chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role, your background, and what's important to you in your next move.

• 
Interview with our Associate Director, Legal (45 minutes) – Meet to discuss how you see your role supporting the business, your approach to compliance culture, and your vision for the legal function.

• 
Final round with our Associate Director and General Counsel (60 minutes) – We'll dive deeper into your legal experience, explore specific scenarios you've handled, and discuss how you approach problem-solving in an in-house environment.

Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!

Last time we hired a Legal Counsel, we received a large number of applications but only a finite number could be selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:

• 
CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI (it’s a big focus for us internally too)but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

• 
Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process.

• 
Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc.

About your application

• 
English first. Since it's our company language, please submit your application in English. You’ll be using it a lot if you join us.

• 
A fair look for everyone. Our talent team reads every single application to ensure the process is fair. To keep things running smoothly, we only accept applications through our system—our support team can’t pass on calls or emails.

• 
Diversity drives us. We can only reach our goals if our team reflects the world around us. That starts with you hitting apply, even if you don't tick every single box. We encourage people from all backgrounds and experiences to join us.

• 
Interview at your best. We want you to feel comfortable throughout the process. If you have any accessibility requirements or need a specific format, email belonging@pleo.io. We’ll design a process that works for you.

• 
Your data is safe. When you apply, we process your personal data as a data processor. For more information on how Pleo processes personal data, read our Privacy Policy here.

• 
Applying for multiple roles? Nothing is stopping you, and we assess every role independently. However, we do look for alignment, so make sure you can explain why your interest and experience are right for each specific role.

• 
Reapplying. If you’re applying for the same role again, please wait six months from your last decision before hitting submit.

Benefits to support your best work

Our benefits package is curated to support you fully, inside and outside of work.

Purchaser at Sekura Cabins in Randers

Have you gained some initial experience in purchasing and are you ready to develop your skills further?

At Sekura Cabins, we are looking for a Purchaser to join our Supply Chain team. You will work closely with suppliers, production and colleagues across the organization, taking responsibility for your own suppliers and tasks while learning from experienced colleagues.

You do not need many years of experience. What matters most is that you have a solid foundation in purchasing or supply chain, are curious, take responsibility and are keen to develop.

About the role

You will join our Supply Chain team of four Senior Purchasers and Purchasers in total, reporting to our Senior Manager, SCM.

Your primary focus will be operational purchasing and day-to-day contact with our suppliers. A key part of the role is following up on deliveries and ensuring that the right materials are available on time so that production can run as planned.

You will also work with selected suppliers and categories, with opportunities to prepare for and participate in negotiations. You will cooperate with our freight forwarders and become a key partner to colleagues across the organization.

The role is varied, and some days are fast-paced. It is therefore important that you can stay organized, see tasks through to completion and remain calm when several things need your attention at the same time.

Your responsibilities will include:

·       Maintaining daily contact with suppliers and following up with them

·       Processing purchase proposals and issuing purchase orders

·       Following up on order confirmations, lead time and deadlines

·       Checking prices and invoices

·       Coordinating and planning material supplies for production

·       Optimizing inventory levels based on forecasts

·       Booking collections and coordinating with our freight forwarders

·       Collaborating and following up across the organization

·       Updating and maintaining master data in our ERP system

About you

We imagine that you have some experience in purchasing, materials planning or supply chain and are now ready to take the next step and develop further.

You may also have a relevant qualification in, for example, Supply Chain Management, purchasing or logistics, combined with practical experience.

You are organized and detail-oriented, with strong communication and relationship-building skills. You enjoy working with a wide range of people and are comfortable picking up the phone, following up and making things happen.

We also value the following:

·       Good communication skills in Danish and English, both spoken and written

·       Knowledge of German is an advantage

·       Confidence using Microsoft 365, particularly Excel

·       Experience with Dynamics 365 Business Central is an advantage

·       Taking ownership of your tasks and seeing them through to completion

What we offer

At Sekura Cabins, you will have the opportunity to develop your skills in purchasing and supply chain in an international manufacturing company where decisions are quickly put into action.

You can look forward to:

·       Thorough training and ongoing support from experienced colleagues

·       Opportunities for professional development and greater responsibility as your skills grow

·       A role involving contact with a wide range of people

·       A canteen scheme

·       Health insurance

·       Dental insurance after three months of employment

We review applications and hold interviews on an ongoing basis and will fill the position once we have found the right candidate.

Please send your application and CV to HR Business Partner Camilla Scharling Markussen at csm@sekura.dk

If you have any questions about the role, please contact Steen Krogh on 87100550.

Spirii has spent the past seven years building the infrastructure behind EV charging in Europe. Today, we operate across multiple markets and support CPOs, fleets, workplaces, and public charging networks with software and hardware solutions that make EV charging simpler to manage and scale. We are headquartered in Copenhagen and part of the Edenred group.

We are now at an important stage of growth. The market is moving fast, our product is maturing, and our organisation is scaling. That brings new opportunities, new complexity, and a need for even stronger alignment and execution across the company.

The role

As Director of Strategy & Execution, you will be the operational centre of gravity for the Spirii leadership team. This is a high-impact role for someone who can hold strategic context, drive cross-functional execution, and step into whatever the moment requires.

In practice, that means moving between the strategic and the operational with ease. One week you may be preparing a board presentation or supporting a key business decision. The next, you are driving alignment across product and commercial, or bringing structure to an initiative that spans multiple teams. The role requires both breadth and depth — and the judgement to know which is needed.

What you will do

Strategic execution

• Work directly with the CEO and leadership team on the company’s most important priorities, translating direction into plans, and plans into measurable outcomes

• Drive the quarterly planning cycle, OKRs, and cross-functional initiatives from kickoff through to follow-through

• Support leadership decision-making by structuring information, surfacing trade-offs, and ensuring the right inputs are in place

Leadership alignment

• Own the operating rhythm of the leadership team — weekly syncs, planning sessions, offsites, and follow-up

• Identify where alignment is breaking down across commercial, product, engineering, and operations — and address it proactively

• Serve as a trusted connector across the organisation, helping teams stay coordinated and focused on shared priorities

Special projects

• Lead high-impact projects that do not naturally sit within one department, and work with Edenred stakeholders on shared initiatives and reporting when needed

• Take complex, ambiguous problems, define them clearly, and drive them through to resolution

Communication

• Support the CEO in communicating clearly across the organisation — all-hands updates, leadership messaging, and internal communications during periods of change

• Prepare board materials, investor presentations, and executive reviews

What we’re looking for

• 4–8 years of experience in a corporate development, management consulting, strategy, or general management role — ideally with exposure to B2B software

• Comfortable operating in ambiguity: you build the structure rather than waiting for it

• Strong written communication — you can turn a messy situation into a one-pager

• Commercially literate enough to sit in a room with customers or partners and follow the conversation

• Fluency in English required; Danish and/or German a plus given our footprint

• Discretion. You’ll see confidential commercial, board, and people matters — trust has to be earned fast and kept

• Genuine curiosity about EV charging, energy, or infrastructure software is a plus, not a requirement — but you’ll need to get fluent in OCPP, ISO 15118, and how CPMS/eMSP actually make money, quickly

Benefits

It is important for us to create a healthy, diverse, fun, and creative working environment, so besides all the basic benefits, we also focus a lot on social activities, flexible working hours and a good work-life balance.

• Flexible Work Environment: Enjoy a collaborative, inclusive, and open workplace designed to fit your needs and support work-life balance.

• Competitive Package: A competitive salary, an 11% company pension plan, and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Time to Recharge: Benefit from 32 paid vacation days and paid parental leave to focus on what matters most.

• Career Growth: Access professional development opportunities and grow your career in a high-impact, high-growth industry.

• Stay Energized: Enjoy excellent coffee, tea, free snacks, and subsidized lunches at the office.

• Stay Active: Use our Spirii gym and shared company car to keep moving.

• Make an Impact: Be part of a team driving the future of sustainable energy while working on meaningful projects.

The position is a permanent position in Copenhagen, Denmark. Danish language is not a requirement, but fluent English language skills are required.

About Spirii – Who We Are

Spirii is a full-service e-mobility provider which offers hardware and software charging solutions to companies in the private and the public sector. Spirii was founded seven years ago as a company. Nevertheless, the people in Spirii have extensive experience working with electric cars and charging, as well as the development of future transport- and energy systems.

Spirii is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage applications from candidates of all backgrounds and experiences. Spirii strives to create an inclusive and diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified applicants to apply regardless of age, gender, race, sexual/religious orientation, or disability.

The position is a permanent position in

Denmark - Copenhagen - Spirii HQ

About Spirii

spirii and edenred logo

We know what it takes to drive electric, and in all our efforts to develop the best EV charging platform solutions and business services, we always put humans behind the wheel first. As part of the Edenred Group, a global technology leader, we are growing smart charging across Europe.

jobs.occupation: Manager - Software Engineering and Developer Tooling
jobs.description:
Denmark

Smørum

We are looking for a people leader for a mature, well-functioning team of 11 software engineers, split roughly equally between Smørum and Warsaw. You will help colleagues build confidence, use their strengths and grow in their careers through trust and honest feedback. You will be based in Smørum and travel to Warsaw up to six times a year.

The role

The team, called Toolbox, owns Gearbox, an essential tool for building, testing and producing our hearing aid products. Gearbox gives departments a common language and shared data abstractions, and it supports all the communication interfaces needed in development and production. It is data driven and works across product generations, programs and chipsets. Our users rely on Gearbox as a stable, validated tool that performs correctly and gives clear feedback on errors and completed requests.

Your main responsibility is the people in the team. You get to know each person, understand what motivates them and what helps them grow, and you coach rather than direct. Together with the Product Owner and the Scrum Master, you form the team's leadership team and share responsibility for its performance and wellbeing. The Product Owner sets direction and priorities, the Scrum Master supports how the team works, and you lead the people side.

Your main responsibilities

• Lead and develop 11 colleagues by coaching them, giving them ownership and helping them grow in a direction that fits both them and the team.

• Hold regular one-to-ones with each person about expectations, feedback, wellbeing and career development.

• Build the capabilities the team needs today and in the future through development, learning and recruitment, in line with product priorities and the technology strategy.

• Notice early when someone is struggling or losing motivation, and step in with support.

• Handle recruitment, compensation, budget and people processes together with your manager and People & Culture.

• Work as one leadership team with the Product Owner and Scrum Master on team health, learning and delivery.

• Understand the team's technical work and developer workflows well enough to remove obstacles for the team.

What you bring

You may already be a people leader, or you may be ready for your first line manager role. What matters most is the following:

• People first: You are motivated by helping others succeed and grow, and you give people trust and room to take ownership.

• Trust and feedback: You listen, build trust and give clear, honest feedback.

• Difficult conversations: You handle difficult conversations, including about performance, with fairness and respect.

• Leadership experience: You have led or developed others, for example as a manager, tech lead, Scrum Master or mentor.

• Technical understanding: You understand software engineering well enough to engage credibly with developers and architects, typically with a degree in engineering or computer science.

• Leading across sites: You can lead a team split between two locations and keep it working as one team.

Success in the role

After 12 to 18 months, you have earned a high level of trust from every member of the team, and you work closely with the Product Owner and the Scrum Master as one leadership team. Every team member has regular one-to-ones with you and a development plan they own and use. The team's engagement results are stable or improving, the team has kept its key people, and open positions are filled with the skills the team needs. Together with the Product Owner, you have an agreed plan for the skills the team needs over the next two years and how to build them. Colleagues in Smørum and Warsaw experience the same leadership and the same opportunities.

Development in the role: Over time, the role can grow into broader leadership, for example driving developer experience across the organisation or taking on a larger area as a senior manager.

Practical details

Workplace: Kongebakken, Smørum, Denmark (Global HQ)

Team: 11 people across Smørum and Warsaw

Travel: Warsaw up to six times per year

Application deadline: 27.11.26.

Hiring manager Jonas Funk Pedersen can be reached by email: jnfp@demant.com.

Interested?

If you are driven by helping people succeed and grow, and by improving the environment in which software is built, we would like to hear from you.

We screen and invite candidates on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

jobs.description:
Product Manager, Collective training – SitaWare Aspire

Ready to turn customer insight and new market opportunities into the next chapter of digital defence training? As Product Manager for SitaWare Aspire Collective training, you will lead the strategy and commercial direction for collective training and work closely with the Product Manager for individual training to shape the shared Aspire roadmap.

The job: Lead collective training. Shape SitaWare Aspire together.

You will lead the development and execution of the product strategy for SitaWare Aspire Collective training, defining its future direction, roadmap and commercial success. You will develop the strategy in close collaboration with the Vice President, and innovation will be driven by customer needs and the opportunities AI brings. The Product Manager for individual training holds the same responsibility for the individual training area. Together, collective and individual training form the SitaWare Aspire product, making a strong, interdependent partnership between the two Product Managers essential. You will jointly agree priorities and define the shared Aspire roadmap, ensuring that decisions in each area support the direction and success of the overall product.

In short, you can look forward to:

• identifying and analysing new market opportunities, building the business case and defining the strategy to realise them

• leading concept development for collective training and jointly agreeing priorities and the shared SitaWare Aspire roadmap with the Product Manager responsible for individual training, using business performance and market trends to adjust strategy and tactics together

• defining market requirements through research and dialogue with customers, Sales and domain experts, and working with Defence Product Management, UX designers and architects to develop innovative solutions

• supporting Defence Sales and Defence Services with proposals, product guidance and key customer engagements

• training Sales and Services colleagues at each product release

Your team: Bringing training closer to real operations

You will join Defence Service Development, a committed team of 40+ professionals across Aarhus and Copenhagen. The team develops SitaWare Aspire, a digital platform that brings realistic, hands-on training to users of the SitaWare suite – our command-and-control software for defence environments. Aspire integrates the actual SitaWare application, so users practise in the same interface they use in real operations. Its collective and individual training areas share cloud hosting and pricing, providing a common foundation for the product.

What you bring: Commercial insight that drives product success

You know what it takes to turn a software product’s potential into measurable success. With some years of experience in product management, you bring concrete examples of the impact you have made - and the curiosity to explore what comes next.

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• a master’s degree in software engineering, business development or a related field connecting technology and business

• experience across the product lifecycle - from market and competitor analysis, product discovery, strategy and planning to business cases, pricing and product launches

• a genuine interest in AI, with the curiosity to explore opportunities and the analytical mindset to assess them

• fluent English and excellent communication and collaboration skills that help you build strong partnerships

• excellent stakeholder management skills and an outgoing, enterprising approach to engaging others and moving ideas forward

• a focus on results, strong decision-making skills and the ability to navigate regulations and processes effectively

You will also have opportunities to meet customers, partners and end-users and attend trade shows. The role involves some business travel - around three weeks last year.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Here, you can take advantage of a range of on-site perks from physiotherapist-led massages and an in-house hairdresser to sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will also enjoy benefits like free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1300 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Gauri Varma Heise, Vice President, Service Development, Defence.

Are you looking for a role where your expertise will directly empower defence customers to excel in their missions? Step into this key position, where your military background, instructional design skills and stakeholder management expertise will shape how armed forces learn, adapt and succeed.

The job: develop and deliver training solutions that combine military expertise with strategic goals

As a Defence Training Specialist, you will play a key role in shaping a standardised and innovative approach to training within Systematic Defence. You will create role-based and collective training solutions for SitaWare users and tailor them to their operational needs in command-and-control (C2) military workflows. This gives users a comprehensive understanding of how to use SitaWare in compliance with their standard operating procedures (SOPs).

You will bridge the gap between the Product Manager’s vision and the Content Development team’s production, transforming military C2 procedures into powerful training products.

Furthermore, you will:

• analyse, design, develop, implement and evaluate (ADDIE) new training courses in collaboration with Systematic trainers across the organisation and the Content Development team

• develop Subject Training Plans (STPs) for the Systematic Defence Standard Training Catalogue

• create generic training scenarios for self-paced and instructor-led training

• standardise training content to align with the Systematic standard training approach

• design and provide C2 guidance for Systematic trainers, content creators and instructional designers

• design simulation scenarios to enhance self-paced and instructor-led training

• provide close support for Systematic’s military trainers in their preparation and delivery of training

• ensure global consistency in training across Systematic’s worldwide organisation.

You should expect some travel abroad as part of the job, about 10–20 days a year.

The team: join Defence Service Development and shape the future of defence training

Defence Service Development was established just a couple of years ago, and we already have a committed team of 20+ professionals in both Aarhus and Copenhagen.

You will join our Training Development team within Service Development in Aarhus. The team’s mission is to develop and maintain the Systematic Defence Standard Training Catalogue, which supports our entire product suite.

The team designs and maintains all training for Systematic Defence. This training is delivered through SitaWare Aspire e-Training, instructor-led sessions and interactive workshops. Our diverse and talented team includes video content creators, instructional designers and domain experts, who all work together to craft impactful learning experiences.

SitaWare Aspire is a digital training platform that provides realistic, hands-on training for users of the SitaWare suite, a C2 software solution used in operational environments. The platform integrates the actual SitaWare application into the training environment, so users can practise with the same interface they use in real operations.

Who you are: a skilled military professional with expertise in training development and strong stakeholder management skills

You bring extensive experience in designing, planning, developing and executing large-scale training programmes, including operational scenario development and STP creation, as well as expertise in C2 workflows. A strong background in staff work at battalion and brigade level is essential, combined with solid knowledge of training methodologies in military training establishments.

To succeed in this role, you are able and keen to dive into the detail to ensure that training content is accurate, relevant and aligned with standards. You will actively take part in the analysis, design, development, implementation and evaluation processes.

Furthermore, we are looking for:

• a Defence Training Specialist who actively performs tasks while providing guidance and support and setting the direction

• proficiency in English.

• Finally, you bring strong stakeholder management skills. You communicate clearly and collaborate effectively with various stakeholders to align training initiatives with organisational goals.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or EU country for the past seven years, as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark, with more than 1,200 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. Systematic is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Welcome to Systematic Aarhus

At our Aarhus office, you can look forward to joining our Employees’ Club, which offers nearly 100 social and professional events a year. You can also enjoy on-site perks such as physiotherapist-led massages, an in-house hairdresser, sports clubs, game tables and even our own padel court. Our canteen is a standout feature, serving a daily selection of delicious and healthy dishes. Beyond the office, you will enjoy benefits such as free ARoS +1 access and various shopping discounts.

Start your development here

We assess applications on an ongoing basis, as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible. Click Apply now and send us your CV today.

If you have any questions, you are welcome to contact Marie Lunde Jørgensen, Manager, Defence Service Development on +45 8943 2000.

As VAT Manager, you will help shape how we manage indirect tax in a complex global business. You will combine strong VAT expertise with digital innovation, making our VAT reporting and advisory more transparent, efficient and data-driven.

You will contribute to our digital transformation — from SAP S/4HANA to AI-powered solutions — connecting your VAT expertise with smart solutions that improve how we work. This is an opportunity to take ownership, deliver quality at pace and make an immediate difference in a global business.

What you’ll bring

Factbird helps manufacturers turn real-time production data into decisions they can actually act on. Since 2016, we've helped manufacturers in 28 countries cut waste, boost uptime, and run smarter — from the shop floor to the boardroom. Over 300 companies trust us to make sense of their operations, and we're a team of 80+ people across Copenhagen and the US who care about making complex things simple.

Our IoT team builds the devices and edge software that connect our customers' production lines to the Factbird platform, from sensors on the line to industrial edge computers running computer vision right next to the machines. We're a small team with broad ownership, and we're hiring an Embedded Platform Engineer to help build and run the platform our edge products stand on.

**This role is onsite in Copenhagen, Denmark. We welcome applications from candidates based in Germany who are open to relocating to Copenhagen.

**

About the Role

As Embedded Platform Engineer, you'll work hands-on across Factbird EDGE, our industrial edge platform, together with the rest of the IoT team: the operating system, the device software, and the vision models that run on it. You'll take ownership of the infrastructure around the devices: provisioning and recovery, over-the-air updates, and fleet observability, the systems that keep our unattended devices reliable, secure, and safely updatable in factories you may never visit.

You'll work in Rust on embedded Linux, with Yocto, AWS IoT Greengrass, GStreamer and ONNX Runtime at the core, alongside our Cloud and DevOps engineers and the people building our AI capabilities. Part of the job is shaping the role with the team as our edge products grow.

You'll thrive here if you like working across a system end to end, from the bootloader to the cloud connection, and if you'd rather fix the root cause in the build than patch around it on the device.

What you'll do

Embedded Linux & the EDGE platform

• Develop our Yocto-based Linux distribution: layers, BSPs, kernel configuration, and reproducible builds

• Build and maintain the Rust components that run on our edge devices

• Bring up new hardware platforms, debug on target, and keep the platform secure and maintainable over a long device lifetime

• Keep our CI and on-hardware testing healthy, so changes reach devices with confidence

Edge inference & vision

• Work with our ML and vision engineers on the device side of our computer vision capabilities: camera pipelines, video streaming, and model inference that runs efficiently on industrial hardware

jobs.occupation: Maximizing use of fresh grass for dairy cows by combining grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Animal and Veterinary Sciences programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Research area and project description:

We are seeking a dedicated PhD student for a 3-year position within the topic of dairy production with fresh grass as a main forage source.

The impact of dairy production on environment and climate is of continued importance and interest. Cropping and feeding fresh grass can potentially improve the impact of dairy production on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen leakage to surrounding fresh waters.

The project investigates the potential of maximizing fresh grass forage intake to reduce enteric methane emission and increase nitrogen utilization, while maintaining milk production. A series of trials with lactating dairy cows are planned investigating combinations of grazing, zero-grazing, and multispecies swards.

This project offers:

• A unique opportunity to contribute to a more sustainable agriculture and environmental-friendly milk production

• An active and stimulating academic environment with several other PhD students and early career staff

• Access to state-of-the-art research facilities for both barn-housing, grazing, and pasture management for dairy cattle

• Collaboration with a range of research partners

• Collaborative projects that foster innovative thinking and practical implementation

Qualifications and specific competences:

Applicants to the PhD position must hold a relevant university degree (MSc) in Animal Science, Agricultural Science, or related fields.

The candidate is expected to have:

• Understanding of ruminant nutrition and digestion

• Experience with data handling and analysis using at least one software.

• Ability and interest in collaborating across disciplines with project partners.

• Ability to communicate effectively in English.

• Good scientific and writing skills.

Place of employment and place of work:

The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, Research center Foulum, Blichers allé 20, 8830 Tjele, Denmark.

jobs.description:
Senior Simulation Engineer – Finite Element Analysis

Hillerød, Denmark

Are you interested in using simulation to develop medical devices that help deliver treatments to patients worldwide? We are looking for an experienced Senior Simulation Engineer specializing in finite element analysis (FEA) to join our team in Hillerød and support the development and maintenance of drug delivery solutions.

Your new role

As our Senior Simulation Engineer, you will take technical ownership of structural simulation activities, helping teams develop reliable products and make informed design decisions. You will work across the product lifecycle, from evaluating early design concepts to supporting validation, product improvements and failure investigations.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Lead finite element analyses: Independently plan and execute structural simulations, selecting appropriate methods to assess performance, durability and safety under realistic loading conditions.

• Build reliable simulation models: Translate engineering requirements and CAD designs into robust models, defining geometry, meshes, material behavior, contacts and boundary conditions. Verify model quality through convergence and sensitivity studies.

• Support design optimization: Collaborate with design and mechanical engineers to improve product performance, material selection and cost. Provide practical recommendations and technical input during design reviews.

• Validate simulations against physical tests: Work with physical test and define validation activities, correlate simulation results with experimental data, assess uncertainty and refine models based on findings.

• Support product development and failure investigations: Contribute structural analysis expertise to cross-functional teams working on new products, product maintenance, validation and root cause analysis.

• Communicate findings clearly: Prepare reports and presentations that explain analysis methods, assumptions, results and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• Advance simulation practices and develop colleagues: Improve simulation methods, workflows and standards, contribute to the structural simulation strategy, and mentor junior engineers and interns.

Your new department

You will join Drug Delivery Innovation (DDI), a new area within Novo Nordisk’s global organization, based in Hillerød.

Our team comprises 14 colleagues across three specialist groups: Structural Simulation, Molding Simulation and Material Science. We work closely together and collaborate with stakeholders across Novo Nordisk, combining expertise in simulation and materials to support the development and maintenance of drug delivery solutions.

In this role, you will contribute structural simulation expertise to projects involving design evaluation, test correlation and product improvements. Your findings will help teams assess design options and make decisions throughout development.

Your skills and qualifications

You bring a strong technical foundation and can independently lead complex simulation work, from defining the analysis approach to communicating recommendations that inform design decisions.

To succeed in this role, you have:

• A master’s degree in mechanical engineering, structural engineering, applied mechanics or a related discipline.

• Substantial practical FEA experience, including independent responsibility for complex structural analyses and recommendations.

• The ability to explain technical findings clearly and collaborate effectively with colleagues across design, testing, manufacturing and quality.

• A solid understanding of structural mechanics, material behavior, nonlinear analysis, contact modelling, fatigue and failure mechanisms.

• Experience validating simulation models against experimental data, assessing uncertainty and translating findings into practical design improvements.

Desirable experience

• Modelling of plastics, elastomers, paper and cardboard, including their material behavior and structural response.

• Working in a regulated industry, particularly pharmaceuticals or medical device development.

You take initiative, work systematically and communicate openly with colleagues and stakeholders. You can manage competing priorities as projects evolve and connect detailed technical findings to their implications for product performance and development decisions.

Working at Novo Nordisk

Every day we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with determination, constant curiosity and a commitment to finding better ways forward. For over 100 years, this dedication has driven us to build a company focused on lasting change for long-term health. One where diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create extraordinary results. When you join us, you're not just starting a job – you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

What we offer

There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordinary results we produce. Being part of a global healthcare company means opportunities to learn and develop are all around us, while our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind.

• Circularity & Products: a degree in environmental engineering, chemistry, sustainability, business or a related field. Technical and business backgrounds are both welcome, as long as you want to influence decisions that affect the environment.

• Climate, Nature & Chemicals: an interest in chemicals, sustainability and regulatory compliance. You are comfortable with large, complex datasets, and you can structure, analyse and communicate information clearly. You are pragmatic and enjoy complex questions where the path forward is not predefined.

• Environmental Performance & Intelligence: a degree in environmental science or a related field, including business, law or engineering with a sustainability focus.

Useful, but not essential:

Experience in climate data analysis or geospatial mapping, gained through coursework, projects or previous work, is particularly welcome for Environmental Performance & Intelligence.

What you’ll do

Your tasks will depend on your background and the team you join:

• Circularity & Products: support initiatives on circular product design and life cycle assessments (LCA) of our current and future portfolio, through research, data collection and assessment, project coordination and clear stakeholder presentations. You could quantify the environmental impact of pharmaceutical products, including Pharmaceuticals in the Environment (PiE), identify where to improve, and explore how this can create commercial value.

• Climate, Nature & Chemicals: support chemical compliance and chemical strategy by helping implement regulatory requirements, update internal guidelines and training, collect and assess chemical data, and develop the processes and systems that support compliance. You will also support the environmental strategy on chemicals with data analysis, stakeholder engagement, decision material and project coordination.

• Environmental Performance & Intelligence: support work on climate adaptation, environmental due diligence and environmental strategy. This could include developing a methodology to prioritise climate risk at production sites and suppliers, identifying how our operations affect the environment to help meet EU sustainability requirements (CSDDD), and researching leading practices for our strategy review.

• Across all teams, turn data and research into clear input that colleagues can use to make decisions.

Who you’ll work with

You will join one of three teams within Environmental Responsibility, part of the CEO office, Transformation & Sustainability area. Environmental Responsibility is a team of around 70 specialists, project managers, consultants and experts. Together they drive Novo’s environmental work, including the strategy ‘Circular for Zero’ and cross-organisational projects.

You will work with project managers and specialists across Novo, and collaborate across disciplines to move work forward. Your closest contacts are the team contacts for each position:

• Circularity & Products: Eva Vestergaard, +45 30758269, ECQV@novonordisk.com

• Climate, Nature & Chemicals: Emilie Marie Reiler, +45 34482317, ELRL@novonordisk.com

• Environmental Performance & Intelligence: Moritz Herber, +45 30751392, OMZH@novonordisk.com

What you can expect here

You will get hands-on learning in a team that is growing alongside Novo, and real responsibility for work that colleagues rely on. You will be supported to perform at your best, trusted to take ownership and encouraged to make your voice heard. The team works across disciplines, and still finds time for fun.

Practicalities:

• Period: full-time for 6 months, with potential extension to 12 months.

• Start date: January/February 2027.

• Location: Novo HQ, Bagsværd, Denmark.

• Pay: if allowed by your educational institution, the internship is paid at a fixed monthly base rate of DKK 15,900, plus a pension scheme (currently 10% employer contribution and 5% employee contribution).

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn environmental knowledge into action, apply by 22 November 2026. Please state in your application which position(s) you are applying for and your level of education. Applications are assessed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

For further information on the positions, contact the relevant person listed above.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

As AI Search Specialist, you will make Novo accurately represented across AI-powered search and generative platforms. You will turn complex performance data into automated insights, scalable workflows and clear recommendations that help markets act faster. Working across regions, you will connect measurement standards with local needs, helping people find trusted health information when they need it supporting lasting health.

What you'll bring

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Digital Media, Computer Science, Data Analytics or a related field or equivalent

• 5–8 years in SEO, GEO, AEO, AI search analytics or digital performance optimisation.

• Hands-on experience with AI visibility dashboards, prompt datasets, citation data and LLM performance metrics.

• Experience building or using AI agents, automation workflows and generative AI tools professionally.

• Coding ability in Python, SQL, JavaScript or similar.

• Working knowledge of APIs, data pipelines, structured data, schema markup, CMS integrations and analytics platforms.

• Ability to translate technical insights into concise, actionable recommendations for non-technical audiences.

• Experience working across functions, markets and senior stakeholders in a global business or agency setting.

What you'll do

You will own the insights platforms and automation layer of SEO and GEO across markets, moving teams from raw data to practical action.

• Build and maintain AI search dashboards tracking visibility, share of voice, citation rate, ranking, sentiment and source influence across markets .

• Analyse GEO performance across prompt clusters, LLM outputs and third-party citations. Identify gaps and turn findings into prioritised recommendations with clear owners.

• Improve discoverability and AI readability through crawlability, indexation, metadata, schema, internal linking, semantic structure and page experience.

• Develop scalable AI agents and automation workflows for insight generation, content briefs, reporting and market activation with appropriate controls.

• Connect data sources through programming, APIs and automation to cut manual analysis and speed up reporting.

• Support AI-ready content optimisation including FAQs, structured summaries, metadata and schema inputs while ensuring accuracy, compliance and alignment with relevant requirements.

Who you'll work with

You will join the Digital Media Activation team in International Operations, working where data, technology and marketing meet to scale AI search optimisation across markets.

Your partners include global, regional and local digital marketing, web and content, data and analytics, brand and communications. Externally, you will work with AI visibility and SEO platform provider, such as Profound, SEMrush and SurferSEO and specialist agencies.

What you can expect here

Real ownership in a fast-moving, cross-market environment. You will design measurement approaches, build automation and set standards that teams across regions rely on. You will sharpen your skills at the forefront of AI search, work across disciplines and markets, and contribute to helping people find accurate health information when they search for it.

What we offer

At Novo, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

As Associate Director, you will build and lead Microbial Expression Delivery, a newly established department that turns microbial expression technologies into dependable protein and peptide deliveries for Novo’s research portfolio. You will set clear direction for a team of 12 scientists and technicians, sharpen handovers and help research projects move with pace and predictability. Your leadership will get researchers the proteins and data they need sooner, supporting progress for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You combine scientific depth in microbial expression with the leadership to bring people together around shared priorities.

• An advanced degree in molecular biology, biotechnology, biochemistry or another relevant scientific discipline.

• People leadership experience and a track record of building trust, developing colleagues and delivering results through collaboration across functions.

• Solid experience with microbial expression of proteins and peptides, and an understanding of how analytical and automated workflows, including LC-MS, turn scientific insight into reliable project impact.

• Experience working in a project-driven or similar matrixed organisation, with the ability to communicate clearly about priorities, dependencies and expectations.

• A collaborative, curious, pragmatic and inclusive way of leading: you invite different perspectives and make it easy for others to succeed through clear direction and respect.

Useful, but not essential:

A PhD in a relevant scientific field.

What you’ll do

You will establish a department that gives colleagues across the Centre for Expression Engineering (CEE) one clear place to request high-quality proteins, peptides and data, and a team that delivers them timely.

• Establish Microbial Expression Delivery as a new department that centralises automated expression technologies and takes end-to-end ownership of timely protein deliveries across the portfolio.

• Take responsibility for our centralised technology platforms, including LC-MS, automated high-throughput workflows, and variant and expression feasibility testing, with clear accountability across interfaces.

• Translate portfolio priorities into clear direction for your team, balancing capacity, dependencies and stakeholder needs to keep deliveries predictable.

• Strengthen handovers and speed up shared deliverables with other CEE departments and internal partners, such as cell line generation, expression optimisation, feasibility assessments, technology implementation and proof-of-concept work.

• Remove organisational barriers across Therapeutic Discovery, apply modular, end-to-end ways of working and align priorities so decisions are made faster.

• Lead visibly: role-model scientific excellence and open communication, and build a respectful, challenge-safe culture where people grow and contribute their best.

Who you’ll work with

You will lead the Microbial Expression Delivery team, made up of 12 scientists and technicians, within the Centre for Expression Engineering. CEE is part of Research Centres of Excellence (RCE), which supports Novo’s research portfolio by enabling microbial strain engineering, strain development and protein production.

Your closest partners are the other CEE departments, scientific and automation experts, and project teams who request deliverables from your centralised workflows. You will also work with colleagues across Therapeutic Discovery, of which RCE is an integral part. In a matrixed organisation, your role is to create clarity on priorities, agree who owns what and keep work moving.

You will work out of our largest research centre in Måløv, Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to build something new and given the support to do it well. You will work with scientific and automation experts, shape how a new capability is set up, and grow your leadership alongside a team that values quality, simplicity and impact.

Clear expectations and a culture that rewards results mean you can focus on delivering your best work. You will also help create the same conditions for your team: an open, collaborative and inclusive environment where colleagues can thrive, develop and make their voices heard.
