jobs.occupation: Associate Consumer Finance & Online Partnerships Director
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Associate Consumer Finance & Online Partnerships Director, you will build the financial foundation for how Novo grows online partnerships in Obesity across Europe and Canada (EUCAN). This is a newly created role: you will set up a European customer profit and loss view and a clear business case approach, so teams know where to invest and can track the return. You will turn complex analysis into decisions that help more people reach treatment.

What you’ll bring

You thrive where commercial business development, consumer behaviour and financial decision making meet. You can build something new, influence without formal authority and turn complexity into action.

• A master’s degree in economics, business administration, finance or an equivalent field.

• Significant experience in commercial finance, business development, M&A finance, financial system change projects or customer profitability, including cross-country, regional or global exposure.

• Strong financial modelling and data interpretation skills.

• Practical experience in pricing, negotiation, customer profitability and stakeholder management in a large organisation.

• Experience bringing structure to new business areas, setting clear priorities and steering the business through influence and relationships.

• The ability to turn complex analysis into clear recommendations and to build new capabilities, standards and frameworks from the ground up.

• Proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, AI modelling, SAP and systematic data consolidation.

• Fluency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience from consumer health companies, including private healthcare organisations.

• Additional languages.

What you’ll do

You will be the finance partner who helps Region Europe and Canada decide where to invest in online partnerships and consumer initiatives, and who shows what those investments deliver.

• Create the framework and shape commercial partnership priorities through sound financial modelling, working with business partners to assess partnership opportunities and consumer investment initiatives.

• Develop and deliver a business case methodology across European markets, so investment decisions are prudent, comparable and grounded in facts as part of the business rhythm.

• Establish an end-to-end view of customer and partner profit and loss, including system tracking and performance updates that follow return on investment.

• Deliver complex cross-functional change projects with Business Development, Finance, Legal, Supply Chain and Commercial Strategy to enable online sales in new European markets.

• Act as Commercial Finance Partner to the commercial unit for business development and to the UK affiliate.

• Improve data definitions, ownership, quality and comparability of online sales channels across markets.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Business Finance team in Region Europe and Canada (EUCAN), part of International Operations, reporting to the Director of Business Finance. The team is a key business partner to the Regional Leadership Team and the European sales affiliates.

Day to day, you will collaborate with European sales affiliate offices, local finance and business development teams, and with colleagues in Marketing, Business Development and Commercial Excellence, Data, Insights & Analytics, Pricing and Access, and Supply Chain. You will build bridges between these functions, so every investment decision rests on evidence and aims to maximise patient reach. Working across markets, you will help drive both the online sales agenda and the consumer finance agenda in Obesity.

The role is based in Ørestad, Copenhagen, Denmark.

What you can expect here

You will shape a new area from the start, with the trust to set direction and the visibility to influence decisions across European markets. Working with colleagues from finance, commercial, legal and supply chain, you will broaden your perspective across the value chain and build new skills through practical, cross-functional experience.

You will be supported to perform at your best, with clear expectations and a culture that values honest input and follows through on decisions.

Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 847,010.00 to 1,245,110.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to build the financial foundation for online partnerships across Europe, apply for the Associate Director, Consumer Finance & Online Partnerships role by 22 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

At NORDEN, we empower global trade through data, technology and deep industry knowledge. Behind every decision, there is a need to understand risk, navigate uncertainty and create transparency.

This is where you will contribute. You will build solutions that are used by risk management and commercial teams to manage their trading books and finance to consolidate the business into the value of NORDEN.

Why this role?

You will work across the full development lifecycle, from architecture to implementing solutions and ensuring stable operations in production. At the same time, you will gain unique insights into risk management in a global shipping company.

Our solutions are built in Python with Azure as cloud platform. We use GitHub Copilot with access to the latest models while insisting on having a firm understanding of our code.

You will join a friendly, collaborative and people-focused environment where your ideas are welcomed, your development is supported and your contributions genuinely matter. You will join an experienced team of seven people with backgrounds in computer science, physics and economics.

What you will be doing

As a full-stack engineer, you will play an important role in developing solutions that support key business decisions across NORDEN.

Among other things, you will:

• Build end-to-end scalable and maintainable solutions based on best practice.

• Develop backend services in Python on Azure, using technologies such as Polars, Durable functions and Delta Lake.

• Develop interactive web frontends in React and TypeScript on Azure App Service.

• Get a business-oriented mindset and a genuine interest in shipping and risk management.

• Work on solutions with data scientists, risk managers and finance business partners.

What you bring

We are looking for an experienced engineer who can contribute from day one and is interested in learning about shipping and risk management.

You have:

• A genuine passion for software development and a proven experience within both frontend and backend development.

• Good experience with development in Python and utilising Azure cloud technologies.

• Up to 5 years of experience from a similar position in shipping or the financial sector with a background in computer science, software engineering or similar.

• Interest in exploring new topics on your own, and work well with others when making and explaining decisions.

• Advanced English communication skills

• The legal right to work in Denmark.

Beyond your technical skills, you enjoy collaborating with others and are comfortable engaging with a variety of stakeholders across the organisation. You are curious by nature, open to new ideas and motivated by continuously improving how things are done.

If you are interested in bringing together software development, business insight and modern cloud technologies at a global company where your work makes a clear difference, we would like to hear from you.

Application

Please upload your motivation letter, resume and relevant diplomas via our website as soon as possible and no later than 3 December 2026. Your motivation letter helps us understand what drives you, why you are interested in the role, and how your skills and experiences could contribute to the team. We are especially interested in your motivation and transferable skills, not a recap of your CV. It is your opportunity to tell us the story behind your application.

We review and interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

We will do our best to get back to you at least within ten working days after the application deadline, 3 December 2026.

In NORDEN we value a range of perspectives, educational backgrounds and professional experience and encourages all qualified candidates to apply.

Our company

We are a global provider of ocean-based freight services for bulk and project cargo of all sizes. We integrate freight solutions with port logistics, helping our customers optimise and decarbonise supply chains. We provide tailored solutions built on flexibility, reliability, and intelligence.

Our agile business model ensures stability by continuously adapting our fleet to market developments and customer needs.

Founded in 1871, NORDEN is one of Denmark’s oldest internationally operating shipping companies. Incorporated in Denmark, we are listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen as part of the OMX Nordic Large Cap index.

With offices across 6 continents, we are a truly integrated part of global trade.

Imagine a future where you shape our view of European power markets and turn deep market insight into commercial action

Application deadline 30th November 2026 , 23:59 CET

Country Denmark

Location Gentofte

Workplace Hybrid (office and home-working) We offer a workplace culture where you´ll arrange with your people leader when you can work from home and from the office.

Working hours full-time

Employment type Permanent

Legal entity Ørsted Salg & Service A/S

Why join?

Proven very high employee satisfaction and motivation

Continuous development opportunities for all employees

Competitive salary, pension scheme, and attractive holiday package

A wide range of health benefits, such as health insurance, nutritious food, and fitness facilities in our office locations

Join us in this role where you’ll own and continuously develop our fundamental view of European power markets. Working at the intersection of market analysis and trading, you’ll bring together insights from across the organisation, form an independent view of where markets are heading, and translate this into clear commercial recommendations.

Working closely with the Trading & Revenue senior leadership, trading desk heads, and traders, you’ll influence decisions around trading strategies, hedging, portfolio management, and PPAs. Rather than supporting decisions from a distance, you’ll be a trusted market expert whose analysis and judgement help shape the positions we take.

**Welcome to Trading & Revenue

**You’ll be part of Forecasting & Analysis where you, together with your colleagues, will provide the market insights and analysis behind key trading and commercial decisions. You’ll work in a dynamic environment close to the trade floor, collaborating with traders, analysts, meteorologists, and dedicated in-house model developers. With strong modelling capabilities around you, you’ll be able to focus on interpreting what is happening in the market, challenging existing assumptions, forming a strong fundamental view, and translating it into commercial opportunities.

As a team, we challenge our thinking, share our expertise openly, and combine different perspectives to make better decisions.

In this role, your analysis becomes action. You’ll engage directly with Trading & Revenue senior leadership team and have the opportunity to shape how we understand European power markets. You’ll play a leading role in strengthening our market analysis capability, bringing in external perspectives and best practices, and developing a more integrated view across Trading & Revenue.

You’ll play an important role in:

• owning, developing, and maintaining our fundamental view of European power markets, with a particular focus on North-Western Europe and the UK, and bringing together perspectives from across Trading & Revenue into a coherent market outlook

• acting as a trusted sparring partner to the Trading & Revenue senior leadership, trading desk heads, traders, and portfolio managers, bringing an independent fundamental market perspective to key strategic and commercial decisions

• identifying structural and emerging shifts across supply, demand, regulation, weather, generation, interconnector flows, electrification, and other market drivers, and assessing what they mean for power prices and market dynamics

• turning market developments into commercial implications, from understanding the impact of changing generation availability or demand assumptions to assessing what these developments mean for our portfolios and trading positions

• translating fundamental market insights into actionable trading and hedging strategies together with our trading teams, helping facilitate discussions on what positions we should take as market conditions and assumptions evolve

• advising senior stakeholders on the market implications of important portfolio, PPA, and other commercial decisions, bringing a clear view of both market opportunities and risks

• advancing our fundamental power market capability by bringing together perspectives from across the organisation, introducing external insights and industry best practices, and strengthening how we form and communicate our market view across Trading & Revenue.

To succeed in the role, you:

• have deep expertise in European power markets and significant experience forming an independent view of how fundamental developments affect power prices and market dynamics

• bring strong commercial judgement and can move confidently from fundamental analysis to clear recommendations on trading, hedging, portfolio, and PPA decisions

• understand the interaction between physical power market fundamentals, forward markets, options, and curve dynamics, and can connect changes in the physical market with their commercial and trading implications

• are comfortable owning a market view, challenging established assumptions, and acting as an equal sparring partner to experienced traders and senior decision-makers

• can look beyond established market assumptions, identify developments or structural shifts that may not yet be fully reflected in the market view, and determine what they could mean for future power prices

• can bring together different sources of analysis, modelling, external intelligence, and perspectives from across the organisation to form a clear and coherent market view

• communicate complex market developments as concise, decisive, and commercially relevant recommendations, including to senior stakeholders

• bring substantial experience from power or closely related European energy markets, whether gained in a utility, trading environment, financial institution, or similar market-facing organization.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

Position salary range:

For this role, the base pay will be determined according to the relevant pay structure for the location where the position is filled. Actual pay will be based on skills, experience, and the expected role fulfilment to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package. Pay details specific to your location will be provided during the interview process.

Pre-employment background checks:

For certain positions, a background check may be required as part of the hiring process. Because we recruit across multiple countries, the specific checks performed will depend on the role and the legal requirements in the location where the position is filled. If a background check is relevant for the role you are being considered for, you will be informed during the recruitment process. All background checks are carried out by an external provider and always in accordance with applicable local laws and regulations.

Ørsted

Ørsteds vision er at skabe en verden, der udelukkende kører på grøn energi. Ørsted udvikler, opfører og driver landvindmølleparker, havvindmølleparker, bioenergianlæg og innovative løsninger, som omdanner affald til energi, og forsyner sine kunder med intelligente energiprodukter. Ørsted har 6200 medarbejdere og har hovedsæde i Danmark.

Shape the technical direction and build software that lasts

At Autorola, we're transforming the global automotive industry through digital solutions, technology and business intelligence.

We're looking for an experienced Staff Software Engineer to take technical ownership of a team's domain, guide architectural decisions and ensure high engineering quality across our software solutions.

You'll combine hands-on software development with technical leadership, working closely with Product Managers, engineers and other technical specialists to turn business needs into robust, scalable and maintainable solutions.

If you're passionate about software architecture, solving complex technical challenges and helping other engineers grow, we'd love to hear from you.

About us

The Autorola Group is a global leader in online vehicle remarketing, automotive IT solutions and business intelligence for the used vehicle market.

Through Autorola Marketplace, Autorola Solutions and Indicata, we help manufacturers, leasing companies, fleet owners and dealers buy, sell and manage vehicles more efficiently using technology, data and digital solutions.

Your role

As Staff Software Engineer, you'll be the team's technical anchor and go-to person, taking ownership of its technical direction, architecture and engineering standards.

You'll remain hands-on in software development while leading technical design discussions, making architectural decisions and guiding the team towards solutions that support both immediate business needs and long-term technical sustainability.

You'll work closely with the Team Lead, Product Manager, Principal Engineers and other department-level technical roles to align team decisions with Autorola's wider technology strategy.

Success means a well-architected and maintainable technical domain, high engineering standards, effective collaboration and a team that continues to grow technically.

What you'll be doing

• Take architectural ownership of the team's technical domain, including services, data models, interfaces, dependencies and technical documentation.

• Guide technical direction and ensure alignment with Autorola's architecture principles, engineering standards and technology strategy.

• Stay hands-on in software development, designing, building, testing and delivering high-quality solutions.

• Lead technical design discussions, reviews and decisions, making trade-offs between business needs, delivery speed and long-term maintainability.

• Drive modernisation initiatives, including breaking down legacy applications, improving system architecture and reducing duplication across teams.

• Collaborate with Principal Engineers and other Staff Engineers to align team architecture with company-wide strategies.

• Mentor and coach engineers, support technical problem-solving and help raise the overall engineering capabilities of the team.

• Promote best practices in automated testing, CI/CD, code reviews and responsible use of AI-assisted development tools.

Who are we looking for

We're looking for a senior software engineer with deep technical expertise, strong architectural understanding and the ability to guide others through complex technical decisions. You are likely to have:

• A bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, software engineering or similar, or equivalent practical experience.

• Typically, 8+ years of professional software development experience, including ownership of system architecture or a technical domain.

• Proven experience designing, building and operating production systems, including architecture, performance, security and monitoring.

• Experience modernising legacy applications and designing scalable, maintainable software architectures.

• Experience with cloud technologies, preferably AWS, and event-driven architecture.

• Strong knowledge of automated testing, CI/CD and code review practices.

• The ability to lead technical initiatives, make sound architectural decisions and communicate complex topics clearly to different stakeholders.

• Experience mentoring and coaching other engineers.

• Experience with technologies such as Java, Spring Boot, REST APIs, relational databases and AWS is relevant.

What success looks like

Within your first 12–18 months, you'll have:

• Established clear technical ownership of your team's domain, including architecture, services, dependencies and documentation.

• Built strong relationships with Product Management, Team Leads, Principal Engineers and other technical stakeholders.

• Guided the team towards consistent engineering standards and sustainable architectural decisions.

• Delivered visible progress on modernisation and reduced technical debt within your domain.

• Improved software quality, maintainability, scalability and operational reliability.

• Helped raise the technical capabilities of the team through mentoring, knowledge sharing and technical leadership.

• Contributed to aligning your team's technical direction with Autorola's wider technology strategy.

Why join Autorola Group?

Autorola Group is a global company with more than 850 employees across 20 subsidiaries in Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.

You'll join an international technology environment where software engineering, business expertise and digital solutions come together to solve complex challenges for leading automotive companies.

As Staff Software Engineer, you'll have a significant influence on our technical direction, architectural decisions and engineering standards. You'll work alongside skilled engineers and technical specialists, with the opportunity to shape solutions, drive modernisation and help build the next generation of Autorola's technology platforms.

We also offer pension and health insurance, social and company events, a great lunch arrangement, access to a fitness room and a lively Friday bar.

Want to join the team?

We're looking to fill the position as soon as possible. Please note that this description reflects our ideal candidate profile. We strongly believe in inclusion and diversity and encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement. Applications and CVs will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, and the advertisement may be removed once the right candidate has been found.

If you have any questions about the position, feel free to contact Christian Gless, Tech Talent Acquisition Partner, on csg@autorola.com.

jobs.occupation: Business Consultant, Corporate Credit, Netcompany Banking Services
jobs.description:
Job Description

Are you interested in the intersection of IT, business and finance? As a Business Consultant, you will work with IT solutions supporting banks' corporate credit processes. You will analyze system issues, understand client needs and translate business requirements into technical solutions while building specialized knowledge within banking and corporate credit.

Netcompany Banking Services

We deliver various IT solutions and services to banks and savings institutions across Denmark and other Nordic countries. We provide a modern, cloud-based core banking platform serving more than 50 Nordic banks with over 2 million end customers. Our solutions encompass daily banking operations, mobile and internet banking, payments, investment management, risk management, compliance, and open banking.

Responsibilities

We are looking for a Business Consultant to join our team, working with IT solutions that support banks' corporate credit processes. You will be involved in the daily operation, maintenance and further development of these solutions, acting as a link between clients, developers and other stakeholders. Your work will involve investigating issues, understanding business needs and ensuring reliable system operations.

You will join an experienced team that will support your onboarding and help you build expertise within corporate credit and IT solutions. Initially, your focus will be on learning the existing solution and its daily operations, with opportunities to take on more responsibility for further development over time.

Your responsibilities will typically include:

• Handling and analyzing client-reported issues and tickets, investigating problems and identifying their root causes to ensure reliable system operations.

• Maintaining and supporting existing IT solutions while contributing to their continuous improvement and further development.

• Engaging in dialogue with clients to understand their needs and challenges, translating business requirements into clear and actionable tasks.

• Collaborating closely with developers and testers to investigate technical issues, clarify requirements and coordinate solutions.

• Supporting the development and implementation of new functionality through requirements analysis, testing and refinement.

About you

You are curious, analytical and motivated by understanding how IT solutions work and how they support business processes. You enjoy investigating problems, asking questions and finding solutions in collaboration with others. You are comfortable communicating with different stakeholders and can translate complex issues into clear and actionable tasks.

We imagine that you have a relevant educational background and some experience working at the intersection of IT and business. Most importantly, you are eager to learn, take ownership and build specialized knowledge within banking and corporate credit.

jobs.occupation: Up to 3 PhD fellowships in Quantum error correction
jobs.description:
The Quantum error correction team at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) invites applicants for up to three PhD fellowships.

  The start date is (expected to be) 1 April, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The programme
 The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Program (NQCP), funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, is building a talented and diverse international team to create a cutting-edge program in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, where the formulation of Quantum Mechanics was born 100 years ago, the ambition is to build a mission-driven full-stack approach which will involve exciting innovations at every level, from the quantum processor to the quantum-classical interface, all the way to quantum algorithms and applications. The vision of the programme is to enable the development of fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve important problems in the life sciences.

  The project
 Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires low logical error rates together with resource-efficient, experimentally feasible approaches to quantum error correction. Our research spans low-overhead quantum error-correcting codes, efficient syndrome extraction, high-fidelity parity measurements, and scalable hardware architectures. We aim to connect these efforts with fault-tolerant logical operations, taking into account the noise characteristics, connectivity, and operational constraints of quantum computing platforms. In our work, we are collaborating closely with all of the different teams at NQCP; see nqcp.ku.dk.

  We are looking for up to three motivated PhD candidates to undertake research within theoretical effort for quantum error-correction. We are interested in developing a project plan with prospective candidates to best match their skills and experience to the activities in the QEC team. We imagine that the candidates would undertake research within one or more of the following topics:

   	
• Investigation of low-overhead and high-threshold error-correctable codes, including low-density parity check codes 	
• Resource estimation and optimization for scalable quantum computing over different hardware platforms 	
• Distributed quantum error correction on modular design and quantum networks 	
• Optimization of syndrome extraction circuits, error correction cycle, and fault-tolerant logical operation   Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of Physics, Computational Physics, Quantum Information, or a closely related field, with a focus on theoretical and/or computational quantum physics.

  Successful candidates will have:

   	
• Strong analytical and computational skills 	
• Strong knowledge of quantum mechanics and quantum information 	
• An interest in developing quantum error correction methods that account for hardware capabilities and limitations 	
• A passion for developing theoretical protocols 	
• Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a dynamic research environment 	
• Knowledge of quantum error correction or quantum computing platforms, including photonic systems and superconducting circuits, is an advantage.   Our group and research - and what do we offer?
 We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment hosted by the NNF Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) at the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen.

  The project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Maryam Khanahmadi, maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk, QEC team lead, and the principal supervisor will be Stefano Paesani, stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk.

  Qualifications needed 
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. a degree in Physics, Applied Physics, Photonics, Quantum Information or similar. For information on eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment 
 Employment as a PhD fellow is full-time and for a maximum of 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  Responsibilities and tasks in the PhD programme

   	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project   We are looking for the following qualifications:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project 	
• Relevant publications 	
• Relevant work experience 	
• Good language and communication skills 	
• Willingness to work in a team 	
• Willingness to engage actively with the other teams at NQCP    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Please note that there is the possibility of including an educational part to the PhD project. Therefore, please indicate in the application whether you would be interested in this.  	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original degree diplomas and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if possible) 	
• Reference letters (if available)   Application deadline
 The deadline for applications is 6 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1. 

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You will be notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process here.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Maryam Khanahmadi: maryam.khanahmadi@nbi.ku.dk

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: PhD in Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms
jobs.description:
The Department of Electronic Systems at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design invites applications for a 3-year PhD stipend in the field of quantum control theory for quantum algorithms within the general study programme Electronical and Electronic Engineering, as per January 1st 2027, or soon hereafter.

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 600 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model. The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide. You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

Your work tasks

The position is part of the research project QUANTA – Quantum Control Theory for Quantum Algorithms, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark. Real quantum computers are open quantum systems: noise and decoherence act on the computation while it runs, so the idealised picture of a sequence of perfect unitary gates acting on an isolated system does not hold in practice. QUANTA therefore regards a quantum program as an open dynamical system, described by Kraus operators in discrete time and by the controlled Lindblad master equation in continuous time, and treats the choice of quantum gates as control decisions. The aim is to use control theory to design quantum algorithms, in particular optimisation algorithms, that are robust to noise and disturbances.

As a PhD student you will work mainly on two parts of the project. The first concerns reach-avoidance for quantum systems: computing the probability that a quantum process reaches a target set of states before it enters a set of forbidden states, and designing control strategies, for example by dynamic programming, that steer the computation towards its goal while respecting such constraints. You will develop this theory for quantum Markov chains described by Kraus operators and for continuous-time systems described by the Lindblad master equation.

The second part applies these results to quantum optimisation. You will develop algorithms in which an optimisation problem, starting with semidefinite programming and continuing with bilinear and polynomial problems, is solved by a quantum system regarded as a control system, including constrained problems formulated as reach-avoidance. You will analyse how the resulting quantum circuits scale with the problem size and test the algorithms on a real quantum computer.

You will work closely with the principal investigator, a postdoctoral researcher on the project and the project's international collaborators, and the project includes research stays at partner institutions abroad. You will present your results at international conferences and in scientific journals, and they will form the basis of your PhD thesis. As part of the PhD programme you will follow PhD courses and take part in teaching and supervision of student projects at the department.

Your competencies You hold a Master's degree in control engineering, electrical engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer science or a related field. We are looking for a candidate with a solid mathematical background, for example in linear algebra, dynamical systems, control theory, optimisation or probability theory, and with a genuine interest in quantum computing.

Knowledge of quantum mechanics or quantum information is an advantage, but not a requirement – what matters is that you are motivated to learn it during the project. Programming experience, for example in Python, is also an advantage. We value curiosity, the ability to work independently and the willingness to share ideas and help colleagues. You communicate well in English, both orally and in writing.

Qualification requirements

PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Technical Doctoral School of IT and Design in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

jobs.description:
At the Faculty of Engineering and Science, AAU Energy, a 24-month postdoctoral position in Dynamic Modelling, Simulation and Optimization of Power-to-X Processes is available from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The project is primarily rooted in process engineering while also addressing interactions between Power-to-X plants and the electrical grid.

Your work tasks
You will develop and apply dynamic process models based on mass and energy balances, thermodynamics, reaction kinetics, and equipment behaviour to simulate integrated Power-to-X plants under changing operating conditions. The work will address renewable fuel production, particularly green methanol and sustainable aviation fuels through methanol-based and Fischer–Tropsch pathways. The work will focus on electrolysers, fuel-synthesis processes, energy storage, heat integration, and interactions with the electrical grid.

You will combine process simulation with operational optimization, process control, techno-economic assessment, and model validation to investigate flexible operation under varying renewable electricity generation and energy prices.

You will collaborate with academic and industrial partners, publish scientific results, contribute to project meetings and deliverables, and present findings at conferences and workshops. The position may also include limited teaching and supervision of bachelor’s and master’s students.

Your competencies
You hold a PhD in chemical engineering, process engineering, or a closely related field, completed by the application deadline. You have documented research experience in process modelling and simulation, preferably including dynamic modelling of chemical or energy processes.

Hands-on experience with Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS, or Aspen Dynamics will be considered a strong advantage. Experience with gPROMS, Modelica, or comparable process-simulation tools is also relevant. Strong skills in MATLAB, Python, or a similar computational environment are expected.

Experience with Power-to-X, renewable fuels, optimization, process control, model validation, techno-economic assessment, or grid-integrated energy systems will strengthen your profile.

You will work closely with industrial and international partners. Therefore, the ability to translate research into practical solutions and communicate effectively across disciplines is essential. We value candidates who are proactive, structured, collaborative, and motivated to publish high-quality research and contribute actively to project activities.

Who we are
You will join the Fluid & Process research group at AAU Energy, Campus Esbjerg, where you will become part of an international and interdisciplinary research environment combining process, chemical, energy and electrical engineering. The group works with modelling, simulation, control, optimization and experimental validation of fluid and energy systems, with applications including Power-to-X, carbon capture and utilization, green fuels and sector coupling. jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient retention in agricultural waters
jobs.description:
The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a two-year postdoc position in the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management in Aarhus, starting 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

The position combines research on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural nitrogen losses to surface waters with a synthesis of greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in mitigation measures for agricultural drainage water.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a two-year position from 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description

We are seeking a motivated postdoc to work on two closely linked research activities throughout the position.

Nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions from nitrogen that leaches from agricultural fields to streams, lakes and other water bodies are estimated to make up around 5% of the Danish agricultural sector’s greenhouse gas emissions, but this estimate is highly uncertain. The Aqua-N2O project, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF), aims to identify the drivers of these aquatic N2O emissions using high-frequency in-situ sensor monitoring, providing the scientific basis for modelling the emissions at regional scale and for evaluating mitigation strategies.

Drainage mitigation measures. Measures that intercept nutrients in agricultural drainage water before it reaches streams, such as surface flow and subsurface flow constructed wetlands, integrated buffer zones, saturated buffer zones and controlled drainage, are a key part of Danish water management. They can remove substantial amounts of nitrogen, but some may also release phosphorus and emit greenhouse gases such as N2O and methane. You will synthesise results on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention from Danish drainage mitigation measures to give an overall assessment of their environmental performance and trade-offs.

Your main tasks will be to:

• carry out fieldwork, including sensor deployment and water and gas sampling

• process and analyse high-frequency sensor data and monitoring data

• compile and synthesise existing data on greenhouse gas emissions and nitrogen and phosphorus retention in drainage mitigation measures

• write scientific papers for international peer-reviewed journals

Your profile

The successful candidate must hold a PhD degree in biogeochemistry, aquatic ecology, environmental science, hydrology or a related field, and have a valid driving licence, as the position involves fieldwork in Danish agricultural landscapes.

It is an advantage if you have:

• experience with measurements of greenhouse gases (e.g. N2O, CH4) in aquatic systems or soils

• knowledge of nitrogen and phosphorus cycling in agricultural catchments, wetlands or constructed wetlands

• experience with analysis of large or high-frequency datasets, e.g. in R or Python

• a documented record of publishing in international peer-reviewed journals

We are looking for a candidate who can work independently as well as in a team, and who has good written and spoken English.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience is engaged in research programs and advisory work covering the major biological sub-disciplines. We conduct innovative, advanced research in the areas of aquatic biology and ecology, Arctic environments and ecosystems, biodiversity, conservation biology, and wildlife management. The Department currently employs approximately 300 academic and technical staff, as well as many PhD students.

The successful candidate will work in a supportive and internationally engaged scientific environment at the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management. The section’s research and advisory work covers nutrient dynamics and hydrology, mitigation measures to reduce nutrient losses to the aquatic environment, and wetlands and greenhouse gases. The section has developed and tested many of the mitigation measures used in Danish water management, including constructed wetlands for treating drainage water, and advises national and international authorities.

The department aims to be a supportive and encouraging workplace that offers interesting challenges, collaborative colleagues, and avenues for academic growth. The department actively facilitates a healthy integration of work and personal life and aspires to recruit and maintain highly skilled individuals who prioritise curiosity and trust.

What we offer

The department offers:

• a well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment

• an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators

• a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research

• a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities

• a workplace characterised by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. Fieldwork will take place at sites in Denmark.

Contact information

For further information, please contact Senior Researcher Joachim Audet, joau@ecos.au.dk.

Deadline

Applications must be received no later than 1 December 2026.

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Technical Operations Manager, Technical Asset Performance DK
jobs.description:
Do you have solid technical know-how and a passion for contributing to the green transition? Then you might be our new Technical Operations Manager in Technical Asset Performance DK!

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Technical Operations Manager to join our dedicated Technical Asset Performance DK team. Based at our office in Hobro, you will be a central link between operations, projects and technical specialists.

Your role

You will play a key role in the performance, reliability and continuous optimization of our portfolio, taking ownership of complex technical topics and driving them from identification to resolution. You will work across Wind, BESS, PV and HV, with responsibilities ranging from daily operations to long-term optimization.

• End-to-end technical asset management, from infrastructure to component level

• Troubleshooting, root cause analysis and incident handling

• Planning and coordinating major maintenance activities and shutdowns

• Commissioning and integration of new parks and turbines

• Analyzing operational data and developing monitoring and performance platforms

• Collaboration with the surveillance team, service providers and contractors

• Technical reporting and sparring for internal and external stakeholders, including investor clarifications

Required competencies and skills

You have a solid technical background, preferably from renewable energy and asset management. You work in a structured, analytical way and balance technical excellence with an understanding of the commercial impact of your decisions.

• A technical education

• Experience within asset management

• Experience within several of Wind, BESS, PV and HV is an advantage

• A hands-on mindset and a strong technical toolbox

• Ability to work autonomously and drive tasks end-to-end

• Proficient English and flexibility to travel to sites a few times a year

• Driver's license (B); full GWO package is an advantage

What we offer

A dynamic role with a high degree of flexibility and variety, where priorities shift with operational needs, technical challenges and project timelines. You will report to Laurits H Østergaard, Manager, Technical Asset Performance DK, and join a dedicated team in our Hobro office, working closely with Asset Management colleagues in and outside Denmark.

• Hands-on ownership of technical topics across Wind, BESS, PV and HV

• Variety between daily operations, projects and deep technical investigations

• A culture where you can speak up, and support for your professional development

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Read more about Eurowind Energy A/S on our website or LinkedIn

Did we capture your attention?

Great! If you see yourself in this role, do not hesitate to apply for the position. Please use the link below. As we continuously review incoming applications, please send us your CV as soon as possible.

Should you have any questions before applying, please feel free to contact Laurits H Østergaard, Manager, Technical Asset Performance DK, at lauo@ewe.dk.

Application deadline:

As soon as possible

At KMD, we build digital solutions used by millions of people around the world. These solutions are the digital foundations of our most important institutions, from governments and public services to financial industries and private companies. Our mission is to ensure that they are reliable, accessible, and efficient.

We believe that the future is what you make it. So a career at KMD is a career with purpose and freedom. One where you’ll have a direct hand in improving the lives of people, while being empowered with the resources and autonomy to shape the course of your own professional journey.

Are you interested in how recruitment and HR-processes play out in a large Danish IT-company? Then you might be our new student Worker in the Talent Acquisition team in KMD!

We are expanding KMD’s Talent Acquisition team and are looking for a Student Worker to join us. The team is part of People, consisting of approximately 47 employees across Denmark and Poland. People supports KMD’s strategy and future direction, with attracting and selecting the right candidates playing a crucial role in achieving these goals.

About the job

The Talent Acquisition team consists of 7 people across Poland and Denmark. In Denmark, the team includes 1 Talent Acquisition Partner and 1 Student Worker. Together, we work towards the common goal of attracting and hiring the best candidates for KMD.

As a Student Worker, you will be part of the daily processes alongside the rest of the team and thus work with a broad spectrum of tasks related to recruitment. The tasks will consist of a mix of own responsibilities and ad-hoc support for the Talent Acquisition Partners and may include:

• Providing administrative support to the Talent Acquisition Partners

• Handling recruitment-related inquiries and managing communication via ServiceNow

• Conducting references

• Updating recruitment material in SharePoint

• Scheduling interviews

• Opportunity to participate in various projects depending on your interests and skills.

In addition to supporting the team with ad hoc recruitment tasks, you will work closely with another Student Worker to manage our student recruitment activities, including:

• Managing student recruitment processes end to end

• Working closely with Hiring Managers and leading recruitment kick-off meetings

• Providing feedback on cognitive assessments

• Handle contract creations.

This position is well suited for candidates considering a career in HR. You will be introduced to core HR and recruitment processes and gain insight into the strategy, goals, value chains and day-to-day operations in a large organization.

We offer an open, honest, and social office culture. As a KMD employee, you can expect a dynamic work environment with close collaboration across borders.

About you

• You are in your second or third year of a relevant bachelor’s and eager to learn about HR and recruitment

• You enjoy collaborating with various stakeholders and have a service-minded approach

• You are organized and detail-oriented

• You communicate fluently in both Danish and English

• You are comfortable using IT tools or are quick to learn new systems.

We work with SuccessFactors, ServiceNow, and Microsoft Office, and will provide thorough training on our tools and processes. We take pride in open communication and learning from each other.

Being a student in People and KMD

The working hours are approximately 15 hours per week. You will primarily work from our office in Ballerup, with the option to work from home. We offer flexibility during exam periods to support your studies.

As a Student Worker at KMD, you will have the opportunity to join our student network and participate in both social and professional events.

You will be supported by experienced colleagues in People and have ample opportunity to build a strong network across the organization through team activities, projects, and company-wide events.

Interested?

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. If you have any questions regarding the position, please feel free to contact Enas Karim at ekm@kmd.dk.

We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.description:
About Us

  NQCP is an ambitious and diverse international programme, located at the Niels Bohr Institute at University of Copenhagen. We are building a world-leading quantum computing programme, that will drive research and innovation at multiple levels, from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to solutions for the quantum-classical control and readout interface, and all the way to quantum algorithms and applications. 

  The programme is supported by Quantum Foundry Copenhagen, a company focused on enabling QPU  fabrication, and assembly and packaging technologies.

  Our program mission is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  About the Role
 We are looking for a Strategic Funding Officer to support the programme in securing external funding and building impactful scientific and industrial development collaborations. The role combines scientific pre-award grant support, strategic fundraising, and facilitation of interdisciplinary partnerships.

  A key responsibility is to identify opportunities for synergy across research groups and bring scientists together to develop competitive collaborative and consortium-based grant applications.

  The role requires you to work at the intersection of university research, innovation and industrial chip manufacturing. The position will eventually cover activities in both organizations, and activities related to Quantum Foundry Copenhagen will be contractually specified.

• Drive the programme’s external funding strategy for scientific and industrial collaborations. Identify and communicate relevant funding opportunities. 	
• Collaborate across research groups and organizations in developing high-quality grant proposals. 	
• Carry out writing for project proposals. 	
• Coordinate large and multidisciplinary funding applications including financial and technical reporting. 	
• Build partnerships with external researchers, funders, and stakeholders. 	
• Work closely with both the strategy team and communications to align funding activities.   Qualifications

   	
• Proven track record in securing substantial grants. 	
• Ability to work in Danish preferred. 	
• Experience setting up and managing research consortia involving academia and industry. 	
• Experience in supporting research applications, including EU calls. 	
• Strong understanding of research funding mechanisms. 	
• Excellent project management and communication skills. 	
• Strong stakeholder management and ability to advance our mission. 	
• Ability to engage and collaborate effectively with researchers across disciplines.

  You can conceptualize and drive a strategy forward. You are also scientifically curious, highly organized, and excel at connecting people and ideas. You enjoy working across disciplines and can translate funding opportunities into successful collaborative research initiatives.

  The ideal candidate is deeply committed to our overall mission and brings a strong sense of ownership to their work. Rather than just fitting into a team, they actively raise the performance of those around them and take accountability for the success of both organizations.

 A central role at the heart of NQCP’s mission, where you will help drive progress across two ambitious organizations. jobs.description:
If you are passionate about advanced MRI technology and want to contribute to the next generation of medical imaging, this PhD position offers a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of radiofrequency detector development in collaboration with leading international researchers in Denmark and Australia.

A typical MRI scanner uses radiofrequency detectors to image water molecules. Imaging other molecules and nuclei requires additional new detectors and antennas. The objective of the PhD project is to demonstrate MR imaging of nuclei other than hydrogen by building MRI detectors and antennas, which can cover frequencies of multiple nuclei.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The main outcome of the project will be a broadband/multinuclear detector array, ready to be implemented in clinical environment. It is a cross-disciplinary project and collaboration with the Department of Health Technology at DTU as well as other national and international institutions, such as University of Queensland, Aarhus University Hospital, GE Healthcare, DRCMR and others is an essential part. 

The tasks and responsibilities include:

• Literature study and evaluation of different multi-frequency detector configurations and identifying the most promising;
• Develop efficient element decoupling strategies minimizing noise correlation between array elements;
• Design and implement multinuclear multichannel radiofrequency coil array for MRI;
• Imaging experiments:
• Coordinate efforts on mechanical and electrical safety tests end approval for clinical use;
• Disseminate the project results to the public and exchange of knowledge with society.
The applicant will take part in research-based teaching. 

Contributing to the development of a good work atmosphere and a thriving environment is essential.

The candidate should have a master’s degree in engineering, preferably in electrical engineering.

It is an advantage to have experience in

• High frequency circuit design, fabrication and testing;
• Use of VNAs, spectrum analysers, noise figure meters and other measurement equipment in circuit testing;

You will build predictive models of expensive analytical calculations and simulations, and use AI to find good solutions to optimization problems that cannot be solved exactly within practical computing budgets. 

You will join the Embedded Systems Engineering section and work with Prof. Paul Pop. The application areas are related to, e.g., software-defined vehicles, datacenters, industrial automation, and energy systems.

• Develop surrogate models that predict results of complex analyses and simulations, such as execution delays, energy use, and resource demands.
• Use machine learning to guide configuration, scheduling, and resource allocation, reducing the need for expensive model evaluations.
• Evaluate solution quality, computing time, uncertainty, and transfer to new systems; check proposed solutions against the original models and constraints.
• Publish your research, collaborate with project partners, and contribute to teaching and student supervision.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

jobs.occupation: One or more PhD Stipends in Direct Air Capture Technologies
jobs.description:
The future of climate action extends beyond reducing emissions
Atmospheric CO2 concentrations continue to rise despite global efforts to reduce emissions. Achieving climate neutrality will therefore require not only deep emission reductions but also large-scale carbon removal solutions. Direct Air Capture (DAC) is one of the few technologies capable of permanently removing CO2 directly from the atmosphere, but significant scientific and engineering challenges remain before DAC can be deployed at gigaton scale. Future DAC systems must be energy-efficient, economically viable, and designed around a fundamental understanding of how materials, processes, and system integration interact.

At Aalborg University, we are seeking ambitious PhD candidates who want to help develop the next generation of DAC technologies through advanced process modelling, experimental studies, and techno-economic evaluations.

The stipend is open for appointment from 1 January 2027 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

In the future, removing CO2 from the atmosphere will become an essential part of climate action.
Atmospheric CO2 is already changing the climate. Reducing emissions is essential, but it may not be enough. We must also learn how to remove carbon already present in the atmosphere. Future Direct Air Capture systems will not simply capture CO2:

They will integrate with renewable energy systems. They will operate flexibly and balance the energy systems. They will become scalable climate infrastructure.

What this PhD is really about
The stipends are designed to contribute to two ambitious research initiatives that aim to accelerate the development of Direct Air Capture technologies:

Development of process-aware methodologies for evaluating emerging DAC liquid and solid sorbents and technologies. Development of predictive frameworks linking sorbent properties to process-level DAC performance.

Together, these efforts seek to establish the scientific foundations required to move DAC development from empirical trial-and-error toward predictive, data-driven design and scale-up.

The research environment and culture you will step into
You will join CarbonLab at Aalborg University, a growing research environment dedicated to carbon capture, carbon removal, and climate-positive technologies. We are a group of approximately 20 people currently represented by 7 different nationalities. Our research combines laboratory experiments, process modelling, experimental validation, techno-economic and LCA assessments, and system integration to accelerate the deployment of DAC solutions at scale.

At CarbonLab, we are building more than technologies; we are building a research community. Our researchers share ideas openly, collaborate across disciplines, and celebrate each other's successes. PhD students are treated as colleagues, encouraged to develop their own scientific identity, and supported in taking initiative from the very beginning. Whether presenting at international conferences, contributing to teaching, leading collaborations, or exploring new research directions, you will be part of a culture that combines scientific ambition with mutual trust and genuine support. We believe that excellent research and an excellent research environment go hand in hand.

Your research qualifications
We are looking for highly motivated candidates who are passionate about addressing climate change through scientific research and technological innovation. The ideal candidate has a strong analytical mindset, enjoys solving complex engineering challenges, and is eager to contribute to the development of next-generation carbon removal technologies.

You should hold a master's degree (or be close to completion) in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Energy Engineering, Chemistry, Physics, or a related discipline.

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

Direct Air Capture, carbon capture, or carbon removal technologies Chemical process engineering and process intensification Mass transfer, reaction engineering, and thermodynamics Experimental design and laboratory testing Spectroscopy and related analytical techniques such as Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR). Measurement and interpretation of gas-liquid and gas-solid equilibrium data and breakthrough experiments. Process modelling and simulation (e.g., Aspen Plus, MATLAB, Python, or similar tools) Data analysis, optimization, and uncertainty assessment Techno-economic analysis and sustainability assessment Energy systems integration and renewable energy technologies

In addition, we value candidates who:

Demonstrate scientific curiosity and creativity Take initiative and ownership of their research Enjoy working both independently and collaboratively Communicate scientific results effectively in written and spoken English Thrive in an interdisciplinary and international research environment Are motivated to contribute to solutions with real-world climate impact

Previous research experience through master's projects, internships, conference contributions, or scientific publications is considered an advantage but is not a formal requirement.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 872 of 6 October 2026 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are    
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners and other academic environments to address real-world energy challenges. The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and from a broad range of national backgrounds. This creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as the working language in research and teaching, which makes it straightforward for international colleagues to integrate. We offer access to advanced laboratories and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday life. New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Project description (2-5 pages), that describes the applicant’s initial thoughts and ideas related to the specific project applied for. This includes a brief state-of-the-art (including short list of references), a time schedule and how the applicant intends to shed light on the project objectives.
• Other relevant documents
The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position. 

Do you have any questions?     
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement).

The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a 2-year position as research assistant in marine taxonomy, focusing on phytoplankton, macroalgae and benthic fauna. The place of work is Aarhus, and the position starts on 1 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2-year fixed-term position from 1 January 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
Taxonomic expertise is the foundation of reliable knowledge about marine biodiversity, and of the monitoring that Danish authorities use to assess the state of the marine environment. You will help maintain and develop the department's taxonomic expertise and link it to new methods such as eDNA, ROV-based surveys and model-ling. Your tasks will include:

• Identification and quantification of phytoplankton, macroalgae and benthic fauna in samples from field surveys and monitoring programmes
• Data management, quality assurance and reporting as part of the department's advisory work for the Danish Environmental Protection Agency

You will work in close collaboration with experienced taxonomists and researchers at the Department of Ecoscience.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience conducts national and international research and advisory projects covering all major subdisciplines within marine, freshwater and terrestrial ecology. We are currently about 340 employees.

You will join the Section for Marine Ecology. Read more at AU Ecoscience - Research in marine ecology. For more information on the department, see https://ecos.au.dk/en/.

Contact information

For further information, please contact: Head of Section, Annette Bruhn, +45 2963 8034, anbe@ecos.au.dk.

Application procedure
Short-listing is used. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.
