Join Our Mission Toward a Safe Digital Future

If you truly want to make a difference and make our world a little bit safer, this is the place for you. At Truesec, you’ll get to be at the forefront of fighting cybercrime instead of reading about it in the news. This is your chance to be part of an exciting journey in a leading cybersecurity company – and learn from some of the best in their field.

So, are you ready to team up with the most dedicated team of experts and be part of a meaningful mission? Then we are excited to get to know you!

We’re looking for a product engineer to help us build better tools for legal research. You’ll work mainly on the backend, with a say in what we build and responsibility for taking it from an early idea to something customers use every day. That includes asking whether we’re solving the right problem, deciding what’s worth shipping first, and knowing when something needs more time.

About Pandektes

Our mission is to rebuild legal research from the ground up. Lawyers still lose countless hours to fragmented sources, outdated systems, and databases that fight them at every turn. We're building the largest AI-powered legal database in the world to make that friction disappear.

We're a team of 40+ based in our Copenhagen HQ, Zurich, London, and Hamburg. We’re a small team with high trust and flat structure. We move fast, argue our positions, and ship. If your input is good, it gets implemented - often within hours, not sprints.

We have has raised more than €4M, including a €2.9M seed round (Feb 2025) led by People Ventures, Interface Capital, and a strong bench of angels. We already serve 400+ customers across Denmark, Germany, and Switzerland, and we're just getting started.

What we value

“How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

Knowing which question to ask is a big part of being an engineer here.

Knowing when it’s good enough

We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

We value people who can find a smaller version worth shipping, explain the trade-offs, and follow through once customers start using it.

Knowing when to slow down

Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.

You’ll have room to make those calls here, and teammates who will question them. We expect you to do the same for us.

Make time to experiment

We enjoy trying things before we know whether they’ll work. A new tool, a different way to use an agent, an idea that might turn out to be useless. Finding out is part of the work.

Once a month, we get together to demo our setups, show what we’re experimenting with, and share what we’ve learned. Sometimes we invite people from outside the team to show us how they work. Those sessions have changed how we build software.

We value curiosity and the generosity to bring other people along. If you find something useful, show us. If an experiment fails, we’d like to hear about that too.

We try to watch this video once a month to keep this value top of mind.

The experience you’ll bring

You’ve built and operated backend systems that real customers depend on. You can work through questions about data, APIs, performance, and security, and explain the consequences of your decisions.

Our stack includes TypeScript, NestJS, GraphQL, Postgres, and Prisma. We also work with OpenAI and Turbopuffer. Experience with these tools is useful; we’re especially interested in what you’ve built with them and the decisions you made along the way.

You enjoy working through a product problem while it’s still taking shape. You ask questions, share unfinished work, and help decide what’s worth building. You’re comfortable taking a feature from those early conversations through implementation, testing, and delivery.

What we offer

You’ll join at a point where there’s still a lot to shape. We offer competitive pay and equity so you can share in the success you help create.

We are usually office based but we all work from home time to time. You’ll have your own Pleo card for the tools and work expenses you need, plus 25 vacation days a year, public holidays, and paid parental leave when your family grows.

We also make time to get together away from our usual work. Our last team trip was to Barcelona, and we’d love to have you along for the next one.

Pandektes is an equal opportunity employer

We believe diverse teams build better products and stronger teams. We embrace and encourage people from all backgrounds to apply regardless of race/ethnicity, colour, religion, nationality, gender, sex, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, socio-economic status, culture or beliefs.

Legal professionals should be able to stand behind every answer. We build the foundation for that: verified legal data, complete across time and traceable to its source, with research tools built for confident legal judgment. Our vision is clear: to be the leading platform for legal information retrieval, enabling in-depth and accurate legal knowledge in a fast, efficient and user-friendly way using artificial intelligence.

jobs.occupation: Tenure track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor Position in the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Mekanik og Produ
jobs.description:
The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering (MPE) at Aarhus University is consolidating its research and teaching activities within the field of Design and Manufacturing and invites applications for a Tenure Track Assistant Professor/Associate Professor within the field of design and manufacturing from July 1st, 2027 or as soon as possible.

The MPE Department seeks an innovative and visionary researcher capable of establishing and leading an internationally recognized research group and delivering research-based teaching at the Bachelor, Master & PhD levels. The chosen candidate is expected to establish effective and visible research programs, develop local and international research collaborations, attract external funding, and contribute to our mechanical engineering bachelor and master programs with teaching at an international level

We welcome candidates with interdisciplinary research backgrounds who can help realize our vision of creating lasting impact by guiding the shift toward a resilient and sustainable industry, society, and planet.

For this open position, we are seeking candidates to advance research in resilient and sustainable design of products and manufacturing solutions.

We prefer candidates that can demonstrate the potential for industrial application of their research. The candidate should bridge existing fields in the section and department, and we encourage applicants to address potential synergies in our educational programs and research activities.

The selected candidate will be required to teach relevant courses in the MPE educational program at the B.Sc., M.Sc., and PhD levels of the Mechanical and Production Engineering programs. 

Expected start date 
July 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible.

To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:
To meet expectations in this role, we expect the candidate to fulfill the following requirements:
- PhD or equivalent in Mechanical or Production Engineering or a closely related subject area.
- Substantial experience conducting high-quality research in the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing with publications in leading international journals that match career stage.
- Familiarity with experimental, computational, or theoretical research method.
- Interest in and prior experience with interdisciplinary collaboration across engineering disciplines and with industry is desired.
- For the position as associate professor, the applicants should, in addition, have:
- Documented teaching experience and a clear commitment to teaching and advancing mechanical engineering courses within the field of Sustainable Design and Manufacturing, from introductory undergraduate instruction through master’s and PhD-level study
- Documented record of self-directed research leadership, external funding acquisition, supervision of PhD students, and teaching and course development at university level.
- The candidate should have proficient communication skills in English.
- It is an advantage if the candidate has the ability or is willing to develop their communication skills in Danish.

Who we are
The engineering field in Aarhus University is evolving with a rapid growth in student population, major research initiatives as well as through the establishment of a number of new physical facilities in the city center of Aarhus. We have comprehensive plans for increased activities in research and education, as well as public and industrial cooperation. The Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering within the Faculty of Technical Sciences has cooperation with universities and advisory service providers in more than 20 countries. The engineering field at Aarhus University is well established with extensive research activities, over 700 mechanical engineering students and a long tradition of industrial cooperation that we wish to extend significantly.

What we offer 
The department offers:
- research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment 
- an exciting interdisciplinary environment with many national, international and industrial collaborators
- a research climate encouraging lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
- a work environment with close working relationships, networking and social activities
- a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance 

Place of work and area of employment 
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Mechanical and Production Engineering, Katrinebjergvej 89, DK-8200 Aarhus N, Denmark.

Contact information
For more information about the position contact Deputy Head of Department for Research Charles Møller (charles@mpe.au.dk / +45 61677786) or Head of Section Ramin Aghababaei ( ra@mpe.au.dk / +45 93508956)

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than January 4th 2027.

Technical Sciences Tenure Track
Aarhus University offers talented scientists from around the world attractive career perspectives via the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme. Highly qualified candidates are appointed as Assistant Professors for a period of six years with the prospect of performance- based advancement to a tenured Associate Professorship. 

The aim of the Technical Sciences Tenure Track Programme is to:

• attract outstanding talented individuals that are competitive at an international level
• to promote the early development of independent research success early in the career of scientists
• to create transparency in the academic career path
As part of the tenure track position, the candidate is offered:

• access to research infrastructure
• capability development, including postgraduate teacher training
• a mentoring programme
• support to develop scientific networks and to secure interdisciplinary research at the highest level
As part of the Aarhus University Tenure Track Programme, the University carries out a mid-way evaluation to review the progress of the tenure track candidate after three years, according to the same criteria used in the final tenure review. The final tenure review is conducted after five and a half years. If the review is positive, the candidate will be offered a tenured position as Associate Professor at Aarhus University.

Please refer to the tenure track guidelines for the tenure review criteria and for the tenure review process.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation. 

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

Job Description

Are you looking for a chance to design complete sorting systems to BEUMER customers ?

We are looking for a Mechanical System Designer to support the Logistics Sales team in BEUMER Group Denmark during the quotation process with focus on layout design for new sorting systems.

Layout design of new sorting systems

As Mechanical System Designer, you will be involved in the system design from the very first customer request. During the quotation process you will be working closely with the technical colleagues from the department to develop a complete sortation solution which meets the customer's expectations. You will be the key person for preparing layout in AutoCAD and designing solutions which includes all necessary equipment to fulfil the sortation requirements defined by the customer.

You will join the Sales & System team in Aarhus, and you will mainly be working together with colleagues in the core design team. The team in Aarhus is also supporting projects in BEUMER Group worldwide, which means that you will also be working together with international colleagues.

The main responsibilities within the job are:

• To prepare 3D sales layouts in AutoCAD for sorting systems quoted to customers worldwide

• To implement BEUMER Group equipment as well as equipment from external suppliers into overall layouts which are used in the sales process.

• To ensure that our design rules are incorporated into the layout in close cooperation with the experienced technical colleagues of the Sales & System team

• To keep the drawing database updated in close cooperation with colleagues in the team.

Strong team player mindset

The daily work is involving different colleagues depending on the individual project, so it is important that you enjoy being part of a team to find the right system solutions. As the design is prepared in close dialog with customers, ideas and layouts might be changed several times during the quotation process. An important part of the job is therefore to keep up the motivation for finding the right system solution together with the quotation team during this process and customer dialog.

We are looking for someone with the following key qualifications:

• Technical education as an engineer, e.g. mechanical or marine engineer.

• Experience in preparing technical solutions within 3D AutoCAD.

• Ready to participate in customer meetings and presenting technical solutions.

• Used to communication in English.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position before sending us your application and CV, please contact Director System Design and proposal, Jens Ege on +45 3066 5178. Invite for interviews will be on an ongoing basis.

BEUMER Group

Conveying, loading, palletising, packing, sortation and distribution – BEUMER Group is a leader within the development and manufacture of high-technological intralogistics systems for global markets. Our employees stand out from others thanks to their ability to supply innovative solutions to our customers. They can do this because they know the industry and are passionate about continuously developing and expanding their knowledge. We support these high standards through teamwork, mutual respect and a work culture based on trust that fosters stability and security for all of our employees. Our common goal is to implement outstanding and innovative projects worldwide.

Your models might start in Python. Their impact goes far beyond it.

Your career in data science might only just be getting started. At NORDEN, you will apply it to real logistics challenges involving vessels, ports, terminals, weather and cargo flows.

At NORDEN, moving cargo from A to B involves vessels, ports, terminals, weather, cargo flows and countless operational constraints. Understanding how all those pieces interact can make a real difference to the decisions we make and at the end our base margin.

As our new Data Scientist in Maritime Logistics, you will turn that complexity into models we can explore, test and learn from, helping us make better operational and commercial decisions.

You do not need years of experience or deep shipping knowledge. What matters is a strong foundation in Python and supply chains and the curiosity to apply it to the real world.

Why this role?

Because you get to take problems that exist in the real world and build models that help us understand what could happen next.

You might be modelling how vessels move through a logistics network, exploring the capacity of a terminal or testing what happens when weather, congestion or operational constraints change. Other times, you could be looking at historical data, improving an existing model or helping colleagues understand what different scenarios could mean commercially and operationally.

A central part of your role will be translating complex logistics systems into simulations that allow us to ask better questions before decisions are made in the real world.

You will work closely with commercial and operational colleagues while learning from experienced colleagues within analytics and shipping. Our broader Quantitative Analytics environment works with Python and technologies including Prefect, Docker and Azure and you will also gain practical experience developing solutions and visualisations using Power BI.

What you will be doing

You will work where shipping, logistics and data science meet. Helping us continuously improve how we work with simulation, optimisation, analytics and software development.

To be more specific you will:

• Design and develop simulation models of supply chains and maritime logistics operations.

• Use discrete-event simulation and agent-based modelling to represent vessels, terminals, ports and other parts of complex logistics systems.

• Analyse logistics networks and explore opportunities to improve capacity, throughput, utilisation and operational efficiency.

• Use historical and operational data to calibrate, validate and continuously improve your models.

• Build analytical tools that allow colleagues to explore scenarios and understand their operational and commercial implications.

• Develop robust analytical models and simulation solutions in Python.

• Create visualisations that make complex outputs easier to understand and use.

What you bring

There is no need to understand every aspect of shipping or every modelling method from day one. What matters is that you have a good analytical foundation, an understanding of supply chains and logistics and the curiosity to keep learning.

Qualification we are looking for:

• Have 0–3 years of relevant professional experience.

• Hold a degree in Supply Chain Management and Logistics, industrial engineering, operations research or another relevant quantitative field.

• Have a good foundation in Python and are comfortable writing structured, maintainable analytical code.

• Are fluent in English, our working language.

• Are eligible to work in Denmark.

What matters just as much is how you work with people. You are curious about how complex operations actually work, you ask questions before jumping to the model and you can explain what your analysis means to colleagues who may never open a line of Python themselves.

Application

Please upload your motivation letter, resume and relevant diplomas via our website as soon as possible and no later than 22 November 2026. Your motivation letter helps us understand what drives you, why you are interested in the role, and how your skills and experiences could contribute to the team. We are especially interested in your motivation and transferable skills, not a recap of your CV. It is your opportunity to tell us the story behind your application.

We review and interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

We will do our best to get back to you at least within ten working days after the application deadline, 22 November 2026.

In NORDEN we value a range of perspectives, educational backgrounds and professional experience and encourages all qualified candidates to apply.

We are a global provider of ocean- based freight services for bulk and project cargo of all sizes. We integrate freight solutions with port logistics, helping our customers optimise and decarbonise supply chains. We provide tailored solutions built on flexibility, reliability, and intelligence.

Our agile business model ensures stability by continuously adapting our fleet to market developments and customer needs.

Founded in 1871, NORDEN is one of Denmark’s oldest internationally operating shipping companies. Incorporated in Denmark, we are listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen as part of the OMX Nordic Large Cap index.

With offices across 6 continents, we are a truly integrated part of global trade.

jobs.occupation: Professor / Associate Professor / Senior Researcher taking lead in Catchment and Freshwater Ecosystem sciences
jobs.description:
Are you an engaged, leading scientist of international standing, with deep expertise in the research of catchments and freshwater ecosystems, and excellent science leadership skills? Do you have the scientific vision to guide the strategic direction for a nationally and internationally recognized research community working with catchments, wetlands, lakes, streams and nature-based solutions?

The Department of Ecoscience at Aarhus University invites applications for a full-time permanent scientific position (Full Professor, Associate Professor, or Senior Researcher) in the Catchment science and Freshwater Ecology (CaFE) focus area. We are looking for a scientist who enjoys taking lead and working strategically with organizational impact covering the range of research areas in CaFE.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a permanent position from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.

Job description

The position centers around research and research based advisory in catchment processes and freshwater ecosystems – including wetlands, streams and lakes and the landscapes like forests, agricultural areas etc. that surround them.  We expect the candidates to have expertise and track record with one or more of the key thematic areas:

• Hydrology and the retention and transport of nutrients and hazardous substances

• Biogeochemical processes and emissions of greenhouse gases from land and water bodies, including interactions with carbon and nutrient dynamics

• Freshwater ecology and the links between abiotic and biotic processes, including ecosystem functioning, biodiversity, and responses to human pressures and climate change

• Nature-based solutions and ecosystem restoration to strengthen biodiversity and resilience and reduce nutrient loss, limit greenhouse gas emissions and regulate water flow in the landscape

• Combining long-term monitoring data with novel research using laboratory, mesocosm and field experiments, in situ sensor data and catchment- and ecosystem modelling

At Department of Ecoscience, all scientific staff in general are expected to contribute to external income generation, dissemination of knowledge, and talent development. Your specific scientific responsibilities may also include:

• Taking the lead on the development and implementation of the CaFE focus area strategy as part of the Department’s strategy, Ecoscience 2030 – including formulating concrete goals and action plans for implementation in dialogue with colleagues and the Department’s management

• Setting the direction and fostering a strong and inclusive research environment across the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions

• Bringing our research and knowledge to Danish ministries and agencies as well as to other relevant national, European and international decision makers through science-based advice, making an impact for the society around us

• Promoting innovation within the focus area and wider department by fostering use of new and/or novel technologies through closer dialogue and interaction with other sections/focus area within the department and across the faculty

• Supporting the scientific development and career paths of colleagues in the focus area

Your profile

We are looking for a scientist with a strong research track record as well as documented experience with science-based advisory work and leadership of research staff. You have expertise within catchment science and freshwater ecology, previous experience working in interdisciplinary teams and from broad sectoral collaborations. Applicants must hold a PhD in hydrology, limnology, freshwater ecology, biogeochemistry, environmental science, physical geography, environmental engineering or a closely related discipline. The level of appointment (Full Professor, Associate Professor or Senior Researcher) will be determined based on qualifications.

We value in particular:

• Excellent leadership experience from similar research environments; e.g., leading larger research groups and taking responsibility for strategic development of larger units (academic citizenship)

• Skills in strategic scientific coordination, strategy development, project management, and building research networks

• An established international network, collaborative skills and relationships within catchment science and/or freshwater ecology and nature-based solutions

• Documented experience in securing and leading externally funded research projects

• Documented experience with science-based advisory work and engagement with authorities and other stakeholders

Excellent written and spoken English; Strong Danish language skills are an advantage.

Who we are

The Department of Ecoscience, with approximately 300 employees in Aarhus and Roskilde, is one of Denmark's leading research environments in applied ecology, spanning terrestrial, freshwater, marine, and Arctic ecosystems. We conduct both fundamental and applied research and deliver Science-based advisory services to authorities in Denmark and Greenland. Our work is grounded in long-term monitoring, field-based data collection, and advanced modelling, and we pride ourselves on a research culture characterized by high scientific integrity, strong interdisciplinary collaboration, and societal relevance. Our values are impact, professionalism, curiosity, collaboration and trust.

CaFE is the department's focus area for catchment science and freshwater ecology, integrating the Section for Catchment Science and Environmental Management, the Section for Freshwater Ecology and the Centre for Nature-based Solutions. We are around 80 research and technical employees working to generate the data and knowledge that qualify decision-making on conservation and recovery of deteriorated wetlands and inland waters. Our vision is to maintain and expand our position as the key national focal point for applied research and modelling within catchment processes and freshwater ecosystem dynamics, helping authorities monitor, manage and mitigate human impacts on wetlands and freshwaters.

We combine long-term monitoring data with experimental approaches and modelling, and we have the strongest national scientific environment within modelling of nutrient transport, biogeochemical processes in wetlands, experimental freshwater ecology, lake ecosystem modelling and lake restoration. Key infrastructure includes a series of living labs in constructed wetlands, lakes, ponds and streams, including the semi-field mesocosm lake experiments at Lemming that have been running for more than 30 years.

Find out more about our current strategy, departmental values and more here: https://ecos.au.dk/en/about-us/au-ecoscience-our-strategy

What we offer

• A full-time permanent scientific position with an internationally competitive research environment and access to unique long-term datasets and world-class field and semi-field infrastructure

• A central role in shaping the scientific direction of CaFE, contributing actively to the focus area strategy under Ecoscience 2030 and beyond

• An interdisciplinary and dynamic working environment across catchment, freshwater, terrestrial, marine and Arctic research

• Highly engaged, motivated and positive colleagues and an innovative and dynamic working environment, where culture and values are important

• A working environment characterized by high scientific standards, trust, and well-being

• Close, trust-based relationships with Danish ministries and agencies and strong national and international research networks

• Access to professional support for international researchers and their families relocating to Denmark

For candidates with the right qualifications and experience in strategic research leadership, a temporary role as Deputy Head of Department with responsibility for the CaFE focus area of the Department of Ecoscience will be possible. This role includes participation in the Department’s management group. Further education/competence building in leadership will be offered. Contact the Head of Department (details below) for a more detailed description of this role.

Place of work and area of employment

The place of work is AU Campus Aarhus, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Head of Department Mikkel Tamstorf (mpt@ecos.au.dk; +45 53 57 50 44).

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment.

Formalities and salary range

Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

You will become part of an international company where you gain hands-on experience, take ownership of your own tasks, and collaborate with stakeholders across the organization.

You will collaborate with functions such as Category Management, Strategic Sourcing, Legal, Finance, Logistics, Operations, and HSEQ. In doing so, you will help translate business needs and category strategies into competitive agreements and measurable value.

Key Responsibilities

• Support sourcing and tender activities, including collecting quotations and comparing supplier solutions.

• Contribute to supplier onboarding, maintenance of supplier data, and follow-up on deliveries and supplier performance.

• Manage contract documentation, procurement data, and other procurement-related records.

• Prepare reports, dashboards, and analyses covering spend, savings, KPIs, and supplier performance.

• Assist with process mapping, improvement initiatives, and the development of templates and frameworks within procurement and supply chain.

Who Are You?

You are analytical and structured, with strong attention to detail while maintaining an understanding of the broader business context. You are curious about procurement and supply chain management and motivated by turning data into actionable insights.

You take ownership of your responsibilities, work independently, and enjoy collaborating across different functions. We do not expect you to know everything from day one, but we do value a proactive mindset and a willingness to learn.

We Imagine That You:

You will become part of CRH Denmark's Supply Chain organization, where we are constantly striving to raise the bar. We rarely accept "the way we've always done it" or standard solutions if there is a better alternative.

I believe the best results are created through trust, collaboration, and a shared commitment to learning and improving. I hope you'll bring your own perspective, challenge us with fresh ideas, and contribute to the team's development as you grow in the role.

My role is to provide direction, sparring, and support so that you can succeed, deliver results, develop your skills, and take the next step in your career. I value open and honest dialogue, where we challenge each other, learn along the way, and turn good ideas into action and results.

What We Offer

• Collaboration with a broad range of business functions and subject matter experts.

Brand

Danfoss engineers solutions that increase machine productivity, reduce emissions, lower energy consumption, and enable electrification.

Our solutions are used in areas such as refrigeration, air conditioning, heating, power conversion, motor control, industrial machinery, marine, and on- and off-highway equipment. We also provide solutions for data centers, renewable energy, energy storage, heat recovery, as well as contribute to district energy solutions for cities.

Lead engineering at a profitable, funded proptech while the team is still small enough to shape.

• Want to set the technical direction for a growing team and still ship code yourself?

• How would you keep a small team shipping to production many times a day, with review and testing that catch problems before customers do, without every decision landing on your desk?

• Where would you draw the line between what an AI agent should suggest and what it can do on a property owner’s behalf?

Sounds like you? Then you might be our next CTO!

A property owner with a portfolio of buildings has a practical question: which repairs belong in next year’s budget, and which can wait? At Proprty.ai, our models estimate the condition and remaining life of building components and the energy and CO2 effect of improving them. Our software turns those estimates into maintenance plans, and our AI agent, Tily, helps owners analyze their portfolios and take action!

Our product went live in 2024 and is used by customers in Denmark, Norway and Germany. We reached profitability by the end of 2025 and raised DKK 21 million in April 2026, and we are not planning to stop there!

There is still so much we can do to make it even better, and you could help shape the future of building maintenance and how engineering is run at Proprty.ai.

Product: TypeScript, React, and Next.js on Vercel, with Supabase (PostgreSQL, row-level security, storage).**

Data and models: Python and PySpark on Databricks (Azure, EU), Python model services, and LLM features on Azure OpenAI. We also run a customer API and an MCP server.

What you get to shape

The team and the code.

You'll lead our product engineering team, work closely with our data engineers and our Chief Data Science Officer, and keep building core features yourself. You might coach a developer through a tricky problem in the morning and ship a feature yourself that afternoon. You'll own engineering hiring as the team grows, from deciding which roles we need to choosing the people you want on the team.

How we build and ship.

You’ll own the platform’s architecture and how we test and release. We release to production many times a day. Your job is to keep that pace while making every release reliable and secure. When an urgent customer request competes with longer-term platform work, you’ll make the call and explain what comes first and why.

Shape what Tily can do next.

Our data scientists build models for building condition, remaining life, cost, and energy across several European markets. Together with our Chief Data Science Officer, you'll get those models in front of customers, decide what Tily may do on an owner's behalf, and use feedback from property owners, Sales, and Customer Success to choose the next problems to solve.

Change how we use AI ourselves.

Change how we use AI ourselves. Our engineers build with Claude Code and Cursor, AI agents review every pull request in our CI/CD pipeline, and agents take on routine work end to end so the team can ship faster. We keep looking for new ways AI can raise our pace, and you'll lead that.

We talk a lot (in a good way). When a problem gets tricky, we pull up a chair and pair on it. We like having a laugh while we figure things out.

What you’ll bring?

You've been CTO or head of engineering at a startup or scale-up while the product, the team, and the rules were still taking shape, and you can show what changed because you were there. You know when to open a pull request yourself, when to let another engineer make the call, and which shortcut will come back to bite you two releases from now.

You bring curiosity about our industry, our customers' problems, and the business acumen to understand how our product delivers business value, so that you can help facilitate features that drive outcomes and make our users' lives easier.

We’re AI-first (the name’s a bit of a giveaway). If you’ve built an agent or shipped an AI feature, we’d love to hear what happened after the demo. What did customers trust it to do, and where did they want the controls back? You’ll get to make those calls with Tily and figure out where AI helps our own engineers ship better software.

The core of what we consider for a candidate

• You’ve led an engineering team, coached developers, and hired people to join it.

• You’re keen to build AI agents that customers can put to work and to explore where AI makes your own team more effective.

• You still build full-stack features with React, TypeScript, and SQL. You can take a feature from technical design through thoughtful user experience to release, and measure what happens when customers get their hands on it.

• Fluent in English

Experience we’d love to hear about

• Taking an engineering team from a startup to a scale-up phase, understanding how and when to mature processes as the team scales, and how that looks different in this new AI era.

• Shipping an AI agent or feature into production. We’re especially curious about what you changed after people started using it.

• How you’ve spoken with customers and industry experts to help ensure we’re on the forefront of solving the right problems in our platform

• Your perspective on the role of a CTO as a thought leader.

• Working with PostgreSQL or Next.js, or building products for real estate or proptech.

Where we work

We spend 4 days a week together in our office near Rådhuspladsen. You’ll need to be based in the Copenhagen area, as we can’t offer relocation or visa sponsorship for this role.

New to proptech? That’s fine. If you’ve led engineers and still enjoy being one, we’d love to hear from you.

Questions? Reach out to Casper Høgh at Csh@ing.dk, who helps us land the right human for the job

Our hiring process

• 
Intro call with Casper Høgh – We’ll talk about your background, what you want from your next CTO role, and any questions you have about proprty.ai.

• 
In-person interview – Meet us at our Copenhagen office for a small demo and talk through the team, the decisions you’d own, and how you like to lead while staying hands-on.

• 
Case interview – Work through an engineering scenario with us. We want to understand what you’d prioritize, which trade-offs you see, and why.

• 
Board interview - Meet with one of our board members. Get their perspective on our journey and talk them through how you would help us in our next phase of growth.

• 
Offer – If we both see a fit, we’ll talk through the offer and next steps together.

TL;DR

Want to get in early with a great team? Love leading engineers and still writing code?

Apply now to lead our dev team and make building maintenance smarter and more sustainable with AI.

jobs.description:
Do you have solid experience in welding and tack welding, and do you thrive in a structured environment with clear expectations and a strong focus on quality and precision? At Give Steel A/S, you will become an important part of our weekend day shift production team, where your contribution helps ensure strong, documented steel structures.

Why Choose Us?

You will become part of a manufacturing engineering and steel construction company with a strong focus on quality, safety, and responsible production. We are committed to employee development and offer a workplace with freedom under responsibility, well-organised working conditions, and opportunities for professional growth.

You will be employed under the Danish Collective Agreement for the Industry Sector (Industriens Overenskomst). In addition, we offer private health insurance and the option to join our canteen scheme.

What Will Your Workday Look Like?

You will join a team manufacturing load-bearing steel structures and steel trusses. The work is carried out on the weekend day shift, where you will follow established work procedures and contribute to ensuring tasks are completed safely, efficiently, and to a high standard of quality.

Your working hours will be from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Tack welding and welding steel structures based on technical drawings and work instructions

• Preparing components and checking measurements, fit, and quality

• Carrying out tasks with a systematic and thorough approach

• Contributing to strong teamwork with colleagues in production

• Complying with all applicable safety, quality, and documentation requirements

What Are We Looking For?

We are looking for an experienced and reliable employee who works in a structured and detail-oriented manner. You thrive in a well-defined environment, can maintain an overview in a busy production setting, and take pride in delivering lasting, high-quality results.

We expect that you:

• Have solid experience as a welder and/or tack welder

• Work thoroughly, responsibly, and with a strong focus on quality

• Can read and understand technical drawings

• Are reliable and a team player

• Contribute positively to a professional and safe working environment

• Speak Danish and/or English

• Live in Denmark within a reasonable commuting distance of Brande

We can provide certification in various welding methods, so it is not important whether you already hold welding certificates.

Interested?

If you have any questions about the position, please contact our Head of Production, Tomas Slepavicius, at tsl@givesteel.com.

We would like to receive your CV, clearly outlining your relevant experience. We are looking for someone who can start as soon as possible, and we will remove the job advertisement once the position has been filled.

About Give Steel A/S

Give Steel A/S is a manufacturing engineering and steel construction company that develops, designs, manufactures, and erects load-bearing steel structures and steel trusses. Quality, safety, and documentation are an integral part of our daily operations, while we also maintain a strong focus on CO₂ reduction and responsible production.

You will become part of an international company with strong technical expertise and opportunities for professional development. Collaboration, responsibility, and integrity are key values in our daily work.

jobs.description:
Har du hænderne skruet rigtigt på, og er du klar på nye udfordringer? Så er det måske dig, vi mangler!

Hos Weisleder Nedrivning har vi rigtig travlt og oplever stor efterspørgsel på vores arbejde. Derfor søger vi løbende dygtige og engagerede nedrivere, som har lyst til at blive en del af vores team.

Vi søger medarbejdere, der ikke er bange for at tage fat, trives med fysisk arbejde og har lyst til en hverdag med spændende og varierede opgaver inden for nedrivning.

Vi forestiller os, at du:

• 
Er mødestabil, ansvarsbevidst og har en positiv indstilling.

• 
Har hænderne godt skruet på og ikke er bange for at tage fat.

• 
Kan arbejde både selvstændigt og sammen med dine kollegaer.

• 
Er kvalitetsbevidst og går op i at udføre et ordentligt stykke arbejde.

• 
Har en god fysik og trives med praktisk arbejde.

• 
Er fleksibel og klar på forskellige typer opgaver.

• 
Har erfaring med nedrivning og miljøsanering

Vi tilbyder:

• 
En arbejdsplads med masser af aktivitet og spændende opgaver.

• 
Gode kollegaer og et godt arbejdsmiljø.

• 
En varieret hverdag, hvor ikke to dage nødvendigvis er ens.

• 
Mulighed for at udvikle dine kompetencer inden for nedrivningsbranchen.

• 
Løn efter kvalifikationer.

• 
Mulighed for at blive en del af en virksomhed i udvikling med masser at se til.

HVORNÅR SKAL DU STARTE?

Vi søger løbende nye medarbejdere og ønsker at ansætte hurtigst muligt. Så hvis du kan starte med kort varsel, hører vi meget gerne fra dig!

Du behøver ikke vente på et bestemt ansøgningsfrist – vi tager imod henvendelser løbende og indkalder relevante kandidater til en snak.

LYDER DET SOM NOGET FOR DIG?

Så tøv ikke med at kontakte os og sende dit CV- vi har brug for dig!

English Version

Weisleder Nedrivning is looking for reliable, motivated demolition workers to join their growing team. Candidates should be physically fit, hands-on, flexible, and able to work independently as well as in a team. Experience in demolition and environmental remediation is preferred. The company offers varied tasks, a good working environment, opportunities for professional development, and competitive pay based on qualifications. Immediate start is possible, and applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

PROJEKTLEDER – FACTSPILOT.COM

Internationalt medieprojekt · AI · Faktatjek · EU-finansiering

Vil du stå i spidsen for udviklingen af en international medieplatform med ambitioner om at arbejde på tværs af Europas lande og sprog?

MinBy™ søger en ambitiøs, selvstændig og resultatorienteret projektleder til Factspilot.com – et internationalt medie- og teknologiprojekt med fokus på journalistik, faktatjek, AI, oversættelse og distribution af nyheder.

Vi søger en person, der kan omsætte en ambitiøs idé til et konkret, finansieret og operationelt projekt.

En central indledende opgave bliver at undersøge, udvikle og koordinere en ansøgning til EU-programmet Creative Europe – Journalism Partnerships, herunder etablering af relevante europæiske samarbejdspartnere.

Det er en stilling for dig, der kan kombinere strategisk forståelse, international projektledelse, finansiering og praktisk gennemførelse.

OM MINBY™ OG FACTSPILOT.COM

MinBy™ udvikler et omfattende digitalt medienetværk med 1.522 ultralokale medier fordelt på Danmarks 98 kommuner samt 30 passions- og situationsbaserede magasinkoncepter.

Factspilot.com er et internationalt dimension med ambitionen om at udvikle en teknologisk platform, der kan understøtte:

• 
Indsamling og bearbejdning af journalistisk indhold fra flere lande.

• 
Faktatjek, kildekontrol og dokumentation.

• 
AI-understøttet oversættelse og flersproget publicering.

• 
Distribution af journalistisk indhold på tværs af lande og medier.

• 
Samarbejde mellem journalister, redaktioner og medieorganisationer.

• 
Nye modeller for international journalistisk produktion.

Målet er at skabe en skalerbar europæisk medieinfrastruktur, hvor teknologi, journalistisk kvalitet og internationale partnerskaber arbejder sammen.

DIN FØRSTE STORE OPGAVE – EU-PROJEKTET

Vi arbejder med muligheden for at søge støtte gennem Creative Europe – Journalism Partnerships.

Projektets foreløbige finansieringsramme tager udgangspunkt i muligheden for EU-støtte på op til 2 mio. euro, afhængigt af den konkrete ansøgningskategori og gældende betingelser.

Din opgave bliver at undersøge og udvikle grundlaget for en kvalificeret ansøgning.

Det omfatter blandt andet:

1. Projektudvikling

• 
Omsætte Factspilots vision til en konkret projektbeskrivelse.

• 
Definere mål, aktiviteter, leverancer og succeskriterier.

• 
Udarbejde projektplan, milepæle og tidsplan.

2. Internationalt partnerskab

• 
Identificere relevante medievirksomheder, organisationer og teknologipartnere i Europa.

• 
Etablere dialog og udvikle samarbejdsaftaler.

• 
Koordinere ansvarsfordeling og bidrag fra projektets partnere.

3. Finansiering og EU-ansøgning

• 
Analysere støtteprogrammets krav og muligheder.

• 
Udarbejde budget, finansieringsmodel og ansøgningsmateriale.

• 
Dokumentere projektets europæiske merværdi, gennemførlighed og forventede resultater.

• 
Koordinere ansøgningsprocessen frem til indsendelse.

4. Teknologi og redaktionel udvikling

• 
Samarbejde med tekniske og redaktionelle ressourcer.

• 
Beskrive platformens funktioner, udviklingsbehov og anvendelse af AI.

• 
Sikre sammenhæng mellem teknologisk udvikling og journalistiske behov.

5. Projektledelse og gennemførelse

• 
Opbygge en operationel projektorganisation.

• 
Koordinere økonomi, ressourcer, leverancer og rapportering.

• 
Forberede projektets implementering, hvis finansieringen opnås.

HVEM ER DU?

Du har erfaring med projektledelse, forretningsudvikling, internationale samarbejder eller finansierede udviklingsprojekter.

Erfaring med EU-programmer, fondsansøgninger eller medieprojekter er en betydelig fordel.

Vi lægger især vægt på, at du:

• 
Kan drive et projekt selvstændigt fra idé til konkret resultat.

• 
Har stærke analytiske, organisatoriske og kommunikative evner.

• 
Kan udvikle projektbeskrivelser, budgetter og finansieringsplaner.

• 
Er god til at skabe relationer og opbygge internationale samarbejder.

• 
Behersker engelsk på et højt professionelt niveau.

• 
Har forståelse for teknologi, AI og digitale forretningsmodeller.

• 
Kan arbejde struktureret med komplekse krav og deadlines.

• 
Har gennemslagskraft, initiativ og et højt ambitionsniveau.

Du behøver ikke være journalist eller programmør. Det afgørende er, at du kan forstå projektets forskellige fagområder og få specialister til at arbejde sammen mod fælles mål.

HVAD TILBYDER VI?

Du får mulighed for at få en central rolle i udviklingen af et internationalt medieprojekt fra en tidlig fase.

Vi tilbyder:

• 
Betydelig indflydelse på projektets strategi og udvikling.

• 
Mulighed for at opbygge et internationalt samarbejdsnetværk.

• 
Arbejde i krydsfeltet mellem journalistik, teknologi, AI og europæisk finansiering.

• 
Direkte samarbejde med MinBy™s strategiske og tekniske ledelse.

• 
Mulighed for at udvikle rollen i takt med projektets finansiering og fremdrift.

Dette er ikke en traditionel administrativ projektlederstilling.

Vi søger en person, der selv kan identificere muligheder, træffe initiativer og skabe målbare resultater.

ANSÆTTELSE OG SAMARBEJDE

Vi er åbne over for forskellige samarbejdsformer afhængigt af kandidatens kompetencer og projektets udviklingsfase.

Arbejdsomfang, ansættelsesvilkår og aflønning aftales individuelt.

ANSØGNING OG UDVÆLGELSE

Vi vurderer kandidater på deres dokumenterede kompetencer, selvstændighed, erfaring og evne til at skabe resultater.

Relevante kandidater kan blive tilbudt en frivillig, praktisk testopgave med udgangspunkt i Factspilot og de konkrete muligheder for europæisk projektfinansiering.

Vi lægger vægt på, at du kan demonstrere, hvordan du vil gribe en kompleks opgave an – ikke blot beskrive dine tidligere erfaringer.

SØG STILLINGEN

Læs mere om MinBy™ på:

https://minbymedie.dk

Ansøgning sker via MinBy™s digitale rekrutteringssystem.

PROJECT MANAGER – FACTSPILOT.COM
International media project · AI · Fact-checking · EU funding

Do you want to head the development of an international media platform with ambitions to work across European countries and languages? MinBy™ is seeking an ambitious, independent, and results-oriented project manager for Factspilot.com – an international media and technology project focused on journalism, fact-checking, AI, translation, and news distribution.

We are looking for someone who can turn an ambitious idea into a concrete, funded, and operational project. A key initial task will be to research, develop, and coordinate an application for the EU program Creative Europe – Journalism Partnerships, including establishing relevant European partnerships.

This position is for you if you can combine strategic understanding, international project management, financing, and practical execution.

ABOUT MINBY™ AND FACTSPILOT.COM
MinBy™ develops an extensive digital media network featuring 1,522 ultra-local media outlets distributed across Denmark’s 98 municipalities, alongside 30 passion- and situation-based magazine concepts.

Factspilot.com is an international dimension with the ambition to develop a technological platform that can support:

• 
Gathering and processing journalistic content from multiple countries.

• 
Fact-checking, source verification, and documentation.

• 
AI-supported translation and multilingual publishing.

• 
Distribution of journalistic content across countries and media.

• 
Collaboration between journalists, newsrooms, and media organizations.

• 
New models for international journalistic production.

The goal is to create a scalable European media infrastructure where technology, journalistic quality, and international partnerships work together.

YOUR FIRST MAJOR TASK – THE EU PROJECT
We are working on the opportunity to apply for funding through Creative Europe – Journalism Partnerships. The project's preliminary financial framework is based on the possibility of EU support of up to EUR 2 million, depending on the specific application category and applicable conditions.

Your task will be to research and develop the foundation for a qualified application. This includes, among other things:

• 
Project Development

• 
Translating Factspilot’s vision into a concrete project description.

• 
Defining objectives, activities, deliverables, and success criteria.

• 
Preparing the project plan, milestones, and timeline.

• 
International Partnership

• 
Identifying relevant media companies, organizations, and technology partners in Europe.

• 
Establishing dialogue and developing partnership agreements.

• 
Coordinating the division of responsibilities and contributions from project partners.

• 
Financing and EU Application

• 
Analyzing the requirements and opportunities of the funding program.

• 
Preparing the budget, financing model, and application materials.

• 
Documenting the project’s European added value, feasibility, and expected results.

• 
Coordinating the application process up until submission.

• 
Technology and Editorial Development

• 
Collaborating with technical and editorial resources.

• 
Describing the platform’s features, development needs, and use of AI.

• 
Ensuring alignment between technological development and journalistic needs.

• 
Project Management and Implementation

• 
Building an operational project organization.

• 
Coordinating finances, resources, deliverables, and reporting.

• 
Preparing for the project’s implementation if funding is secured.

WHO ARE YOU?
You have experience in project management, business development, international collaborations, or funded development projects. Experience with EU programs, grant applications, or media projects is a significant advantage.

We place particular emphasis on you being able to:

• 
Drive a project independently from idea to concrete results.

• 
Possess strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills.

• 
Develop project descriptions, budgets, and financing plans.

• 
Excel at building relationships and establishing international partnerships.

• 
Master English at a high professional level.

• 
Understand technology, AI, and digital business models.

• 
Work structured with complex requirements and deadlines.

• 
Demonstrate impact, initiative, and a high level of ambition.

You do not need to be a journalist or a programmer. The crucial factor is that you can understand the project’s various professional fields and make specialists work together toward common goals.

WHAT WE OFFER
You will have the opportunity to take on a central role in the development of an international media project from an early stage. We offer:

• 
Significant influence on the project’s strategy and development.

• 
The opportunity to build an international network of collaborators.

• 
Work at the intersection of journalism, technology, AI, and European funding.

• 
Direct collaboration with MinBy™’s strategic and technical leadership.

• 
The opportunity to develop the role in tandem with the project’s funding and progress.

This is not a traditional administrative project management position. We are looking for an individual who can identify opportunities, take initiative, and create measurable results themselves.

EMPLOYMENT AND COLLABORATION
We are open to different forms of collaboration depending on the candidate’s competencies and the project's development phase. Workload, terms of employment, and remuneration will be negotiated individually.

APPLICATION AND SELECTION
We assess candidates based on their documented competencies, independence, experience, and ability to deliver results. Relevant candidates may be offered a voluntary, practical test assignment based on Factspilot and the specific opportunities for European project funding.

We emphasize that you can demonstrate how you would approach a complex task – not just describe your past experiences.

APPLY FOR THE POSITION
Read more about MinBy™ at: https://minbymedie.dk
Applications must be submitted via MinBy™’s digital recruitment system.

About Driversnote

Driversnote is a profitable, product-led SaaS company based in Copenhagen that helps over 4.5 million users simplify mileage tracking, with paying customers in 100+ countries. Our core product is a freemium mobile app, often paired with our iBeacon hardware for precise, automated mileage logging, and backed by a powerful web platform.

We’re a close-knit team of 50 working together across design, mobile and web development, marketing, support, sales and customer success. We’ve quadrupled our ARR in the last three years by staying focused on delivering real value to our users, and we’re now expanding from B2C into B2B, building advanced features for teams.

Our Customer Success and Support team is locally anchored in Denmark, Canada and Australia. Customers get help in their own time zone from people who know their market, its rules and how its businesses work.

The role

As Customer Success Manager for EMEA, you own a portfolio of our larger business customers and make sure they get real value from Driversnote, renew, and grow.

This is an outcome-led role, not a usage-monitoring one. Teams today can build their own tracking or buy a system that includes it, so we win by helping customers save money, stay compliant and run their mileage process with less effort. You’ll be the person who makes that happen for your accounts.

Success looks like this after your first year:

• 
Your accounts renew, and you know why the few that leave did

• 
New accounts are live and in use within weeks, not months

• 
Your accounts grow in licences and use more of what we offer

• 
Customers see you as a trusted adviser on mileage, reimbursement and compliance, and Driversnote is built into how they work, from their mileage policy to their payroll and AI tools

What you’ll do

• 
Own retention and renewals. Manage renewals for your accounts from start to finish, spot risk early and act on it.

• 
Get new accounts live. Run onboarding for new teams, with kickoffs for admins, managers and drivers, so the first year sets them up for success.

• 
Grow your accounts. Find expansion opportunities where it makes sense, help teams roll out to more drivers and pass qualified leads to Sales.

• 
Lead outcome-focused reviews. Run annual and quarterly business reviews built around what customers achieve, not just how much they use the app.

• 
Be the expert. Advise customers on mileage reimbursement policy, tax compliance and audit-readiness in your markets.

• 
Get Driversnote deeper into their processes. Help customers improve how they handle mileage end to end: shaping their mileage policy, connecting Driversnote to payroll, finance and AI tools, and removing manual steps, so we become part of how they work, not just an app they use.

• 
Help shape new services. Work with us as we build new offers, such as fleet mileage reports, CO2 reporting and compliance checks.

• 
Keep the data clean. Use HubSpot, health scores and AI tools to manage your portfolio, and log why customers leave so we can learn from it.

• 
Be the customer’s voice. Share what you hear with Product, Sales and Support to improve the product.

What we’re looking for

• 
A few years’ experience in customer success, account management or implementation, ideally in B2B SaaS

• 
Experience owning renewals or a revenue target, or helping customers get live with a new system

• 
Native or near-native English, written and spoken, since many of our customers are in the UK

• 
A commercial mindset: you can turn a customer’s goals into a reason to renew and grow

• 
Comfortable with data, CRM tools and AI; you use numbers to spot risk and show value

• 
A real interest in using AI to create more value, not just to work faster. We take AI seriously here, not as a buzzword: you’ll use and help shape the AI agents and workflows our team relies on every day

• 
Clear, warm communication with everyone from drivers to finance directors

• 
The role is based in our Copenhagen office, and you need a valid permit to work in Denmark

Nice to have

• 
Experience with expansion and upsell in existing accounts

• 
Additional languages are a plus

• 
Knowledge of mileage reimbursement, fleet management, payroll or tax compliance

• 
Experience with HubSpot

This role is probably not for you if…

• 
You want to stay at a strategic distance. This is a hands-on role: you’ll run onboardings, dig into data, fix problems and talk to drivers as well as finance directors.

• 
You only want large accounts. Your portfolio will be a mix of smaller teams and large accounts, and you need to enjoy both.

• 
You’re looking for enterprise sales. We don’t do long, complex corporate sales cycles. If large enterprise selling is what drives you, this isn’t the right fit.

What we offer

• 
Ownership from day one: a high-impact role where you own our B2B customers in the EMEA region.

• 
Shape how we do it: help build the B2B success motion for an established, profitable company.

• 
People to learn from: work with a team of highly experienced entrepreneurs and tech people, across Denmark, Canada and Australia.

• 
Growth: a clear career path in Customer Success, with specialisations as our services grow.

• 
Balance: a healthy work-life balance.

• 
Location and benefits: our Copenhagen office, pension and a learning budget.

We work in a relaxed environment in new offices near the Meatpacking District. Every day there’s a tasty, freshly cooked lunch (with a vegetarian option) and great coffee. We also have cosy Friday drinks and great events, from our running club and gaming nights to our epic Christmas and summer parties.

How to apply

Fill out an application here

We review applications and respond to candidates on an ongoing basis, so apply soon. We aim for a start date of 1 December or 1 January, depending on your availability, but finding the right fit matters more to us than a deadline. Expect a case during the interview process: it represents the kind of work you’ll do with us.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Lighting Product Developer – Egmont Living Nordic (AndLight) (Fuldtidsstilling, København) 

“This role is responsible for developing innovative, aesthetically appealing, functional, and commercially viable lighting products that align with our brand identity, target market, quality standards, and pricing objectives.

You are have strong understanding of lighting design, materials, finishes, manufacturing processes, and product construction, combined with excellent project management, communication, and problem-solving skills. A passion for home décor, interior styling, craftsmanship, and emerging design trends is essential.

Reaponsibilties:

• 
Concept & Trend Research: keep oneself updated with latest design & interior trends based on market research and sales data, particularly in the Nordic market. This includes monitoring of emerging styles, colors, materials, finishes, shapes, and decorative details relevant to lamps and lighting accessories.

• 
Technical Design, Specification & Engineering: Define every aesthetic and technical details for the products in development, according to the appropriate design and usage, and liaising directly to supplier and factory engineers for the best solution.

• 
Sourcing & OEM/ODM Management: Partner with specialized supplier and manufacturer to build prototypes, evaluate samples, negotiate MOQ (Minimum Order Quantity) with suppliers and control of the quotations and economics for new units.

• 
Compliance & Certifications: Ensure both supplier and units meet all the EU market safety regulation and energy requirement (e.g., CE, UKCA, RoHS, EPREL depending on target markets), and support the approval process of test reports with the Compliance Department.  

• 
Packaging & Unboxing Experience: Responsibility over design of packaging that meets e-com standards, clear installation manuals, accurate datasheet, and all everything that follows under the PPWR regulation in packaging and accessories.

Role requirement:

• 
Bachelor or Masters in Lighting/Product Design, Industrial Design, Interior Design, or a related field.

• 
2–4 years of experience in product development, preferably in lighting, home décor, or furniture products.

• 
Good understanding of materials, finishes, product construction, and manufacturing processes.

• 
Experience working with suppliers and managing product samples.

• 
Ability to prepare product specifications and review technical details.

• 
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.

• 
Good attention to detail and ability to manage multiple projects.

• 
Proficiency in Adobe package; experience with design software is an advantage.

• 
Knowledge of lighting components and safety requirements is preferred."

Applicants are invited for a double degree PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Biological and Chemical Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 January 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

The position is part of the MSCA project TagTIC - Target mining for the development of therapeutics against pathogen-induced cancers, ID: 101311627, Call: HORIZON-MSCA-2025-DN-01-01. Project website: tagtic.eu

Note that this is a double degree PhD project within an MSCA Joint Doctorate. Under the currently planned arrangement, the candidate will work for approximately three years at TissueGnostics GmbH in Vienna, Austria, and one year at Aarhus University, Denmark.

Title:

Artificial intelligence for infection-driven cancers

Research area and project description:

Microbial infections are increasingly recognized as important contributors to cancer, but identifying the spatial tissue features and molecular signatures associated with infection-driven disease remains challenging. Integrating tissue imaging with spatial transcriptomics and microbiome information offers opportunities to characterize disease-associated patterns and improve biomarker discovery.

Consortium: This PhD postion is part of the interdisciplinary TagTIC consortium, which brings together expertise in microbiology, virology, oncology, immunology, medicinal chemistry, imaging, AI, and bioinformatics, with support from associated partners in biotech, diagnostics, and science communication. Its collaborative structure allows doctoral candidates to work within a network where discovery science, technology development, training, and societal impact are closely connected.

Project DC11: This PhD is part of the TagTIC consortium. It combines machine learning with image analysis to support precision oncology. The aim is to develop AI algorithms that integrate tissue imaging, spatial transcriptomics and microbiome data (multiomics) to identify biomarkers and predict disease progression.

Project description: For technical reasons, you must upload a project description. Please simply copy the project description above and upload it as a PDF in the application.

jobs.occupation: Research Assistants in Medical Robotics (Navigation & Control)
jobs.description:
The Department of Computer Science invites applications for one-year research assistant positions focused on developing innovative robot control and navigation techniques using simulation-based learning for medical robotic endoscope devices.

  Project Background
 This project addresses two critical challenges in the field of medical robotics to improve patient care through advanced simulation and control:

   	
• Image-Based Navigation: Creating reward functions for scoring navigation policies for medical robotic devices moving inside the human body, relying solely on image information and accounting for environment changes through interaction models. 	
• Soft Robot Control: Developing learning-based methods to control a soft robot endoscope via high-level navigation policies to perform clinical procedures inside the human body, including quality assessment of these methods during in-vivo interventions.   The successful candidates will join a multidisciplinary and collaborative team renowned for cutting-edge research in medical imaging and simulation technologies, operating within a global network across France, Germany, and Spain.

  Roles and Responsibilities
 The successful candidates will play a central role in the project’s technical and scientific success. While the level of autonomy will vary by position, both roles will share the following core responsibilities:

   	
• Technical Development & Implementation: Designing and implementing machine learning methods for motion planning and control. This includes integrating simulation-based learning frameworks and demonstrating the resulting systems on real robotic hardware and soft robot endoscopes. 	
• Research & Scientific Contribution: Contributing to the project’s core objectives by producing impactful research outputs. This includes writing high-quality papers for peer-reviewed journals and presenting findings at international conferences. 	
• Collaboration & Knowledge Exchange: Facilitating collaborations with industrial partners and academic collaborators to ensure that the developed methodologies are meaningful and translatable to real-world clinical practice. 	
• Professional Growth & Mentorship: Engaging in a high-growth research environment. The positions can be extendable and towards a PhD depending on the future funding status. The project has a trackrecord of landing members in top PhD program and faculty positions. 	
• Interdisciplinary Integration: Actively participating in team discussions and workshops to integrate expertise across medical imaging, physics simulation, and robotics control.   Profile
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• MSc in the fields mentioned above. 	
• You have a strong foundation and track record in robotics simulation, robot control, computer vision and/or machine learning for physical systems. 	
• You are highgly experienced in numerical optimization algorithms, preferably applied to motion planning or reinforcement learning. Hands-on experience on real robots especially soft robot systems is a plus. 	
• Proficient scientific computing and programming (C++/Python) and experience with libraries such as PyTorch, JAX, Warp, Taichi, or ROS. 	
• Excellent communication skills and a high level of motivation to work in a multidisciplinary, international research environment.   Desireable experience and skills

   	
• Experience in publishing peer-reviewed research in top-tier robotics or AI venues. 	
• Familiarity with physics simulation such as MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, Newton Physics, SOFA etc.   Terms of employment
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 1 year. The starting date is 15 February or after agreement

  Salary, pension and other conditions of employment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organisation.

  Foreign and Danish applicants may be eligible for tax reductions, if they hold a PhD degree and have not lived in Denmark the last 10 years.

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. 

  Questions
 Further information on the Department is linked at http://www.science.ku.dk/english/about-the-faculty/organisation/. Inquiries about the positions can be made to kenny@di.ku.dk and hayi@di.ku.dk.

  Application procedure

   	
• Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format 	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a Master of Science certificate. 	
• List of publications.   Deadline for applications: 30 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.
 We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

   

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.
