Join Copenhagen Energy Trading as our new Machine Learning Engineer

Machine learning is becoming an increasingly important part of how we understand energy markets, improve forecasts, and make trading decisions. We are therefore looking for a Machine Learning Engineer to move our models from research to production, building robust, scalable pipelines that continuously improve our strategies.

At Copenhagen Energy Trading (CET), we combine deep market expertise with machine learning, quantitative research, data, and engineering to automate and optimise how we trade power. We’re a small, highly ambitious team based in central Copenhagen, specialising in power trading and asset management across Europe and North America. Technology is at the core of how we operate, supported by one of Europe’s most advanced automated and analytical trading environments for power markets.

The Opportunity

Energy markets produce vast amounts of data and are continuously shaped by weather, power production, transmission constraints, and market behaviour. Using that data meaningfully requires accurate models and reliable software and infrastructure that allow those models to run in production.

As our Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll work across machine learning and software development. Alongside quantitative researchers, software engineers and traders, you’ll build the production systems behind our ML pipelines, making our trading more performant, more reliable and more automated.

You’ll own the full lifecycle around the model: from data management to the pipelines and frameworks that deploy and monitor our models, keeping them reliable and adaptive as markets evolve. The opportunity for impact is large, and so is what it asks of you: dedication, real talent and the willingness to grind through hard problems. This is a hands-on engineering role at the centre of how CET uses machine learning to trade.

What You Will Do

• Strengthen our ML framework: Build and improve the framework our researchers use to build models and quantitative strategies.

• Build production-ready software: Design and develop reliable, scalable, and well-tested Python software that integrates machine learning into our internal trading platforms.

• Develop data infrastructure: Build and maintain data pipelines and storage solutions for ingesting, transforming, and serving diverse market and fundamental data.

• Ship and operate models: Take models from experiment to production, including deployment, serving, monitoring and experiment tracking

• Improve our ML and engineering practices: Help strengthen our approach to MLOps, testing, CI/CD, code reviews, and the wider model development lifecycle.

• Shape our technical solutions: Evaluate and introduce tools and technologies that improve how we develop, deploy, and operate machine learning solutions.

• Collaborate across disciplines: Work closely with quantitative researchers, traders, and software engineers to turn business and market needs into practical technical solutions.

• Build energy-market expertise: Develop a deep understanding of power markets and how machine learning, data, and software can improve trading decisions.

What We're Looking For

We value strong technical ability, sound judgement, curiosity, and motivation to learn. While we don't expect a perfect match, many of the following qualifications will help you succeed in the role:

• Strong software engineering skills: Experience building clean, scalable, tested, and production-ready software. Strong Python skills are essential, as Python is our primary development language.

• MLOps and development practices: Proficiency in Git, code reviews, CI/CD, experiment tracking, model deployment, and monitoring.

• Cloud computing: Experience with Azure, AWS, or GCP, ideally including relevant data and machine learning services.

• Problem-solving and communication: The ability to structure complex problems, communicate clearly, and collaborate with colleagues across technical and commercial disciplines. Full professional proficiency in English is required.

• Ownership: The ability to work independently and deliver in a fast-paced environment.

• Interest in energy markets: Curiosity about power markets, trading, and energy systems. Previous experience in energy or trading is an advantage, but not a requirement.

• Education: A degree with a strong technical focus, e.g., Computer Science, Software Engineering, or other relevant fields. We welcome different educational backgrounds and levels of qualification.

What We Offer

• Growth environment: Become part of a young, ambitious, and expanding tech-driven trading company where talented people are given responsibility and room to grow.

• Exceptional team: Work closely with experienced quantitative researchers, software engineers and power traders.

• Competitive compensation: Receive a competitive salary package and attractive benefits that reflect your skills and contributions.

• Strong culture: Participate in both social and professional events, including team sports, company parties, team-building, and informal gatherings that strengthen our team spirit.

• Central Copenhagen location: Work from our office in Carlsberg Byen, located in beautifully renovated historic Carlsberg buildings.

How to Apply

If this opportunity feels like the right fit for you, we would love to hear from you.

Please apply via LinkedIn and submit your cover letter, CV, and university transcripts as a single PDF. Please note that applications that do not meet these requirements may not be considered.

Application deadline: November 27, 2026

If you have any questions, please contact Carl Frederik Grønvald (Senior Quantitative Analyst) at cfg@copenhagen-energy.com or Anna Schumann (People & Culture Manager) at as@copenhagen-energy.com.

All Gravy: All the people stuff in one employee app - built for hospitality Hospitality is one of the largest employment sectors in Europe. It's also one of the most chaotic to operate. The average multi-site restaurant group or hotel brand manages hundreds of hourly workers across dozens of locations - none of whom sit at a desk, have a work email, or receive information through the same channel twice. The result is predictable. New starters show up on day one not knowing what to do. Training happens inconsistently, or not at all. Managers spend half their day answering the same questions on repeat. Communication happens in WhatsApp groups that the business doesn't own, can't audit, and can't control. Staff churn - already the highest of any industry, averaging 75% annually - gets worse. And operators have no way of knowing why. The tools that exist to solve this were built for office workers. They assume laptops, corporate email, and people who sit still. Hospitality doesn't work like that. All Gravy is the fix. We're a communications and learning app built specifically for multi-site hospitality operators - restaurant groups, hotel brands, contract caterers, quick-service chains. Our customers typically manage between 200 and 1,000 staff across multiple locations in the UK, Scandinavia, and Germany. The product gives operators one place to run everything people-related: Staff communications - a branded, structured feed that works like social media. Managers post to the right people by location, role, or team. Employees are notified. Everything is documented. No more WhatsApp chaos. Onboarding journeys - automated, role-specific sequences that start the moment a new hire is added to the system. They arrive on day one prepared, connected to the brand, and knowing what's expected of them. Training and learning - a full LMS designed for deskless workers, supporting both digital courses and in-person sessions, with attendance tracking, completion records, and automated reminders built in. Digital handbooks - a living, searchable library that employees access from their phone. Update once, everyone sees it instantly. No more outdated PDFs or laminated binders no one reads. AI assistant - trained on the operator's own content, not the internet. Employees get instant, accurate answers to questions about policies, procedures, and their role. Managers stop answering the same things over and over. The employee experience looks and feels like a social media app - because that's what people actually use. Adoption is high because the product meets people where they already are. The admin side is a web dashboard where operators build and manage everything centrally, with full visibility into engagement, training completion, onboarding progress, and team sentiment across every location. The problem is big. There are roughly 90 million deskless workers in Europe. Hospitality alone employs millions, with vacancy and churn rates that cost the sector billions in lost revenue every year. The tools available to operators haven't kept up with what the problem actually requires. The opportunity is clear. Operators who invest in their people's experience - making them feel informed, connected, and supported from day one - see measurably lower turnover, better training compliance, and lower management overhead. All Gravy makes that investment easy, scalable, and consistent across every location in a business. We've raised €5.8M+ to date, backed by Moonfire Ventures, Scale Capital, and a syndicate of angels including senior operators and investors from Google, Deliveroo, and Peakon. Our customers include some of the largest hospitality operators in Northern Europe. We're building the operating layer for the front-line hospitality workforce - the infrastructure that makes it possible to run a great team at scale, not just at one site, but across all of them.

ABOUT THE JOB

Flatpay is on a mission to simplify payments for small and medium-sized businesses. We provide transparent, low-cost payment solutions combined with fast onboarding and real human support - fair pricing, great technology, and local support that merchants can rely on. One of the fastest-growing fintech companies out of the Nordics and Denmark's fastest-ever unicorn, we've scaled to 2,500+ colleagues across multiple markets, and we're just getting started. Pay is our terminal-only product: a card terminal, flat transparent pricing, and nothing the merchant has to configure. It is the product most of our merchants gets first, it carries the majority of our processing volume, and it is the product we lead with in every new market. This is a deliberately commercial product leadership role. Flatpay's whole model rests on a single visit: a rep walks into a bakery, a salon or a bike shop unannounced, explains flat, transparent pricing, demos the terminal, installs it and trains the staff. Everything Pay does exists to make that visit convert and to keep the merchant on the terminal afterwards. If you've only ever led product through a research team and a dashboard, this won't be the role for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own Pay end to end

• 
Own the Pay product globally - terminal hardware, the payment experience, onboarding and activation, the merchant app, settlement and reporting. One roadmap, all markets.

• 
Set the Pay strategy and defend it: what we build, what we deliberately do not build, and what stays the same across every market so the product does not fragment as we add countries.

• 
Keep the product radically simple. Our merchants are not technical and have no IT function; simplicity is the product, and protecting it is your job before it is anyone else's.

Lead the team

• 
Lead and grow the Pay product team (three PMs today, with the reporting track dotted in), setting the bar for discovery, delivery and written thinking.

• 
Be a player-coach. You'll run your own track on the hardest problems, not only review other people's.

• 
Partner with Engineering, Design and Data in Copenhagen to turn the Pay roadmap into shipped product on roughly two-month cycles, MVP mindset - get it live, learn, iterate.

The field

• 
Get out into the field. Sit with merchants, ride along with sales, spend time with support, and turn what you hear into product decisions. We expect this of a Head of Pay as much as of a PM.

• 
Partner with Sales, Support and Marketing across markets to surface what is actually happening with merchants, and feed it straight into the roadmap.

• 
Build and hold the competitive view for Pay: how competitors package and price terminal and Pay-only offers in Europe and the US, and where they are beatable.

Markets and expansion

• 
Make Pay launch-ready for each new market - acquiring setup, local payment behaviour, regulation, hardware logistics - and work with the US team in New York on what the US needs from the European product.

• 
Own outcome metrics for Pay: activation, processing volume, retention, churn, support load, and the commercial metrics above.

WHO YOU ARE

• 
3+ years in product, with experience leading product managers - and still extremely hands-on.

• 
A commercial, results-driven mindset. You think in merchants, conversion, volume and margin, and you can point to a pricing or product decision you made that moved one of them.

• 
Evidence of field-driven discovery: a decision you can name that came directly from time in front of merchants or sales, not from a research readout.

• 
A track record of shipping fast in a low-structure environment, and comfort building the structure as you go rather than waiting for it.

• 
A generalist and builder who thrives in a fast-paced scale-up and is happy working outside their comfort zone.

• 
Excellent stakeholder management across functions, markets and time zones, and excellent written and spoken English.

AI IS PART OF THE JOB

• 
Flatpay's cost advantage comes from doing things with fewer people than the incumbents. AI is how we keep that true as we add markets, and we expect a Head of Pay to treat it as part of the product, not as a side project.

• 
Use it yourself, daily. You prototype with it, you write specs and analysis with it, you run your own competitive and pricing research with it. You'll be setting the bar for three PMs, and the bar is that a PM who cannot get a working prototype or a data answer in an afternoon is slower than the role now requires.

• 
Know where it does not belong. Nothing in the authorisation path, nothing the merchant has to supervise, nothing that makes a terminal less predictable. Our merchants are not technical and have no IT function.

• 
Be honest about the economics. Inference cost, error rate and the cost of being wrong are product decisions. You should be able to argue why a model belongs in a flow at our volumes, or why a rule set is the better answer.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Positions in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The research group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen at the Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for two Postdoctoral Researcher positions in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics.

  Professor Mikkelsen’s group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group’s experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI’s new building. Postdocs joining now will help build the laboratory and shape its first experiments. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

  The positions span three axes of control over light–matter interaction; the balance between them will depend on the candidates:

  Spatial structure — shaping the vacuum around an emitter and concentrating the field for nonlinear optics, with examples including Purcell tensors, the nanophotonic Lamb shift, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients.

  Emitter number — cavity QED with exactly one, two or several emitters, including the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and multi-exciton emission that outruns Auger recombination.

  Temporal control — ultrafast and time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, optically dressed states in quantum materials embedded in nanogaps, and time-varying cavities.

  We seek outstanding, creative, and highly motivated experimentalists with a PhD in physics, chemistry, materials science, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline, and a strong background in one or more of: nanophotonics or cavity QED; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic spectroscopy of solid-state emitters or two-dimensional materials; ultrafast optical spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Candidates are encouraged to propose directions of their own within this scope; the programme will be shaped by the people who join.

  The successful candidates will carry out experimental research, help set up the new laboratory, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet, a tunable femtosecond laser system and single-photon confocal spectroscopy, publish and present results, and participate in the supervision of students. The positions may also include collaboration with national and international research partners and other academic duties as required. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

   

  Further information on the Department at https://nbi.ku.dk/english/. Informal inquiries are welcome and can be made to Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen, maiken.mikkelsen@nbi.ku.dk.

  The positions are for three years, starting as soon as possible, with flexible start dates into 2027.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

  Terms of employment

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff. 

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. 

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below. 

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Please include 

   	
• Cover letter describing your motivation and research interests (max 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including publication list 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD degree, or documentation of expected PhD completion date) 	
• Names and contact details of two or three references   The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee. 

  You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Interviews are not yet scheduled.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor (fixed-term) in Experimental Nanophotonics and Quantum Optics
jobs.description:
The Niels Bohr Institute (NBI), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a fixed-term Assistant Professor position in experimental nanophotonics and quantum optics, in the group of Professor Maiken H. Mikkelsen. The position is for four years, open from as soon as possible; a later start in 2027 can be negotiated.

Professor Mikkelsen's group studies how light and matter interact when light is confined to nanometre-scale volumes. Using plasmonic nanocavities — metallic nanogaps fabricated deterministically around a chosen emitter — the group reaches a regime far beyond the reach of conventional optical cavities: Purcell factors above 10,000, single-photon emission at telecom wavelengths with lifetimes of tens of picoseconds at room temperature, and second-harmonic generation enhanced more than ten-million-fold in materials with no bulk second-order nonlinearity. In this regime, light–matter behaviour appears that was not previously thought possible, and the group's experiments are increasingly directed at the nonlinear and ultrafast optics it opens up. Experiments combine nanofabrication, single-photon and photon-correlation spectroscopy, cryogenic magneto-optics and ultrafast pump–probe optics. The group has recently relocated from Duke University to NBI, supported by a DKK 35 million RECRUIT award from the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and is establishing a laboratory in NBI's new building. Recent work: https://mikkelsenphotonics.com.

The Assistant Professor will lead an independent research direction within the group’s programme on light–matter interaction in nanocavities. Directions of particular interest include:

• 
Cavity QED with few emitters — strong coupling with exactly one, two or several quantum emitters in deterministically fabricated nanogaps, the crossover from room-temperature to cryogenic strong coupling, collective emission, and quantum light generation from nanocavity-coupled emitters

• 
Quantum and two-dimensional materials in nanogaps — out-of-plane excitations (interlayer excitons, dark excitons, trions) coupled to the vertical field of a nanogap at cryogenic temperatures and in vector magnetic fields; optically dressed states of 2D semiconductors and magnets driven inside a nanogap and read out by single-cavity ultrafast spectroscopy

• 
Ultrafast and nonlinear nanophotonics — time-resolved experiments on single nanocavities, including single-nanocavity pump–probe spectroscopy, harmonic generation in nanoscale volumes, time-varying cavities, and forbidden and two-photon transitions opened by field gradients

 Candidates are expected to define their own experimental programme within this scope, and proposals that cut across these directions are welcome.

This is a leadership position for an early-career scientist ready for independence. The Assistant Professor will be the senior scientist in the group alongside Professor Mikkelsen, with day-to-day responsibility for one research direction and its students. The successful candidate will take scientific ownership of the group's new cryogenic and ultrafast facilities, including a 1.7 K cryostat with a vector magnet and a tunable femtosecond laser system, co-supervise PhD and master's students, and develop their own funding portfolio, with active support from the group and the institute. They will be supported in applying as principal investigator for Danish and European early-career grants, and the position includes a dedicated budget line for a student and consumables. The group fabricates its cavities in the NBI cleanroom and at DTU Nanolab, Denmark's national nanofabrication centre.

We seek an outstanding experimentalist, typically three to seven years after the PhD, with a strong publication record, demonstrated independence, and hands-on expertise in several of: nanophotonics, cavity QED or plasmonics; quantum optics and photon-correlation measurements; cryogenic optical and magneto-optical spectroscopy; ultrafast pump–probe spectroscopy; nanofabrication. Expertise in the exfoliation, transfer, assembly and encapsulation of van der Waals heterostructures, including gated devices, is an asset. Experience supervising students and an interest in teaching are expected. The group is simultaneously recruiting postdoctoral researchers; candidates may apply to both positions.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, funded by external research grants, and is not tenure-track. The objective is that the successful candidate concludes the appointment with an established research direction, an independent funding record, and a strong case for a permanent position at the University of Copenhagen or elsewhere.

The assistant professor’s duties will primarily include research, including obligations with regard to publication/scientific communication and research-based teaching with associated examination obligations within quantum optics and photonics. To a limited extent this may also include performance of other duties. 

Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

General criteria apply to the appointment of Assistant Professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

Jupiter Bach is taking the next step in its development as a partner to the global wind industry. Building on our strong position within composite manufacturing, we are expanding our capabilities across engineering, assembly and full-system delivery, supporting leading wind OEMs globally.

This means getting involved earlier in the customer dialogue and taking greater ownership of how customer requirements translate into technically sound and commercially viable solutions.

As our new Customer Solutions Engineer, Composites, you will be an important part of that development.

The opportunity

You will work at the intersection of customers, Sales and Engineering, shaping composite solutions from early customer engagement through to handover to Product Execution.

Your role is to understand the customer need, challenge and clarify requirements, and apply your composite engineering expertise to develop the right solution. Working closely with customer technical teams and specialists within Jupiter Bach, you will drive the technical dialogue and pre-project activities while considering both engineering feasibility and commercial implications.

This is a role for an engineer who wants to use technical depth beyond the traditional engineering function. You will be close to the customer, influence solutions at an early stage and help create a strong foundation for successful engineering and execution.

What you will work with

You will take responsibility for the technical side of customer opportunities during pre-sales and early project phases.

A key part of the role will be to:

• Act as the technical interface towards customers during pre-sales and early project phases

• Translate customer requirements into feasible composite engineering solutions

• Apply your understanding of composite structures, loads, geometry and strength to solution development

• Support Sales in customer meetings, proposals and negotiations

• Drive pre-project activities and technical alignment between customers and internal specialists

• Prepare and validate technical cost calculations and provide input to pricing decisions

• Assess engineering changes and their technical and commercial impact

• Support customer claims through root cause analysis and corrective actions

• Work within PPAP and APQP4Wind processes to ensure quality and robustness

You will be part of a growing team that combines different technical competencies with ownership of specific customers and opportunities.

Who we are looking for

We are looking for an engineer with strong composite expertise who is motivated by applying that knowledge in a customer- and solution-oriented role.

You understand how composite products move from requirements and design through manufacturing and into serial production. Just as importantly, you can communicate your technical knowledge and work effectively with customers, engineers, manufacturing specialists and commercial colleagues.

We expect you to bring:

• An engineering background in Composites, Materials, Structural or Manufacturing Engineering, or another relevant discipline.

• Experience with the design and manufacturing of composite structures or GFRP products

• Understanding of load conditions, geometry and strength evaluation in composite design

• Relevant experience from the wind industry or another technically complex manufacturing environment

• Good understanding of manufacturing processes and engineering interfaces

• The ability to balance technical, operational and commercial considerations

• Strong communication and stakeholder management skills

• Professional fluency in English

Experience with PPAP and APQP4Wind is an advantage. Danish language skills are an advantage but not a requirement.

Why Jupiter Bach?

Jupiter Bach is expanding from a strong composite manufacturing base towards broader engineering and full-system capabilities.

For an experienced composites engineer, this creates an opportunity to move closer to the customer and influence solutions much earlier in the process.

You will join an international organisation working with leading wind OEMs and have the opportunity to contribute directly to how Jupiter Bach develops its future engineering and customer solution capabilities.

Contact

For more information about the role, please contact recruitment partner, Lotte Christensen, at loc@slaterconsult.com.

Slater Consult is Jupiter Bachs’s recruiting partner for this position.

**Overview

**The Senior Manager, Clinical Trial Planning is an individual contributor focused on supporting Clinical Trial Teams (CTTs) in the effective management of clinical trial timelines across the portfolio. The role drives planning system enablement (Planisware), owns and maintains a standardized Microsoft Project (MSP) trial planning template, and develops high-quality timeline visualizations to support trial execution and governance decision-making.

The role partners closely with Global Trial Leaders (GTLs), who are accountable for the overall delivery of their trials and retain ownership of trial timelines within internal planning systems. The Clinical Trial Planner complements this accountability by ensuring planning data is structured, standardized, and translated into clear, actionable insights that enable effective execution and decision-making.

**Responsibilities/tasks

****Planisware Enablement & Trial Support

**

• Partner with GTLs across the portfolio to drive effective use of Planisware and ensure trial plans reflect agreed assumptions, dependencies, and execution strategy, while GTLs retain overall accountability.

• Liaise with Development Program Managers (DPMs) to align trial-level plans with program- and asset-level timelines and milestones.

• Collaborate with the Portfolio Planning team to provide structured trial-level insights and recommendations that inform ongoing refinement and maintenance of Planisware templates and standards.

**MS Project (MSP) Template Ownership & Standardization

**

• Develop and maintain a fit for purpose Microsoft Project (MSP) Trial Planning template for GTL use across study phases.

• Ensure alignment between the MSP template, Planisware, and portfolio-level planning standards.

• Provide guidance to GTLs to promote consistent, high-quality timeline development using the MSP template.

**Data Visualization

**

• Develop and deliver clear visualization templates derived from Planisware and/or MSP data, displaying key milestones and activities.

• Tailor visual outputs to support CTTs, governance, and leadership discussions.

**Process & Tool Adoption

**

• Act as a Planisware subject matter expert at the trial-support level.

• Reinforce GTL training through hands-on guidance and real-time coaching.

• Apply and promote standardized planning methodologies and visualization standards across the portfolio.

**Governance Awareness & Decision Support

**

• Prepare timeline views and supporting materials aligned with governance forum expectations (e.g., Project Board, Portfolio Board, Operational Review Committee).

• Anticipate governance triggers based on timeline changes or emerging risks.

• Translate planning data into concise, decision-ready visuals and summaries.

**Requirements/Preferences

****Senior Manager

**

• Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.

• Approximately 7-10+ years of experience in clinical trial operations, project management, trial planning, or related roles.

• Demonstrated experience driving planning system adoption and influencing cross-functional stakeholders.

• Experience developing or standardizing planning templates, tools, or reporting frameworks across multiple studies.

• Strong understanding of portfolio-level planning considerations and governance expectations.

• Advanced analytical capability and ability to provide structured execution insight to leadership forums.

$131,040.00---$196,560.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

jobs.description:
Location: Søborg, Copenhagen, Denmark. AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark.

Working hours: 08:00–19:04

**About The Job

**Are you quality-minded, reliable, and motivated by working in a structured production environment where accuracy and compliance are essential? Do you take pride in your work and understand the importance of following procedures, even when working under time pressure? Then you may be our new Technician in Buffer Solution Preparation at AGC Biologics.

You will join our Solution Preparation team in SYD22, a new, state-of-the-art facility currently in the ramp-up phase. Production supports preclinical, clinical, and commercial manufacturing for a wide range of international clients.

The team consists of three skilled technicians who work closely together and collaborate with key stakeholders, including QA and Manufacturing Product Support. As part of the team, you will contribute to reliable, high-quality buffer preparation while ensuring compliance with cGMP requirements and minimizing the risk of deviations.

In this role, you will be responsible for planning and preparing the buffers used in protein purification processes. The position requires a strong quality mindset, attention to detail, a sense of urgency, and the ability to maintain an overview of your tasks while ensuring that established procedures and quality standards are never compromised.

**Your Work Will Include

**

• Planning and executing daily buffer preparation activities according to approved production records, recipes, and procedures.

• Ensuring buffers are prepared and delivered on time to support production schedules.

• Completing batch documentation accurately and promptly, ensuring that all activities are documented in accordance with GMP requirements.

• Following cGMP requirements, Manufacturing Production Records (MPRs), and approved procedures at all times.

• Working in compliance with regulatory and quality systems, including TrackWise, where relevant.

• Supporting daily production planning and coordinating activities to ensure timely delivery.

• Assisting with troubleshooting, production-related challenges, and ad hoc tasks.

• Identifying opportunities for continuous improvement and contributing to their implementation.

• Working independently and reliably while maintaining close collaboration with colleagues and relevant stakeholders.

• Maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality, and compliance, including when working under time pressure.

**About You

**We imagine that you:

• Preferably hold an education as a Process Operator, Process Technologist, Industrial Operator, or a similar relevant qualification.

• Have preferably at least two years of experience in the biopharmaceutical industry and experience working in a cGMP-regulated environment.

• Have experience preparing buffers according to recipes and instructions defined in production records.

• Have a good understanding of GMP documentation and the importance of accurate, timely documentation.

• Have an understanding of LEAN, 5S, and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Can speak, read, and understand English fluently.

• Work systematically and consistently, including when performing repetitive tasks.

• Communicate clearly and collaborate effectively with colleagues and stakeholders.

As a person, you take pride in your work and understand that quality and compliance are essential in pharmaceutical manufacturing. You remain calm and maintain an overview when priorities change or time pressure increases. You know when to act with urgency and when to stop and seek clarification rather than compromise established standards or procedures.

You are positive, flexible, and willing to take on new assignments and responsibilities. You work independently when needed but also value teamwork and contribute to a professional and supportive working environment.

**Working Hours

**The position follows a defined shift schedule, with working hours from 08:00 to 19:04. Production operates 24/7, including weekends and public holidays, and flexibility to work during these periods is required according to the assigned shift plan.

**What We Offer

**

• A hands-on operational role in a modern production facility supporting preclinical, clinical, and commercial manufacturing.

• An international working environment at AGC Biologics, with close collaboration across functions such as QA and Manufacturing Product Support.

• A strong focus on safety, quality, and compliance, supported by structured processes and clear expectations in a cGMP environment.

• On-the-job training and opportunities to develop your technical skills within buffer preparation.

• A professional and collaborative team culture with experienced colleagues and a strong emphasis on teamwork, accountability, and reliability.

• A structured shift-based work model supporting round-the-clock production operations.

• Competitive employment terms, including salary, pension, health insurance, and employee benefits in accordance with local agreements.

• Access to a paid canteen arrangement with meals prepared by professional chefs.

• An active Employee Club offering social events and activities throughout the year.

• Opportunities to receive discounts on a variety of leisure activities and experiences throughout the year.

**Application and Contact

**We are eager to welcome a new colleague as soon as possible.

Please submit your application no later than 22 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close the vacancy before the deadline if a suitable candidate is found. We therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

_Please note that AGC Biologics does not offer relocation assistance. Applicants must already reside in Denmark.

_**Who We Are

**AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

We are looking for motivated and reliable warehouse employees to join the inbound department at Imerco, one of Scandinavia’s largest merchandise companies. As we head into the busy Black Friday and Christmas season, we need dedicated night shift workers to help ensure that incoming goods are received and handled efficiently.

The job

Your working hours will be from 23:00 to 07:00, Monday to Friday. The job starts in week 45 or 46 and includes training shifts. It is important that you are available to start during these weeks and can work through to the end of December.

It will be approximately full-time from November. This is a great opportunity to earn extra money while gaining valuable warehouse experience.

Your tasks in the inbound department include:

• 
Receiving incoming shipments

• 
Opening, lifting, and moving boxes

• 
Unloading pallets

• 
Working with the Autostore

We are looking for candidates who enjoy working at night and can stay focused and productive throughout their shifts. You should be comfortable with physical work, routine tasks, and a busy warehouse environment.

Additionally, we expect you to:

• 
Have experience working in a warehouse – experience with an Autostore is an advantage

• 
Be comfortable working night shifts from 23:00 to 07:00

• 
Prefer practical, hands-on, and structured work

• 
Be physically fit and able to stay active throughout the shift

• 
Be reliable, punctual, and able to work independently

• 
Communicate well in either English or Danish

We offer valuable warehouse experience during the busy Black Friday and Christmas season, along with the opportunity to earn money during the winter period. You will become part of a friendly and supportive team, where tasks are clearly defined and workflows are well structured.

Working hours, salary and location

• 
Working hours: Monday to Friday, 23:00–07:00

• 
Start: Week 41, including two consecutive training shifts

• 
Employment period: Through the end of December

• 
Salary: DKK 156.34 per hour, including Fritvalgskonto

• 
An ekstra 35 kr/hour when working the night shift

The warehouse is located in Vallensbæk, with good bus connections, nearby train stations, and free parking available.

Ready to join the night shift team?
Apply today! We conduct recruitment on an ongoing basis and look forward to hearing from you.

Sparrow Quantum is seeking an experimental physicist to develop deterministic entanglement sources for photonic quantum computing. You will build and automate experiments on single quantum emitters coupled to photonic nanostructures, taking responsibility for the optical setup, the supporting electronics and the control software, and translate the results into technical direction for device and system development.

Your role

• 
Design, build and operate quantum optics experiments combining integrated photonics, cryogenics and single-photon detection

• 
Take ownership of the software for instrument control, experiment automation and data acquisition, and keep it maintainable, versioned and usable by the rest of the team

• 
Design and build simple electronics and hardware for the lab, such as driver circuits, interface boards, interlocks and mechanical fixtures

• 
Contribute to research activities on photonic quantum computing and share results clearly with the team

• 
Collaborate with academic and industrial partners in national and European projects

Must have

• 
PhD in physics or a closely related field

• 
Hands-on experience in an optics lab, in academia or industry

• 
Strong practical skills in free-space and fibre optics, lasers and spectroscopy

• 
Solid programming skills, ideally in Python, for controlling hardware and automating experiments, and a genuine drive to write good code rather than just enough to get by

• 
Curiosity and the persistence to track down problems and refine the final result

• 
Willingness to collaborate and deliver results in a clear and structured way

• 
Strong focus on the final goal, self-discipline and prioritisation

Nice to have

• 
Experience with Git and GitHub, including code review and collaborative development

• 
Experience with single quantum emitters, such as quantum dots, colour centres, atoms, ions or molecules

• 
Experience with cryostats, single-photon detectors and time-tagging electronics

• 
Familiarity with FPGA or real-time control, electro-optic modulators and fast electronics

• 
Experience with InAs/GaAs quantum dots and integrated quantum photonics, including waveguides, photonic crystals or cavities

• 
Knowledge of quantum information, including multiphoton entanglement, cluster states or photonic quantum computing

• 
A track record of scientific publications

What you can expect

• 
A central role in building the experimental and software infrastructure of a company at the forefront of photonic quantum computing

• 
A high-performance team of highly motivated people working towards photonic quantum computing

• 
Contributing to scientific publications and patents

• 
Competitive salary

• 
Lunches paid by the company

• 
The possibility of travelling to our collaborators for new insights and knowledge sharing

• 
A steep learning curve in a supportive environment at the boundary between research and industry

How to apply

If you share our passion for delivering a real-world impact through the development of unique quantum photonic technology and have the skills we believe are essential for future Sparrows, we would love to hear from you.

We are committed to creating a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace at Sparrow Quantum and welcome applicants from all backgrounds and identities.

How to apply: Scroll down to apply with your CV and a short cover letter (in English).

Application deadline: November 23.

Starting date: As soon as possible.

Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis

Short-listed candidates will be invited for an in-person interview in Copenhagen. Travel and accommodation will be covered.

For questions, contact Alexey Tiranov.

About Sparrow Quantum

Sparrow Quantum is a Danish quantum technology company dedicated to advancing light-matter interfaces for quantum technologies. We are recognized globally for our high-performance single-photon sources and our foundational contributions to the quantum internet and quantum computing.

jobs.description:
Student Assistant for Supply Chain & Logistics, Salling Group

_Are you an ambitious student looking to gain insight into logistics in Denmark’s largest retail organisation? Are you ready to combine your theoretical knowledge with practical experience and make a difference in a young and dynamic team?

_We are looking for an engaged Student Assistant to join our Logistics Development & Support department at Salling Group. You will have the opportunity to develop your skills and put theory into practice. As part of the team, you will contribute to optimising the journey of goods from our central warehouses to the shelves in Salling Group’s stores.

Your responsibilities

• Analyse large datasets to optimise flows and processes

• Support both large and small projects across Supply Chain & Logistics

• Take part in the daily operations of our Inbound Handling team

• Ad hoc tasks

Who are you?

We imagine that you will start a cand.merc. this summer, preferably in Operations and Supply Chain Analytics. You have strong Excel skills, and experience with VBA, Python or similar programming languages is an advantage. You are fluent in written and spoken English and thrive in a collaborative environment where humour is a natural part of everyday life.

We are looking for a responsible and reliable person who is comfortable taking ownership of projects and is motivated to make a difference. You take initiative, identify opportunities for improvement, and have an interest in logistics and optimisation. With strong analytical skills and a structured approach to your work, you are able to work independently while building strong relationships across the organisation.

What we offer

• The opportunity to apply your theoretical knowledge in practice

• A young and talented team where sparring and development are prioritised

• A varied working day with great colleagues and the opportunity to build a broad network across Salling Group

• Insight into day-to-day warehouse operations through project work and internal inspiration visits

• Opportunities for an internship and collaboration on your Master’s thesis

Practical information

We expect you to work an average of 16 hours per week, with flexibility during exam periods. The position is based in Aarslev, Aarhus.

Please upload your application, CV, transcript of grades and any relevant references no later than Sunday, 22 November 2026. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis. Start date is as soon as possible, with the position continuing until the completion of your master’s degree.

If you have any questions, please feel free to contact Senior Logistics Developer, Camilla Enevoldsen, on +45 22 99 40 09.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Help shape content across Sanos’ brands and LinkedIn channels, and gain hands-on experience with marketing in an international life science organization.

Sanos is looking for a Student Assistant to join our Business Development team for approximately 10 hours per week.

You will work closely with our Brand & Marketing Manager and support the planning, coordination and development of content across Sanos and our specialist brands.

This is a newly created role, giving you the opportunity to help shape it over time. We are looking less for the perfect CV and more for someone who is curious, proactive and motivated to make things happen.

About you

You are probably studying marketing, communication, business, media or another relevant field, but your specific degree matters less to us than your motivation and approach to the work.

We imagine that you:

• Have a genuine interest in LinkedIn, content and digital communication

• Are curious, proactive and comfortable taking initiative

• Are organized and able to keep track of several activities at once

• Have a good eye for language and engaging communication

• Can work independently while collaborating with colleagues across the organization

• Are comfortable communicating in English

Previous experience with social media, content creation or marketing, including tools such as Canva or Adobe, is an advantage, but motivation and drive matter more to us than having done the job before.

About the position

Your tasks will primarily include:

• Planning and coordinating content across our LinkedIn channels

• Developing and drafting social media content based on input from colleagues across the organization

• Turning scientific, commercial and employer branding topics into clear and engaging communication

• Supporting campaigns, conferences and other marketing activities

• Creating and adapting simple marketing materials and visual assets

• Following content performance and using insights to improve future content

You will work across several brands and help move content from idea to publication.

Work location: Telefonvej 8D, 2860 Søborg, Denmark

Working hours: Approximately 10 hours per week, with flexibility around study schedules and exams.

Why join Sanos?

You will become part of our Business Development team and work closely with our Brand & Marketing Manager on marketing activities across Sanos.

The role offers broad exposure to content, branding, social media and commercial marketing in a science-driven organization. As the role develops, there may be opportunities to take on more responsibility within areas such as campaigns, employer branding, analytics or digital marketing.

At Sanos, we have short decision paths, broad responsibilities and a culture where people are trusted to take ownership of their work.

Are we the right cultural fit?

Our commitment to you is encapsulated in our promise to every one of our employees saying,

‘Trust in you – in your development and impact’.

This pledge extends uniformly across all entities within the Sanos organization, ensuring that you feel its effects from the very outset of your interaction.

If you are curious about whether you would thrive within the Sanos culture and the Sanos way of leading, reflect on whether you see yourself working within our principles:

Take on - Responsibility is given, and we inspire you to take it

Try out - Explore diverse tasks and grow professionally

Team up - We don’t just work together; we thrive together

Ready to join us?

We look forward to hearing from you, so please send your application through the “apply” link.

We will be performing interviews throughout the process and look to fill the position as soon as possible. We close the position when we find the right candidate.

Who are we?

Sanos is a clinical development group built around specialized CROs, dedicated clinical research sites and in-house capabilities that support patient recruitment, digital outcomes and clinical supply.

We work across carefully selected therapeutic areas, combining scientific depth with strong execution and close collaboration.

The Impact You'll Make

As a Student Worker, Communications & Events, you’ll help bring communication to life across Danfoss Power Solutions. Through creative content, visual storytelling, and event support, you’ll help colleagues stay informed, connected, and engaged.

Your work will contribute to meaningful communication experiences that help leaders and teams share ideas, business priorities, and important updates across a global organization.

This is an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in communications, content creation, and events while developing practical skills that make a real impact from day one.

What You’ll Be Doing

• 
Create visual and digital communication content that helps employees understand and engage with key messages.

• 
Support video editing, graphic design, presentations, and multimedia projects to strengthen internal communication.

• 
Prepare and maintain communication materials and brand-aligned visual assets that ensure consistency and quality.

• 
Assist with internal events, leadership meetings, and workshops to deliver engaging and well-organized experiences.

• 
Collaborate with colleagues across communications and business teams to contribute ideas, coordinate activities, and support ongoing projects**.**

What We're Looking For

• 
You are currently enrolled as a student in Denmark and able to combine the role with your studies.

• 
You have a strong interest in communications, content creation, visual storytelling, or digital media.

• 
You can use Adobe Creative Cloud tools such as Premiere Pro, Photoshop, Illustrator, or After Effects to create engaging content.

• 
You are comfortable using PowerPoint and standard Microsoft Office applications.

• 
You are organized, dependable, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple priorities while working collaboratively with others.

What You'll Get from Us

• At Danfoss, you’ll join a collaborative communications team where learning and development are part of everyday work.

• You’ll have the opportunity to work on real projects that support a global business while building practical experience in communication, content production, visual design, and events.

• You’ll work alongside experienced professionals who are committed to sharing knowledge, encouraging new ideas, and helping you grow your skills.

• Your contributions will be valued, and you’ll have the chance to see the direct impact of your work.

• Based in Nordborg, you’ll gain exposure to a global communication environment and build relationships across multiple functions and teams.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If this role excites you, we’d love to hear from you! Apply now to start the conversation and learn more about where your career can go with us.

Our Commitment to Transparency

Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

Want to know more? Please visit our FAQ Page.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or other protected category.

Brand

Danfoss engineers solutions that increase machine productivity, reduce emissions, lower energy consumption, and enable electrification.

Our solutions are used in areas such as refrigeration, air conditioning, heating, power conversion, motor control, industrial machinery, marine, and on- and off-highway equipment. We also provide solutions for data centers, renewable energy, energy storage, heat recovery, as well as contribute to district energy solutions for cities.

Our innovative engineering dates back to 1933. Danfoss is family-owned and employs over 39,000 people. We create long-term value for our customers in more than 100 countries with a global footprint of around 100 factories.

jobs.occupation: Senior Associate, Global Clinical Drug Supply Execution
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

Genmab is searching for an energized Senior Associate to be part of Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery team in Copenhagen within commute distance from our office locations to work according to your hybrid work arrangement.

With an impressive pipeline and many ongoing clinical trials, you will have a central role in supporting inspection readiness across our late-stage clinical development portfolio. Your work will help ensure that documentation is complete, compliant and readily available to support the successful execution of business-critical GMP and GCP inspections.

You will support inspection readiness activities within Global Clinical Supply, collecting, organizing and performing completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation. During inspections, you will participate in back-office activities and help ensure timely retrieval and follow-up of requested information.

The role also offers opportunities to develop beyond inspection readiness. Working closely with Clinical Supply Managers in the Portfolio & Project Delivery team and colleagues across the department, you will support selected operational tasks and initiatives while gaining broader exposure to clinical trial management. Through collaboration with Clinical Trial Operations and CROs, and hands-on involvement in clinical supply activities, you will further develop your GCP and clinical supply knowledge.

The position is based in Copenhagen.

**Responsibilities

**

• Support inspection readiness across late-stage clinical trials by collecting, organizing and maintaining relevant clinical supply documentation.

• Perform completeness and compliance checks of trial-specific documentation against applicable procedures and inspection-readiness expectations.

• Participate in back-office activities during GMP and GCP inspections, including document retrieval, request coordination and tracking of responses and follow-up items.

• Support preparation for mock inspections, audits and health authority inspections, including compilation and review of supporting documentation for completeness and readiness.

• Support activities related to day-to-day trial management, including coordination, follow-up and preparation of relevant material and documentation.

• Support distribution and logistics, including tasks related to shipment documentation, in alignment with the Drug Supply Managers.

• Build knowledge of especially GCP but also GMP and clinical supply activities within Global Clinical Supply, Portfolio & Project Delivery function

• Participate in maintenance and continuous improvement of procedures, tools and ways of working supporting inspection readiness and clinical supply activities.

• Responsible for being compliant with Genmab´s quality system.

**Requirements

**

• Minimum a bachelor’s degree or equivalent.

• Some experience working with documentation, quality or compliance activities in the pharmaceutical, biotech, clinical research or another regulated environment is an advantage.

• Knowledge and understanding of GCP and GMP; experience with inspection or audit readiness is an advantage.

• Strong interest in documentation, quality and compliance, with a structured and detail-oriented approach to your work.

• Ability to coordinate activities, maintain structure and follow up on actions involving multiple stakeholders.

• Ability to work successfully under pressure in a fast-paced environment and with tight timelines, including during inspections.

• Ability to be proactive, enthusiastic, curious and goal orientated, with a willingness to learn new GCP/GMP-related activities.

• A team player with demonstrated ability to work effectively cross-functional with internal and external stakeholders.

• Strong communication skills in English - both oral and written.

**The Team

**You will be part of a highly competent team focused on end-to-end trial management including planning and maintenance of supplies for clinical trials, working closely with cross-functional stakeholders in both CMC and Clinical Trial Operations.

Together with Global Clinical Supply Manufacturing and Global Clinical Supply Systems, the teams make up the Global Clinical Supply department. We foster a supportive, international, and fast-paced work environment centered on collaboration, excellence, and a can-do attitude to achieve results.

The proposed gross annual/hourly base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK544.000,00---816.000,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on the role will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Location: On location in Copenhagen, Denmark

Employment type: Full-time

About Teton

Teton is building the autonomous operating system for care. Our technology gives senior living and care teams greater visibility into resident wellbeing, movement, sleep, and care delivery, helping them respond faster, work more efficiently, and provide more personalized care.

The Role

The Finance Systems Engineer will own the systems, data infrastructure, and internal tooling that power Teton’s finance function.

As Teton continues to scale, we need reliable financial data, connected systems, and automated workflows that allow the business to operate efficiently and make informed decisions. You will help strengthen our operational finance capabilities by ensuring our data is accurate, our systems work as intended, and our internal processes are scalable.

This is a hands-on role at the intersection of finance, systems engineering, and data. You will build integrations between our accounting platform, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems, develop tools that make business intelligence data easier to access, and establish controls that maintain data integrity.

What You’ll Own

Finance Data and Systems Infrastructure

• 
Own the systems and data flows supporting Teton’s finance function, ensuring financial information is accurate, accessible, and reliable.

• 
Maintain and improve integrations between accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal product systems.

• 
Identify infrastructure gaps and implement scalable solutions that support Teton’s growth.

Systems Integrations and Automation

• 
Build and maintain integrations and automated workflows that reduce manual work across finance and business operations.

• 
Troubleshoot integration issues, resolve data discrepancies, and implement lasting technical solutions.

• 
Identify opportunities to streamline processes through automation and better system design.

Data Integrity and Financial Controls

• 
Develop internal tools and automated checks to identify missing data, inconsistencies, and potential errors across systems.

• 
Establish reliable reconciliation processes and improve the traceability of financial data.

• 
Strengthen data validation and controls to support accurate reporting and dependable financial operations.

Operational Finance Support

• 
Partner with the finance team to improve day-to-day workflows, reporting capabilities, and access to business-critical information.

• 
Translate operational needs into practical technical solutions that reduce administrative overhead.

• 
Build a scalable systems foundation that supports increasingly sophisticated financial and business intelligence needs.

What Success Looks Like

In your first year, you will have:

• 
Built a reliable, scalable finance systems infrastructure with accurate data and strong integrations across accounting, ERP, CRM, and internal platforms.

• 
Automated key workflows and implemented data validation tools that reduce manual work, improve data integrity, and strengthen financial controls.

• 
Improved access to business intelligence and streamlined finance operations to support Teton’s continued growth.

What We’re Looking For

• 
Experience in finance systems, data engineering, business systems, or a similar technical role.

• 
Degree in Finance, Engineering, Analytics, or a related field.

• 
Strong technical skills in integrations, automation, APIs, and data workflows.

• 
Familiarity with accounting platforms, ERP systems, CRM systems, and financial data integrity.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills, ownership, and the ability to work independently in a fast-growing environment.

• 
Experience with finance automation or in a startup/scale-up environment is a plus.

About Us

Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.

Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on.

Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members.

We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.

The position requires a physical presence at our office in Copenhagen, Denmark. If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.

The Job

We're looking for a talented and driven Product Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build across the whole stack, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Your goal is to shrink the time from a customer request to a deployed solution, without cutting corners on reliability or on the privacy of residents' health data.

In this role, you will focus on:

• 
Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them.

• 
Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward.

• 
Fast Iteration: Break large designs and features into small shippable pieces. Get MVPs in front of users quickly, measure how they're used, and iterate or kill them.

• 
Backend & APIs: Design and build the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them.

• 
Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Build test coverage and use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on.

Qualifications

• 
Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build.

• 
Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native.

• 
Comfortable working across the stack: you've built backend APIs and worked with relational databases (e.g. Postgres), not just UI.

• 
Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed.

• 
Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions.

• 
Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team.

Nice to Have

• 
Experience with React Native and Expo in production.

• 
AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience.

• 
Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications.

• 
Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR).

• 
Experience shipping products across multiple markets and languages.

What We Offer

• 
Participation in our warrant program (stock options).

• 
A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.

• 
A Copenhagen-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture.

• 
Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate.

Join Our Team

We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.

At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.

If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

IST develops software for the education sector across Scandinavia. In Denmark, our system Studie+ handles student administration for vocational colleges, upper secondary schools, AMU, FGU and VUC. It’s a business-critical platform where data quality matters every single day.

We’re now looking for a senior backend developer to take ownership of development and data quality in Studie+. You’ll work in Java Spring Boot and PostgreSQL, act as the team’s database expert, and play a key role in migrating data from other systems into our platform. Like the rest of the team, you’ll use AI tools as a natural part of your day, for coding, reviews and documentation. We don’t expect you to be an expert, just curious and willing to make the most of them.

jobs.description:
About ChemoMetec

ChemoMetec is a worldwide leading manufacturer of cell counting and analysis equipment. We specialize in developing and producing high-precision instrumentation, delivering consistent data for thousands of customers across biotech, pharma, and academic segments.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly motivated and analytically skilled Product Specialist - Technical Support & Data Analysis to support customers and colleagues using our cell-counting instruments. In this role, you will combine cell culture biology with data analysis to help users achieve reliable results, investigate unexpected data, and turn insights into product improvements. The ideal candidate holds a PhD in a relevant field, has hands-on cell culture experience, and enjoys working with data in Python.

We are hiring two Product Specialists for our technical support team: one focused on data analysis and one on documentation. You will be part of the Product Management Department and work closely with R&D, QA, Field Application Scientists, and commercial teams. You will provide application and technical support, analyze instrument and experimental data, and contribute to the successful testing and launch of new products.

This position is based at our headquarters. The role includes occasional travel, both domestically and internationally, depending on needs.

Key Responsibilities

• Provide application and technical support for our instruments, helping customers and colleagues with assay setup, sample preparation, and interpretation of results.

• Analyze customer and internal data sets to identify the root causes of unexpected results and recommend solutions.

• Write and maintain Python scripts to automate data analysis, visualization, and reporting.

• Design and analyze experiments and comparison studies for new features and product releases.

• Support product launches with a focus on application readiness, validation data, and training.

• Contribute to technical documentation, including application notes, troubleshooting guides, and data analysis protocols.

• Assist in troubleshooting instrument software, including reading logs to support root cause analysis.

Qualifications

• PhD in Cell Biology, Biotechnology, Biomedical Science, or a related field.

• Hands-on experience with cell culture and common cell-based assays.

• Solid statistical knowledge, including experimental design and method comparison (e.g., precision, linearity, and regression analysis).

• Strong data analysis and data visualization skills.

• Experience with Python scripting for data analysis (e.g., pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib).

• Familiarity with pharmaceutical workflows and regulated lab environments (e.g., GMP) is a strong advantage.

• Structured, curious, and detail-oriented, with a passion for problem-solving.

Preferred Skills

• Experience with software debugging and troubleshooting, such as reading code and log files.

• Experience with cell counting, image cytometry, flow cytometry, or microscopy.

Why join ChemoMetec?

At ChemoMetec, we believe that great people make a great workplace. We value both personal and professional development and offer an environment where you can grow, take responsibility, and make an impact. You will become part of a team of talented and supportive colleagues who enjoy working together in an informal and welcoming atmosphere. We also believe that strong relationships go beyond the workplace, which is why we regularly bring colleagues together through company-wide events to build connections and strengthen relationships across the organization.

Practical information
