jobs.occupation: Two-year postdoc in developing inventory of agricultural nitrous oxide emissions
jobs.description:
The Department of Environmental Science and the Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, welcomes applications for a postdoctoral researcher position in developing a Tier 3 model-based national inventory of N₂O emissions modelling from cultivation of soils. The position is part of the SmartField project, which is a cross-organizational research project aimed at obtaining knowledge about N₂O emissions from agricultural fields and solutions for mitigation strategies. Additionally, SmartField will develop and deliver an improved methodology for accounting N₂O emissions at farm and national scale.

Expected start date and duration of employment
The position is to be filled by February 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter and is a two-year fixed-term position.

Job description
You will be part of a research environment addressing greenhouse gas emissions and sustainability transition of agricultural systems, with a particular focus on nitrous oxide emissions from agricultural soil aiming to scale emission estimates from the field to the national scale. Your role will primarily involve supporting the development and implementation of a model-based approach for the national of N₂O emissions from diverse agricultural soils, as well as developing the data pipeline. This will include creating and updating spatio-temporal datasets on soils, cropping systems, and field management, and calculating and assessing and comparing the resulting inventories to other approaches. Scenarios will be used to explore how mitigation technologies and management measures could reduce N₂O emissions and to assess the suitability of the proposed Tier 3 modelling framework for Denmark's national N₂O emission inventory. Your work will support a Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) system, enabling transparent, robust and science-based reporting of mitigation progress regarding agricultural field N₂O emission. You will work in close collaboration with colleagues developing and testing process-oriented models, as well as with those responsible for the national greenhouse gas inventory.

Your profile
We are searching for a highly motivated candidate who has:

• A PhD in agronomy, soil science, data science, environmental sciences, engineering, agroecology, biology, or a related field.
• Experience working with models, managing and analyzing large datasets. 
• Experience working with models related to nitrogen/carbon turnover in soil is considered an advantage but is not required.
• Documented experience in scientific writing and publishing in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
• The ability to communicate effectively in English (both written and oral).
• Good collaboration skills and ability to take responsibility to work independently and proactively on the project
Who we are
The position is shared between the Department of Environmental Science and the Department of Agroecology under the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University, and it will be hosted by the Land-CRAFT Center at the AU campus in Aarhus.

The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department with expertise ranging from physics, chemistry, microbiology, engineering, social science, geography, economics, to policy analysis. Basic as well as applied research are conducted on some of the major challenges facing society, such as pollution and pollution control mechanisms, management of land, soil, water, air and biodiversity, protection of ecosystem services, and climate change. Advisory services within these areas are offered to governmental organizations, non-governmental organizations and companies. The department consists of five sections and currently about 160 staff (including postdocs and Ph.D. students). 

The Department of Agroecology contributes to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 400 highly skilled employees.

This position is hosted by Land-CRAFT - the Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Future, which aims to bring transformational solutions to agricultural systems. Land-CRAFT is a section within the Department of Agroecology. Therefore, there is a strong focus on climate change mitigation and adaptation strategies.

Both departments believe in equality, diversity, inclusion, and creating an attractive work/life balance.

What we offer 
• A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.
• An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.
• A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.
• An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.
• An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.
• Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme.
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Aarhus University (LandCRAFT Center), Ole Worms Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. The affiliation will be with the Department of Environmental Science. However, it should also be expected that there will be work-related and meeting activities at the Department of Environmental Science which is located at Risø in Roskilde.

Contact information
Further information may be obtained by contacting Head of Section Emissions and Atmospheric Modelling, Professor Peter L. Langen (plangen@envs.au.dk +4520618369), Professor Jørgen E. Olesen (jeo@agro.au.dk +4540821659), or Special consultant related to the national emission inventory Mette Hjorth Mikkelsen (mhm@envs.au.dk +4587158579). 

Deadline
All applications must be received no later than November 27, 2026. 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

•    A proven track record in the development and execution of global and/or local marketing initiatives, with a history of successful product launches.

Reporting to the VP, Head of Legal, Regulatory and QA, you will operate as a senior individual contributor and legal owner across key business areas. Although the role has no direct line management responsibility, it carries a clear functional leadership mandate: you will shape legal strategy, challenge and support senior stakeholders, lead cross-functional initiatives and set standards for how Legal enables the organisation.

Your mandate

• Strategic legal leadership: Develop and implement legal strategies and risk mitigation frameworks for key business areas, aligned with Fertin’s business objectives, group requirements and legal risk appetite.

• Executive and senior stakeholder counsel: Provide expert, commercially pragmatic legal advice to senior management and cross-functional leaders on complex legal, commercial, regulatory, governance and reputational matters.

• Commercial contracts and business support: Own the legal strategy, negotiation approach and risk position for material commercial agreements, including customer, supplier, development, manufacturing, licensing and strategic collaboration arrangements.

• IP and confidential know-how: Lead the legal framework for protecting Fertin’s IP, know-how and confidential information in commercial and R&D collaborations, including ownership, access rights, confidentiality and contractual protections

• Compliance/GDPR: Lead and implement legal compliance and data protection frameworks in relevant areas, including GDPR, confidentiality, sanctions, third-party risk and group policies, in coordination with PMI Legal where relevant.

• Regulatory, quality and product-related legal matters: Act as legal owner for strategic input into regulatory, quality and product-related matters, identifying legal risks and developing practical solutions across functions and jurisdictions.

• Corporate governance: Develop and implement governance processes, powers of attorney, corporate approvals, board/management documentation and internal legal policies to support clear decision-making and accountability.

• Disputes and claims: Lead the legal handling of disputes, claims and settlement strategies, including legal assessment, risk exposure, negotiation strategy and coordination with external counsel.

• Group and intercompany matters: Support legal structuring and documentation for intercompany arrangements, intra-group services and group governance matters, ensuring clear responsibilities and alignment with business, tax and Finance stakeholders.

• Legal processes, templates and standards: Develop and improve legal processes, contract standards, templates, playbooks and ways of working to strengthen quality, efficiency, consistency and risk management across the organisation.

• AI adoption in Legal: Lead responsible use of AI tools within Legal, including identifying use cases, setting governance principles and ensuring confidentiality, quality and legal risk controls.

The senior profile we are looking for

• You hold a Master of Laws, cand.jur., cand.merc.jur. or an equivalent legal qualification.

• You bring at least five years of relevant experience from an international in-house legal function and/or a law firm, with a track record that demonstrates senior-level judgement and ownership.

• You have substantial experience with sophisticated commercial agreements and legal risk management; experience within compliance, governance, IP or regulated industries will be a strong advantage.

• You are comfortable operating where matters are complex, cross-border or ambiguous, and you know when to decide, challenge, involve others or escalate.

• You can move confidently between strategic advice and hands-on execution—from executive counsel and negotiation strategy to drafting, implementation and follow-through.

• You communicate with authority and clarity, build credibility quickly and can influence stakeholders without relying on formal management authority.

• You are commercially pragmatic without compromising legal integrity, and you are motivated by building solutions and standards that last.

Your impact

This role offers the opportunity to influence decisions close to the business, own matters of strategic importance and leave a visible mark on how Legal operates across Fertin Pharma. Your success will be reflected not only in sound legal outcomes, but also in stronger decision-making, clearer risk ownership and legal frameworks that enable the organisation to move forward with confidence.

Interested?

If you are an experienced legal professional who wants more than a traditional advisory role—and are ready to take ownership, influence senior stakeholders and shape the legal agenda in an international and highly regulated environment—we would like to hear from you.

Special Conditions

As part of our recruitment process, we conduct background checks on all candidates who accept an offer of employment with Fertin. A satisfactory background check is a condition of employment.

The background check is a standard and important part of our hiring process and is carried out in accordance with applicable laws and regulations, as well as Fertin’s internal compliance and integrity requirements.

Do you have a passion for robotics and automation? And would you like to see the solutions you work with come to life at customer sites around the world?

At Inwatec, we develop and build advanced automation and robotic solutions for industrial laundries worldwide. We are looking for a Software Commissioning Engineer who enjoys combining software, robotics, and hands-on problem solving.

You will work closely with our engineers in Denmark, but a big part of your job happens where our solutions are put into action: at customer sites around the world.

YOUR TASKS

• Programming and configuring robots, machines PC and PLC systems

• Testing and commissioning systems at customer sites

• Implementing our automation solutions worldwide

• Troubleshooting software, PLC, network and machine-related issues

• Fine-tuning systems to ensure stability and performance

• Supporting customers during installation and start-up by being the ”Face on-site”

• Being co-responsible in cutomer teaching of our system during training and meetings

YOUR PROFILE

• You have a degree in robotics, automation, software, engineering or a similar technical field

• You have an interest in programming, robotics, and industrial automation

• You enjoy hands-on problem solving, and seeing your solutions work in the real world

• You are curious, independent, and comfortable taking responsibility on-site

• The opportunity to follow solutions from testing in Denmark to full operation at customer sites

• International experience through projects around the world, involving travel from a few days to a couple of weeks, and occasionally longer trips with the possibility of a break along the way

INWATEC - THE LAUNDRYNERDS

JENSEN-Group is a global leader in industrial laundry technology, with roots on Bornholm and a strong developmental focus. Inwatec ApS is part of JENSEN-GROUP, and Inwatec develops and produces machines and robots for industrial laundries worldwide. Are you the kind of person who notices when something could be better, and has the drive to make it happen? At DISA, quality is not just a checkpoint at the end of the process. It is built into the way we design, source, produce and deliver world-class foundry machines. We are looking for a Quality Engineer who wants to be close to the product, close to production and close to the decisions that improve how we work.

This role is for someone who enjoys solving real quality challenges in a manufacturing environment. Someone who is structured, curious and persistent enough to follow an issue from first observation to sustainable improvement.

What You’ll Do

• Take ownership of quality improvements across supplier quality, production quality and internal quality processes.

• Handle non-conformities, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, and ensure follow-up until issues are properly closed.

• Work closely with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers to identify risks, solve quality challenges and prevent repeat issues.

• Support and develop supplier quality performance through audits, structured follow-up, documentation and improvement plans.

• Use data, facts and structured problem-solving tools to analyze trends, set priorities and recommend practical quality improvements.

• Contribute to audits, customer requirements and management systems, with ISO 14001 as an area where you have basic knowledge or interest.

Why You’ll Love Working with Us

• A role where quality is at the center — not a side responsibility.

• The chance to work hands-on with complex, high-precision equipment and see the impact of your improvements in real production.

• A workplace where your structure, curiosity and follow-through help prevent issues before they reach the customer.

• Close collaboration with production, engineering, procurement and suppliers, so you can turn observations into practical improvements.

• The opportunity to help strengthen quality culture in a global industrial company with strong products, proud craftsmanship and long product lifetimes.

You will not be sitting far away from the product or the people making it. You will be part of the daily dialogue around quality, helping colleagues and suppliers understand what went wrong, why it happened and how we make sure it does not happen again.

Who You Are

• You have a background in Engineering, Quality Management, Manufacturing, Production Technology or a similar field.

• You have experience with quality work in a manufacturing, production or industrial environment.

• You are motivated by root cause analysis, corrective actions and the satisfaction of closing issues properly.

• You understand supplier quality or are eager to work closely with suppliers on deviations, audits, documentation and improvement plans.

• You like being close to the shop floor and working with people across functions to solve practical quality challenges.

• You are analytical and structured, but also pragmatic enough to find solutions that work in real life.

• You follow through — because you know that quality improvements only matter when they are actually implemented and sustained.

• You have knowledge of ISO 14001 or an interest in building a basic understanding of environmental management systems.

If you are driven by quality, manufacturing and continuous improvement, and if you enjoy turning problems into clear actions and better ways of working, we would like to hear from you. You do not need to tick every box; what matters most is your quality mindset, your curiosity and your ability to follow through.

About Norican

NORICAN. Metal. Made. Possible.

We are Norican, a global industrial group designing, building and supporting best‑in‑class machines and technologies for metal formation and surface treatment.

Bringing together five leading brands - DISA, Simpson, StrikoWestofen, Wheelabrator and Monitizer – we deliver one connected solution across the production process, supported by full‑service expertise and digital solutions.

Across green sand molding, die casting, sand preparation, melting, transport and dosing, and surface treatment, we help manufacturers improve performance and transform production across a wide range of industries. We build lifetime quality and long‑term partnerships by combining the strengths of our legacy brands to lead the industry through innovation, sustainability and profitable growth.

DISA:

DISA design, build and support premium green sand moulding and cashing machines for the ferrous and non-ferrous foundry industries. For 125 years they have delivered machines that last for decades, and they are highly respected by customers and peers for excellent levels of quality and service. DISA machines keep customers producing relentlessly to the very highest standards. And they empower foundry productivity with a lifetime of efficient and a lower cost per casting.

Want to know more? Ready to apply?

We will review candidates continuously, so please send your application as soon as possible. If you have any questions about the role, please contact Johnny Rasmussen at johnny.rasmussen@norican.com.

jobs.occupation: Technical Lead - Substation Automation and Communication Systems
jobs.description:
Do you have experience with automation and communication systems for high-voltage substations? Can you lead technical work packages and coordinate specialist contributions to deliver an integrated solution? Join COWI as our new Technical Lead and contribute to the development of Denmark’s electricity transmission infrastructure.

Take technical responsibility for substation automation projects

We are looking for an experienced engineer to take technical responsibility for substation automation and communication systems in high-voltage substation projects. You will work on projects ranging from new substations to extensions, refurbishment and replacement of systems at existing sites. You will coordinate specialist contributions, manage technical interfaces and ensure that individual work packages meet the requirements of the overall substation automation solution.

The role combines technical expertise with responsibility for coordinating engineering activities, monitoring progress and ensuring the quality of technical deliverables. You will work closely with the project manager, technical specialists and other engineering disciplines throughout project execution.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Lead and coordinate the technical delivery of substation automation and communication systems.

• Plan and follow up on engineering activities, technical deliverables and milestones within your scope.

• Coordinate specialist contributions and ensure consistency across technical work packages.

• Ensure that technical solutions and documentation comply with project requirements, customer specifications and applicable standards.

• Manage technical interfaces between automation, communication systems, protection systems, primary equipment and auxiliary systems.

• Identify and resolve technical issues in collaboration with specialists and other engineering disciplines.

• Participate in project meetings and advise the project manager on technical matters, dependencies and risks within your area of responsibility.

• Coordinate technical activities with customers, suppliers and other project stakeholders.

Your expertise

You combine a strong technical foundation with a structured approach to planning and coordination. You can assess how individual systems and specialist contributions fit together, communicate technical requirements clearly and follow through on agreed actions.

You work independently and build effective working relationships with colleagues, customers and project partners.

You will also bring:

• A degree in electrical engineering or an equivalent technical qualification, together with more than five years of relevant experience in automation for high-voltage substations.

• A solid understanding of substation automation systems, including control and monitoring functions, communication networks and interfaces to protection equipment.

• An understanding of how substation secondary systems interface with high-voltage primary equipment.

• Experience coordinating technical work packages, planning engineering activities and following up on specialist deliverables.

• The ability to assess technical solutions, manage interfaces and maintain an overview of quality, progress and dependencies.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• The ability to obtain the required security clearance and fulfil the requirements for the designated on-site role of “holdleder” at high-voltage substations.

Your place of work

Depending on project requirements, you may work from one of COWI’s offices in Denmark, at Energinet project locations or partly from home. Travel within Denmark is expected.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

jobs.occupation: Hydrographic Surveyor & Systems Technician at HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor
jobs.description:
Would you like to become the technical go-to person for the systems that keep a fleet of working vessels accurate and operational? At HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor, you will take ownership of dredging systems, survey equipment and onboard IT across the fleet, with plenty of freedom to shape how the area is run.

Take technical ownership across the fleet

HØJ Nordic Marine Contractor has delivered marine construction projects since 1958 and today works across Northern Europe within dredging, offshore wind, coastal protection and maritime infrastructure.

As the fleet grows, HØJ wants to bring more technical knowledge in-house. You will join the technical team in Horsens, where you will take specialist responsibility for the systems connecting dredging operations, positioning, survey equipment and onboard IT. While your colleagues cover other technical areas across the fleet, your primary focus will be the dredging systems and the related IT and survey technology.

Your main focus will be the 3D dredging systems across seven vessels, including Teledyne PDS, positioning equipment, sensors and the supporting IT setup. You will work closely with skippers, crews, project managers and suppliers and become the person they turn to when systems need to be set up, improved or brought back online.

Some days, you will work alongside your colleagues in the technical team in Horsens, planning and coordinating maintenance, configuring systems or supporting vessels remotely. Other days, you will be on board troubleshooting equipment, preparing a vessel for a new project or carrying out planned service and maintenance.

The aim is not only to solve problems when they occur, but to create a more consistent, well-documented and reliable setup across the fleet.

More specifically, you will:

• Take technical ownership of the fleet’s dredging systems and Teledyne PDS setup

• Work with positioning, sensors, multibeam and other survey equipment

• Support and improve onboard IT, networks and communication systems

• Plan preventive maintenance, calibrations and service

• Document the technical setup on each vessel and prepare relevant reports

• Support crews and project managers with troubleshooting and project preparation

One of your first tasks will be to map the existing system landscape across the vessels. You will also help commission the dredging system on a new vessel and establish clearer standards across the fleet.

Good decisions start with good data. But good data does not just happen. At NORDEN, data comes from many places and is used across our business to understand markets, automate processes and make better decisions. Your job is to make sure that data is actually ready to be used.

As our new Data Engineer, you will build the pipelines and datasets that move data through our organisation and turn raw information into something people can trust and work with.

You will not be sitting far away from the business maintaining pipelines no one really talks about. You will work closely with digital and commercial colleagues, understand what they need and build the data foundation that helps them solve real problems.

And while shipping knowledge is something you will pick up along the way, curiosity about data and how to make it useful is something we hope you bring from day one.

Why this role?

Because there is a lot to build, improve and figure out.

You will join nine colleagues in our Data Engineering team in Copenhagen, working with large and varied datasets using PySpark, SQL, Azure DevOps and Microsoft Fabric. And our team is growing beyond Copenhagen. We are setting up a Data Engineering team in Singapore, starting with two colleagues, giving you an even broader team to work and share ideas with.

Some days will be about building something new. Others will be about improving what already exists, finding a smarter way to structure data or figuring out why something is not working quite as expected.

What connects it all is the purpose behind it: making data easier to trust, access and use across NORDEN.

You already know your way around data engineering. Now you are looking for a role where you can have more of a say in how things are built, not just build what has already been decided.

You will manage your solutions, contribute to technical decisions and collaborate closely with the business to understand what our data needs to do.

What you will be doing

You will work across the journey from raw data to reliable datasets that colleagues and systems across NORDEN can actually use.

You will:

• Build and maintain scalable data pipelines.

• Bring internal and external data together and turn it into trusted datasets.

• Transform raw data into useful features and insights.

• Improve how we capture, validate and enrich data.

• Build solutions that are reliable today without making life difficult for whoever needs to work with them tomorrow.

• Work with digital and commercial colleagues to understand what they need from our data and translate that into technical solutions.

What you bring

You know that good data solutions are not only about getting things to work, but about making them reliable, scalable and useful to others.

Besides this you likely have:

• Around 5 years of practical experience in data engineering or a similar role.

• A degree within data, IT, engineering or another analytical field.

• Eligibility to work in Denmark.

FPRT is looking for a Senior Composite Process Technology Manager for our new composite production in Vojens, Denmark, and Moment Professionals manages the recruitment on our behalf. We are looking for a composite specialist with real depth in the technology who can convert transferred know-how into controlled, scalable and repeatable industrial processes. The role suits you if you want to build a production from the ground up and would rather build processes where little is written down yet than step into a production where everything is already in place.

Your everyday at FPRT

You report to the Chief Production Officer, Composite Manufacturing, and you build and lead the composite technology team of composite process engineers and materials and polymer engineers. You work closely with Production, Quality and NDT, HSE, Maintenance and Engineering, Planning and Supply Chain, and you support the competency and qualification standards for supervisors, technicians and operators together with Production and HR. You are the technical authority for composite manufacturing processes, with the mandate to define process parameters, technical standards and work instructions, and to require technical containment, a process review or a production stop when process integrity, product quality or safety is at risk.

Production starts from an existing process that is being transferred to Vojens, and experienced specialists from the group come to the site to hand it over. You lead the technical transfer and convert it into FPRT-controlled specifications, work instructions, training content and qualification requirements, and you define the technical requirements for equipment, tooling, fixtures, utilities and production conditions through trials, pilot builds and ramp-up. You make sure FPRT has clear local ownership of the critical processes and keeps the technical knowledge for the long term. From day one, you are expected to spot where a step can be done smarter and to have the composite understanding to back that view.

Your time is split between the desk and the floor. You own process flows, critical parameters, material requirements and process-control standards, and you define process qualification, inspection points, acceptance criteria and quality gates together with Quality and NDT. When a process starts to drift, you are the primary escalation point: you go to the floor, lead root-cause analysis, non-conformity investigations and corrective actions, and turn the lessons into updated standards and training. The weight of the role lies in the moulding stage and the material side of the process: resin systems, reinforcements such as carbon fibre, adhesives, curing and the conditions that decide whether porosity and voids are designed out or created. You need a sound grasp of finishing, but your depth is in why a part comes out of the mould as it does.

This is a greenfield site. New buildings are under construction on the site, systems are being selected, and support functions such as maintenance, IT and HR are being built in parallel. In the first period you will help shape how things are done well beyond your own field, and the composite team grows as production scales towards stable serial production.

The role is based in Vojens, and being on site is essential during the build-up. English is the working language in instructions and with colleagues across the group. Danish is a strong advantage in daily life on the floor, and if you are not fluent yet, your willingness to learn it counts.

And then there are the benefits:

Real authority over the processes you own, greenfield impact with no legacy to work around, a professional, international environment with a clear mission and purpose, a modern office with gym, sauna and social spaces, and top-of-market compensation for the right experience.

To succeed in the role…

…you do not need to have carried a manager title or to come from defence. What matters is that you know composite technology in depth: why a resin system behaves as it does, what creates strength and what creates defects, and how the environment affects the part. You may come from composite manufacturing in wind energy, marine, aerospace, defence or another high-performance industry, and work today in process or manufacturing engineering, production, materials or as a technical composite specialist. You also take pride in:

• challenging an established method, including one handed over by experienced colleagues, and agreeing on a better answer together.

• taking ownership and making decisions where little is written down yet.

• going to the floor when a process drifts and staying until the root cause is found.

• turning know-how into standards, instructions and training that engineers and operators can work from.

• developing engineers through technical reviews, coaching and structured problem solving.

What you need to bring:

• Either a relevant technical degree or equivalent strong industrial experience, and at least five years in composite manufacturing, process engineering, manufacturing engineering or materials engineering.

• Practical experience with industrial manufacturing of fibre-reinforced composite components and thermoset resin systems such as epoxy, phenolic or other thermosets, and hands-on experience with one or more of resin infusion or transfer processes, filament winding, lay-up, moulding, curing, bonding or composite machining and finishing.

• A proven track record of developing, transferring, industrialising, qualifying or stabilising manufacturing processes into repeatable production, with a solid grip on process control, documentation, process risk assessment, root-cause analysis, non-conformity handling and technical change management.

• Experience leading, mentoring or coaching engineers and production specialists, or acting as their technical authority.

About the Role:

QuNorth is looking for a Quantum Error Correction (QEC) Lead to help develop and lead our collaborative Quantum Error Correction program, in addition to participating in other aspects of operationalizing Magne, QuNorth’s Neutral Atom quantum computer, in a fast-paced but stable startup environment.

QuNorth is a new Nordic Hub for quantum exploration, providing the region’s enterprises, researchers, and startups with the capability to test, learn, and build on Magne, a world-leading Level 2 quantum computer. With strong backing from EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation, QuNorth will operate Magne as a shared platform for Nordic industries, research organisations, and start-ups. Our aim is to provide the access, tools, expertise, and support needed to explore new quantum applications across all relevant areas, including, but not limited to, life sciences, innovative materials, biochemistry, and AI.

Magne’s physical layer, developed by Atom Computing, includes 1200+ Ytterbium-171 atoms, serving as physical qubits with all-to-all connectivity. It can be operated seamlessly in logical mode enabled by Microsoft, providing tens of logical qubits depending on QEC code. Magne can also be operated in physical mode with mid-circuit measurement and feedforward, which in conjunction with its all-to-all connectivity at scale turns Magne into an excellent platform for exploration of novel QEC techniques, unconstrained by “chip topology”. We envision QEC projects and broader QEC-related partnerships to be a strong component of QuNorth’s portfolio. Working directly with the CTO, and interfacing with the CPO team and QuNorth’s users and partners, the QEC Lead will help shape this key component of the QuNorth portfolio. This role will, at least initially, be mostly a technical leadership role, rather than a managerial position.

We are a small and committed team working to build QuNorth from the ground up as a reliable and transparent organization that contributes to the long-term strength of the Nordic quantum computing ecosystem.

Your Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will eagerly engage in many of the following directions:

• Lead QuNorth’s technical work on quantum error correction, including strategy, architecture assessment, simulation, benchmarking, resource estimation, and roadmap development.

• Evaluate and compare QEC codes, decoding approaches, logical gate schemes, error models, and fault-tolerant architectures.

• Work with hardware, software, and theory collaborators to connect QEC requirements and assumptions to realistic device constraints.

• Help identify which QEC approaches are most relevant to QuNorth’s mission and which are not.

• Work closely with QuNorth’s CTO and Quantum Applications and Algorithms Lead to explore the interplay between applications, algorithms, QCVV, compilation, QEC, noise, error mitigation, and logical-mode operation, including opportunities for integration and co-design.

• Represent QuNorth in collaborations, including with universities, research institutes, startups, and enterprises.

• Contribute to proposals, grant applications, reports, publications, presentations, and internal documents.

• Help recruit, mentor, and coordinate future team members working on QEC, quantum architecture, simulation, and related topics.

• Participate in broader company-building work, including technical due diligence, collaborator or partner discussions, product strategy, documentation, and operational tasks.

• Use AI tools effectively and responsibly to accelerate research, coding, literature review, writing, planning, analysis, operations, and internal workflows.

• Help establish a high standard for scientific rigor, clear communication, and effective execution within the company.

Your Experience and Qualifications:

We expect strong candidates to have many of the following:

• A PhD or equivalent experience required in quantum information, quantum computing, physics, computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a related field.

• 3+ years of experience in QEC beyond PhD.

• Deep understanding of quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

• Deep familiarity with topics such as surface codes, qLDPC codes, color codes, bosonic codes, subsystem codes, concatenated codes, holographic codes, and other conventional or emerging QEC approaches.

• ‘Hands-on’ experience with decoding algorithms, error models, threshold analysis, logical error rates, resource estimation, and architecture-level tradeoffs.

• Deep familiarity with QCVV techniques, including benchmarking approaches.

• Deep familiarity with protocols for mitigation and characterization of noise and error, and their relationship with QEC and relevant thresholds.

• Strong programming experience, preferably in Python or similar scientific computing environments, with experience developing simulations, analysis workflows, notebooks, benchmarking tools, or research software.

• Experience collaborating across disciplines with comfort, especially between theory, software, and experimental teams.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfort working in an early-stage environment where priorities evolve and everyone contributes beyond their formal job title.

• Practical experience using AI tools such as LLMs, coding assistants, literature tools, agentic workflows, and AI-enabled analysis environments.

• Good judgment about when AI tools are useful, when they are unreliable, and how to verify their outputs.

The Team:

The position is based in our new offices at Rønnegade 6 in Copenhagen, where Magne is also currently being built. You will be part of the Technology team under the CTO, and will interact closely with the Product team under the CPO and the rest of QuNorth as well.

Like many start-ups, we are building QuNorth as we go. You will join a very entrepreneurial team, driven by curiosity about the technology, with a desire to make an impact while working in a fun and engaging workplace. As an early employee, you will be an important contributor to building this environment along with us.

What We Offer:

A unique opportunity to be part of standing up and operating a quantum computing company with strong backers, in modern offices located centrally in the Innovation District Copenhagen with convenient public transport and lunch service.

Comprehensive remuneration package, including benefits that support an environment where people can grow and do their best work.

This position will be based in Copenhagen, which offers a rare combination of international outlook, strong quantum and deep-tech ecosystem, and excellent quality of life, consistently ranked amongst the most liveable cities in the world.

All applications will be treated in the strictest confidence.

We look very much forward to receiving your application.

Job Description:

Drivetrain Engineer – Wind Power

Goldwind Denmark is looking for a Drivetrain Engineer to contribute to the development of wind turbine drivetrain systems. You will join an international engineering environment where colleagues in Denmark and China work together to develop mechanical concepts, evaluate design solutions and support their implementation.

This opportunity suits you if you enjoy combining component design with an understanding of the complete drivetrain. In a growing company with ambitious technology goals, you can influence new concepts and help turn them into practical solutions while broadening your expertise.

The role

You will develop and evaluate drivetrain concepts, balancing reliability, weight, cost and serviceability. Working with engineering specialists and suppliers, you will translate system requirements and turbine loads into mechanical solutions.

Your responsibilities include:

• Developing concepts for main shafts, bearing arrangements, housings, supporting structures and interfaces with gearboxes and generators.

• Developing mechanical designs supported by calculations, CAD models and technical specifications.

• Assessing load paths, stiffness, alignment, tolerances and component interactions alongside FEA specialists.

• Comparing solutions to improve performance, manufacturability, assembly and maintenance.

• Supporting colleagues in China during detailed design and participating in design reviews.

• Assessing suppliers’ component capabilities, resolving technical questions and supporting design verification and testing.

• Documenting recommendations, assumptions and design risks.

Your profile

You take a systematic, practical approach to engineering, develop concepts independently and challenge assumptions constructively. You involve specialists when needed, take responsibility for your work and communicate your findings clearly.

We expect you to have:

• A degree in mechanical engineering or a related discipline.

• At least five years of relevant experience in mechanical design and development.

• Practical knowledge of one or more drivetrain components, such as shafts, bearings, housings, couplings or gearbox support arrangements.

• A solid grounding in strength, fatigue, stiffness, materials and tolerances.

• Experience with 3D CAD, engineering drawings and mechanical calculations, together with the ability to interpret simulation results and use them to guide design decisions.

• Good written and spoken English and the ability to communicate effectively across teams and cultures.

Experience with wind turbine drivetrains or comparable large rotating machinery is preferred. Experience with rolling or plain bearings, large cast or forged components, drivetrain dynamics, prototype testing or wind turbine certification is an advantage. We also welcome specialists who want to broaden their understanding of the complete drivetrain.

What can you look forward to?

You will have the opportunity to influence drivetrain concepts and help develop them into practical engineering solutions. Your work will span concept development, component design, design reviews and validation, allowing you to see how technical decisions translate into working designs.

Through close collaboration with an international engineering team and specialist suppliers, you will exchange knowledge, explore different approaches and develop both your specialist expertise and your understanding of the complete drivetrain.

About Goldwind

Goldwind Energy ApS (also called Goldwind Denmark) is a R&D focused subsidiary of GOLDWIND SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY CO., LTD. (Goldwind), a world leading wind turbine technology and energy solutions provider headquartered in Beijing, China.

Through the implementation and investment in industry-leading turbine technology, water treatment solutions and other green energy technological ventures, Goldwind has been hailed as one of China’s most innovative companies.

The successful candidate combines scientific credibility with commercial awareness and a genuine interest in understanding client needs. We are looking for a person who can translate complex scientific and regulatory matters into clear advice and practical solutions.

You are:

• Client-oriented and commercially aware, with the confidence to initiate conversations, develop opportunities and build lasting professional relationships.

• An effective project leader, able to maintain direction and quality across technically complex assignments.

• A clear communicator, capable of engaging scientific experts, decision-makers, authorities and other stakeholders.

• Collaborative and internationally oriented, with an interest in working across disciplines, markets and organisational boundaries.

Why join DHI?

To work at DHI means being part of an organisation that is the global leader in solving the world’s toughest challenges in water, environment and sustainability.

In this position we offer to you the opportunity to join a strong company with dedicated colleagues to:

• Shape and grow DHI’s ecotoxicology and environmental advisory business.

• Work at the intersection of chemicals, water environments, environmental regulation and data-driven decision-making.

• Collaborate with ecotoxicologists, environmental scientists, toxicologists, water specialists and modellers across an international organisation.

• Lead meaningful assignments for industry, authorities, utilities and partners.

DHI is a global and independent company dedicated to working on challenges within the fields of water and environment and sustainability. Within these fields, we provide a wide range of advisory, digital advisory, research and water governance services as well as providing leading edge MIKE technologies and products to the market. At DHI, we are constantly looking for passionate and talented people who are eager to join our team.

By joining DHI, you will not only become part of a dynamic and collaborative global team of experts; you will be empowered to innovate, engage and grow in your area of expertise. DHI is committed to disseminate our knowledge effectively and across our worldwide network of offices.

Location & Mobility

Travelling must be expected in the role to enable collaboration with clients and/or inside DHI. Travelling rules as included in employment contract

**Your Responsibilities

**💰 🇩🇰 up to 46,000 DKK gross/month (depending on seniority level)

**Intro

Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you’ll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully - and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people - sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You’ll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We’re looking for a Jun/Mid Level Engineer who’s ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us - through the grind and the wins.

This Is What You Will Achieve

• Owned an OCPP hardening project - chased down a recurring class of vendor quirks (malformed messages, connection drops, the long tail of hardware oddities), shipped the fix, and measurably cut failed sessions or disconnections for that device family.

• Helped shift the team from reacting to incidents to preventing them, through alerting and observability work that catches problems earlier.

• Made real progress on OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPI standards work that other services and front-ends across Monta now rely on.

What You Will Do

• Build and maintain backend services in NetOps' OCPP and charge point domain - protocol handling, message processing, device state, integrations with hardware vendors.

• Debug things that only break in the field. A charge point in Belgium disconnects every 40 minutes - you'll read the OCPP traffic, reproduce it against our emulator, find the cause, and fix it.

• Improve observability and alerting. Add the metrics, dashboards, and alerts that mean the next person doesn't have to guess.

• Take part in on-call once you're ramped up, with a team that treats a rough night as a reason to fix the system, not a rite of passage.

• Automate manual work away - a meaningful part of NetOps' job is removing the human steps that don't scale as our network grows.

• Collaborate across Product, Support, and the operations teams who live with the consequences of what we ship. You won't work in a silo.

**A Brief Overview Of Our Tech Stack

**

• Kotlin services (JVM), with Java where it already lives

• PHP/Laravel monolith - parts of our charge point domain still run here

• OCPP 1.6 / 2.0.1 and OCPI protocol handling

• Event-driven work with Kafka where message volume calls for it

• Observability via Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch/Kibana

• AWS + Kubernetes, with Terraform for infrastructure

What We’re Looking For

• 1–4 years of backend engineering experience, or a strong junior track record with real production exposure. You write clean, readable code and finish what you start.

• Comfortable in a JVM language - Kotlin preferred, Java fine, and we'll help you get there from another stack if the fundamentals are strong. Willingness to touch PHP in our legacy monolith when the work calls for it.

• You enjoy debugging, genuinely - logs, traces, packet-level detail, weird one-off reports from a single customer.

• A sense of ownership - you follow your work into production, watch it, and flag problems early rather than waiting to be asked.

• Nice to have: curiosity about the physical world (our systems talk to metal boxes with electricity in them); clear communication - you can explain what broke and why to someone who isn't an engineer; advanced, deliberate use of AI tools in your daily engineering workflow.

• Bonus points for: exposure to OCPP, OCPI, EV charging, or the EV industry as a driver or enthusiast; IoT, embedded, or telemetry systems where devices in the field misbehave; event-driven architectures (Kafka) or high-volume message processing; reliability/monitoring/on-call experience (Prometheus, Grafana, SLOs); Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code exposure.

**If the mission excites you but your experience isn’t a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway - we care about potential, not perfection.

**AI Competency

• You’ll be expected to work with AI-powered tools. Some we use:

• GitHub Copilot / Claude Code

• ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude

• Notion AI (docs, knowledge, meeting notes)

• Analytics & ML: Langfuse, PyTorch, Mastra

• AI-enhanced testing & monitoring (e.g., generative QA, Grafana ML)

• We don’t expect mastery of all - but we expect comfort learning, experimenting, and adopting AI responsibly.

Why Monta

• Impact, not easy mode - your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one - we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real - priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• The people are extraordinary - talented, driven, and fun to work with. You’ll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

What We Offer

• A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

• A friendly and social company culture with movie nights, Friday bars, pub crawls, and more.

• Free lunch every day.

• Pension & health coverage to keep you secure for today and tomorrow.

• Paid parental leave to support life's big moments.

• Warrants program - be part of our growth story.

• Flexible working hours; as long as you're at key meetings and delivering great work, we trust you to manage your schedule.

Please send us your application in English.

To succeed in this position, your spoken and written English skills need to be proficient. Since Monta is a globally active company, you'll be communicating often and regularly with our co-workers and partners around the world, making your professional English knowledge essential.

Please note that we don't accept unsolicited applications from headhunters or recruitment agencies. Unsolicited applications sent to our company or co-workers are considered to be the property of Monta, and we won't agree to pay any referral compensation or recruiter fee without a signed agreement.

Find out more by visiting https://monta.com/uk/careers/

Would you like to play a key role in ensuring a smooth and professional experience for our clients while working at the intersection of energy, data, systems and operations?

The team is responsible for the operational client journey after a contract has been signed. This includes onboarding and offboarding assets, managing master data, coordinating operational processes, and ensuring that the necessary systems, registrations, and stakeholders are aligned.

The position is full-time, fixed-term maternity cover expected to run from January through December 2027.

Your primary responsibilities

We need a colleague who enjoys working with structure, data and systems, and who takes responsibility for getting processes safely across the line. If you like working in detail, keeping track of many dependencies and at the same time being curious about smarter solutions, you will fit in perfectly here with us.

Anders Borup

Head of Energy Asset Integration & Operations

Who you are

You are structured, thorough, and comfortable working with detailed and data-intensive processes. You take ownership and follow tasks through, even when they involve several systems, teams, and external stakeholders.

At the same time, you are pragmatic and service minded. You communicate clearly, ask questions when something is unclear, and enjoy helping both clients and colleagues find workable solutions.

You do not need to be an energy-market expert from day one. However, you should be curious about the energy sector and motivated to learn how commercial agreements, market processes, data, and physical assets are connected.

• Communicate professionally with both clients and internal stakeholders.

• Are curious about process improvements, automation and the practical use of AI.

• Are fluent in English, both written and spoken. Danish or another European language is an advantage.

Ideally have experience from the energy sector, although this is not a requirement.

Your educational background may be commercial, technical or administrative. Your approach to the work and your ability to create structure and follow through are more important than a specific degree.

We offer

You will join an ambitious energy-trading company operating in a rapidly developing market. You will become part of a collaborative environment with short decision paths, significant responsibility and close interaction between commercial, operational and technical specialists.

The role offers a broad insight into energy trading and the operational management of renewable and flexible assets. Although the position is temporary, you will be given genuine responsibility and the opportunity to make a visible contribution to the team and our clients from the beginning.

Interested?

If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Anders Borup, Manager of Energy Asset Integration & Operations, at +45 44 14 00 95.

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions about this opportunity

Anders Borup

Head of Energy Asset Integration & Operations

abo@norlysenergytrading.com

Flatpay is not just another payment solution; we're dedicated to innovating the market for payment solutions and financial services in the SME segment with our customer-centric and transparent services. As we scale, our Operations organisation needs to scale with us. We are therefore looking for an additional Global Operations Analyst to join the team and to help us build smarter workflows, make better decisions and turn ideas into measurable results across every market.

What you'll do

The next, you might analyse how AI can remove manual work from a customer service process, investigate an urgent escalation or help turn a commercial opportunity into a workflow used by hundreds of agents. • 
Are interested in AI and how it can improve real operational workflows

• 
Enjoy switching between deep analysis, stakeholder management and urgent operational problem solving

Are comfortable working with senior stakeholders across different markets and functions

Are proactive, accountable and motivated by measurable results

• 
Have a genuine get shit done attitude

Are fluent in English and Danish, both verbally and in writing

Job Description

Do you want to help shape how a large IT company measures, manages and documents its information security? Are you motivated by turning data, risk and regulation into practical decisions? If so, you may be our next colleague in the newly established GRC team in Netcompany's Group CISO Office.

Responsibilities and technologies

As a member of the GRC team, you will help ensure that Netcompany has an accurate, data-driven view of the effectiveness of its security controls and its level of compliance. The team takes a pragmatic and technically grounded approach to governance, risk and compliance, and works closely with the Application Security team, the Operations organisation, Internal IT and other business functions across the group.

The GRC team is a small team of colleagues with complementary profiles. We do not expect any one candidate to cover every area described below. Instead, we are looking for broad profiles with solid experience across several of these areas and the motivation to develop within the rest.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing and maintaining risk scenarios, assessing the effectiveness of mitigating controls against the scenarios, and conducting risk assessments to support business decisions

• Establishing automated measurements and KPIs that provide insight into the implementation and effectiveness of security controls across the business

• Interpreting regulatory and contractual security requirements and translating these into Netcompany's security baselines and standard methodologies

• Planning and executing security awareness activities, including phishing simulations, targeted micro-learning, and onboarding/yearly awareness training

• Driving smaller security improvement projects from planning to implementation, combining coordination with hands-on execution

• Developing, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuityDeveloping, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuity

About you

You have broad experience within information security and a solid understanding of its technical aspects alongside a general understanding of the software development life cycle. You combine this with the ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical solutions. Furthermore, you are pragmatic, take ownership of your work and prefer a hands-on approach.

To succeed in this role you:

• Hold a relevant degree or equivalent experience; within IT, engineering, computer science or a similar field.

• Strong analytic skills, with the ability to interpret data and draw meaningful conclusions independently.

• Experience within several of the areas listed in the overview of responsibilities in the role.

• Solid communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to engage effectively with technical teams, business functions, management and, on occasion, customers.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken).

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

We provide a structured career model that allows you to build on your existing experiences.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will support your development and help you achieve your personal and professional goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague in management gives you concrete insights into the various business areas and responsibilities that match your interests and desires.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars tailored to you and where you are in your career. All courses are taught by experienced Netcompany colleagues, ensuring that all content is highly relevant and builds upon your professional skills. Partaking alongside colleagues from across the company helps you build a solid network and provides a strong foundation for your career at Netcompany, both professionally and socially.

Join an inclusive community

At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand your network.

Send us an application

Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance. #LI-SA1

Are you passionate about IT, business, and finance? As a Business Consultant, you will specialise in banking and investment, collaborating with clients and experienced colleagues to design IT solutions and develop expertise in investment processes and corporate actions.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Integration of High-Temperature Heat Pumps in Industrial Processes - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Do you want your research to help industry decide how to electrify its heat supply? At DTU Construct you will combine thermodynamics, optimisation and machine learning to build tools that make the business case for industrial high-temperature heat pumps clear, fast and reliable.

We invite applications for a fully funded PhD position in the Thermal Energy Section of the Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at the Technical University of Denmark. The position is part of HeatMinds, a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network funded by Horizon Europe. HeatMinds brings together 6 universities and research institutes and 12 industrial and research partners across Europe to develop industrial high-temperature heat pumps that upgrade low-grade waste heat to up to about 250 °C.

Your project will address decision making support for heat pump end-users from a first viability check to integration with the process, to flexible operation. You will demonstrate the findings in industrial use cases together with our partners.

Supervision: Prof. Ahmad Arabkoohsar and Prof. Adriano Sciacovelli.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall goal will be, through adequate methodological advancements, to cuts the time and effort needed to assess where and how high-temperature heat pumps should be integrated into industrial sites, and what is their economic value. Your main task will be:

• Develop models to rapidly estimate performance and break-even point for specific sites
• Extent methods for heat pump integration that co-optimize heat recovery, electrification and flexibility provided by heat pumps
• Refine and validate methods during industrial secondments 
• Publish in international journals, present at conferences and take part in HeatMinds network training, summer schools and outreach.
 
You have:

• A solid background in engineering thermodynamics, heat transfer and energy technologies, e.g. conversion or storage systems 
• Familiarity with modelling and numerical simulations, for example for MSc thesis or student projects 
• Programming skills, preferably in Python, Matlab, Modelica or similar 
• Excellent written and spoken English, and the motivation to work in an international, goal-oriented environment.
 
MSCA eligibility: at the time of recruitment, you must not already hold a doctoral degree. You must also not have resided or carried out your main activities (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before your recruitment date.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The PhD salary will be based on the Marie S. Curie compensation scheme conditions and according to the grant agreement. Based on seniority the candidate will receive a minimum of DKK 30.264,08 (base salary) and DKK 1580,90 (PhD supplement). In addition, DTU will also pay pension consisting of 18,07%. Finally, it is possible to apply for family allowance. 

The period of employment is 3 years. The position is a full-time position. Starting date is anticipated as 1 April 2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Professor Ahmad Arabkoohsar ahmar@dtu.dk and Professor Adriano Sciacovelli adrsc@dtu.dk.

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 24 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of thesis (if available) or other publications (if available)
• A short critical literature review (max. 3 pages) on integration of high-temperature heat in industrial processes: select up to 5 relevant publications and explain your choice, compare their methods & findings, identify possible open research questions, explaining how your background would help you address them. Include at least one figure or table of your own making. 
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Join IBSA Nordic as Operative Business Specialist and play a key role in operational support and commercial execution within the Dermo Aesthetics business.
