About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like

• Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

• The opportunity to shape the voice of a high-impact climate technology company in one of its first markets.

• A central role in connecting Photoncycle's customers, product and brand.

• A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant ownership.

• An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BLOXhub with lunch benefits and unlimited coffee.

Photoncycle is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience, and potential.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering?

Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells, a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data.

In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners.

Successful candidates must document:

• Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE)
• Python programming skills
• Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar)
• Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
You will be assessed against the responsibilities and qualifications stated above and the following general criteria:

• Atomistic modelling and DFT experience
• Python programming experience
• Machine learning experience
• Knowledge of materials science, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Communication skills
We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is from 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Alexander Bagger (alexbag@dtu.dk).

You can read more about DTU Physics at https://physics.dtu.dk/.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. jobs.employer_name: Natural Sciences - Institut for Fysik og Astronomi
jobs.description:
The Department of Physics, Aarhus University, invites applications for a 2-year full-time postdoc position in the project “Probing nanoscale heterogeneity in ultrafast phase transitions”.

The position is available from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project
This project will use a recently developed soft X-ray imaging method to probe the dynamics of light-induced phase transitions at the nanoscale using X-ray Free Electron Lasers. The work will also combine lab-based experiments on time-resolved nonlinear optics.

Job responsibilities
The postdoc will be expected to:

• Lead XFEL and synchrotron experiments in soft X-ray imaging
• Prepare and characterise samples
• Lead experiments in nonlinear optics in the laboratory
Qualifications
Applicants must have:

• A PhD degree in Physics, Chemistry or a related field
• Experience with ultrafast lasers and/or X-rays and/or quantum materials
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Ny Munkegade 120, 8000 Aarhus C, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Further information
For further information about the position, please contact: Simon Wall, simon.wall@phys.au.dk.

Application deadline
The application deadline is 16 December 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

**Finance Partner / Senior Finance Partner

****Kalundborg and Taastrup, Denmark

Would you like a role where you can combine hands-on budgeting and financial controlling with exposure to senior stakeholders and some of Novo’s key manufacturing activities?

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship/scholarship, Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Mekanik og Produ
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Mechanical and Production Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells

Research area and project description:
As part of the ERC Starting Grant project DISSEX, which aims at developing a sex-aware multiscale framework to predict vascular dissection risk, we are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our multi-disciplinary Cardiovascular Engineering (CareEng) group at Aarhus University. This PhD project specifically aims at quantifying how human coronary arteries respond to systemic hormonal fluctuations and biomechanical stress through both experimental and computational techniques. There are 2 objectives.

Objective 1: Experimental investigation of vascular adaptation
The candidate will use innovative microfluidic platforms and ex vivo human coronary arteries to recreate physiological and pathological vascular environments. By exposing vascular tissues to controlled flow, pressure, and hormone profiles representative of daily fluctuations in estradiol, cortisol, and testosterone, the project will quantify how endothelial and smooth muscle cells respond in terms of proliferation, apoptosis, signalling, and biomechanical function. Particular attention will be given to endothelial pathways involving nitric oxide and endothelin-1, providing a unique dataset on how systemic and mechanical stimuli jointly influence vascular health.

Objective 2: Development of a multiscale computational model
Building on the experimental findings, the candidate will develop a multiscale computational framework linking cellular activity to vessel-scale biomechanics. Combining agent-based modelling with computational fluid dynamics, the model will integrate hormonal regulation, cellular adaptation, and biomechanical stresses within the vascular wall. The resulting digital platform will enable mechanistic investigation of vascular remodelling processes and provide a foundation for understanding conditions that may predispose arteries to dissection.

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in vascular physiology, Cardiovascular biomechanics, microfluidics and fabrication; computational modelling, and clinical cardiovascular medicine. The project includes close collaboration with clinicians, biologists, and engineers and provides access to state-of-the-art laboratory and computational research facilities.

Qualifications and specific competences:
We are looking for highly motivated and independent candidates with the intention to complete a 3-year PhD at Aarhus University. The ideal candidate is expected to have most of the following qualifications:
 
• Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Biotechnology or relevant fields.
• In-depth knowledge in fluid mechanics and cardiovascular applications.
• Experience with cell culture and tissue engineering
• Familiarity with numerical modelling (CFD), and software such as COMSOL, SimVascular, or similar software
• (optional) Previous exposure to agent-based modelling or systems biology
• excellent written and spoken English (optional Danish).

Place of employment and place of work:
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Department of Mechanical and Production Engineering, Aarhus University, Katrinebjergvej 89F, 8200 Aarhus N.
Contacts:

• Mahdi Abkar, e-mail: abkar@mpe.au.dk (main supervisor)

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics Technology Development
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year postdoctoral position in mass spectrometry and proteomics technology development at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (MBG), Aarhus University, Denmark.

The position is available in the Nielsen Laboratory, which focuses on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based technologies to understand regulatory protein states, post-translational modifications (PTMs), and cellular signalling.

We are seeking an ambitious and technically skilled researcher with demonstrated experience in developing, establishing, or optimizing mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies. Candidates should have a strong background in at least one area of proteomics technology development, including LC-MS/MS method development, chromatographic optimization, sample preparation, PTM analysis, or related analytical technologies.

The position offers an exciting opportunity to pursue innovative technology development while taking an active role in building and shaping a growing research group at Aarhus University.

Expected start date and duration of employment

The position is a two-year postdoctoral appointment with the possibility of extension.
The expected start date is 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
The successful candidate will join a growing research programme focused on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based proteomics technologies and applying these to fundamental questions in molecular and cellular biology.

Our research integrates state-of-the-art mass spectrometry, quantitative proteomics, analytical method development, peptide and protein chemistry, and PTM biology to investigate how regulatory protein states control cellular function.

A central objective of the position is to develop innovative analytical methodologies that expand the capabilities, sensitivity, robustness, and throughput of modern proteomics. Potential research directions include advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition strategies, quantitative PTM proteomics, chromatographic optimization, automated sample preparation, and novel approaches for studying protein regulation.

The position provides considerable scientific freedom to develop and pursue new technological ideas, with opportunities to establish independent research directions and translate methodological innovations into high-impact scientific publications.

As an early member of a newly established research group at Aarhus University, the successful candidate will also have a unique opportunity to actively contribute to the development of the laboratory's scientific activities, technological capabilities, and future research directions.

Primary responsibilities

• Develop, establish, and optimize innovative mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies.
• Design and independently drive research projects with a strong emphasis on analytical innovation and technological advancement.
• Explore and implement new approaches to improve proteomics sensitivity, quantitative accuracy, reproducibility, and analytical throughput.
• Develop and apply advanced proteomics technologies to investigate PTMs and regulatory protein states.
• Contribute to establishing new experimental workflows and analytical capabilities within the laboratory.
• Collaborate with national and international research partners across proteomics, analytical chemistry, and molecular biology.
• Communicate research findings through publications in leading international scientific journals and presentations at scientific conferences.
• Contribute to the scientific development and continued expansion of the research group, including mentoring junior researchers and developing new collaborative projects.
Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in proteomics, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, or a closely related discipline.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have demonstrated the ability to develop, establish, or substantially improve experimental and analytical methodologies, rather than solely applying established proteomics workflows.

Applicants must demonstrate significant hands-on experience and scientific contributions in at least one of the following areas:

• Mass spectrometry method development: Establishment or optimization of advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition methodologies, including data-independent acquisition (DIA), fragmentation strategies, instrument parameter optimization, or related approaches for improving analytical performance on modern mass spectrometry platforms.
• Liquid chromatography and separation technologies: Development and optimization of chromatographic methodologies for proteomics, including LC gradient design, peptide separation, nanoLC or microflow LC, improved peak capacity, or approaches to enhance sensitivity, robustness, and throughput.
• Proteomics sample preparation and workflow development: Development or substantial optimization of protein and peptide sample preparation methodologies, including automated or high-throughput workflows, digestion strategies, sample clean-up, enrichment techniques, or quantitative proteomics applications.
• Post-translational modification proteomics: Development and optimization of methodologies for PTM enrichment, characterization, or quantitative analysis, including phosphorylation, ADP-ribosylation, ubiquitination, or other regulatory protein modifications.
• Peptide and protein chemistry: Development of innovative approaches involving peptide or protein chemistry, chemical modification, affinity enrichment, selective capture, or related analytical strategies relevant to mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
• Innovative proteomics technologies: Development of other advanced analytical approaches, such as low-input or single-cell proteomics, alternative fragmentation techniques, novel sample processing technologies, or integrated analytical workflows.
Expertise in one of these areas is sufficient. Applicants are not expected to possess experience across all the listed technologies. We particularly welcome researchers with a strong technical specialization who are motivated to expand their expertise into complementary areas of proteomics technology development.

Demonstrated scientific achievements
A central selection criterion will be the applicant's demonstrated contribution to methodological development and technological innovation.

Applicants are expected to document relevant expertise through at least one first-author research publication in which they have made a substantial contribution to the development, establishment, or optimization of an analytical method or experimental technology.

In their application, candidates should identify the publication(s) most relevant to this requirement and briefly describe their personal contributions, the technological challenge addressed, and the methodological advances achieved.

Additional qualifications
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage but is not required:

• Proteomics data processing, bioinformatics, quantitative data analysis, or systems biology.
• Advanced computational analysis of LC-MS/MS data, including DIA data processing and statistical evaluation.
• Mammalian cell culture, including experimental perturbations and cellular model systems.
• Handling and processing of biological tissues, clinical samples, or other complex biological materials.
• Development or implementation of laboratory automation and high-throughput experimental workflows.
• Protein biochemistry, molecular biology, or functional studies of protein regulation.
• Programming, scripting, or computational workflow development, including R or Python.
• Experience working across interdisciplinary projects involving analytical technology development and biological applications.
 
Personal qualifications
We are looking for a researcher who:

• Is scientifically ambitious, highly motivated, and driven by developing innovative solutions to challenging analytical problems.
• Demonstrates creativity, initiative, and a strong ability to translate scientific ideas into experimental advances.
• Takes ownership of research projects and has the determination to drive them from initial concept to publication.
• Enjoys solving technical challenges and continuously improving experimental methodologies.
• Thrives in a dynamic research environment where new ideas, technologies, and scientific directions are actively developed.
• Works independently while contributing positively to a collaborative and supportive research environment.
• Has strong scientific communication skills and an interest in developing an independent research profile.

Who we are
The position will be based in the Nielsen Laboratory at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (MBG), Aarhus University.

Our research focuses on understanding how dynamic post-translational modification networks regulate protein function and cellular behaviour. We develop and apply innovative mass spectrometry-based technologies to characterize regulatory protein states and uncover fundamental mechanisms controlling cellular function in health and disease.

The laboratory builds on more than 15 years of internationally recognized research in regulatory proteomics, ADP-ribosylation biology, and mass spectrometry-based technology development.

We are currently establishing and expanding our research activities at Aarhus University, combining technological innovation with fundamental biological discovery.

Joining the laboratory at this stage provides a particularly attractive opportunity for a motivated researcher to help build a research environment, influence its technological development, establish new analytical capabilities, and contribute to defining future research priorities.

The group benefits from strong international scientific connections and an interdisciplinary research environment spanning molecular biology, genome stability, structural biology, enzymology, and advanced proteomics.

MBG provides an outstanding interdisciplinary research environment with state-of-the-art infrastructure and a strong commitment to scientific excellence.

More information:
https://mbg.au.dk

What we offer 
We offer:

• A unique opportunity to take an active role in establishing and shaping a growing proteomics research group at Aarhus University.
• Considerable scientific freedom to develop innovative technologies and pursue independent research ideas.
• Access to advanced mass spectrometry and proteomics research infrastructure.
• Opportunities to pioneer analytical workflows and establish technological capabilities with broad scientific applications.
• A research environment where technological innovation, scientific ambition, and independent initiative are strongly encouraged.
• Strong opportunities for high-impact scientific publications, international collaborations, and conference participation.
• Support for career development, scientific networking, and applications for independent research funding.
• Close interaction with national and international researchers working at the forefront of proteomics, PTM biology, and molecular biology.
• A collaborative and supportive environment that values scientific creativity, technical excellence, and intellectual curiosity.

Place of work and area of employment 
Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, Universitetsbyen 81, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

Contact information
For further information, please contact:

Professor Michael L. Nielsen

Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics

Aarhus University

Email: mln@mbg.au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 23 November 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). • Research ability documented through rising publication and citation records evidenced by appropriate bibliometric parameters in reputable international peerreviewed journals.

Who we are
The Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University is a growing engineering environment with a clear vision for the future of the built environment.

Established in 2021, the department today includes more than 100 researchers and educators and around 1.050 students. The construction sector is facing major challenges related to climate, resource consumption, and the way we design and build our cities and buildings.

Through research, education, and collaboration with industry and public-sector partners, we contribute to developing technological solutions that support a more sustainable built environment.

Our research and development activities are closely connected to the needs of industry and society, and many projects are carried out in collaboration with companies, public authorities, and other research environments. This ensures that the knowledge and technologies developed at the department are relevant in practice and create value beyond the university.

Education is a central part of the department’s identity. We offer Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD programmes in engineering and continuously work to improve the connection between research, teaching, and practice.

Across our programmes, students work with real-world challenges, current technologies, and sustainable solutions for the construction sector.

What we offer
We offer an innovative and collaborative teaching and research environment with close interaction between students, researchers, and industry partners. The department provides well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, and access to shared technical facilities. We offer an interdisciplinary environment with national, international, and industrial collaborators. Our academic environment is built on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and professional dialogue. The workplace is characterised by professionalism, flexibility, and a healthy work–life balance. The department is located at Navitas on the waterfront in Aarhus, Denmark

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is at Navitas, Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, 8000 Aarhus C, Denmark. The area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associate Professor, Giuseppe Abbiati +45 93 52 17 51, abbiati@cae.au.dk.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than December 14 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

jobs.occupation: Experienced High Voltage Specialist wanted for Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst
jobs.description:
Do you have at least three years of high voltage experience? At Bravida, you will install circuit breakers, disconnectors and switchboards and help build substations. Here, you will put your experience to use on critical electrical infrastructure projects that help secure Denmark’s power supply and support the green transition.

On behalf of Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst, Career | a JKS Company is recruiting experienced High Voltage Specialists for projects across Zealand and Lolland-Falster.

Bravida El-Infrastruktur Øst has secured the framework agreement with Energinet, becoming a regular supplier of high voltage installation work across Zealand and Lolland-Falster. With this agreement and a strong order book, Bravida is expanding the department. You will join the team responsible for building, expanding, refurbishing and maintaining the infrastructure that the power grid of the future relies on.

Installation and construction of high voltage installations
You will work at substations and other high voltage installations, putting your experience into practice. You will take responsibility for your own tasks and work alongside your team to deliver safe, high-quality work.

Your responsibilities will include:

• 
Installing and replacing circuit breakers, disconnectors and other substation components

• 
Carrying out cable work and working on earthing systems

• 
Working on switchboards, electrical installations and dismantling tasks

• 
Contributing to the construction, refurbishment and maintenance of high voltage installations

• 
Carrying out quality assurance and maintaining documentation

Over time, you will also share your knowledge by helping apprentices and new colleagues get to grips with their tasks.

You bring solid high voltage experience and take responsibility
You are a qualified electrician or have an equivalent electrical qualification, with at least three years of hands-on experience in high voltage work. You are familiar with the tasks described and comfortable working independently. You take initiative, recognise what needs doing and understand that safety is integral to every task.

We are looking for someone who:

• 
Works independently and takes a structured approach

• 
Takes responsibility for the safety and quality of their work

• 
Is proactive, well-presented and works well with others

• 
Is physically fit and comfortable with hands-on work outdoors and at height

• 
Holds a category B driving licence and can provide a criminal record certificate

You must be able to communicate clearly in English and have a valid work permit for Denmark.

A company vehicle to take home and no on-call duties
At Bravida, you will join a team of skilled, dedicated technicians who take pride in their work.

You will work daytime hours with no on-call duties, normally five days a week. Start times depend on the project, and the working week can be discussed. The role is paid hourly, with pay based on qualifications, plus pension contributions and a flexible benefits allowance under the Danish “fritvalgsordning” scheme.

You will have a company vehicle equipped with the tools and equipment you need, which you can take home. Your exact location is therefore less important, provided you are willing to work at different sites across Zealand and Lolland-Falster.

We look forward to hearing from you
If this sounds like the right role for you, please send us your CV. We review applications and invite suitable candidates to interviews on an ongoing basis, and will close the vacancy once the right candidates have been found.

If you have any questions about the role that are not covered in this advertisement, please contact Recruitment Specialist Kristine Askjær on +45 3085 1302.

Please note that, for GDPR reasons, applications submitted directly by email will not be processed or receive a response.

• The ability to deal positively with change and comfort working in a global environment.

• Strong organizational abilities and flexibility to work in a fast-paced, performance driven environment managing multiple project priorities.

Our restaurant in Kalundborg is a well-run, busy operation with a proven concept, experienced ownership and a clear direction. Located right in the middle of Kalundborg's main pedestrian street, we are a lively, pulsing part of the town and a gathering place for its residents. Our purpose is to create a vibrant place for the people of Kalundborg, built on quality ingredients and good food. We are now strengthening our kitchen team and are looking for chefs who want to become part of a structured, professional kitchen and contribute to consistent, high-quality service every day.

Our concept is based on modern Danish cuisine with a Nordic twist, combined with well executed brasserie classics and a varied à la carte menu. We focus on quality ingredients, solid craftsmanship and seasonal cooking, with dishes that combine flavour, comfort and consistency. Our menu includes both classic meat dishes, such as pepper steak, pasta dishes and other popular brasserie favourites.

Alongside our à la carte service, we have a private dining and events room, which you will also be part of. It brings welcome variety to the daily kitchen work, with menus that differ from the standard à la carte and the chance to cook for parties, celebrations and special occasions.

You will be joining a business with an already proven concept, an organised kitchen and a strong operational foundation. The setup is stable and well prepared, giving you a secure framework in which to do great work and develop your craft. Here you also get the freedom to bring your own ideas to life. We are not a place where everything is dictated from above — our chefs and kitchen staff are given the room to develop dishes, contribute to the menu and put their own mark on the food.

We are a serious but friendly workplace with respectful leadership, an organised kitchen environment and a no-drama culture. We believe strong kitchens are built on structure, teamwork and professionalism.

We are looking for chefs / cooks who:
• Have experience working in a professional kitchen

About the job

At Saxo, we believe access to global capital markets should be simple and accessible. As Senior Legal Counsel, you will play a key role in supporting Saxo's continued growth, innovation and strategic ambitions.

Reporting to the General Counsel, you will provide trusted legal advice across a broad range of business initiatives, regulatory developments, corporate matters, commercial activities, governance matters and strategic projects. Working closely with stakeholders across our offices in both Denmark and abroad, you will help ensure that legal considerations enable business success while maintaining the highest standards of governance, integrity and regulatory compliance.

This role combines strong legal expertise with stakeholder management and business partnership. As Senior Legal Counsel, you will act as a trusted advisor across Saxo, providing pragmatic legal guidance and partnering with stakeholders at all levels of the organisation to navigate legal complexity and support informed decision-making.

Responsibilities

As Senior Legal Counsel, you will:

• Provide strategic legal advice to key stakeholders across Saxo.

• Support commercial, corporate, governance and regulatory matters affecting the business.

• Advise on marketing activities, customer communications, commercial partnerships and strategic business initiatives.

• Partner with business stakeholders to ensure legal risks are appropriately identified and managed.

• Support product development, business expansion initiatives and corporate projects.

• Contribute to effective legal governance frameworks and decision-making processes.

• Collaborate closely with Compliance, Risk Management, Internal Audit and other control functions.

• Manage relationships with external counsel and legal service providers.

• Monitor regulatory developments and support the implementation of relevant legal and regulatory requirements.

• Contribute to the continuous development of the Legal function and strengthen its role as a proactive business partner.

Your profile

You are an experienced legal professional with a strong legal foundation and a proven ability to navigate complex business challenges in a highly regulated environment.

You bring solid legal expertise, sound commercial judgement and the credibility to serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders across the organisation. You are comfortable balancing legal risk with business priorities and have a pragmatic, solution-oriented approach to legal advisory.

To succeed in this role, you will preferably have:

• A master's degree in law or an equivalent legal qualification.

• Solidlegal experience preferably gained either within the financial services industry or at a leading law firm advising clients in regulated sectors.

• Understanding of the legal and regulatory framework governing financial institutions and financial markets.

• Experience advising business stakeholders on legal matters in relation to strategic initiatives and commercial matters.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex legal matters into practical business advice.

• A proactive, commercially minded and collaborative approach.

Beyond your technical legal capabilities, you are a trusted business partner who builds strong relationships across the organisation and enables informed decision-making while maintaining a high standard of legal governance and integrity.

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

Für das Hotel Hesselet wird ein Kellner gesucht.

Möchten Sie dazu beitragen, ein neues Restauranterlebnis im Hotel Hesselet zu eröffnen? Am 1. März 2027 eröffnen wir das Restaurant Hi – ein neu erbautes Pavillonrestaurant im Hotel Hesselet, das als exklusives kulinarisches Universum mit offener Küche, einladendem Ambiente und einem starken Fokus auf Gastfreundschaft, Kultur und ganzheitliche Erlebnisse geschaffen wurde.

Das Hotel Hesselet liegt an einem der schönsten Orte Fünens. Direkt dort, wo der Wald auf das Meer trifft und man die Brücke zwischen Seeland und Fünen sehen kann. Das Hotel befindet sich in Nyborg, das im Mittelalter der Treffpunkt des Königs mit den wichtigsten Persönlichkeiten des Reiches war. Heute ist das Hotel ein Ort der Begegnung, an dem Gastfreundschaft zur Geborgenheit wird.

Das Hotel ist nach dem Wald benannt, in dem es liegt. Hesselet bedeutet „Ort, wo die kleinen Haselnusssträucher wachsen“. Wir sind stolz darauf, zu Dänemarks beliebtesten Strandhotels zu gehören und bemühen uns, all unseren Gästen ein außergewöhnliches Erlebnis zu bieten – egal ob sie bei uns übernachten, speisen oder an einer Konferenz teilnehmen.

Das Hotel Hesselet verändert sich – und ist in guten Händen

Im Jahr 2024 wurde das Hotel Hesselet vom Carama Family Office übernommen, das eine klare Vision verfolgt: die Seele von Hesselet zu bewahren und gleichzeitig das Hotel für zukünftige Gästeerlebnisse weiterzuentwickeln – ohne dabei die Geschichte und die Wärme des Ortes zu beeinträchtigen.

Die neuen Eigentümer haben mit einer behutsamen Renovierung der Hoteleinrichtungen, des Restaurants und der Außenanlagen begonnen. Es wird sowohl in das Ambiente als auch in die Mitarbeiter investiert – mit einem starken Fokus auf Professionalität, Wohlbefinden und erstklassigen Service.

Das Ziel ist ambitioniert, aber klar: Das Hotel Hesselet soll zu den attraktivsten Hotels Dänemarks zählen – sowohl für Gäste als auch für Mitarbeiter. Hier soll man die besondere Ruhe, Qualität und Atmosphäre spüren können, für die Hesselet seit 1967 bekannt ist – in einer zeitgemäßen und modernen Interpretation.

Möchten Sie dazu beitragen, exzellenten Service und großartige Gästeerlebnisse zu bieten?

Wir suchen einen Kellner, der Teil eines kompetenten Teams werden möchte, in dem stolze Traditionen, hohe Qualität und eine gute Atmosphäre Hand in Hand gehen.

Als Teil unseres Servicepersonals arbeiten Sie in unserem Restaurant, in Veranstaltungsräumen und bei Konferenzen.

Sie werden ein wichtiger Bestandteil des Gästeerlebnisses sein – vom Frühstück und Mittagessen bis zum Abendservice und besonderen Veranstaltungen.

Wir bieten:

• Ein starkes, engagiertes Team mit tollen Kollegen und einem Fokus auf Zusammenarbeit

• Ein Arbeitsplatz mit hohem Serviceniveau und vielen Stammkunden

• Möglichkeit zur beruflichen Weiterentwicklung und Übernahme von Verantwortung

• Ein abwechslungsreicher Alltag mit alltäglichen Gästen, Partys und Treffen

• Eine fantastische Lage und ein Haus mit Seele und Geschichte

Wir erwarten von Ihnen Folgendes:

• Er ist ein Kellner und legt großen Wert auf guten Service und Gastfreundschaft.

• Behalten Sie den Überblick, bleiben Sie ruhig und lächeln Sie – auch wenn es mal hektisch zugeht.

• Ist flexibel und kann Termine einhalten

• Blüht in Teamarbeit auf, kann aber auch selbstständig Verantwortung übernehmen.

• Ich interessiere mich für Wein, Essen und Gästeerlebnisse.

Arbeitsumfeld

Im Hotel Hesselet pflegen wir eine herzliche, familiäre und freundschaftliche Atmosphäre – sowohl unter Kollegen als auch gegenüber unseren Gästen. Wir sind überzeugt, dass die besten Ergebnisse durch echte Zusammenarbeit, gegenseitige Präsenz und Interesse entstehen.

Wir erwarten von Ihnen, dass Sie Ihre Persönlichkeit, Ihre Energie und Ihr Engagement einbringen – sowohl in Ihrer Arbeit als auch im Umgang mit Kollegen und Gästen. Im Gegenzug bieten wir Ihnen ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem wir uns gegenseitig unterstützen und als Team zusammenarbeiten, wobei Wohlbefinden und Erfolg gleichermaßen im Fokus stehen.

Wir arbeiten intensiv daran, einen der besten Arbeitsplätze der Branche in Dänemark zu schaffen – und als Teil unseres Serviceteams werden Sie Teil eines engagierten und dynamischen Unternehmens mit ambitionierten Zielen und hoher Professionalität. Wir bieten gute Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten, ein gesundes Arbeitsumfeld und viel Raum, um mit den Aufgaben zu wachsen.

Gehalt und Konditionen

Gehalt nach Qualifikation. Zusätzlich bieten wir Altersvorsorge, Krankenversicherung und weitere Beschäftigungsbedingungen gemäß Tarifvertrag und gegebenenfalls weiterer Vereinbarung. Es handelt sich um eine Vollzeitstelle mit frühestmöglichem Eintrittstermin oder nach Vereinbarung.

Senden Sie Ihre Bewerbung und Ihren Lebenslauf an unseren Restaurantleiter Rasmus Weimar unter rasmus@hesselet.dk – am besten so bald wie möglich, da wir laufend Vorstellungsgespräche führen.

Sollten Sie Fragen zur Stelle haben, können Sie ihn gerne direkt unter der Telefonnummer (45) 65 31 30 29 kontaktieren.

Klingt das nach etwas, von dem Sie gerne hören würden? Dann freuen wir uns darauf, von Ihnen zu hören.

Do you want to build intelligent software that powers the future of sports coaching? Are you passionate about transforming raw data and AI model predictions into meaningful, real-world metrics for professional American football players? Then come and join our ambitious and collaborative product team!

Data is revolutionizing sports. Join our team to play.

This is a great opportunity to join our growing New Sports team within our Tracking Department. Our team is responsible for the development of the firmware for our American football products. We are developing cutting-edge solutions that leverage deep learning, classic computer vision, machine learning, and signal processing algorithms to deliver product features. Through our market leading radar and computer vision-based tracking technology, we are building products used by some of the best athletes in the world.

Example projects we are working on:

• 
Detecting and tracking objects, such as balls, players, and clubs, across several different sports

• 
Optical flow for determining ball flight characteristics

• 
Calibration between radar and camera data for drawing tracks in broadcast television

• 
Human pose tracking for analyzing athlete performance

Are you our new colleague?

Our ideal candidate is specialized the area of computer vision and machine learning. You will be joining a team of specialists within these fields and together we strive to remain the best in the world at what we do. Your responsibilities will include development of new and existing products and core processes based on your experience and skills.

In the new sports team we value teamwork and openness. Therefore, we expect you to enjoy working with other highly motivated colleagues and help provide a good working environment. We do not expect that you can be an expert on every aspect of being a developer, but rather strive to improve and learn together with the team.

Responsibilities:

• 
Develop advanced DL, ML, classic computer vision, algorithms.

• 
Write production ready code, with emphasis on deployment, monitoring and supportability

• 
Design and execute experiments to acquire and prepare datasets for algorithm development

• 
Develop and extend tooling for computer vision development. This can include data visualization, annotation and debugging

• 
Develop appropriate system architecture for edge-based and server solutions

• 
Collaborate with engineers within Vision & AI and the tracking department to produce high quality cutting edge systems

Job requirements

• 
Master’s Degree or Ph.D. in computer vision, machine learning, computer science, mathematical modelling, or equivalent

• 
3+ years of practical experience in implementing and deploying computer vision systems, with a proven track record of successful project execution and system optimization

• 
Strong software development and programming skills within Python and C++

• 
Experienced in computer vision techniques, including object detection, video tracking, and image analysis, as well as deep learning and convolutional neural networks in machine learning

• 
You have an entrepreneurial mindset and thrive on taking an idea from concept to a polished implementation.

Nice to haves:

• 
Experience with or knowledge of image acquisition, camera calibration

• 
Preferably experience with or knowledge of video formats and camera hardware, drivers and low-level software

Working in a fast-paced, team-based environment also demands a certain degree of self-planning, as well as the ability to work independently. Your colleagues are highly skilled, innovative and pro-active in their work approach. They possess strong analytical skills, are good communicators in English, and take pride in their job and deliverables. We expect you to be of a similar caliber.

We offer:

Highly skilled colleagues

World class office facilities

International environment with more than 35 nationalities in our HQ

Social activities

jobs.occupation: AIV Planner - help turn spacecraft assembly into a scalable production flow
jobs.description:
In our Satellite Assembly, Integration, and Verification Team, you will be at the center of planning how spacecraft are assembled, integrated, tested, and tracked. You will translate complex AIV activities into executable production flows and system structures, while coordinating the interfaces that make the flow work in practice. If you combine strong systems understanding with structure, initiative, and a drive to build better solutions, this is your opportunity to shape how we manufacture satellites.

About the Position as AIV Planner

As AIV Planner, you will own the planning framework supporting spacecraft assembly and verification. You will establish and maintain production flows, routings, and planning data in our ERP system while coordinating activities across AIV, production, project management, and logistics to ensure efficient execution.

You will play a key role in developing scalable planning processes, improving digital ways of working, and connecting future ERP and MES capabilities to the needs of spacecraft production. Your experience and ideas will directly influence a more controlled, digital, and scalable production flow.

Responsibilities include:

You will ensure that spacecraft build plans are translated into controlled and executable work in our operational systems, while aligning the interfaces needed for reliable AIV execution.

Production Planning and System Execution

• Create and maintain AIV routings, production orders, planning parameters, and relevant production master data in the ERP system.

• Translate engineering structures and AIV plans into practical production sequences with clear dependencies, revisions, effectivity, and material requirements.

• Monitor order progress and data quality, resolve planning issues, and help establish the ERP system as the operational source of truth for spacecraft build execution.

Cross-functional Planning and Material Flow

• Coordinate with Electronic Production, Project Management, AIV, engineering, warehouse, and other planners to align readiness, priorities, materials, and handovers.

• Coordinate AIV inventory and material flow, including allocation, kitting, shortages, transfers, returns, and controlled movement of hardware.

Configuration, Change, and Improvement

• Maintain configuration and traceability in the ERP system, including correct parts, revisions, serial numbers, routings, effectivity, material movements, and as-built status.

• Assist the ECR/ECO process by identifying affected routings and production orders, supporting change-impact assessment, and implementing approved changes in the ERP system with the required traceability.

What you bring

At GomSpace, it’s not just your technical skills that matter - your character is also important. We value individuals who bring a positive, proactive attitude and can build trust across cultures. The ideal candidate will be comfortable taking ownership in an environment that is still being built, combining a strong systems understanding with practical knowledge of production flows and the ability to quickly learn new tools and processes.

You likely:

• Have minimum 3 years of experience in production planning, working with ERP, MES, or similar operational systems. Experience with IFS is a strong plus, but not mandatory.

• Practical understanding of production flows, routings, production orders, material availability, sequencing, and master data.

• Ability to understand system relationships and translate engineering and operational inputs into a clear, executable production flow.

• Experience with configuration management, revision control, serial-number traceability, and as-built records.

• Ability to coordinate across multiple interfaces and turn incomplete or changing inputs into a structured plan.

• Strong drive, ownership, and a solution-oriented mindset, with the ability to establish and improve processes rather than only operate existing ones.

• Clear written and verbal communication in English.

Here’s why you’ll love working with us:

At GomSpace, we’re on a mission to shape the future of space – one mission at a time. Here, you’ll be part of something bigger than just a project or a product. You’ll help build systems that connect people, enable science and expand humanity’s reach beyond Earth.

We believe the best results come when talented people are trusted, supported, and inspired to push boundaries together.

• Be part of a global company making a real impact in the space industry

• Get freedom under responsibility from day one – and grow with us

• Join a dynamic, full-service environment where no two days are alike

• Work across borders and build a strong international network

• Be part of a culture where collaboration beats competition – and milestones are celebrated together

Join our mission

You are welcome to send your application in Danish or English. Interviews will be conducted on a continuous basis. Apply for the job by following the link below.

If you have any questions with regard to the position do not hesitate to contact: Simon Holt Olsen, Head of AIV, shol@gomspace.com.

Workplace will be at our premises at Langagervej 6, Aalborg, Denmark and it is expected that most of the time is in the offices.

As part of our recruitment process, employment requires you to complete a background check conducted by an authorized third-party provider in accordance with applicable legislation.

At GomSpace WE MAKE SPACE YOURS

GomSpace is a globally leading designer, integrator and manufacturer of high-end nano and microsatellites for customers in the academic, government and commercial markets. Our positions of strength include systems integration, small satellite subsystems and advanced miniaturized radio technology. At the core of our mission are our core values: Be helpful, communicate openly and frequently, and show true leadership.

Our international team is devoted to understanding our customers’ requirements and delivering high quality. We are listed in Stockholm (GOMX), headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in Sweden, Singapore, France, North America and Luxembourg. Join us in shaping the future of space exploration!

Polyteknik AS is expanding, and we are therefore searching for an excellent leader for our competent mechanical engineering team. The mechanical engineering team designs highly advanced production systems for the semicon/mems/sensor and ICT industries primarily in Europe.

Tasks

Our team of mechanical engineers takes Polyteknik’s advanced production systems from initial concept through detailed design to the production-ready BOM. The team currently consists of 7 people. Polyteknik has grown rapidly the recent years and continues to expand, and the mechanical engineering team will grow with it. One of your tasks as team leader will be to drive the development and expansion of the team.

You will manage the team and, in close collaboration with the process and automation engineers, physicists and skilled technicians, design and construct advanced PVD systems. The job involves coordination of a wide range of mechanical engineering tasks from idea generation to overviewing the design of complete systems involving structural, electrical, vacuum, and pneumatic components as well as ensuring the documentation and user manuals for the systems.

• Further development and implementation of the different Polyteknik design standards

• Resource and task planning for the team

• Ensure knowledge sharing and coordination with the other teams at Polyteknik

• Ensure that best practice is shared and efficient work methods are adapted across the team

• Degree in Mechanical engineering or similar relevant education

• Preferably with a vast practical technical knowhow

• Proven management skills and a dialogue inviting people person

• Interest in design and vast experience with 3D construction in Solidworks

• Analytical and structured work approach and accustomed to working with deadlines

• Good at cooperating across tasks and teams, internally and externally, to achieve common goals

Polyteknik AS is a Danish PVD systems manufacturer with an innovative and best service approach. With more than 30 years in business, an international reference list, and an excellent platform of technology, Polyteknik AS has proved to be an appreciated partner in the thin film industry.

Are you passionate about shaping how product data connects engineering, manufacturing, service, commercialization and sustainability? Join us as we strengthen the data foundation behind our Product Lifecycle Management landscape and create trusted, governed and reusable product information that can support digital transformation, analytics and AI.

As our new Lead PLM Data Architect, you will shape and evolve the data architecture for PLM across the full product lifecycle. You will connect business meaning and governance with logical information models, data products, Systems of Record and their implementation across our PLM and enterprise system landscape.

You will play a leading role in turning product data into a strategic business asset and ensuring that our PLM data landscape becomes more coherent, governed, interoperable and ready for future digital capabilities.

What you will be doing

In the Global PLM & Data Management team, you will provide architectural leadership for PLM-related data and information. You will work across business, data governance, PLM, IT and transformation initiatives to create a coherent connection between business needs, governed information and technical implementation.

Your main responsibilities include:

• Own and evolve the PLM data architecture, ensuring alignment between PLM strategy, enterprise data principles, business capabilities and the broader enterprise IT landscape.

• Translate business needs into governed information structures, connecting business terminology, logical information models, data products and physical system implementation.

• Shape PLM information models and semantics, including product structures, classifications, attributes, relationships, metadata and lifecycle information.

• Define and architect PLM data products as reusable and trusted business assets with clear definitions, ownership, stewardship, quality expectations, lifecycle states and authoritative sources.

• Establish clear architectural relationships between data ownership, information models and Systems of Record, supporting consistent implementation of governed product information.

What makes you a great fit

You are a systems thinker and data architecture leader who understands that successful PLM transformation depends not only on applications, but on having clear, governed and connected product information.You can move comfortably between business language, information models, data governance and technical architecture, and you are able to simplify complex data topics for stakeholders across functions.

We also imagine that you have:

• A master’s degree in engineering, computer science, information systems, data management or similar, or equivalent experience
