jobs.description:
Company Description

With more than 8,000 employees, Deloitte is one of the largest professional services firms across the Nordics. We help clients navigate complex business and technology transformations by combining deep industry expertise with leading capabilities in Audit, Tax, Advisory, and Consulting.

Are you passionate about the financial services sector and ready to contribute to high-quality audits in one of the most complex, dynamic and highly regulated industries? We are looking for talented audit professionals to join our Banking & Insurance team in Deloitte Denmark.

We serve a broad range of clients, from major Nordic banks and insurance companies to specialised financial services providers. Our work combines strong audit quality, deep sector knowledge and close collaboration as we help clients navigate complex financial reporting, regulatory and risk-related requirements.

Our Audit & Assurance Banking & Insurance practice brings together approximately 35 professionals. You will join an environment where quality and professional development come first, supported by structured learning, mentorship and exposure to challenging, real-world assignments. We value collaboration, different perspectives and an inclusive culture where people can contribute authentically and develop their careers.

Whether you aspire to become a state-authorised public accountant, deepen your expertise within banking or insurance, or build a broader profile combining audit and advisory experience, we will support your development. Join a community committed to continuous learning and creating lasting value for financial institutions across the Nordics.

Job Description

As an Assistant or Senior in our Banking & Insurance practice, you will play a central role in delivering high-quality audit and assurance services to commercial banks, investment banks, insurance companies and other regulated financial institutions across the Nordics.

Your responsibilities will span the audit lifecycle, from planning and risk assessment to execution and reporting. Depending on your experience level, you will either contribute to defined audit areas with support from experienced colleagues or take broader ownership of workstreams, client interactions and the development of junior team members. Your work will focus on financial reporting, regulatory requirements, operational risks and emerging topics such as cybersecurity, data and digital transformation.

The position is based in our Copenhagen office. Your work will include time at client locations.

In this role, you will

• Own audit workstreams appropriate to your experience level, demonstrating initiative and sound judgement in complex situations.

• Contribute to consistently high audit quality by applying professional scepticism, robust methodology and attention to detail.

• Develop deep sector knowledge of banking and insurance, including the regulatory frameworks, business models and risk profiles that shape these industries.

• Build trusted relationships with clients and colleagues through professionalism, reliability and a genuine interest in their success.

• Use analytical tools and data-driven approaches to identify relevant risks, patterns and insights.

• Mentor and support junior team members, contributing to a culture of continuous improvement and knowledge sharing.

• Use data analytics, automation and AI-enabled tools to support risk assessment, test relevant populations and identify patterns, anomalies and risk indicators that require further audit attention.

You will work in a collaborative environment where your voice is heard, your development is prioritised and your contributions influence how we serve our clients.

Qualifications

You hold a master's degree in accounting, auditing or a related field, or you are actively pursuing such a qualification.

What we're looking for:

• 2–6 years of audit experience, with a demonstrated ability to take ownership of assignments and drive progress.

• A strong analytical mindset: You are curious about how things work, comfortable with data and numbers, and able to identify patterns and anomalies.

• Risk-oriented thinking: You understand that audit is fundamentally about risk assessment and can apply this perspective to complex business scenarios.

• Clear communication: You can explain complex financial and regulatory topics to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Fluent Danish: You can communicate confidently in Danish, both verbally and in writing, as you will work with Danish clients and documentation. This is a requirement for the role.

• Strong English skills: You can work effectively in English, both verbally and in writing, as English is our firm language.

• A genuine interest in people: You listen actively, support colleagues and recognise the value of diverse teams.

• A commitment to growth: You are eager to deepen your expertise, learn from experienced professionals and support the development of others.

Even if you do not meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply if you believe you can contribute meaningfully to our team.

What we offer:

• Continuous learning and development: Access to technical training, sector-specific workshops, professional development programmes and support from experienced colleagues.

• Exposure to leading financial institutions: Opportunities to understand how the Nordic banking and insurance sectors operate.

• Structured mentorship: Guidance from experienced partners and senior colleagues who are invested in your development.

• Flexibility and autonomy: Trust and support to manage your work within flexible working arrangements.

• A vibrant community: A team that values professional connection as well as social activities and events.

• Career pathways: Support whether your ambition is state authorisation, leadership, sector specialisation or a broader audit and advisory profile.

Additional Information

Do you want to be part of our team?

Click the "I am interested" button above if you are ready to join our team.

Send your application, CV, a brief cover letter outlining your interest in banking and insurance audit and assurance work. We process applications and arrange interviews continually, so we recommend that you apply as soon as possible.

Please do not hesitate to contact Contact Kristian Ehrenreich Hansen, Partner, or Lica Lyngsø Møller, Partner. They would be happy to discuss the role and our Banking & Insurance team.

At Deloitte, we value different skills, perspectives, and experiences, as it enables us to effectively solve complex challenges for our clients. We encourage you to apply for the position if you believe your skills can contribute to our team´s success.

We encourage all candidates to apply for the position regardless of, e.g., age, gender (gender identity and gender expression), sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, nationality, or disability.

By applying for this job, you will be assessed against the Deloitte Global Talent Standards. We have designed these standards to provide a consistent and exceptional Deloitte employee experience globally.

We look forward to connecting with you!

In Deloitte, you will find passionate, caring people who are curious by nature and striving to evolve. We value our different skills, perspectives and experiences and foster an environment where innovative powers thrive. To us, success is the feeling that the work we are doing will outlast us. The impact we make is not about what we achieve as individuals, but how we enable those around us to be their very best. From professional development to leadership opportunities, we empower our people to be extraordinary by playing to their strengths – because that is how we can make a difference.

Do you want to work on complex, business-critical problems, shape senior-level decisions and help drive the major transformation in Tryg’s CFO area?

As our new Strategic Transformation Manager, you will work at the centre of our finance transformation spanning data, systems, processes and organisation. You will help shape the direction of the transformation, bring structure to its most complex challenges and provide the insights and challenge that enable senior leadership to make the right decisions.

You will join a small Transformation Office with significant exposure and influence across the programme, working closely with senior leaders, project managers and subject-matter experts across Tryg.

About the role | Strategic thinking and hands-on transformation

The Transformation Office sits at the heart of the Finance transformation, creating clarity across the programme, challenging direction and helping ensure that critical issues are resolved.

As Strategic Transformation Manager, you will take significant ownership across the programme and act as a key sparring partner to the Head of Transformation Office.

In this role, you will:

• Shape and drive key transformation topics, bringing structure to ambiguous problems, challenging assumptions and priorities, and getting hands-on when important issues, risks or dependencies need to be resolved.

• Drive executive decision-making, turning complex topics into clear recommendations and high-quality materials for steering committees, the CFO and Executive Board.

• Act as a trusted challenger to project managers and workstream leaders, strengthening plans, connecting topics across the transformation and help create momentum and accountability around critical actions.

• Drive stakeholder alignment and change, identifying where engagement is needed and translating transformation decisions into clear narratives and communication for leaders and the wider organisation.

• Strengthen programme governance and transparency, ensuring that the right topics reach senior leadership at the right time and connecting progress, risks, resources, costs and benefits into a coherent programme view.

You will need to move comfortably between the big picture and the detail – from developing an Executive Board storyline to diving into an unfamiliar data, system or finance-process issue with subject-matter experts.

What we offer

• A front-row seat to a major transformation, turning strategic decisions into real organisational impact and change.

• A highly visible role with direct exposure to senior leaders & decision-makers across Tryg.

• The variety and intellectual challenge of consulting, working across strategy, finance and transformation on business-critical topics.

• Real opportunity to influence important decisions, challenging direction and helping solve complex transformation issues.

• A steep learning curve across finance, data, technology, processes and organisation.

• A small, high-impact & collaborative team with a strong focus on sparring, feedback and professional development.

• A strong platform for further career development & opportunities within Tryg.

About you | Consulting mindset with a drive to create impact

We are looking for someone with a strong strategic problem-solving toolkit who is equally comfortable thinking at executive level and getting into the details.

You are naturally curious and do not need to be the subject-matter expert from day one. You enjoy learning how things work, asking the questions that get to the heart of an issue.

You combine analytical rigour with pragmatism: you know when further analysis is needed and when it is time to make a recommendation or decision and move forward.

To succeed in this role we expect you to:

• Have from 4 years of relevant experience, for example from a top-tier management consultancy, in-house consulting team or a comparable strategy & transformation environment.

• Have a strong foundation in structured problem solving, executive communication, and working with senior stakeholders.

• Have proven ability to structure complex and ambiguous problems and translate them into clear recommendations.

• Be comfortable challenging senior stakeholders and subject-matter experts constructively.

• Be proactive, take ownership and naturally look ahead for emerging issues and opportunities.

• Be curious and willing to learn and dive into the details of unfamiliar topics across finance, technology, data and processes.

• Be fluent in a Scandinavian language (Danish, Swedish or Norwegian) and English.

Experience from finance or insurance is an advantage, but not a requirement.

About us | Transformation Office, CFO Area

The Transformation Office is currently a small team of 3 people within Strategic Finance & Transformation in Tryg’s CFO area.

Our role is not to run every initiative ourselves. Instead we work across the transformation to create clarity, challenge plans and assumptions, resolve cross-cutting issues and ensure that senior leadership has the insights and decision support needed to drive the programme forward.

You will join a small team with significant responsibility and exposure, where analytical curiosity, high-quality thinking and a willingness to challenge are central to how we work.

We look forward to hearing from you

Send your application and CV no later than 25 November 2026. We encourage you not to attach a photo to your CV.

We continuously invite relevant candidates for interviews, so we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. Once the right candidate has been identified, the recruitment process will be concluded.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please feel free to contact at Anders Hess-Auregård, Head of Transformation Office, CFO Area at anders.hessauregaard@tryg.dk

We encourage everyone regardless of gender identity, age, background, disability or origin to apply for the position. We are proud to have high employee satisfaction, strong professionalism and equal opportunities to develop your career in the Tryg Group. Tryg is the largest non-life insurance company in Scandinavia with activities in Denmark, Norway and Sweden. Every day we strive – each in our own way – to create peace of mind and affect the lives of most Scandinavians. Read more at www.tryg.com

We are extra[not]ordinary

*(ex· tra· not· or· di· nary |\ ik-ˈstr-not-ȯr-də-ˌner-ē)

Adjective: A unique word for Genmab meaning to go way beyond what is

usual; to be remarkable; proudly unique and authentic

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

The Senior Manager, Quality Global Affiliates Excellence, develops and owns selected shared Quality processes that enable Genmab’s affiliates to operate compliantly and efficiently as the business expands. A key responsibility is ownership of the affiliate training framework, including shared curricula, governance and ongoing maintenance. Process ownership and scalable ways of working

Affiliate training framework

• Own and maintain the affiliate training framework in partnership with Global Training, including role and task curricula, assignment principles, onboarding pathways and change governance

• Lead the affiliate training coordinator network and coordinate consistent implementation across markets. Maintain shared training matrices and coordinate updates following changes to global procedures

• Establish efficient arrangements for training assignment, administration and reporting with Global Training and affiliate coordinators. Retain clear local responsibility for identifying local requirements and confirming role applicability

• Monitor training completion and effectiveness, address recurring gaps with relevant stakeholders, and simplify training requirements and administration where justified

Quality oversight and continuous improvement

• Streamline affiliate Quality Management Reviews through common inputs, reporting and follow-up tools, and facilitate Quality Risk Management activities across affiliates

• Use process performance, affiliate feedback, inspection findings and workload data to identify improvements. Measure benefits through reduced duplication and effort, timely implementation and sustained process effectiveness

• Partner with relevant system owners to introduce proportionate digitalisation and automation

Project delivery and capability building

• Lead cross-functional improvement projects from problem definition through implementation and benefit evaluation, managing priorities and dependencies across multiple affiliates

Requirements

• Strong understanding of Good Distribution Practice and other GxP requirements relevant to affiliate operations, with experience implementing or improving Quality Management Systems

• Demonstrated experience owning or substantially improving processes across multiple markets or functions, with measurable gains in simplicity, efficiency or effectiveness

• Experience with Quality Risk Management and inspection readiness, including the ability to coordinate these activities across multiple markets

• Experience developing and implementing Quality guidance, tools, and training to enable structured, consistent, and scalable ways of working across affiliates

• Strong analytical, problem-solving, and process-improvement capabilities, with the ability to identify trends, simplify processes, and drive harmonization across markets with differing regulatory requirements

• Strong stakeholder management, communication, and influencing skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across global and local organizations and drive outcomes without direct authority

DKK666.400,00---999.600,00

jobs.occupation: Senior Embedded Software Engineer, Real-Time Vision - Simulator Technology
jobs.description:
Shape the future of real-time vision in sports technology

Join Trackman’s new Simulator Technology team and help build next-generation camera systems for the world’s leading golf simulators. We are looking for an experienced engineer with expertise in real-time video pipelines, camera integration, and low-latency systems.

About the team

Trackman is the global leader in indoor golf technology, delivering advanced simulator experiences through precision tracking, virtual golf software, and in-bay technology.

Our new Simulator Technology´s (SimTech) mission is to drive innovation across the entire in-bay customer experience: cameras, projectors, kiosks, moving floors, and the software that ties them together. The team works in close collaboration with Trackman's hardware, tracking, ML, and Virtual Golf teams to deliver seamless, world-class experiences. This is a unique opportunity to become one of the first engineers shaping the future of Trackman’s simulator technology used by elite athletes and golfers around the world.

The role

You will help build a Windows-based real-time vision platform that captures camera streams, runs AI-based image analysis, and outputs video overlays. The role focuses on low-latency camera integration and high-performance video pipelines. This work sits at the heart of SimTech's camera platform the low-level foundation that everything from swing capture to AI coaching will be built on. Our current team is strong in vision/ML, and we need an engineer who specializes in camera integration and real-time video pipelines.

What you will do

• 
Design and implement low-latency camera capture pipelines on Windows.

• 
Integrate with 3rd party cameras using vendor SDKs as well as our own custom camera modules

• 
Build reliable frame pipelines from capture to inference handoff to overlay output.

• 
Optimize for stable FPS, low jitter, and deterministic end-to-end latency.

• 
Implement robust camera lifecycle handling: hot-plug, disconnect/reconnect, error recovery.

• 
Work closely with ML engineers to define frame formats, metadata, and timing contracts.

• 
Build diagnostics: dropped-frame counters, latency telemetry, and health logging.

• 
Support production readiness across different camera models and hardware configurations.

Success in this role means delivering stable, low-latency dual-camera pipelines with reliable recovery mechanisms, robust telemetry, and a well-documented architecture that enables the broader SimTech team to confidently build on the platform.

Job requirements

• 
5+ years in real-time video, machine vision, or camera systems engineering.

• 
Strong C++ (C++17 or newer) - preferably on Windows.

• 
Hands-on with Media Foundation and/or DirectShow capture stacks.

• 
Proven integration experience with industrial camera SDKs (IDS peak / uEye SDK strongly preferred).

• 
Deep understanding of pixel formats, color conversion, timestamps, and buffering.

• 
Solid grasp of USB3 Vision / GenICam concepts and camera controls (exposure, gain, trigger modes).

• 
Experience with multithreaded/parallel pipelines and performance profiling.

• 
Practical OpenCV experience for image handling and overlay operations.

• 
Experience designing fault-tolerant long-running services/applications.

Preferred qualifications: Experience with GStreamer or FFmpeg, GPU acceleration, multi-camera synchronization, inference runtimes, hardware-in-the-loop testing, and GenICam / USB3 Vision standards is considered a plus.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

For additional information about the position, please contact Anton Husby at anton.husby@trackman.recruitee.com Applications are continuously assessed, so please send your application as soon as possible.

Build the platform – and the team around it

As Head of Data Platform, you will lead the design, implementation, and operation of the platform, built around AWS and Databricks. You will work across architecture, data pipelines, reusable data products, governance, and security while translating scientific and business needs into technical priorities.

About the team:

The Pandora SecOps team is part of the Global Security department, responsible for detection and response across Pandora's entire value chain. Over the past few years, we have built a robust technology platform that allows us to respond to alerts and incidents with greater speed and accuracy. This evolution has shifted the team towards an engineering-led approach, where the platform itself is treated as a product: designed, built, and continuously improved through code. The team owns the entire platform and all the technology components within, which enables full control and autonomy of the design decisions.

Pandora's broader shift towards PaaS and SaaS solutions is changing what our platform and team must deliver. Detection and response can no longer be anchored solely in traditional infrastructure telemetry; it must extend into application-level monitoring and the services our internal product teams build and operate. At the same time, operational technology (OT) across Pandora's manufacturing and production environments is becoming an increasing part of the detection and response scope, adding a new class of telemetry, constraints, and stakeholders to the platform. Practices like vulnerability management and exposure management are also capabilities that heavily rely on proper data platforms and pipelines.

This represents a paradigm shift in the SecOps operating model. From operating a security stack in relative isolation to engineering a data and detection platform in close collaboration with application and product teams across Digital & Technology (D&T).

About the role:

As a SecOps Platform Engineer, you will own the engineering, evolution, and reliability of the core detection and response platform, including our XDR, SIEM and NDR and the pipelines that feed it.

A central part of the role is driving and delivering the data foundation required for the shift towards application monitoring: onboarding new telemetry from PaaS and SaaS services, engineering scalable and cost-efficient ingestion, ensuring data quality, and building the platform capabilities that allow detection and response to cover applications and enterprise infrastructure. You will take ownership of selected components in our detection-as-code pipeline and the workflow integrations that connect the platform into the wider SecOps ecosystem. Also, practices like vulnerability management and exposure management, which rely heavily on proper data platforms and pipelines, are converging ever closer with detection and response, and platform engineering plays a key role in integrating these capabilities into one coherent operational system.

As part of the role, you will also be expected to take part in the internal SecOps on-call roster, ensuring coverage for critical alerts and incidents outside normal business hours. On-call participation is compensated in accordance with our on-call compensation scheme.

This is a senior role within the team. As with all senior members of Pandora SecOps, you will be expected to step in and drive incident response efforts when needed.

Key responsibilities:

• Own the continuous improvement of the SecOps technology platform, including XDR, SIEM and NDR, with a platform-as-code and infrastructure-as-code approach (versioned, peer-reviewed, CI/CD-deployed).

• Drive the data platform agenda: design and deliver scalable telemetry ingestion and log onboarding for PaaS and SaaS services, cloud platforms, and internally developed applications.

• Engineer and maintain workflow integrations across the SecOps ecosystem (SIEM, NDR, EDR, SOAR, IAM, ITSM), ensuring stable, secure, and observable connector and integration performance.

• Partner with application and product teams across D&T to embed security monitoring into new services, define logging and telemetry requirements, and shape the collaboration model between SecOps and product engineering.

• Collaborate closely with Detection Engineers, SOC Analysts, and Security Principal Architects to ensure platform capabilities are grounded in real operational needs and enable the full detection and response lifecycle.

• Ensure platform reliability, health, and performance through monitoring, capacity management, and root-cause analysis.

Qualifications:

• At least 5 years of full-time experience in security engineering, security operations engineering, or SecOps platform engineering, with demonstrable seniority appropriate to a manager-level individual contributor role.

• Solid hands-on experience from working within a SOC or incident response setup.

• Proven experience engineering and operating SIEM platforms, including data connectors, analytics rules, workspace architecture, ingestion optimization, and cost management. Experience with NDR platforms is a strong plus.

• Applied experience with infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Terraform, Bicep/ARM, or equivalent), including managing security platform content and configuration through version control rather than manual administration.

• Demonstrated working experience with Git, DevOps practices, and CI/CD pipelines applied to security tooling - for example detection-as-code, automated content deployment, or pipeline-driven platform changes.

• Proficiency in Python for building integrations, API clients, data onboarding tooling, and automation supporting platform operations.

• Solid understanding of cloud and identity ecosystems relevant to Pandora's environment: Azure, Entra ID, and Active Directory

• Knowledge about monitoring patterns for PaaS/SaaS services and modern application architectures is a plus.

• Experience integrating security platforms with enterprise tooling (e.g., SOAR, ITSM) and maintaining stable, secure, and well-documented integrations.

• Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work directly with application and product teams, translate security requirements into engineering deliverables, and influence without formal authority.

Further Information:

This role is a Career Band 4B (Individual Contributor) and reports directly to the Director, Information SecOps, Analytics & Incident Response and will join a team of 4 colleagues.

If you see yourself in the position and would like to become a part of Pandora’s future, please do not hesitate to apply. We look forward to hearing from you! Job Description: Do you want to work on complex, business-critical problems, shape senior-level decisions and help drive the major transformation in Tryg’s CFO area?

As our new Strategic Transformation Manager, you will work at the centre of our finance transformation spanning data, systems, processes and organisation. You will help shape the direction of the transformation, bring structure to its most complex challenges and provide the insights and challenge that enable senior leadership to make the right decisions.

You will join a small Transformation Office with significant exposure and influence across the programme, working closely with senior leaders, project managers and subject-matter experts across Tryg.

About the role | Strategic thinking and hands-on transformation

The Transformation Office sits at the heart of the Finance transformation, creating clarity across the programme, challenging direction and helping ensure that critical issues are resolved.

As Strategic Transformation Manager, you will take significant ownership across the programme and act as a key sparring partner to the Head of Transformation Office.

In this role, you will:

• Shape and drive key transformation topics, bringing structure to ambiguous problems, challenging assumptions and priorities, and getting hands-on when important issues, risks or dependencies need to be resolved.

• Drive executive decision-making, turning complex topics into clear recommendations and high-quality materials for steering committees, the CFO and Executive Board.

• Act as a trusted challenger to project managers and workstream leaders, strengthening plans, connecting topics across the transformation and help create momentum and accountability around critical actions.

• Drive stakeholder alignment and change, identifying where engagement is needed and translating transformation decisions into clear narratives and communication for leaders and the wider organisation.

• Strengthen programme governance and transparency, ensuring that the right topics reach senior leadership at the right time and connecting progress, risks, resources, costs and benefits into a coherent programme view.

You will need to move comfortably between the big picture and the detail – from developing an Executive Board storyline to diving into an unfamiliar data, system or finance-process issue with subject-matter experts.

What we offer

• A front-row seat to a major transformation, turning strategic decisions into real organisational impact and change.

• A highly visible role with direct exposure to senior leaders & decision-makers across Tryg.

• The variety and intellectual challenge of consulting, working across strategy, finance and transformation on business-critical topics.

• Real opportunity to influence important decisions, challenging direction and helping solve complex transformation issues.

• A steep learning curve across finance, data, technology, processes and organisation.

• A small, high-impact & collaborative team with a strong focus on sparring, feedback and professional development.

• A strong platform for further career development & opportunities within Tryg.

About you | Consulting mindset with a drive to create impact

We are looking for someone with a strong strategic problem-solving toolkit who is equally comfortable thinking at executive level and getting into the details.

You are naturally curious and do not need to be the subject-matter expert from day one. You enjoy learning how things work, asking the questions that get to the heart of an issue.

You combine analytical rigour with pragmatism: you know when further analysis is needed and when it is time to make a recommendation or decision and move forward.

To succeed in this role we expect you to:

• Have from 4 years of relevant experience, for example from a top-tier management consultancy, in-house consulting team or a comparable strategy & transformation environment.

• Have a strong foundation in structured problem solving, executive communication, and working with senior stakeholders.

• Have proven ability to structure complex and ambiguous problems and translate them into clear recommendations.

• Be comfortable challenging senior stakeholders and subject-matter experts constructively.

• Be proactive, take ownership and naturally look ahead for emerging issues and opportunities.

• Be curious and willing to learn and dive into the details of unfamiliar topics across finance, technology, data and processes.

• Be fluent in a Scandinavian language (Danish, Swedish or Norwegian) and English.

Experience from finance or insurance is an advantage, but not a requirement.

About us | Transformation Office, CFO Area

The Transformation Office is currently a small team of 3 people within Strategic Finance & Transformation in Tryg’s CFO area.

Our role is not to run every initiative ourselves. Instead we work across the transformation to create clarity, challenge plans and assumptions, resolve cross-cutting issues and ensure that senior leadership has the insights and decision support needed to drive the programme forward.

You will join a small team with significant responsibility and exposure, where analytical curiosity, high-quality thinking and a willingness to challenge are central to how we work.

Can you own the platform and pipelines that EIVA’s software is built on?

EIVA is an equipment and software engineering company delivering solutions to the international maritime industry. Our customers operate within renewable energy, oil & gas exploration, seabed-to-surface construction and hydrographic surveying – often in demanding environments where timing, precision and safety margins matter.

You do not need to know the subsea domain to apply. Here, your product is the software itself, and your users are the other engineering teams who build and ship on the platform you own. What matters is curiosity – the ability to ask the right questions and translate what you hear into good technical decisions – and a collaborative, team-first mindset.

The position is based at EIVA’s Danish office in Stilling (just one minute from the E45, approximately 15 minutes from Aarhus by car and easily accessible by bus).

What's involved?

As Tech Lead – Infrastructure, you'll own the platform, pipelines and infrastructure that our NaviSuite software is built on.

Around 80% of the role is hands-on: working directly in the team's technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and tooling. The rest is technical leadership – owning architecture within the Infrastructure team, making the final call on anything inside the team's decision domain, and knowing when a question needs to go further, to our architects or to alignment with other teams. You'll also help keep that decision domain itself well defined: what the team can decide on its own, and where it needs external alignment.

There could be occasional travel – around one to two short trips a year.

Your responsibilities…

• Doing hands-on development and engineering work across the team's core technical domains – platform, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, environments and internal tooling (around 80% of the role)

• Making the final technical decisions within the team's decision domain, and helping define where that domain's boundaries sit versus where the team needs external alignment

• Securing technical quality in the team – code and infrastructure-as-code review, best practices, testing and automation standards

• Owning architecture in the team – ensuring platform and pipeline work aligns with EIVA's overall architecture, and explaining the interdependencies to the team

• Participating in refinement, securing that features, stories and tasks describe architectural dependencies, feasibility, quality requirements and operational aspects such as reliability, security, cost and developer experience

• Cross team alignment – representing the Infrastructure team's technical position and making sure its work fits with adjacent work elsewhere in the organisation

• Driving clarification with architects on technical questions that sit outside the team's decision domain

Also part of the role…

• Providing technical mentoring and sparring for the team's engineers

• Supporting the other development teams as users of the platform – helping with adoption, guidance and acting on their feedback

• Taking operational responsibility for the platform and pipelines

• Keeping the team's technical practices current – seeking out training, evaluating new tooling and sharing that knowledge internally

• Maintaining technical documentation for the platform, pipelines and environments

• Giving technical input to hiring and onboarding new engineers on the team

• Giving technical input to estimation and planning together with the Team Manager/Product Owner

The ideal candidate…

• Has a background in software engineering or computer science

• Has hands-on experience building and maintaining platforms, CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code and internal tooling

• Has experience managing complex DevOps systems and workflows, and is comfortable making final technical calls within a defined decision domain

• Is familiar with tools such as Git/GitHub, artifact storage, Ansible and Terraform

• Has a collaborative mindset – comfortable gathering feedback from stakeholders across teams and using it to design clean, well-reasoned solutions

• Is a team player who's good at knowledge-sharing and educating peers, and takes proactive ownership of their domain

• It's a bonus if you also have experience with licence management systems, but not a requirement.

Joining the EIVA crew

At EIVA, you'll join a team that values openness, informality and collaboration – while working with high-end, innovative technology in an inspiring environment. We appreciate personal responsibility and proactivity, and there is room to make your mark if you spot new opportunities. Work-life balance matters to us and is reflected in the 15th, 20th and even 25th work anniversaries commonly celebrated at EIVA. We offer…

• A pension scheme and health insurance

• A canteen that no one leaves hungry

• An active social calendar

ROLE DESCRIPTION

INVISIO is looking for a commercially minded and pragmatic Corporate Legal Counsel to support its global business. This is a broad legal generalist role with a strong commercial focus, where you will work closely with the business and provide legal support across a wide range of matters, with particular emphasis on international contracts, tenders, customer projects and other commercial legal matters.

As Corporate Legal Counsel, you will become part of a small legal team together with Signe Karstoft, Legal Director, to whom you will report. The role is based at INVISIO’s headquarters in Hvidovre, and the legal function is organisationally anchored within INVISIO’s Sales & Program function, which consists of approximately 50 employees globally, including around 25-30 in Denmark. You will primarily support the global sales organisation and work closely with colleagues across the business. Much of your work will involve large and complex customer contracts, tenders and projects.

You will provide legal support across INVISIO’s international business, including in relation to US contracts, such as contracts within the defence sector, and support sales teams across Europe and other markets. You will also support INVISIO in connection with major public tenders, including tenders involving ministries and defence organisations, providing legal support on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

As a technology company, intellectual property is an important part of INVISIO’s business. While dedicated specialists handle areas such as patents, you may also advise on IP-related matters as part of the broader commercial legal support. Experience with IP or from a technology or other IP-intensive business would therefore be an advantage.

In addition to the day-to-day legal support, you will contribute to developing and improving the way Legal supports the business. This includes driving legal improvement initiatives, maintaining and developing contract templates and legal guidelines, and conducting workshops and awareness activities for the business.

The role is highly international and outward-facing, with significant interaction with customers and stakeholders at all levels. You will have opportunities to join customer visits and negotiate contracts abroad, as well as participate in trade fairs in Denmark, Europe and the US.

The role is expected to involve approximately 25 travel days per year.

As INVISIO continues to grow rapidly, you will work in a fast-paced environment where priorities can change quickly, and no two days are the same.

AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY

INVISIO is looking for an independent and commercially minded lawyer who takes ownership and enjoys working closely with customers and colleagues across the organisation. Your key responsibilities will include:

Commercial contracts and negotiations:

• 
Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of commercial contracts, including large international sales contracts, non-disclosure agreements, letters of intent, consulting agreements, tender-related contracts and distribution agreements.

• 
Take an active role in customer dialogue and contract negotiations and provide commercially focused legal advice, working closely with relevant stakeholders to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives.

• 
Provide pragmatic legal advice on contractual and other commercial matters arising in the day-to-day business.

**

Tenders and customer projects:**

• 
Provide legal support in connection with major public tenders, including reviewing tender documentation and advising on contractual and other legal questions arising throughout the tender process.

• 
Advise on legal and contractual aspects of tender structures, including which INVISIO entity should participate and any related intercompany arrangements.

• 
Support and, where relevant, take a coordinating role in customer projects and other commercial initiatives, including advising on contractual set-ups, priorities and how existing solutions can be applied in different markets etc.

**

IP and export control:**

• Ad hoc Advise on IP and export control matters, including IP considerations in commercial agreements and questions relating to export restrictions and requirements in connection with international sales and customer projects.

**

Legal development and business support:**

• 
Develop, maintain and improve contract templates, legal guidelines and other tools.

• 
Drive legal improvement initiatives and conduct workshops and legal awareness activities for the business, for example in relation to NDA’s.

• 
Provide ad hoc legal advice and support across INVISIO as required.

REPORTING AND TITLE

Reporting to: Signe Karstoft, Legal Director.

Title: Corporate Legal Counsel.

IDEAL EXPERIENCE

Education: You hold a master’s degree in law (cand.jur. or cand.merc.jur.).

Work experience: You have approximately 3-6 years of relevant legal experience from an in-house role, for example in a technology or software company or another larger international industrial company.

Legal areas of specialisation: You have strong experience in drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements and are comfortable handling contractual matters independently. You also have experience supporting tender processes and advising on the legal and contractual matters that arise in this context.

In addition, you have a broad legal profile and are able to navigate a varied range of legal matters. Experience with IP-related matters, particularly from a technology or other IP-intensive business, would be an advantage. Knowledge of export control would also be beneficial.

Commercial: You have a strong commercial mindset and understand how legal advice fits into the broader business context.

You have experience working directly with customers and are comfortable collaborating with colleagues at all levels of the organisation. You are able to balance legal considerations with commercial objectives and provide pragmatic, solution-oriented advice.

Language skills: You are fluent in Danish and English, both written and verbal.

PERSONAL CAPABILITIES

Independent & proactive: You work independently, take ownership of your responsibilities and proactively drive matters forward.

Outgoing & interpersonal: You are outgoing and enjoy interacting with people with different backgrounds and at all levels, both internally and externally. You have strong interpersonal skills and are comfortable engaging with customers, colleagues and senior management.

Analytical & pragmatic: You have strong analytical skills and are able to understand complex legal and commercial matters while maintaining a pragmatic and solution-oriented approach.

Structured & able to prioritise: You work in a structured manner, maintain a good overview of your responsibilities and are able to prioritise effectively in a fast-paced environment where new and urgent matters frequently arise. You remain calm and focused when priorities change or deadlines are tight.

Stakeholder management & collaboration: You build strong relationships and collaborate effectively across functions and organisational levels. You are a team-oriented colleague who contributes to a strong sense of teamwork across the organisation and is able to influence stakeholders in a constructive manner.

Positive & constructive: You have a professional approach to your work and interact with others with maturity and integrity. You bring positive energy, are resilient when challenges arise and remain constructive in a busy environment.

INVISIO’S VALUE PROPOSITION TO YOU

INVISIO is a rapidly growing company with ambitious growth targets. The company achieves these ambitions through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts will be important to INVISIO’s continued success, and by joining the company, you will become part of an international headquarter with an informal working environment.

INVISIO offers a wide range of professional and social employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

ABOUT INVISIO

INVISIO is a global leader in communications technology for professionals working in mission-critical environments. Established in Denmark in 1999, the company develops and markets advanced, integrated communication systems for defence and public safety professionals, helping users communicate clearly and safely in demanding environments.

INVISIO’s modular and scalable portfolio includes headsets, control units, intercom systems, hubs and software designed to work together across dismounted, vehicle-based and command operations. The solutions are marketed under the INVISIO and Racal Acoustics brands.

Headquartered in Copenhagen, INVISIO has an international presence across Europe, North America and Asia. The company has approximately 330 employees globally, including around 215 in Denmark, and is growing rapidly. INVISIO is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (Large Cap).

INVISIO is characterised by a strong focus on innovation, close customer collaboration and an international working environment. Its core values are Passion, Innovation, Teamwork and Customer First.

About Us

The Job

Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.

In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:

• 
Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.

• 
OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.

• 
Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.

• 
Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.

• 
Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.

• 
Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.

Qualifications:

• 
Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs.

• 
Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python

• 
Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices.

• 
Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers.

• 
Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards.

• 
Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers

• 
Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT.

• 
Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods.

• 
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team.

• 
Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus.

• 
Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus.

• 
Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus.
